# Rashi on Psalms

רש"י על תהילים

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms)

הפירוש הנפוץ והמוכר ביותר לתורה, המבאר את פשטי המקראות בתוספת הרחבות פרשניות; חובר במאה ה-11.

Most widely-read biblical commentary, compiled in the 11th-century, explaining the simple meaning of the text with interpretive elaborations.

Sections: Chapter-Verse-Comment

Location: Tanakh/Rishonim on Tanakh/Rashi/Writings

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Sefaria vocalized edition (Segments: 2521, License: unknown)

Version (En): The Judaica Press complete Tanach with Rashi, translated by A. J. Rosenberg (Segments: 2497)


## Chapter 1


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 1:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:1:1)


**אַשְׁרֵי הָאִישׁ.** בַּעֲשָׂרָה לְשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁל זֶמֶר נֶאֱמַר סֵפֶר זֶה, בְּנִצּוּחַ, בְּנִגּוּן, בְּמִזְמוֹר, בְּשִׁיר, בְּהַלֵּל, בִּתְפִלָּה, בִּבְרָכָה, בְּהוֹדָאָה, בְּאַשְׁרֵי, בְּהַלְלוּיָהּ, כְּנֶגֶד עֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁאֲמָרוּהוּ, אָדָם, מַלְכִּי צֶדֶק, אַבְרָהָם, מֹשֶׁה, דָּוִד, שְׁלֹמֹה, אָסָף, וּשְׁלֹשָׁה בְּנֵי קֹרַח, וַחֲלוּקִין עַל יְדוּתוּן (קהלת רבה ז,לט). יֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אָדָם הָיָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים (דברי הימים א טז:לח), וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אֵין יְדוּתוּן שֶׁבְּסֵפֶר זֶה אֶלָּא עַל שֵׁם הַדָּתוֹת וְהַדִּינִים שֶׁל גְּזֵרוֹת שֶׁעָבְרוּ עָלָיו וְעַל יִשְׂרָאֵל:


**The praises of a man** This book was composed with ten expressions of song: 1) with conducting, 2) with melody, 3) with musical accompaniment, 4) with song, 5) with praise, 6) with prayer, 7) with blessing, 8) with thanksgiving, 9) with praises, and 10) with “Praise God.” These correspond to the ten men who composed them: 1) Adam, 2) Malchizedek, 3) Abraham, 4) Moses, 5) David, 6) Solomon, 7) Asaph, and 8-10) the three sons of Korah. Concerning Jeduthun, there is a dispute. Some say that Jeduthun was a man, as is written in Chronicles. Others maintain that Jeduthun mentioned in this Book means nothing else but the ordinances (דתות) and laws of the decrees that were passed over him and over Israel.


###### Rashi on Psalms 1:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:1:2)


**אַשְׁרֵי הָאִישׁ.** (לישפלישמנ״ץ בלע״ז) אִשּׁוּרָיו שֶׁל אִישׁ וּתְהִלּוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם אֵלּוּ הֵם **אֲשֶׁר לֹא הָלַךְ**, כִּי מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא הָלַךְ **לֹא עָמַד**, וּמִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא עָמַד **לֹא יָשָׁב**:


**The praises of a man** Heb. אשרי les felicements(?) in Old French. The praises of a man, and these are the praises of a man: that he did not follow, because since he did not follow, he did not stand, and since he did not stand, he did not sit.


###### Rashi on Psalms 1:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:1:3)


**לֵצִים.** (גאבור״ש בלע״ז. מלה נשנית גאבערס בל״א שפעטטער:)


**scorners** (Old French, gabors.)



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 1:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:2:1)


**כִּי אִם בְּתוֹרַת ה׳ חֶפְצוֹ.** הָא לָמַדְתָּ, שֶׁמּוֹשַׁב לֵצִים מְבִיאוֹ לִידֵי בִּטּוּל תּוֹרָה (עבודה זרה יח:):


**But his desire is in the law of the Lord** Hence you learn that the company of scorners brings one to neglect the study of Torah.


###### Rashi on Psalms 1:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:2:2)


**וּבְתוֹרָתוֹ יֶהְגֶּה.** בִּתְחִלָּה הִיא נִקְרֵאת **תּוֹרַת ה׳**, וּמִשֶּׁעָמַל בָּהּ הִיא נִקְרֵאת תּוֹרָתוֹ (עבודה זרה יט.):


**and in his law he meditates** In the beginning, it is called the law of the Lord, and after he has toiled to master it, it is called his own Torah.


###### Rashi on Psalms 1:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:2:3)


**יֶהְגֶּה.** כָּל לְשׁוֹן הֶגֶה בַּלֵּב הוּא, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר ״וְהֶגְיוֹן לִבִּי״ (תהלים יט:טו), ״לִבְּךָ יֶהְגֶּה אֵימָה״ (ישעיהו לג:יח), ״כִּי שֹׁד יֶהְגֶּה לִבָּם״ (משלי כד:ב):


**he meditates** Heb. יהגה. Every expression of הגה refers to the heart, as you say (below 19:15): “and the meditation (והגיון) of my heart”; (Isa. 33:18), “Your heart shall meditate (יהגה) in fear”; (Prov. 24:2), “For their heart thinks (יהגה) of plunder.”



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 1:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:3:1)


**שָׁתוּל.** פְּלַנְדִי״ץ בְּלַעַ״ז:


**planted** Heb. שתול, plonte in Old French (plante).


###### Rashi on Psalms 1:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:3:2)


**פַּלְגֵי.** רָאוּיְיָארוֹ״שׁ בְּלַעַ״ז:


**rivulets** ruyseys in Old French, (ruisseaux), brooks (as in Ezek. 32:6).


###### Rashi on Psalms 1:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:3:3)


**וְעָלֵהוּ לֹא יִבּוֹל.** אֲפִלּוּ הַפְּסֹלֶת שֶׁבּוֹ לְצֹרֶךְ הִיא. שִׂיחָתָן שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים לְצֹרֶךְ הִיא וּצְרִיכָה לִמּוּד (עבודה זרה יט:):


**and its leaves do not wilt** Even the inferior part of it serves a purpose. The conversation of Torah scholars is essential and requires study.


###### Rashi on Psalms 1:3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:3:4)


**לֹא יִבּוֹל.** לְשׁוֹן כָּמוֹשׁ, פְּלִישְׁטִי״ר בְּלַעַ״ז:


**do not wilt** Heb. יבול, an expression of wilting, fleistre in Old French.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 1:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:4:1)


**כַּמּוֹץ.** לְשׁוֹן קַשׁ, קוֹמְבְּלָ״א בְּלַעַ״ז:


**like chaff** An expression of straw, come bale in Old French (comme paille), like straw.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 1:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:5:1)


**עַל כֵּן וְגוֹ׳.** דָּבוּק הוּא לַמִּקְרָא שֶׁל אַחֲרָיו:


**Therefore, etc.** This refers to the verse following it.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 1:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/1:6:1)


**כִּי יוֹדֵעַ ה׳ וְגוֹ׳.** לְפִי שֶׁהוּא יוֹדֵעַ דֶּרֶךְ צַדִּיקִים, וּלְפָנָיו הוּא לְהַכִּירָהּ תָּמִיד, **וְדֶרֶךְ רְשָׁעִים** שְׂנוּאָה בְּעֵינָיו וּמַעֲבִירָהּ מִלְּפָנָיו, עַל כֵּן לֹא תְהֵא הֲקָמַת רֶגֶל לָרְשָׁעִים לְיוֹם הַדִּין, וְלַחַטָּאִים לִיכָּתֵב בַּעֲדַת צַדִּיקִים:


**For the Lord knows the way, etc.** Because He knows the way of the righteous, and it is before Him to recognize it constantly; the way of the wicked is hateful to Him, and He removes it from before Him. Therefore, the foot of the wicked will not stand up on the day of judgment, neither shall the sinners be written in the congregation of the righteous.



## Chapter 2


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 2:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:1:1)


**לָמָּה רָגְשׁוּ גוֹיִם.** רַבּוֹתֵינוּ (ברכות ז:) דָּרְשׁוּ אֶת הָעִנְיָן עַל מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ, וּלְפִי מַשְׁמָעוֹ יִהְיֶה נָכוֹן לְפוֹתְרוֹ עַל דָּוִד עַצְמוֹ, כְּעֵין שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים כִּי מָשְׁחוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת דָּוִד לְמֶלֶךְ עֲלֵיהֶם וַיִּקָּבְצוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים אֶת מַחֲנֵיהֶם״ (שמואל ב ה:יז), וְנָפְלוּ בְיָדוֹ, וַעֲלֵיהֶם אָמַר **לָמָּה רָגְשׁוּ גוֹיִם** וְנִתְקַבְּצוּ כֻּלָּם:


**Why have nations gathered** Our Sages (Ber. 7b) expounded the passage as referring to the King Messiah, but according to its apparent meaning, it is proper to interpret it as referring to David himself, as the matter is stated (II Sam. 5:17): “And the Philistines heard that they had anointed David as king over Israel, and all the Philistines went up to seek, etc.,” and they fell into his hands. Concerning them, he says, “Why have nations gathered,” and they all gathered.


###### Rashi on Psalms 2:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:1:2)


**וּלְאֻמִּים יֶהְגּוּ.** בְּלִבָּם רִיק:


**and kingdoms think** vain things in their heart.


###### Rashi on Psalms 2:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:1:3)


**וּלְאֻמִּים.** מְנַחֵם פָּתַר לְאֻמִּים וְאֻמִּים וְגוֹיִם כֻּלָּם קְרוֹבֵי עִנְיָן:


**and kingdoms** Heb. ולאמים. Menachem interprets לאמים, אמות, and גוים as all closely related.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 2:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:2:1)


**יִתְיַצְּבוּ מַלְכֵי אֶרֶץ וְרוֹזְנִים נוֹסְדוּ יָחַד וְגוֹ׳. וְרוֹזְנִים.** שִׁינְיוֹ״רְשׁ בְּלַעַ״ז:


**Kings of a land stand up and nobles take counsel, etc.** Heb. רוזנים, senors (seigneurs) in Old French, lords.


###### Rashi on Psalms 2:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:2:2)


**נוֹסְדוּ.** לְשׁוֹן סוֹד, פורקונשילרוו״ט בְּלַעַ״ז. וּמַה הִיא הָעֵצָה?


**take counsel** Heb. נוסדו, an expression of counsel (סוד), furt konsilez in Old French (furent conseilles), they hold counsel (see below 55:15). And what is the counsel?...



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 2:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:3:1)


**נְנַתְּקָה אֶת מוֹסְרוֹתֵימוֹ.** דִּישְׁרוֹנְפְרוֹיְמ״שׁ לוֹיְקוֹרַאנְגְל״שׁ בְּלַעַ״ז, אֵלּוּ רְצוּעוֹת שֶׁקּוֹשְׁרִין הָעוֹל בָּהֶם:


**Let us break their bands** Deronproms lor koyongles in Old French (as in Jer. 27:2). These are the bands with which the yoke is tied.


###### Rashi on Psalms 2:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:3:2)


**עֲבוֹתֵימוֹ.** לוֹיִקוֹרְדוֹ״שׁ בְּלַעַ״ז:


**their cords** Heb. עבתימו, lor kordes (leur cordes) in Old French.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 2:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:4:1)


**יִשְׂחָק יִלְעַג יְדַבֵּר.** לְשׁוֹן הֹוֶה הֵם מְשַׁמְּשִׁין:


**laughs...mocks...speaks** They are meant as the present tense.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 2:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:5:1)


**אָז יְדַבֵּר אֵלֵימוֹ.** כְּמוֹ עֲלֵיהֶם, וּמַה הוּא הַדִּבּוּר?


**Then He speaks to them** Heb. אלימו, like אליהם. And what is the speech?...



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 2:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:6:1)


**וַאֲנִי נָסַכְתִּי מַלְכִּי.** לָמָּה רְגַשְׁתֶּם, וַאֲנִי מִנִּיתִי לִי אֶת זֶה לִנְסֹךְ וְלִמְלֹךְ **עַל צִיּוֹן הַר קָדְשִׁי**?


**But I have enthroned My king** Why have you gathered together? I have appointed this one for Me to govern and to reign on Zion, My holy mount.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 2:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:7:1)


**אֲסַפְּרָה אֶל חוֹק.** אָמַר דָּוִד: חֹק קָצוּב הוּא, וּמְקַבֵּל עָלַי לְסַפֵּר זֹאת וּלְהוֹדִיעַ:


**I will tell of the decree** Said David, “This is an established decree, and [one] that I have received to tell this and to make known.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 2:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:7:2)


**ה׳ אָמַר אֵלַי.** עַל יְדֵי נָתָן וְגָד וּשְׁמוּאֵל (שמואל ב ז:ד; שמואל א ג:כא):


**The Lord said to me** through Nathan, Gad, and Samuel.


###### Rashi on Psalms 2:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:7:3)


**בְּנִי אַתָּה.** רֹאשׁ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, הַקְּרוּיִין בַּתּוֹרָה ״בְּנִי בְכוֹרִי״ (שמות ד:כב), וְהֵם יִתְקַיְּמוּ עַל יָדְךָ. כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּאַבְנֵר (שמואל ב ג:יח): ״כֹּה אָמַר ה׳ בְּיַד דָּוִד עַבְדִּי אוֹשִׁיעַ אֶת עַמִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל״, וּבִשְׁבִילָם אַתָּה לְפָנַי כְּבֵן, שֶׁכֻּלָּם תְּלוּיִין בְּךָ:


**You are My son** The head over Israel, who are called “My firstborn son.” And they will endure through you, as is stated concerning Abner (II Sam. 3:18): “for God said, etc., ‘By the hand of My bondsman David shall I deliver...Israel.’” And for their sake, you are before Me as a son because they are all dependent upon you.


###### Rashi on Psalms 2:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:7:4)


**אֲנִי הַיּוֹם.** שֶׁהִמְלַכְתִּיךָ עֲלֵיהֶם:


**this day have I** for I have enthroned you over them.


###### Rashi on Psalms 2:7:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:7:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:7:5)


**יְלִדְתִּיךָ.** לִהְיוֹת קָרוּי בְּנִי, וְחָבִיב עָלַי כְּבֵן בִּשְׁבִילָם; כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברי הימים א יד:ב) ״וַיֵּדַע דָּוִיד כִּי הֱכִינוֹ ה׳ לְמֶלֶךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכִי נִשֵּׂאת מַלְכוּתוֹ בַּעֲבוּר עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל״, וּמָצִינוּ בְּמַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַחֲבִיבִין לְפָנָיו שֶׁקְּרוּיִין בָּנִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמואל ב ז:יד) בִּשְׁלֹמֹה ״הוּא יִהְיֶה לִּי לְבֵן וַאֲנִי אֶהְיֶה לּוֹ לְאָב״. וְעוֹד מָצִינוּ בְּדָוִד בְּמִזְמוֹר פ״ט ״הוּא יִקְרָאֵנִי אָבִי אָתָּה אֵלִי וְצוּר יְשׁוּעָתִי״ (תהלים פט:כז):


**begotten you** to be called My son and to be beloved to Me as a son for their sake, as it is stated (I Chronicles 14:2): ‘And David knew that the Lord had established him as king over Israel, and that his kingdom was highly exalted for the sake of His people Israel.’ And we find that the kings of Israel who were beloved before Him were called sons, as it is stated (II Sam. 7:14) concerning Solomon: “I will be to him a father, and he shall be to Me a son.” We find further concerning David (Ps. 89:27) “He shall call Me, ‘You are my Father, my God, and the Rock of my salvation.’”



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 2:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:8:1)


**שְׁאַל מִמֶּנִּי.** הִתְפַּלֵּל אֵלַי בְּכָל עֵת שֶׁאַתָּה בָּא לְהִלָּחֵם בְּאוֹיְבֶיךָ:


**Request of Me** Pray to Me whenever you come to battle your enemies.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 2:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:9:1)


**תִּרְעֵם.** תְּרוֹצְצֵם:


**You shall break them** Heb. תרעם [like] תרוצצם.


###### Rashi on Psalms 2:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:9:2)


**בְּשֵׁבֶט בַּרְזֶל.** הִיא הַחֶרֶב:


**with an iron rod** That is the sword.


###### Rashi on Psalms 2:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:9:3)


**תְּנַפְּצֵם.** תְּשַׁבְּרֵם, וְהוּא לְשׁוֹן נָפוֹץ בְּכָל הַמִּקְרָא: חֶרֶס הַמְּשֻׁבָּר לִשְׁבָרִים דַּקִּים:


**you shall shatter them** Heb. תנפצם, you shall break them, and that is the expression of נפוץ throughout the Scriptures, a potsherd that is bro ken into fine pieces.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 2:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:10:1)


**וְעַתָּה מְלָכִים הַשְׂכִּילוּ.** נְבִיאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אַנְשֵׁי רַחֲמִים, וּמוֹכִיחִים אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לָסוּר מֵרָעָתָם (תנחומא, בלק א), שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא פּוֹשֵׁט יָד לָרְשָׁעִים וְלַצַּדִּיקִים:


**And now, [you] kings, be wise** The Jewish prophets are merciful people. They reprove the heathens to turn away from their evil, for the Holy One, blessed be He, extends His hand to the wicked and to the righteous.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 2:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:11:1)


**וְגִילוּ בִּרְעָדָה.** כְּשֶׁתָּבוֹא אוֹתָהּ רְעָדָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּהּ (ישעיהו לג:יד) ״אָחֲזָה רְעָדָה חֲנֵפִים״, תָּגִילוּ וְתִשְׂמְחוּ אִם עֲבַדְתֶּם אֶת ה׳:


**and rejoice with quaking** When the quaking, about which it is written (Isa. 33:14): “Trembling seized the flatterers,” comes, you will rejoice and be happy if you have served the Lord.



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Psalms 2:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:12:1)


**נַשְּׁקוּ בַר.** זָרְזוּ עַצְמְכֶם בְּבַר לֵב. (נוסח אחר) **נַשְּׁקוּ בַר.** אַרְנִישְׁמְנְט בְּלַעַ״ז, וּמְנַחֵם פָּתַר אוֹתוֹ לְשׁוֹן תַּאֲוָה כְּמוֹ ״וְאֶל אִישֵׁךְ תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ״ (בראשית ג:טז):


**Arm yourselves with purity** Arm yourselves with purity of the heart. Some explain נשקו as garnimont in Old French, equipping. (This is from the verb, garnir. Garnimont means to provide, as in Gen. 41:40). Menachem (p. 179) interprets it as an expression of desire, as (in Gen. 3:16): “Your longing (תשוקתך) shall be for your husband.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 2:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:12:2)


**פֶּן יֶאֱנַף.** פֶּן יִקְצֹף:


**lest He become angry** Heb. יאנף, lest He become angry.


###### Rashi on Psalms 2:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:12:3)


**וְתֹאבְדוּ דֶרֶךְ.** כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְדֶרֶךְ רְשָׁעִים תֹּאבֵד״ (תהלים א:ו):


**and you perish in the way** Like the matter that is stated (above 1:16): “but the way of the wicked shall perish.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 2:12:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:12:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/2:12:4)


**כִּי יִבְעַר כִּמְעַט אַפּוֹ.** כִּי בְרֶגַע מוּעָט יִבְעַר אַפּוֹ עֲלֵיכֶם פִּתְאוֹם, וְאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה **אַשְׁרֵי כָּל חוֹסֵי בוֹ** – יִהְיוּ נִכָּרִים אִשּׁוּרֵי הַחוֹסִים בּוֹ:


**for in a moment His wrath will be kindled** For in a short moment His wrath will suddenly be kindled against them, and at that time, the praises of all those who take refuge in Him will be discerned, the praises of all who take refuge in Him.



## Chapter 3


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 3:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:1:1)


**מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד בְּבָרְחוֹ.** הַרְבֵּה דְּרָשׁוֹת דָּרְשׁוּ בְּנֵי אַגָּדָה בַּדָּבָר, וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ (ברכות ז:): מִשֶּׁאָמַר לוֹ הַנָּבִיא ״הִנְנִי מֵקִים עָלֶיךָ רָעָה מִתּוֹךְ בֵּיתֶךָ״ (שמואל ב יב:יא) הָיָה לִבּוֹ סוֹעֵר שֶׁמָּא עֶבֶד אוֹ מַמְזֵר יָקוּם עָלַי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְרַחֵם עָלַי, כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּדַע שֶׁבְּנוֹ הוּא שָׂמַח. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: עַל שֶׁרָאָה טַכְסִיסוֹ קַיֶּמֶת, שֶׁהָיוּ עֲבָדָיו וְהַכְּרֵתִי וְהַפְּלֵתִי, שֶׁהֵם סַנְהֶדְרִין, מַחֲזִיקִים אֲדָנוּתוֹ עֲלֵיהֶם; כְּשֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם ״קוּמוּ וְנִבְרְחָה מִפְּנֵי אַבְשָׁלוֹם״ (שמואל ב טו:יד), מַה כְּתִיב שָׁם? ״כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר אֲדֹנִי הַמֶּלֶךְ הִנֵּה עֲבָדֶיךָ״ (שמואל ב טו:טו); וּכְשֶׁבָּא מַחֲנַיִם, ״וְשֹׁבִי בֶן נָחָשׁ וּמָכִיר בֶּן עַמִּיאֵל וּבַרְזִלַּי הַגִּלְעָדִי״ (שמואל ב יז:כז) יָצְאוּ לִקְרָאתוֹ וְכִלְכְּלוּהוּ שָׁם:


**A song of David, when he fled** The Aggadists expounded many homilies on this matter. Our Sages said (Ber. 7a): When the prophet said to him (in II Sam. 12:11), “Behold I will raise up against you evil out of your own house etc.,” his heart was quaking, perhaps a slave or a mamzer [a child of an illicit union] will rise up against me, who will not have mercy on me. As soon as he found out that it was his son, he was happy. The Midrash Aggadah (Midrash Psalms 3:3) [states]: Because he saw his order intact, for his servants, and the Kerethite and Pelethite, who were the Sanhedrin were affirming his lordship over themselves. When he said to them (ibid. 15:14), “Arise and let us flee etc. from Absalom,” what is written there? (verse 15) “Whatever my lord the king shall choose, behold your servants [are ready to do].” And when he came to Mahanaim (ibid. 17:27), “Shobi, etc. and Machir the son of Amiel, etc. and Barzilai the Gileadite” came to meet him and sustained him there.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 3:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:2:1)


**רַבִּים קָמִים עָלָי.** בְּנֵי אָדָם גְּדוֹלִים בַּתּוֹרָה, גְּדוֹלִים בְּחָכְמָה, גְּדוֹלִים בְּעֹשֶׁר, גְּדוֹלִים בְּקוֹמָה; כְּגוֹן שָׁאוּל (שמואל א טז:ז) וִילִידֵי הָרָפָה (שמואל ב כא:טז-כב), דּוֹאֵג (שמואל א כא:ח) וַאֲחִיתֹפֶל (שמואל ב טו:יב):


**Great men rise up against me** Men great in Torah, great in wisdom, great in wealth, tall in stature, such as Saul; the children of Raphah; Doeg, and Ahitophel.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 3:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:3:1)


**אוֹמְרִים לְנַפְשִׁי.** עַל נַפְשִׁי:


**say concerning my soul** Heb. לנפשי, concerning my soul.


###### Rashi on Psalms 3:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:3:2)


**אֵין יְשׁוּעָתָה לּוֹ בֵאלֹהִים סֶלָה.** לְפִי שֶׁבָּא עַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ:


**“He has no salvation in God to eternity”** Because he was intimate with a married woman.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 3:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:6:1)


**אֲנִי שָׁכַבְתִּי וָאִישָׁנָה.** לִבִּי אָטוּם בִּדְאָגָה וָפַחַד:


**I lay down and slept** My heart was clogged from worry and fear.


###### Rashi on Psalms 3:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:6:2)


**הֱקִיצוֹתִי.** מִדְּאָגָתִי, כִּי בָטַחְתִּי **כִּי יְהוָה יִסְמְכֵנִי**:


**I awoke** from my worry, because I trusted that the Lord would support me.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 3:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:7:1)


**שָׁתוּ.** לְשׁוֹן ״שְׁאִיָּה״ (ישעיה כד:יב) גאטירנ״ט בְּלַעַ״ז. וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: שָׁתוּ כְּמוֹ שָׂמוּ, כְּמוֹ ״לְמַעַן שִׁתִי אֹתֹתַי״ (שמות י:א):


**have set themselves** Heb. שתו, an expression of desolation, gatiront in Old French, to destroy. Others say that שתו is like שמו, they placed, like (Exod. 10:1): “in order that I set up (שתי) my signs.”



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 3:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:8:1)


**כִּי הִכִּיתָ אֶת כָּל אוֹיְבַי לֶחִי.** מַכַּת בִּזָּיוֹן הִיא, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר: ״יִתֵּן לְמַכֵּהוּ לֶחִי״ (איכה ג:ל), ״בַּשֵּׁבֶט יַכּוּ עַל הַלֶּחִי״ (מיכה ד:יד). וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: מַכַּת הַפֶּה, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר: ״וַיְצַו אֶל בֵּיתוֹ וַיֵּחָנַק״ (שמואל ב יז:כג):


**for You have struck all my enemies on the cheek** This is a disgraceful blow, as you say (Lam. 3: 30): “Let him offer his cheek to the smiter”; (Micah 4:14), “with a rod they strike...on the cheek.” According to the Midrash Aggadah (Mid. Ps. 3:7), this is a sickness of the mouth, [choking, croup] as you say (II Sam. 17:23): “And he [Ahithophel] gave charge to his household and he strangled himself.

### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 3:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/3:9:1)


**לַה׳ הַיְשׁוּעָה וְגוֹ׳.** עָלָיו לְהוֹשִׁיעַ אֶת עֲבָדָיו וְאֶת עַמּוֹ, וְעַל עַמּוֹ מוּטָּל לְבָרֵךְ וּלְהוֹדוֹת לוֹ **סֶּלָה**:


**It is incumbent upon the Lord to save, etc.** It is incumbent upon Him to save His servants and His people, and it is incumbent upon His people to bless Him and thank Him forever.



## Chapter 4


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 4:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:1:1)


**לַמְנַצֵּחַ בִּנְגִינוֹת.** מִזְמוֹר זֶה יָסַד דָּוִד, שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּהוּ בְּנֵי לֵוִי הַמְנַצְּחִין בִּנְגִינוֹת בְּשִׁיר עַל הַדּוּכָן. לְשׁוֹן נִצּוּחַ נוֹפֵל בַּמִּתְחַזְּקִים בָּעֲבוֹדָה, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״יַעַמְדוּ הַלְוִיִּם מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה לְנַצֵּחַ עַל מְלֶאכֶת בֵּית ה׳״ (עזרא ג:ח):


**To the conductor with melodies** David established this psalm so that the Levites who conduct the melodies when singing on the platform should recite it. The expression of נצוח denotes those who apply themselves to the service, as the matter is stated (Ezra 3:8): “and appointed the Levites from twenty years old and upwards to conduct the work of the house of the Lord.”



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 4:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:2:1)


**בַּצָּר הִרְחַבְתָּ לִּי.** בַּיָּמִים שֶׁעָבְרוּ עָלַי, וּמֵעַתָּה חָנֵּנִי וּשְׁמַע תְּפִלָּתִי:


**in my distress You have relieved me** in the days that have passed over me. From now on, be gracious to me and hearken to my prayer.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 4:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:3:1)


**בְּנֵי אִישׁ.** בְּנֵי אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב הַקְּרוּיִים אִישׁ, בְּאַבְרָהָם נֶאֱמַר (בראשית כ:ז) ״הָשֵׁב אֶת אֵשֶׁת הָאִישׁ״, בְּיִצְחָק נֶאֱמַר (בראשית כד:סה) ״מִי הָאִישׁ הַלָּזֶה״, בְּיַעֲקֹב נֶאֱמַר (בראשית כה:כז) ״אִישׁ תָּם״:


**Sons of man** The sons of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who are called man. About Abraham it is stated (in Gen. 20:7): “Restore the man’s wife.” About Isaac it is stated (ibid. 24:65): “Who is that man...?” About Jacob, it is stated (ibid. 25:27): “and Jacob was a plain man.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 4:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:3:2)


**עַד מֶה כְבוֹדִי לִכְלִמָּה.** עַד מָתַי אַתֶּם מְבַזִּים אוֹתִי? הֲרְאִיתֶם אֶת בֶּן יִשַׁי (שמואל א כב:ט), ״מִי דָוִד וּמִי בֶן יִשָׁי״ (שמואל א כה:י), ״בִּכְרָת בְּנִי עִם בֶּן יִשַׁי״ (שמואל א כב:ח), ״כִּי בוֹחֵר אַתָּה לְבֶן יִשַׁי״ (שמואל א כ:ל), אֵין לִי שֵׁם?


**how long will my honor be disgraced** How long will you disgrace me? (I Sam. 20:30): “that you choose the son of Jesse”; (ibid. 22:8), “when my son made a covenant with the son of Jesse”; (ibid. verse 9), “I saw the son of Jesse”; (ibid. 25:10), “Who is David, and who is the son of Jesse?” I have no name.


###### Rashi on Psalms 4:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:3:3)


**תְּבַקְשׁוּ כָזָב.** תִּרְדְּפוּ לִמְצוֹא כְּזָבִים, כְּגוֹן הַזִּיפִים שֶׁמַּלְשִׁינִים עָלַי, וְלִי הָיוּ מַרְאִים שָׁלוֹם, וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָהֶם דִּילָטוֹרִין שֶׁהָיוּ בִּימֵי שָׁאוּל: ״הֲלֹא דָוִד מִסְתַּתֵּר בְּגִבְעַת הַחֲכִילָה״ (שמואל א כג:יט), וְכֵן הַרְבֵּה:


**will you constantly seek lies** Will you chase to find lies, e.g., the Ziphites, who inform on me, yet show me friendliness, and other informers like them who were in Saul’s time (I Sam. 23:19): “Is David not hiding...in the hill of Hachilah?” And so, many.

**רִגְזוּ.** חִרְדוּ מִלִּפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, **וְאַל תֶּחֱטָאוּ**:


**Quake** Tremble before the Holy One, blessed be He, and do not sin.


###### Rashi on Psalms 4:5:2

**אִמְרוּ בִלְבַבְכֶם עַל מִשְׁכַּבְכֶם.** הָשִׁיבוּ עַל לְבַבְכֶם שֶׁהִזְהִיר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל כָּךְ:


**say [this] in your heart on your bed and be forever silent** Bring back to your heart [the thought] that the Holy One, blessed be He, admonished [you] concerning that.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 4:6:1

**זִבְחוּ זִבְחֵי צֶדֶק.** הַצְדִּיקוּ מַעֲשֵׂיכֶם, וַהֲרֵי אַתֶּם כִּמְקְרִיבִים זְבָחִים:


**Offer up sacrifices of righteousness** Perform righteous deeds, and it will be as if you are offering up sacrifices.


###### Rashi on Psalms 4:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:6:2)


**וּבִטְחוּ אֶל ה׳.** שֶׁיַּשְׁפִּיעַ לָכֶם טוֹבָה, וְאַל תֶּחֱטָאוּ לוֹ בִּשְׁבִיל מָמוֹן, שֶׁאַתֶּם מְצַפִּים לְקַבֵּל שָׂכָר מֵאֵת שָׁאוּל:


**and trust in the Lord** to lavish upon you goodness, and do not sin against Him for money, in the hope that you will be rewarded by Saul.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 4:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:7:1)


**רַבִּים אוֹמְרִים מִי יַרְאֵנוּ טוֹב.** רַבִּים מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ שֶׁרוֹאִין רְשָׁעִים בְּעֹשֶׁר וּבְשַׁלְוָה וְאוֹמְרִים: מִי יַרְאֵנוּ טוֹב לִהְיוֹת עֲשִׁירִים וּמַשִּׂיגֵי תַּאֲוָה כָּאֵלּוּ?


**Many say, “Who will show us goodness?”** There are many Jews who see the nations of the world in wealth and tranquility, and say, “Who will show us goodness,” to be wealthy and achieve desires like these people?


###### Rashi on Psalms 4:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:7:2)


**נְסָה עָלֵינוּ.** הָרֵם עָלֵינוּ לְנֵס אֶת אוֹר פָּנֶיךָ, לְשׁוֹן ״הָרִימוּ נֵס״ (ישעיהו סב:י), ״אָרִים נִסִּי״ (ישעיהו מט:כב). לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: **נְסָה עָלֵינוּ.** רֶפְלַנְבִּי״ר בְּלַעַ״ז, כְּמוֹ ״אַבְנֵי נֵזֶר מִתְנוֹסְסוֹת״ (זכריה ט:טז). אֲבָל אֲנִי אֵינִי מְקַנֵּא בָּהֶם, כִּי שִׂמְחָה נְתוּנָה בְלִבִּי מֵעֵת דְּגָנָם וְתִירוֹשָׁם רַבּוּ. בָּטוּחַ אֲנִי: אִם לְמַכְעִיסִים כָּךְ, לְעוֹשֵׂי רְצוֹנוֹ עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה, לֶעָתִיד, שֶׁהוּא יוֹם קִבּוּל שְׂכָרָם:


**Raise up over us** Heb. נסה Raise up over us for a banner the light of Your countenance, an expression of (Isa. 62:10): “lift up a banner (נס)”;(ibid. 49:22), “I will raise My standard (נסי).” Another interpretation: נסה is reflordir(?) (resplendir) in Old French, gleam, as (Zech. 9:16), “crown stones gleam (מתנוססות).” But I do not envy them, for joy has been given into my heart from the time that the corn and the wine of the nations have increased. I am confident that if those who anger Him [have] such [tranquility], how much more will those who perform His will have it in the future, which is the day of the reception of their reward!



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 4:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:9:1)


**בְּשָׁלוֹם יַחְדָּו אֶשְׁכְּבָה וְאִישָׁן.** אִם הָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּשָׁלוֹם יַחְדָּו עִמִּי, הָיִיתִי שׁוֹכֵב וְיָשֵׁן בֶּטַח וְלֹא הָיִיתִי יָרֵא מִכָּל צַר וְאוֹיֵב:


**In peace together, I would lie down and sleep** If Israel were in peace together with me, I would lie down and sleep in confidence, and I would not fear any adversary or enemy.


###### Rashi on Psalms 4:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/4:9:2)


**לְבָדָד לָבֶטַח.** כְּמוֹ ״בֶּטַח בָּדָד עֵין יַעֲקֹב״ (דברים לג:כח), לְשׁוֹן מִבְטָח וָשֶׁקֶט הוּא, שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהוֹשִׁיב גְּיָסוֹת עִמּוֹ:


**alone in safety** As (in Deut. 33:28): “secure and alone, the fountain of Jacob.” It is an expression of safety and tranquility, that he need not station troops with him.



## Chapter 5


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 5:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:1:1)


**אֶל הַנְּחִילוֹת.** מְנַחֵם פָּתַר בְּכֻלָּן: נְחִילוֹת וַעֲלָמוֹת, גִּתִּית, יְדוּתוּן – כֻּלָּם שְׁמוֹת כְּלֵי זֶמֶר הֵם, וּנְעִימַת הַמִּזְמוֹר הָיְתָה לְפִי שִׁיר הָרָאוּי לְאוֹתוֹ כְּלִי. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה יֵשׁ מְפָרְשִׁים נְחִילוֹת לְשׁוֹן נַחֲלָה; וְאֵין זֶה מַשְׁמָעוּת הַתֵּיבָה, וְגַם עִנְיַן הַמִּזְמוֹר אֵינוֹ מְדַבֵּר בְּנַחֲלָה. וְיִתָּכֵן לִפְתּוֹר נְחִילוֹת – גְּיָסוֹת, כְּמוֹ נָחִיל שֶׁל דְּבוֹרִים (בבא קמא י:); וּכְמוֹ ״וְנַחֲלֵי בְלִיַּעַל״ (שמואל ב כב:ה), וְתִרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״סִיעַת חַיָּבִין״. תְּפִלָּה בִּשְׁבִיל גְּיָסוֹת אוֹיְבִים הַבָּאִים עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל; וְאוֹמֵר הַמְשׁוֹרֵר מִזְמוֹר הַזֶּה בִּשְׁבִיל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל:


**on nehiloth** Menachem interpreted all of them: nehiloth, alamoth, gittith, jeduthun, that they are all names of musical instruments, and the melody of the psalm was according to the melody fit for that instrument. However, [in the] Midrash Aggadah (Mid. Ps. 5:1,2,4) some explain “nehiloth” as an expression of heritage, but that is not the meaning of the word; moreover, the contents of the psalm do not deal with heritage. It is, however, possible to interpret נחלות as troops, like “a swarm (נחיל) of bees,” (Bava Kamma 114a, 81b), and like (II Sam. 22:5), “Bands (נחלי) of scoundrels would affright me,” which Jonathan renders: Bands (סיען) of sinners. [This is] a prayer concerning the bands of the enemies that come upon Israel, and the Psalmist recited this psalm on behalf of all Israel.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 5:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:2:1)


**אֲמָרַי הַאֲזִינָה ה׳.** כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ בִּי כֹּחַ לִשְׁאֹל צְרָכַי לְפָנֶיךָ, וּכְשֶׁאֵין בִּי כֹּחַ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל לְפָנֶיךָ וְהַדְּאָגָה עֲצוּרָה בְּלִבִּי, **בִּינָה הֲגִיגִי.** הָבֵן הֲגִיוֹן לִבִּי. כָּךְ מְפֹרָשׁ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ. כָּל בִּינָה שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא הַטַּעַם תַּחַת הַנּוּ״ן, חוּץ מִזֶּה וַחֲבֵרוֹ (איוב לד:טז) ״וְאִם בִּינָה שִׁמְעָה זֹאת״, שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֵׁם דָּבָר אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן הָבֵן, כְּמוֹ (משלי כג:א) ״בִּין תָּבִין אֶת אֲשֶׁר לְפָנֶיךָ״, לְפִיכָךְ הַטַּעַם תַּחַת הַבֵּי״ת:


**Give ear to my words, O Lord** when I have strength to ask before You and, when I have no strength to pray before You and the worry is confined to my heart...**consider my meditation** Heb. בינה. Consider the meditation of my heart. So it is explained in Midrash [Psalms 5:6]: In every [instance of] בינה in Scripture, the accent is under the “nun,” except this one and its fellow (in Job 34: 16): “And if you wish, understand (בִּנָה), hearken to this,” which is not a noun but an expression of “understand,” like (Prov. 23:1): “you should understand well (בין תבין) who is in front of you.” Therefore, the accent is under the “beth.”



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 5:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:4:1)


**בֹּקֶר תִּשְׁמַע קוֹלִי.** בַּבֹּקֶר אֲנִי קוֹרֵא לְךָ עֲלֵיהֶם, שֶׁהוּא עֵת מִשְׁפָּט בָּרְשָׁעִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״לַבְּקָרִים אַצְמִית כָּל רִשְׁעֵי אָרֶץ״ (תהלים קא:ח), ״הֱיֵה זְרוֹעָם לַבְּקָרִים״ (ישעיהו לג:ב), ״כִּי בַבֹּקֶר בַּבֹּקֶר יַעֲבֹר״ (ישעיהו כח:יט):


**in the morning You shall hearken to my voice** In the morning, I call out to You about them, because it is a time of judgment for the wicked, as it is stated (below 101:8): “Morning by morning will I destroy all the wicked of the land”; (Isa: 33:2), “Be their arm every morning”; (ibid. 28:19), “for every morning it shall pass.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 5:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:4:2)


**בֹּקֶר אֶעֱרָךְ לְךָ.** תְּפִלָּתִי עַל זֹאת, אֶעֱרֹךְ לְשׁוֹן מַעֲרָכָה הוּא, כָּךְ חִבְּרוֹ מְנַחֵם:


**in the morning I shall arrange to You** my prayer concerning this. [The word]: אערך is an expression of arrangement (מערכה). Menachem (p. 138) classifies it in this manner.


###### Rashi on Psalms 5:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:4:3)


**וַאֲצַפֶּה.** שֶׁתַּעֲשֶׂה בָּהֶם מִשְׁפָּטִים:


**and I shall look forward** that You execute justice upon them.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 5:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:5:1)


**כִּי לֹא אֵל חָפֵץ רֶשַׁע אָתָּה.** וְנָאֶה לְךָ לְאַבֵּד הָרִשְׁעָה מִן הָעוֹלָם:


**For You are not a God Who desires wickedness** Therefore, I arrange my prayer to You in the morning (appears only in certain editions) and it befits You to destroy wickedness from the world.


###### Rashi on Psalms 5:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:5:2)


**לֹא יְגֻרְךָ רָע.** לֹא יָגוּר אֶצְלְךָ:


**evil does not abide with You** Heb. יגרך, it will not abide beside You.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 5:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:6:1)


**הוֹלְלִים.** מִשְׁתַּטִּים, וּבִלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה מְעֻרְבָּבִין:


**Confused people** who make themselves mad, and in the language of the Mishnah, מערבבין, confused.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 5:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:7:1)


**אִישׁ דָּמִים וּמִרְמָה.** זֶה עֲמָלֵק וְזַרְעוֹ:


**a man of blood and deceit** This [refers to] Esau and his descendants.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 5:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:8:1)


**וַאֲנִי אָבוֹא בֵיתְךָ.** לְהוֹדוֹת לְךָ **בְּרֹב חַסְדְּךָ** שֶׁהִפְלֵאתָ עָלֵינוּ, לְהַרְאוֹתֵנוּ נְקָמָה מֵהֶם:


**I...shall enter Your House** to thank You for Your great loving-kindness that You have wondrously bestowed upon us, to grant us revenge upon them.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 5:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:9:1)


**שׁוֹרְרָי.** עוֹיְנַי הַמְּצַפִּים שֶׁאֶבְגּוֹד בְּךָ וְתַעַזְבֵנִי, שׁוֹרְרָי כְּמוֹ ״אֲשׁוּרֶנּוּ וְלֹא קָרוֹב״ (במדבר כד:יז):


**those who lie in wait for me** Heb. שוררי, those who look after me, who look forward to my betraying You, so that You should forsake me. [The word] שוררי is like (Num. 24:17): “I behold it (אשורינו), but it is not near.”



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 5:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:10:1)


**כִּי אֵין בְּפִיהוּ נְכוֹנָה.** נִרְאִים כְּאוֹהֲבִים, וְהֵם אוֹיְבִים:


**For there is no sincerity in his mouth** They appear as friends but they are enemies.


###### Rashi on Psalms 5:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:10:2)


**קִרְבָּם הַוּוֹת.** מַחְשְׁבוֹתָם מִרְמָה:


**there is malice in their heart** Their thoughts are deceitful.


###### Rashi on Psalms 5:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:10:3)


**קֶבֶר פָּתוּחַ גְּרוֹנָם.** לִבְלֹעַ יְגִיעַ אֲחֵרִים כְּקֶבֶר הַבּוֹלֵעַ אֶת הַגּוּף:


**their throat is an open grave** to swallow others’ toil, like a grave that swallows up the body.


###### Rashi on Psalms 5:10:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:10:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:10:4)


**יַחֲלִיקוּן.** דִּבְרֵי חֲלַקְלַקּוֹת:


**they make their tongue smooth** with words of flattery.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 5:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:11:1)


**מִמּוֹעֲצוֹתֵיהֶם.** שֶׁהֵם יוֹעֲצִים עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאָז יִשְׂמְחוּ כָּל חוֹסֵי בָךְ:


**by their own counsels** which they formulate against Israel. Then all who take shelter in You shall rejoice.



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Psalms 5:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:12:1)


**וְתָסֵךְ עָלֵימוֹ.** תָּגוֹנֵן וּתְסוֹכֵךְ עָלֵימוֹ:


**and You shall shelter them** You shall shield and shelter them.


###### Rashi on Psalms 5:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:12:2)


**וְיַעַלְצוּ בְךָ.** כְּשֶׁיִּרְאוּ שֶׁאַתָּה תְּבָרֵךְ רֵעֶיךָ וְאוֹהֲבֶיךָ:


**exult in You** when they see that You bless the righteous man, Jacob, and his seed.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Psalms 5:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:13:1)


**כַּצִּנָּה.** הַמַּקֶּפֶת שָׁלֹשׁ רוּחוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם:


**like a shield** which encompasses a man from three sides.


###### Rashi on Psalms 5:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:13:2)


**רָצוֹן.** נַחַת רוּחַ, אֵפִּימַנְ״ט בְּלַעַ״ז:


**will** satisfaction, apayement in Old French; appeasement, kindness, peace of heart.


###### Rashi on Psalms 5:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/5:13:3)


**תְּעַטְּרֶנּוּ.** תְּסוֹבְבֶנּוּ, כְּמוֹ (שמואל א כג:כו) ״וְשָׁאוּל וַאֲנָשָׁיו עוֹטְרִים אֶל דָּוִד וְאֶל אֲנָשָׁיו״:


**You shall encompass him** תעטרנו, You shall encompass him (in Sam. 23:26): “but Saul and his men were encircling (עוטרים) David and his men.”



## Chapter 6


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 6:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:1:1)


**עַל הַשְּׁמִינִית.** כִּנּוֹר שֶׁל שְׁמוֹנָה נִימִין, וְשְׁמִינִית שְׁמוֹ. וְכֵן מָצִינוּ (דברי הימים א טו:כא) פְּלוֹנִי וּבָנָיו ״עַל הַשְּׁמִינִית לְנַצֵּחַ״:


**on the sheminith** A harp of eight strings, known as sheminith, and so we find (in I Chron. 15: 21): “So-and-so and his sons on the sheminith to conduct.”



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 6:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:3:1)


**אֻמְלָל.** נִשְׁחַת וְדַל כֹּחַ (קונפונדו״ץ בלע״ז), כְּמוֹ ״הַיְּהוּדִים הָאֲמֵלָלִים״ דְּעֶזְרָא (נחמיה ג:לד):


**languish** אמלל, devastated, and poor in strength, konfondouc in Old French, confounded, perplexed as “these feeble Jews (האמללים),” of Ezra (Neh. 3:34).



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 6:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:4:1)


**וְאַתָּה ה׳ עַד מָתָי.** תַּבִּיט וְאֵינְךָ רוֹפֵא?


**and You, O Lord, how long** will You look on and not heal [me]?



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 6:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:5:1)


**שׁוּבָה ה׳.** מֵחֲרוֹנְךָ:


**Return, O Lord** from Your anger.


###### Rashi on Psalms 6:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:5:2)


**חַלְּצָה נַפְשִׁי.** מֵחוֹלְיִי:


**rescue my soul** from my illness.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 6:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:7:1)


**אַשְׂחֶה בְכָל לַיְלָה מִטָּתִי.** לְשׁוֹן ״סְחִי וּמָאוֹס״ (איכה ג:מה), ״וְהָיְתָה נִבְלָתָם כַּסּוּחָה״ (ישעיהו ה:כה) – מְמָאֵס אֲנִי מִטָּתִי בִּדְמָעוֹת. וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ עִם ״כַּאֲשֶׁר יְפָרֵשׂ הַשֹּׂחֶה לִשְׂחוֹת״ (ישעיהו כה:יא), וְעִם ״מֵי שָׂחוּ״ (יחזקאל מז:ה):


**every night I sully my bed** Heb. אשׂחה an expression of (Lam. 3:45): “scum (סחי) and refuse”; (Isa. 5:25), “and their corpses were like spittle (כסוחה).” I sully my bed with tears. Menachem (p. 172), however, associated it with (Isa. 25:11): “as the swimmer (השׂחה) spreads out [his hands] to swim (לשׂחות),” and with (Ezek. 47:5), “water to swim in (שׂחו).”


###### Rashi on Psalms 6:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:7:2)


**בְּדִמְעָתִי עַרְשִׂי אַמְסֶה.** אֲלַחְלֵחַ וְאַרְטִיב כְּמוֹ מַיִם:


**I wet my couch with my tears** I moisten and wet as with water.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 6:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:8:1)


**עָשְׁשָׁה.** לְשׁוֹן עֲשָׁשִׁית, עַיִן שֶׁמְּאוֹרָהּ כֵּהָה, וְדוֹמֶה לוֹ כְּאִלּוּ הוּא רוֹאֶה דֶּרֶךְ זְכוּכִית שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד עֵינָיו. וּמְנַחֵם פֵּרְשׁוֹ לְשׁוֹן רִקָּבוֹן, כְּמוֹ (תהלים לא:יא) ״וַעֲצָמַי עָשֵׁשׁוּ״, וְכֵן כָּל לְשׁוֹן עָשׁ:


**is dimmed** Heb. עשׁשׁה, an expression of a lantern (עשׁשׁית), an eye which has impaired vision and seems to see through glass [held] before its eyes. Menachem (p. 139) defines it as an expression of decay, and so every expression of עשׁ, like (below 31:1 1) “and my bones are wasted away (עשׁשׁו).”


###### Rashi on Psalms 6:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:8:2)


**עָתְקָה.** נִתְיַשְּׁנָה וְנִזְדַּקְּנָה עֵינִי בִּכְהִיַּת אוֹר, וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ עִם ״וַיַּעְתֵּק מִשָּׁם הָהָרָה״ (בראשית יב:ח):


**it has aged** Heb. עתקה. My eye has aged and become old in that its light has dimmed. Menachem (p. 139) associated it with (Gen. 12:8): “And he moved (ויעתק) from there to the mountain.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 6:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:8:3)


**בְּכָל צוֹרְרָי.** בִּשְׁבִיל צָרוֹת שֶׁמְּצִירִין לִי:


**because of all my adversaries** Because of the troubles that distress me.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 6:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:11:1)


**יֵבֹשׁוּ וְיִבָּהֲלוּ וְגוֹ׳.** מַהוּ **יָשׁוּבוּ יֵבֹשׁוּ** פַּעַם שְׁנִיָּה? אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן : לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא דָּן אֶת הָרְשָׁעִים וּמְחַיְּבָן לַגֵּיהִנֹּם, וְהֵם מִתְרַעֲמִין עָלָיו, וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַחֲזִירָן וְחוֹזֵר וּמַרְאֶה גִּלְיוֹנִין שֶׁלָּהֶם וְדָן אוֹתָם וּמִתְחַיְּבִין, וְהוּא מַחֲזִירָן לַגֵּיהִנֹּם. הֲרֵי בּוּשָׁה כְּפוּלָה. רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אוֹמֵר : לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא כָּל אֻמָּה קוֹרְאָה לֵאלֹהֶיהָ וְאֵין עוֹנֶה, וְחוֹזְרִין וְקוֹרְאִין לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וְאוֹמֵר לָהֶם: אִלּוּ אֵלַי קְרָאתֶם תְּחִלָּה, הָיִיתִי עוֹנֶה אֶתְכֶם. עַכְשָׁו עֲשִׂיתֶם עֲבוֹדַת גִּלּוּלִים עִקָּר וְאוֹתִי טְפֵלָה, לְפִיכָךְ אֵינִי עוֹנֶה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״יִשְׁוְעוּ וְאֵין מוֹשִׁיעַ״ (תהלים יח:מב) – זוֹ עֲבוֹדַת גִּלּוּלִים, וְאַחַר כָּךְ ״אֶל ה׳ וְלֹא עָנָם״ (שם). לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר: **יָשֻׁבוּ יֵבֹשׁוּ**:


**shall be ashamed and very frightened, etc.** What is the meaning of “they shall return and be ashamed” a second time? Said Rabbi Johanan: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will judge the wicked of the nations of the world and sentence them to Gehinnom. Because they will complain to Him, He will take them back and again show them their records, and He returns them to Gehinnom. This is a double embarrassment. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani says: In the future, every nation will call to its god, but it will not answer. Consequently, they will call to the Holy One, blessed be He. He will say to them, “Had you called Me first, I would have answered you. Now you have made the idols of primary importance and Me of secondary import. Therefore, I will not answer,” for it is stated (below 18:42): “They pray, but no one saves them.” This refers to the idols, and afterward, “to the Lord, but He answered them not.” Therefore, it is said: “they shall return and be ashamed.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 6:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/6:11:2)


**רָגַע.** בִּמְעַט זְמַן:


**in a moment** In a short time.



## Chapter 7


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 7:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/7:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/7:1:1)


**שִׁגָּיוֹן לְדָוִד.** מְנַחֵם אָמַר שֶׁגַּם זֶה אֶחָד מִשְּׁמוֹת הַזֶּמֶר עַל שֵׁם הַכְּלִי, וְכֵן פֵּרֵשׁ ״עַל שִׁגְיֹנוֹת״ (חבקוק ג:א), וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ פֵּרְשׁוּ לְשׁוֹן מִשְׁגֶּה שֶׁנִּתְוַדָּה וְנִתְפַּלֵּל עַל הַשִּׁגָּיוֹן שֶׁאָמַר שִׁירָה עַל מַפַּלְתּוֹ שֶׁל שָׁאוּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיְדַבֵּר דָּוִד לַה׳ וְגוֹ׳״ (שמואל ב כב:א), אֲבָל עִנְיַן הַמִּזְמוֹר אֵינוֹ מוֹכִיחַ עַל כָּךְ. וְאוֹמֵר אֲנִי שֶׁאֲמָרוֹ עַל עִסְקֵי יִשְׁבִּי בְנֹב (שמואל ב כא:טז) שֶׁבָּא עָלָיו עַל עָנְשׁוֹ שֶׁל שָׁאוּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁפֵּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל יָדְךָ נִטְרַד דּוֹאֵג הָאֲדוֹמִי עַל יָדְךָ נֶהֱרַג שָׁאוּל וּבָנָיו כוּ׳ (כִּדְאִיתָא בְּחֵלֶק שְׁגִיאוֹת שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ דָּוִד לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהִמָּסֵר בְּיַד שׂוֹנֵא וְלֹא יִכְלֶה זַרְעוֹ ס״א אינו), וְהָפַךְ דָּוִד אֶת תְּפִלָּתוֹ וְהִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁלֹּא יִפֹּל בְּיַד אוֹיֵב. וְכֵן פִּתְרוֹנוֹ מִשְׁגֶּה שָׁר דָּוִד לַה׳ עַל שֶׁשָּׁגַג לוֹמַר לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמָסְרוֹ בְּיַד אוֹיֵב עַל דִּבְרֵי שָׁאוּל שֶׁנֶּהֱרַג עַל יָדוֹ. דָּבָר אַחֵר: עַל שִׁגָּיוֹן כְּנַף הַמְּעִיל אֲשֶׁר כָּרַת לְשָׁאוּל (שמואל א כד:ה):


**A shiggayon of David** Menachem says (p. 170) that this, too, is one of the names of a melody named for the instrument, and so he explained “on shigyonoth,” [in Habakkuk 3:1]. But our Sages (Mid. Ps. 7:18) explained it as an expression of error, that he confessed and prayed about the error that he had [committed by] reciting a song upon Saul’s downfall, as it is stated (in II Sam. 22:1): “And David spoke to the Lord, etc.” The contents of the psalm, however, do not indicate this, because it speaks of the nations (in verse 9): “May the Lord judge the peoples.” I, therefore, say that he recited it concerning Ishbi in Nob (II Sam. 21:16), who came upon him as a punishment for Saul; as our Rabbis explained, that the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, “Through you, Doeg the Edomite was banished; through you, Saul and his sons were slain, etc.” as is stated in “Chelek” (Sanh. 95a). The errors that David asked of the Holy One, blessed be He, [were] that he [himself] be delivered into the hands of his enemies and that his descendants should not be destroyed. (The last sentence does not appear in all editions.) [Therefore, because his life was endangered,] David reversed his prayer and prayed that he should not fall into the hands of his enemies. Now this is its meaning: An error that David sang to the Lord because he had erred in saying to the Holy One, blessed be He, to deliver him into the hands of his enemies on account of Saul, who was slain because of him. Another explanation: Concerning the error of the skirt of Saul’s coat, which he had severed.


###### Rashi on Psalms 7:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/7:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/7:1:2)


**כּוּשׁ.** מַה כּוּשִׁי מְשֻׁנֶּה בְּעוֹרוֹ, אַף שָׁאוּל מְשֻׁנֶּה בְּמַעֲשָׂיו (מועד קטן טז:):


**Cush** Just as a Cushite has unusual skin, so did Saul have unusual deeds.

**rending it to pieces** Heb. פרק, an expression of (Exod. 32:2): “Break off (פרקו) the golden rings.”

**אִם עָשִׂיתִי זֹאת.** מַה שֶּׁמְפֹרָשׁ אַחֲרָיו:


**if I have done this** What is delineated after it.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 7:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/7:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/7:5:1)


**אִם גָּמַלְתִּי שׁוֹלְמִי רָע.** אִם גְּמַלְתִּיו כִּגְמוּלוֹ:


**if I repaid the one who did evil to me** If I repaid him according to his deeds.


###### Rashi on Psalms 7:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/7:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/7:5:2)


**וָאֲחַלְּצָה צוֹרְרִי רֵיקָם.** שִׁחַתִּי אֶת חֲלִיצָתוֹ בְּכָרְתִּי אֶת כְּנַף מְעִילוֹ, אִם לְהַשְׁחִית וּלְחַלְּצוֹ וּלְהַעֲמִידוֹ רֵיקָם וּבְשִׂנְאָה עָשִׂיתִי? אֶלָּא לְהוֹדִיעוֹ, שֶׁהָיָה מָסוּר בְּיָדִי לְהָרְגוֹ וְלֹא הֲרַגְתִּיו. **וָאֲחַלְּצָה** לְשׁוֹן הַפְשָׁטָה:


**and I stripped my adversary into emptiness** I destroyed his garment when I severed the skirt of his coat. Did I do it to destroy and to strip him and cause him to stand empty, and [was it done] with hatred? Only to let him know that he was delivered into my hand to kill him, and I did not kill him. [The word] חלצה is an expression of stripping off clothing.

**קוּמָה ה׳ בְּאַפֶּךָ.** עַל שׂוֹנְאַי, כְּגוֹן יִשְׁבִּי וְאֶחָיו וּפְלִשְׁתִּים (שמואל ב כא:טז), שֶׁלֹּא אֶמָּסֵר בְּיָדָם:


**Arise, O Lord, with Your wrath** against my enemies, such as Ishbi and his brothers and the Philistines, that I should not be delivered into their hands.


###### Rashi on Psalms 7:7:2

**הִנָּשֵׂא.** הִתְפָּאֵר לְהַרְאוֹת נִקְמַת עֶבְרָה בְּהִתְעַבֶּרְךָ עֲלֵיהֶם:


**exalt Yourself** boast, to show me the revenge of Your anger when You become angry with them.


###### Rashi on Psalms 7:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/7:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/7:7:3)


**וְעוּרָה אֵלַי.** שֶׁאוּכַל לַעֲשׂוֹת בָּהֶם **מִשְׁפָּט** נְקָמָה אֲשֶׁר **צִוִּיתָ**, וְהֵיכָן צִוִּיתָ? ״תְּרֹעֵם בְּשֵׁבֶט בַּרְזֶל״ (תהלים ב:ט), ״וְאָיַבְתִּי אֶת אֹיְבֶיךָ״ (שמות כג:כב). זֶה מָצָאתִי בַמִּדְרָשׁ:


**and awaken for me** that I should be able to execute upon them the judgment of revenge that You commanded. Now where did You command [it]? “You shall break them with an iron rod” (above 2:9). “Then I will be an enemy to your enemies” (Exod. 23:22). I found this in the Midrash (Mid. Ps. 7:6; Tan. Ki Thissa 20, Buber 13 with variations).



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 7:8:1

**וַעֲדַת לְאֻמִּים תְּסוֹבְבֶךָּ.** אִם יַחְזְרוּ אַחֲרֶיךָ לְהוֹשִׁיעָם אַל תִּשְׁמַע לְקוֹלָם, הִתְרַחֵק מֵעֲלֵיהֶם וְשׁוּב וְשֵׁב בִּמְקוֹמְךָ בַּמָּרוֹם רפיש״א בְּלַעַ״ז. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **לַמָּרוֹם שׁוּבָה** לְהַרְאוֹת לָהֶם שֶׁיָּדְךָ עֶלְיוֹנָה:


**And [if] a congregation of kingdoms surrounds You** If troops of nations follow You to save them, do not hearken to their voice. Distance Yourself from them and go back to sit in Your place on high; repoxa in Old French, repose. Another interpretation: Return on high to show them that You have the upper hand.

### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Psalms 7:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/7:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/7:13:1)
