###### Rashi on Psalms 15:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/15:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/15:4:3)


**וְלֹא יָמִיר.** שְׁבוּעָתוֹ, קַל וָחֹמֶר שֶׁאֵינָהּ מֵמִירָהּ בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵינָהּ לְרָעָתוֹ:


**and does not retract** his oath. How much more does he not retract it if it concerns something that is not to his hurt!



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 15:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/15:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/15:5:1)


**וְשֹׁחַד לֹא לָקַח.** עַל עָנִי לְהַרְשִׁיעוֹ בַּדִּין, לְהַטּוֹת מִשְׁפָּטוֹ. וְעוֹד פֵּרְשׁוּהוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ (ספרי דברים קמד): **לֹא לָקַח שֹׁחַד עַל נָקִי** לְנַקּוֹתוֹ בְּדִינוֹ, קַל וָחֹמֶר שֶׁאֵינוֹ לוֹקֵחַ שֹׁחַד לְהַטּוֹת הַמִּשְׁפָּט:


**nor did he accept a bribe, etc.** against a poor man, to condemn him in judgment by judging perversely. Our Sages explained it further to mean that he would not accept a bribe to exonerate him in judgment, and he certainly will not take a bribe to pervert the judgment.


###### Rashi on Psalms 15:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/15:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/15:5:2)


**לֹא יִמּוֹט.** וְהוּא רָאוּי לָגוּר בְּאָהָלֶיךָ (ספרים אחרין אינו):


**shall not falter** and he deserves to sojourn in Your tent.


###### Rashi on Psalms 15:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/15:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/15:5:3)


**לֹא יִמּוֹט לְעוֹלָם.** אִם יִמּוֹט, אֵין מֻטָּתוֹ מֻטָה עוֹלָם, אֶלָּא מִתְמוֹטֵט וְעוֹלֶה:


**shall not falter forever** If he falters, his faltering will not be permanent faltering, but he will falter and ascend.



## Chapter 16


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 16:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:1:1)


**מִכְתָּם לְדָוִד.** אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ (סוטה י:): לְדָוִד שֶׁהָיָה מָךְ וְתָם, שֶׁהָיְתָה מַכָּתוֹ תַמָּה, שֶׁנּוֹלַד מָהוּל. וְאֵין שִׁיטַת הַמִּקְרָא נוֹפֵל עַל הַמִּדְרָשׁ כָּאן. יֵשׁ מִזְמוֹר שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ ״לְדָוִד מִכְתָּם״ (תהלים נו:א), שָׁם יֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ: שִׁיר זֶה לְדָוִד שֶׁהָיָה מָךְ וְתָם, אֲבָל כָּאן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר מִכְתָּם לְדָוִד אֵין לְפָרְשׁוֹ כֵּן. וְאוֹמֵר אֲנִי שֶׁהוּא אֶחָד מִן שְׁמוֹת מִינֵי נְעִימוֹת הַזֶּמֶר וְחִלּוּק בִּנְעִימוֹת הַשִּׁיר. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **מִכְתָּם לְדָוִד** לְשׁוֹן עֲטָרָה כְּמוֹ ״כֶּתֶם״ (שיר השירים ה:יא), שֶׁמַּשְׁמָע דָּבָר זֶה הָיָה רָגִיל לוֹמַר דָּוִד **שָׁמְרֵנִי אֵל כִּי חָסִיתִי בָךְ** וְהָיָה לוֹ כַּעֲטָרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (תהלים ה:יג) ״כִּי כַצִּנָּה רָצוֹן תַּעְטְרֶנּוּ״ (ס״א אינו):


**A michtam of David** Our Sages said (Sotah 10b, Mid. Ps. 16:1): Of David, who was poor (מך) and perfect (ותם), whose wound (מכתו) was perfect (תמה), for he was born circumcised. However, the sequence of the verse here does not lend itself to be interpreted according to the Midrash. There are psalms prefaced by the title לדוד מכתם, which may be interpreted: This song is David’s, who was poor and perfect, but here, where it is stated מכתם לדוד, it cannot be interpreted in this manner. I therefore say that it is one of the names of the various types of melodies and the variations in the music. Another explanation: מכתם is an expression of a crown, like כתם, meaning that David was accustomed to say, “O God, guard me for I have taken refuge in You.” And this was to him as a crown, as it is stated (5:13): “You shall crown him with will.”



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 16:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:2:1)


**אָמַרְתְּ לַה׳ אֲדֹנָי אַתָּה וְגוֹ׳.** לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל אָמַר דָּוִד: יֵשׁ עָלַיִךְ לוֹמַר לַה׳: אָדוֹן אַתָּה, וְיָדְךָ עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה לְכָל הַבָּא עָלַי. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **אָמַרְתְּ לַה׳ אֲדֹנָי אַתָּה**, לְנַפְשׁוֹ הָיָה אוֹמֵר. וְכֵן מָצִינוּ דֻגְמָתוֹ: ״וַתְּכַל דָּוִד״ (שמואל ב יד:לט), וּפִתְרוֹנוֹ: ׳וַתְּכַל נֶפֶשׁ דָּוִד׳; אַף כָּאן: אָמַרְתְּ נַפְשִׁי לַה׳ – אַתְּ, נַפְשִׁי, יֵשׁ עָלַיִךְ לוֹמַר כֵּן לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא (ס״א אינו):


**You should say to the Lord, “You are my Master, etc.”** David addresses the Congregation of Israel. “It is your duty to say to the Lord, ‘You are the Master, and You have the upper hand in all that befalls me.’” Another explanation: You should say to the Lord, “You are my Master.” He [David] was saying this to his soul. Similarly, we find on this order (in II Sam. 13:39): “And David longed,” which means: And the soul of David longed. Here too, “You, my soul, have said to the Lord,” you my soul, should say to the Holy One, blessed be He. (The second interpretation appears in very few early editions.)


###### Rashi on Psalms 16:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:2:2)


**טוֹבָתִי בַּל עָלֶיךָ.** טוֹבוֹת שֶׁאַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה לִי, לֹא עָלֶיךָ הֵם לְגָמְלֵנִי, כִּי לֹא בְצִדְקָתִי אַתָּה מֵטִיב לִי:


**my good is not incumbent upon You.** The benefits that You do for meit is not incumbent upon You to bestow [them] upon me, because You do not benefit me on account of my righteousness.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 16:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:3:1)


**לִקְדוֹשִׁים אֲשֶׁר בָּאָרֶץ הֵמָּה.** בִּשְׁבִיל הַקְּדוֹשִׁים אֲשֶׁר הֵמָּה קְבוּרִים בָּאָרֶץ, אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלְּכוּ לְפָנֶיךָ בֶּאֱמֶת:


**For the holy ones who are in the earth** For the sake of the holy ones who are buried in the earth, who walked before You with sincerity.


###### Rashi on Psalms 16:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:3:2)


**וְאַדִּירֵי כָּל חֶפְצִי בָם.** הֵם הָאַדִּירִים, אֲשֶׁר כָּל חֶפְצִי בָם וְכָל צְרָכַי נַעֲשִׂים בִּשְׁבִילָם:


**and the mighty ones in whom is all my delight** They are the mighty ones in whom is all my delight and for whose sake all my necessities are accomplished.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 16:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:4:1)


**יִרְבּוּ עַצְּבוֹתָם וְגוֹ׳.** כָּל זֶה אָמְרִי לַה׳: יִרְבּוּ עַצְּבוֹתָם שֶׁל כּוֹפְרִים בְּךָ, הַמְּהִירִים וַחֲרֵדִים לַעֲבוֹדַת אֵל אַחֵר. לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: **מָהָרוּ** לְשׁוֹן ״מֹהַר״ (בראשית לד:יב), דוֹאִירְנְ״ט בְּלַעַ״ז:


**May the sorrows...increase** All this you should say to the Lord, “May the sorrows of those who do not believe in You increase,” viz. those who hasten and scurry to idolatry. Another explanation: מהרו is an expression of מֹהַר, dowry, douaire in French.


###### Rashi on Psalms 16:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:4:2)


**בַּל אַסִּיךְ נִסְכֵּיהֶם מִדָּם.** אֲנִי לֹא אֶהְיֶה כְּמוֹתָם, לִזְרֹק דָּם לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְלֹא אֶשָּׂא שֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה עַל שְׂפָתַי:


**I will not pour their libations of blood** I will not be like them, to sprinkle blood for pagan deities, neither will I take up the name of pagan deities upon my lips.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 16:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:5:1)


**ה׳ מְנָת חֶלְקִי וְכוֹסִי.** כָּל טוֹבָתִי הֵימֶנּוּ. לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: **וְכוֹסִי** וְחֶשְׁבּוֹנִי, כְּמוֹ ״תָּכֹסּוּ עַל הַשֶּׂה״ (שמות יב:ד), וְכֵן חִבְּרוֹ מְנַחֵם:


**The Lord is my allotted portion and my cup** All my benefit is from Him. Another explanation: כוסי means “my share,” as (in Exod. 12:4): “you shall make your count (תכסו) on the lamb.” This is how Menachem (p. 107) associated it.


###### Rashi on Psalms 16:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:5:2)


**אַתָּה תּוֹמִיךְ גּוֹרָלִי.** אַתָּה הוּא אֲשֶׁר הֲנִיחוֹתָ יָדִי עַל הַחֵלֶק הַטּוֹב, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הַחַיִּים וְהַמָּוֶת נָתַתִּי וְגוֹמֵר וּבָחַרְתָּ בַּחַיִּים״ (דברים ל:יט). כְּאָדָם הָאוֹהֵב אֶחָד מִבָּנָיו וּמַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ עַל הַחֵלֶק הַטּוֹב וְאוֹמֵר: אֶת זֶה בְּחַר לְךָ:


**You guide my destiny** It is You Who placed my hand on the good share, as it is stated (in Deut. 30:19): “I have set life and death before you...Choose life...” as a man who loves one of his sons and lays his hand on the better share, saying, “Choose this one for yourself.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 16:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:5:3)


**תּוֹמִיךְ.** הִשְׁפַּלְתָּ יָדִי עַל הַגּוֹרָל, לְשׁוֹן ״יִמַּךְ הַמְּקָרֶה״ (קהלת י:יח) – יִשְׁפַּל. כָּךְ הוּא נִדְרָשׁ בַּסִּפְרִי (ספרי דברים כג). וְגַם יֵשׁ לְפוֹתְרוֹ לְשׁוֹן תְּמִיכָה, לְמִדְרַשׁ הָאַגָּדָה, כְּמוֹ ״וַיִּתְמֹךְ יַד אָבִיו״ (בראשית מח:יז):


**guide** Heb. תומיך. You lowered my hand onto the portion, an expression of (Ecc. 10: 18): “the rafter sinks (ימך),” is lowered. In this manner it is expounded upon in Sifrei (Deut. 11:26, 27). It can also be interpreted as an expression of support, according to the Midrash Aggadah, as (in Gen. 48:17) “he supported (ויתמך) his father’s hand.”



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 16:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:6:1)


**חֲבָלִים נָפְלוּ לִי בַּנְּעִימִים.** כְּשֶׁנָּפַל לִי הַגּוֹרָל לִהְיוֹת בְּחֶלְקְךָ, חֶבֶל נָעִים הוּא זֶה. אַף עָלַי שָׁפְרָה נַחֲלָה כָּזוֹ:


**Portions have fallen to me in pleasant places** When the lot fell to me to be in Your portion, it is a pleasant portion. Also, such an inheritance is pleasing to me.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 16:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:7:1)


**אֲבָרֵךְ אֶת ה׳.** עַד כָּאן נִבָּא דָּוִד עַל כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁתֹּאמַר כֵּן, וְעַכְשָׁיו אוֹמֵר: וַאֲנִי, גַּם אֲנִי **אֲבָרֵךְ אֶת ה׳ אֲשֶׁר יְעָצָנִי** לִבְחוֹר בַּחַיִּים וְלָלֶכֶת בִּדְרָכָיו:


**I will bless the Lord** Until here, David prophesied concerning the Congregation of Israel, that she would say this, and now he says, “I, too, will bless the Lord, Who counseled me to choose life and to go in His ways.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 16:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:7:2)


**אַף לֵילוֹת יִסְּרוּנִי כִלְיוֹתָי.** לְיִרְאָה אוֹתוֹ וּלְאַהֲבָה. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ פֵּרְשׁוּהוּ עַל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, שֶׁלָּמַד תּוֹרָה מֵאֵלָיו עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה. אַף אָנוּ צְרִיכִין לְיַשֵּׁב הַמִּקְרָאוֹת עַל סִדְרָן:


**even at night my conscience instructs me** to fear Him and to love Him. Our Sages though, (Mid. Ps. 16:7) explained it as referring to our father Abraham, who learned Torah by himself before the Torah was given, but we must reconcile the verses according to their sequence.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 16:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:8:1)


**שִׁוִּיתִי ה׳ לְנֶגְדִּי תָמִיד.** בְּכָל מַעֲשַׂי שַׂמְתִּי מוֹרָאוֹ לְנֶגֶד עֵינַי, וְלָמָּה? **כִּי מִימִינִי** הוּא תָּמִיד לְעָזְרֵנִי לְ**בַל אֶמּוֹט**. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **שִׁוִּיתִי ה׳ לְנֶגְדִּי תָמִיד.** סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה הָיָה עִמּוֹ לִקְרוֹת בּוֹ כָּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו (דברים יז:יט), וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: **מִימִינִי בַּל אֶמּוֹט.** עַל שֵׁם הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּתְּנָה בִּימִינוֹ, שֶׁאֲנִי עוֹסֵק בָּהּ וּלְפִיכָךְ בַּל אֶמּוֹט (סנהדרין כב.) (ס״א אינו):


**I have placed the Lord before me constantly** In all my deeds, I have placed His fear before my eyes. Why? Because He is always at my right hand to help me so that I should not falter. Another explanation: I have placed the Lord before me constantly. [This alludes to] the sefer Torah [that] was with him [for him] to read all the days of his life [as in Deut. 17:19]. This is what he states: “from my right hand I will not falter,” meaning that because of the Torah in which I am engaged, which was given with His right hand, I will not falter. (This interpretation does not appear in any manuscript. It does, however, appear in several early printed editions.) Rashi to Sanhedrin explains that the “right hand” alludes to the Torah scroll that the king would carry suspended from his arm. David is confident that in the merit of that scroll, he will not falter.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 16:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:9:1)


**לָכֵן שָׂמַח לִבִּי וְגוֹ׳.** לְפִי שֶׁאֲנִי בּוֹטֵחַ כִּי לֹא תַעֲזֹב נַפְשִׁי לִשְׁאוֹל, שֶׁהֲרֵי בַּעֲוֹן עֲבֵרָה גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁהָיְתָה בְּיָדִי בִּשַּׂרְתַּנִי ״גַּם ה׳ הֶעֱבִיר חַטָּאתְךָ״ (שמואל ב יב:יג), קַל וָחֹמֶר שֶׁמֵּעַתָּה לֹא תַעַזְבֵנִי לָסוּר מִמְּךָ:


**Therefore, my heart rejoiced, etc.** because I am confident that You will not forsake my soul to the grave. Since, concerning the iniquity of a grave transgression which I committed, You sent me the tidings (in II Sam. 12:13): “Also the Lord has removed your sin,” certainly from now on You will not forsake me [to cause me] to turn away from You.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 16:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:11:1)


**תּוֹדִיעֵנִי אֹרַח חַיִּים.** לְשׁוֹן עָתִיד הוּא, וְאֵינוֹ לְשׁוֹן תְּפִלָּה:


**You shall let me know the way of life** This is the future tense, not an expression of prayer.


###### Rashi on Psalms 16:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:11:2)


**שֹׂבַע שְׂמָחוֹת.** שִׂמְחָה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ קֵץ וְתַכְלָה הִיא הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁל עָתִיד (ס״א אינו):


**the fullness of joys** Endless joy. That is the joy of the future. (Found only in certain manuscripts.)


###### Rashi on Psalms 16:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/16:11:3)


**אֶת פָּנֶיךָ.** שְׂמָחוֹת אֲשֶׁר לְפָנֶיךָ, בַּכַּת הַקְּרוֹבָה לְךָ:


**in Your presence** Joys that are before You, in a company that is near You.



## Chapter 17


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 17:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:2:1)


**מִלְּפָנֶיךָ מִשְׁפָּטִי יֵצֵא.** עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבְּיָדִי, שֶׁאֲנִי רָאוּי לְהִשָּׁפֵט עֲלֵיהֶם בְּיִסּוּרִין, יֵצְאוּ מִלְּפָנֶיךָ, וְלֹא יָבוֹאוּ לְפָנֶיךָ בַּדִּין:


**May my judgment come forth from before You** May the sins for which I deserve to be judged with torments, go forth from before You and not come before You in judgment.


###### Rashi on Psalms 17:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:2:2)


**עֵינֶיךָ תֶּחֱזֶינָה מֵישָׁרִים.** אִם יֵשׁ בְּיָדִי זְכֻיּוֹת, בָּהֶן תֶּחֱזֶינָה בְּמֵישָׁרִים עֵינֶיךָ:


**may Your eyes see [my] upright acts** If I have merits, may Your eyes see the upright acts.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 17:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:3:1)


**בָּחַנְתָּ לִבִּי וְגוֹ׳.** יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יֵשׁ עֲבֵירָה בְּיָדִי, וְאִם מִשְׁפַּט עָנְשִׁי יָבֹא לְפָנֶיךָ לֹא אֶצְדַּק בַּדִּין, אֲשֶׁר כְּבָר **בָּחַנְתָּ לִבִּי**:


**You have tried my heart, etc.** I know that I am guilty of a transgression, and, if the judgment of its punishment comes before You, I will not be declared innocent in the judgment, for You have already tried my heart.


###### Rashi on Psalms 17:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:3:2)


**פָּקַדְתָּ לַּיְלָה.** לְעֵת הָעֶרֶב בַּעֲוֹן בַּת שֶׁבַע, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיְהִי לְעֵת הָעֶרֶב וַיָּקָם דָּוִד וְגוֹמֵר״ (שמואל ב יא:ב):


**You have visited [upon me] at night** at eventide for the iniquity of Bathsheba, concerning which it is stated (in II Sam. 11:2) “And it came to pass at the time of evening, that David arose, etc.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 17:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:3:3)


**צְרַפְתַּנִי.** נִסִּיתַנִי:


**You have refined me** You have tested me.


###### Rashi on Psalms 17:3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:3:4)


**בַּל תִּמְצָא.** לֹא מָצָאתָ בִּי חֶפְצְךָ:


**and not found** You have not found in me Your desire.


###### Rashi on Psalms 17:3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:3:5)


**זִמּוֹתִי בַּל יַעֲבָר פִּי.** אִם תַּעֲלֶה עוֹד בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתִּי לִיבָּחֵן לְפָנֶיךָ, בַּל יַעֲבָר פִּי לוֹמַר עוֹד בְּחָנֵנִי וְנַסֵּנִי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְתִּי כְּבָר כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״בְּחָנֵנִי ה׳ וְנַסֵּנִי״ (תהלים כו:ב). שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: מִפְּנֵי מָה אוֹמְרִים אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם וְאֵין אוֹמְרִים אֱלֹהֵי דָוִד? אָמַר לוֹ: אֲנִי בְּחַנְתִּיו בְּעֶשֶׂר נִסְיוֹנוֹת וְנִמְצָא שָׁלֵם. אָמַר בְּחָנֵנִי וְנַסֵּנִי, כִּדְאִיתָא בְּמַסֶּכֶת שַׁבָּת (שבת קנג:):


**If I think, let it not pass my mouth** If it enters my thoughts again to be tried before You, let it not pass my mouth to say again, “Try me, O Lord, and test me,” as I have already said, as is written (26:2) “Try me, O Lord, and test me,” for David asked the Holy One, blessed be He, “Why do they say, ‘the God of Abraham,’ yet they do not say, ‘the God of David’?” He replied, “I tested him with ten tests, and he was found perfect.” He [David] said, “Try me and test me,” as appears in tractate Shabbath (?).



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 17:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:4:1)


**לִפְעֻלּוֹת אָדָם בִּדְבַר שְׂפָתֶיךָ וְגוֹ׳, תָּמוֹךְ אֲשׁוּרַי וְגוֹ׳.** מֵאָז וָהָלְאָה לְכָל פְּעֻלַּת אָדָם שֶׁבָּאתִי לִפְעֹל, אֲנִי שָׁמַרְתִּי בִּשְׁבִיל דְּבַר שְׂפָתֶיךָ אָרְחוֹת פָּרִיץ לִנְטוֹת מֵהֶם, שֶׁלֹּא אֵלֵךְ בָּהֶם, אַךְ לִתְמֹךְ אֲשׁוּרַי תָּמִיד בְּמַעְגְּלוֹתֶיךָ, לֹא נָמוֹטוּ מֵהֶם פְּעָמַי. פֵּרוּשׁ אַחֵר: **לִפְעֻלּוֹת אָדָם בִּדְבַר שְׂפָתֶיךָ וְגוֹ׳**, לְפִי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ אָדָם לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בִּפְעֻלּוֹתָיו לְפִי יִשְׁרַת דְּבַר שְׂפָתֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר אָמַרְתָּ ״לֹא תִנְאָף״ (שמות כ:יג), אֲנִי שָׁמַרְתִּי אָרְחוֹת פָּרִיץ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעָשִׂיתִי שֶׁלֹּא כָּרָאוּי בְּטוֹבָתְךָ:


**As for man’s deeds, because of the word of Your lips, etc. To support my feet, etc.** From then on, for every deed of man that I came to perform, I watched myself because of the word of Your lips; [I watched] the ways of the profligate, to turn away from them, so that I should not walk in them, but [would] support my feet constantly in Your paths, that my feet should not falter from them. Another explanation: **For the deeds of man according to the word of Your lips, etc.** Since a person must use his deeds according to the uprightness (decree - early editions) of the word of Your lips, as You said, “You shall not commit adultery,” I kept myself from the ways of the profligate although I behaved unseemly according to the good You have done.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 17:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:5:1)


**תָּמוֹךְ אֲשֻׁרַי וְגוֹ׳.** מֵאָז וָהָלְאָה לְכָל פְּעֻלַּת אָדָם שֶׁבָּאתִי לִפְעוֹל אֶת הַמֵּישָׁרִים תֶּחֱזֶינָה עֵינֶיךָ, וְהַמִּשְׁפָּט מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יֵצֵא:


**To support my feet** From then on, for every deed of man that I did improperly, may Your eyes see the upright deeds, but my judgment shall go forth from before you.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 17:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:6:1)


**כִּי תַעֲנֵנִי אֵל.** כִּי בָּטוּחַ אֲנִי שֶׁתַּעֲנֵנִי:


**because You shall answer me, O God** Because I am confident that You will answer me.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 17:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:7:1)


**הַפְלֵה חֲסָדֶיךָ.** דֵּשִׁיבְרָ״א בְּלַעַ״ז, כְּמוֹ ״וְנִפְלִינוּ אֲנִי וְעַמְּךָ״ (שמות לג:טז). מוֹשִׁיעַ בִּימִינְךָ אֶת הַחוֹסִים בְּךָ מִמִּתְקוֹמְמִים עֲלֵיהֶם. **הַפְלֵה חֲסָדֶיךָ מוֹשִׁיעַ חוֹסִים** הֲרֵי זֶה מִקְרָא מְסֹרָס: הַפְלֵה חֲסָדֶיךָ לְהוֹשִׁיעַ בִּימִינְךָ אֶת הַחוֹסִים וְגוֹ׳:


**Distinguish Your kind acts** Heb. הפלה, esevre in Old French, to separate, as (in Exod. 33:16): “and I and my people will be distinguished (ונפלינו).” With Your right hand You save those who take refuge in You from those who rise up against them. (This does not appear in manuscripts or in most early editions.) [The literal meaning is:] Distinguish Your kind acts, You Who save those who take refuge, etc. This is a transposed verse, meaning: Distinguish Your kind acts to save with Your right hand those who take refuge, etc.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 17:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:8:1)


**כְּאִישׁוֹן.** הוּא הַשָּׁחוֹר שֶׁבָּעַיִן, שֶׁהָאוֹר תָּלוּי בּוֹ. וְעַל שֵׁם שַׁחֲרוּרִיתוֹ הוּא קָרוּי אִישׁוֹן, לְשׁוֹן חֹשֶׁךְ (משלי כ:כ). וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הֵכִין לוֹ שׁוֹמֵר, אֶת רִיסֵי הָעַיִן הַמְכַסִּין אוֹתוֹ תָּמִיד:


**as the apple** Heb. (כאישון). That is the pupil (lit. the black) of the eye, on which the vision depends. Because it is black, it is called אישון, an expression of darkness, and the Holy One, blessed be He, prepared a guard for it, viz. the eyelids, which constantly cover it.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 17:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:9:1)


**זוּ שַׁדּוּנִי.** בִּשְׁבִיל זֹאת שֶׁשּׁוֹדְדִים אוֹתִי אוֹיְבַי, אֲשֶׁר **בְּנֶפֶשׁ יַקִּיפוּ עָלָי.** לִטּוֹל נַפְשִׁי:


**who have robbed me** Because of this: my enemies, who encompass me to take my life, rob me.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 17:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:10:1)


**חֶלְבָּמוֹ סָגְרוּ.** בְּחֶלְבָּם וּבְשֻׁמָּנָם סָגְרוּ לִבָּם וְעֵינֵיהֶם מֵהַבִּיט אֶל פָּעֳלְךָ לִירָאָה מִפָּנֶיךָ:


**[With] their fat, they closed themselves up** With their fat, they closed their heart and their eyes from looking at Your deeds, in fear of You.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 17:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:11:1)


**אַשֻּׁרֵינוּ עַתָּה סְבָבוּנוּ.** אֶת עֲקֵבֵנוּ עַתָּה סְבָבוּנוּ הָאוֹיְבִים, וְ**עֵינֵיהֶם יָשִׁיתוּ לִנְטוֹת בָּאָרֶץ** לִפְשֹׁט בָּאָרֶץ. וְנִרְאֶה לִי שֶׁנִּתְפַּלֵּל דָּוִד תְּפִלָּה זוֹ לְאַחַר שֶׁבָּא לְיָדוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁל אוּרִיָּה, וְיוֹאָב וְיִשְׂרָאֵל הָיוּ בְּאֶרֶץ בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן צָרִים עַל רַבָּה (שמואל ב יא:א), וַיִּירָא דָּוִד שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּשְׁלוּ שָׁם בִּשְׁבִיל עֲבֵרָה שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ, וְיִשְׁמְעוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים וּמוֹאָב וֶאֱדוֹם וְכָל שְׁכֵנֵי אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הָרָעִים הַמְצַפִּים לְיוֹם אֵידָם, וְיָבֹאוּ עֲלֵיהֶם:


**[By] our footsteps they surround us now** By our footsteps, the enemies surround us now, and they set their eyes roaming over the land, to raid the land. It appears to me that David prayed this prayer after the incident of Uriah and Joab had happened to him, and the Israelites were in the land of the children of Ammon besieging Rabbah (II Sam. 11), and David feared that they would be defeated there because of the sin that he had committed, and the Philistines, Moab, Edom, and all the evil neighbors of Eretz Israel, who looked forward to the day of their misfortune, would hear and march against them.



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Psalms 17:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:12:1)


**יִכְסוֹף.** יַחְמוֹד, כְּמוֹ ״כִּי נִכְסֹף נִכְסַפְתָּ״ (בראשית לא:ל):


**which yearns** Heb. יכסף, yearns, as (in Gen. 31:30): “for you yearned (נכסף נכספתי).”

###### Rashi on Psalms 17:13:3

### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Psalms 17:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:14:1)


**מִמְּתִים יָדְךָ.** מִן הַמֵּתִים בְּיָדְךָ עַל מִטָּתָם אֲנִי בּוֹחֵר לִהְיוֹת:


**Of those who die by Your hand** I choose to be one of those who die by Your hand on their bed.


###### Rashi on Psalms 17:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:14:2)


**מִמְּתִים מֵחֶלֶד.** מֵאוֹתָם שֶׁמֵּתִים בְּזִקְנָה, מִשֶּׁהֶעֱלוּ חֲלֻדָּה, רְדוּיִילָ״א בְּלַעַ״ז, וּמִן הַצַּדִּיקִים אֲשֶׁר **חֶלְקָם בַּחַיִּים**:


**of those who die of old age** Heb. מחלד. Of those who die of old age, after they have “rusted” (חלודה), rodijjl in Old French, [rouille in Modern French] rust, and of the righteous, whose share is in life.


###### Rashi on Psalms 17:14:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:14:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:14:3)


**וּצְפוּנְךָ תְּמַלֵּא בִטְנָם.** וּמֵאוֹתָם אֲשֶׁר תְּמַלֵּא מְעֵיהֶם מִטּוּבְךָ אֲשֶׁר צָפַנְתָּ לִירֵאֶיךָ (תהלים לא:כ):


**and whose belly You will fill with Your hidden treasure** And of those whose innards You will fill with Your good, which You have hidden for those who fear You.


###### Rashi on Psalms 17:14:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:14:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:14:4)


**יִתְרָם.** נִכְסֵיהֶם אֲשֶׁר יַשְׁאִירוּ בְּמוֹתָם:


**their abundance** Their property that they leave over when they die.



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Psalms 17:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:15:1)


**אֲנִי בְּצֶדֶק אֶחֱזֶה פָנֶיךָ.** לֶעָתִיד, אוֹ **בְּצֶדֶק אֶחֱזֶה פָנֶיךָ** מִשְׁפָּטִי הוֹצֵא מִלְּפָנֶיךָ, וְהַצְּדָקוֹת שֶׁבְּיָדִי אֱחוֹז, וּבָהֶם אֶחֱזֶה פָנֶיךָ:


**I will see Your face with righteousness** In the future, take my judgment away from before You and grasp the righteous deeds that I have performed, and through them I will see Your face.


###### Rashi on Psalms 17:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/17:15:2)


**אֶשְׂבְּעָה בְהָקִיץ תְּמוּנָתֶךָ.** אֶשְׂבְּעָה מֵרְאִיַּת תְּמוּנָתְךָ בְּהָקִיץ הַמֵּתִים מִשְּׁנָתָם. לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: אֶשְׂבְּעָה מֵרְאוֹת פָּנֶיךָ בְּהָקִיץ הַמֵּתִים מִשְּׁנָתָם, שֶׁהֵם בִּדְמוּת תְּמוּנָתְךָ, שֶׁכֵּן נֶאֱמַר ״כִּי בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם״ (בראשית ט:ו):


**I will see Your face with righteousness** in the future (Mid. Ps. 17:13), or **I will see Your face with righteousness** Take my judgment away from before You and grasp the righteous deeds that I have performed, and through them I will see Your face. In other editions, this is one interpretation: **I will be satisfied with Your image upon the awakening** I will be satisfied with the vision of Your image when the dead awaken from their sleep. In many editions, the following appears at this point: Another explanation: I will be satisfied from seeing Your face when the dead awaken from their sleep, for they are in the likeness of Your image, for so it is stated (in Gen. 9:6): “For in the image of God, He made man.”



## Chapter 18


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:1:1)


**בְּיוֹם הִצִּיל ה׳ אוֹתוֹ וְגוֹ׳.** כְּשֶׁהִזְקִין, וּכְבָר עָבְרוּ עָלָיו כָּל צָרוֹתָיו וְנִצּוֹל מֵהֶם:


**on the day the Lord saved him etc.** When he became old and all his troubles had already passed over him and he was saved from them.


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:1:2)


**וּמִיַּד שָׁאוּל.** וַהֲלֹא שָׁאוּל בִּכְלָל הָיָה? אֶלָּא לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה קָשֶׁה עָלָיו וְרוֹדְפוֹ יוֹתֵר מִכֻּלָּם. כְּיוֹצֵא בַדָּבָר אַתָּה אוֹמֵר: ״וְרָאוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ וְאֶת יְרִיחוֹ״ (יהושע ב:א):


**and from the hand of Saul** Was not Saul included? But [he is mentioned specifically] because he was the harshest to him and pursued him more than all of them. Similarly, you say (in Josh. 2:1): “see the land and Jericho.”



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:2:1)


**אֶרְחָמְךָ.** אֲאַהֶבְךָ, כְּדִמְתַרְגֵּם ״וְאָהַבְתָּ״ (ויקרא יט:יח): ״וְתִרְחַם״ (תרגום אונקלוס):


**I love You** Heb. ארחמך, I love You, as the Targum renders (Lev. 19:18): “and you shall love your neighbor,” ותרחם.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:3:1)


**סַלְעִי.** שֶׁעֲזַרְתַּנִי בְּסֶלַע הַמַּחְלְקוֹת, כְּשֶׁהָיִיתִי מְצֻמְצָם בֵּין שָׁאוּל וַאֲנָשָׁיו לְהִתָּפֵס, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְשָׁאוּל וַאֲנָשָׁיו עוֹטְרִים אֶל דָּוִד וְגוֹמֵר״ (שמואל א כג:כו):


**my rock** For You saved me at the Rock of the Divisions (I Sam. 23:28), when I was trapped between Saul and his men, to be caught, as it is stated (in I Sam. 23:26): “but Saul and his men were encircling to David and his men etc.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:3:2)


**וּמְצוּדָתִי.** לְשׁוֹן מִבְצָר:


**and my fortress** Heb. ומצודתי, an expression of a fortress.


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:3:3)


**צוּרִי.** לְשׁוֹן סֶלַע:


**my rock** Heb. צורי, an expression of a rock.


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:3:4)


**אֶחֱסֶה.** אַבְרִיאַיְי״ר בְּלַעַ״ז:


**I will take refuge** Abrier in French (to protect, cover; cf. Rashi to Isa. 30:2, Joel 4:16).


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:3:5)


**אֶחֱסֶה בּוֹ.** אֶתְכַּסֶּה בְּצִלּוֹ, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וּמִבְּלִי מַחְסֶה חִבְּקוּ צוּר״ (איוב כד:ח) – שֶׁהַסְּלָעִים כִּסּוּי וּמָגֵן לְהוֹלְכֵי דְרָכִים מִן הָרוּחוֹת וּמִזֶּרֶם גְּשָׁמִים:


**I will take refuge in Him** I will take shelter in His shade, as the matter is stated (in Job 24:8): “and without shelter (מחסה) they embrace the rocks,” because the rocks are a shelter and a shield for the travelers from the winds and from the downpour of rains.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:4:1)


**מְהֻלָּל אֶקְרָא ה׳.** בְּהִלּוּלִים אֶקְרָא וְאֶתְפַּלֵּל לְפָנָיו תָּמִיד, כְּלוֹמַר אַף לִפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּעָה אֲנִי מְהַלְּלוֹ, לְפִי שֶׁבָּטוּחַ אֲנִי שֶׁ**אִוָּשַׁע** מֵאוֹיְבַי:


**With praise I call to the lord** With praises I call Him and pray before Him constantly, i.e., even before the salvation I praise Him, because I am confident that I will be saved from my enemies.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:5:1)


**אֲפָפוּנִי חֶבְלֵי מָוֶת.** פְּעָמִים רַבּוֹת סְבָבוּנִי רְשָׁעִים, אֲפָפוּנִי כְּמוֹ סְבָבוּנִי, וְכֵן ״אָפְפוּ עָלַי רָעוֹת״ (תהלים מ:יג):


**Bands of death have encompassed me** On many occasions wicked men have surrounded me. אפפוני is like סבבוני. Similarly (below 40:13), “For countless evils...have encompassed (אפפו) me.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:5:2)


**חֶבְלֵי מָוֶת.** מַחֲנוֹת אוֹיְבִים, כְּמוֹ ״חֶבֶל נְבִיאִים״ בְּסֵפֶר שְׁמוּאֵל (שמואל א י:ה). וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: ״כְּאִתְּתָא דְּיָתְבָא עַל מַתְבְּרָא״, לְשׁוֹן ״חֶבְלֵי יוֹלֵדָה״ (הושע יג:יג):


**Bands of death** Heb. חבלי, camps of enemies, as (in I Sam. 10:5): “a band (חבל) of prophets.” But Jonathan renders: as a woman who sits on a birthstool, an expression of the pangs (חבלי) of a woman in confinement.


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:5:3)


**וְנַחֲלֵי בְלִיַּעַל.** אַף הוּא לְשׁוֹן גְּיָסוֹת שׁוֹטְפִים כְּנַחַל:


**and streams of scoundrels** That too is an expression of troops that flood like a stream.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:6:1)


**חֶבְלֵי שְׁאוֹל.** כְּמוֹ **חֶבְלֵי מָוֶת** – ״מַשְׁרְיָן רַשִׁיעָן״ (תרגום יונתן שמואל ב כב:ו), וַאֲנִי מָה הָיִיתִי עוֹשֶׂה?


**Bands of the nether world** Like “bands of death,” camps of wicked men, and I - what did I do?



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:7:1)


**בַּצַּר לִי אֶקְרָא.** אֲנִי הָיִיתִי קוֹרֵא לַה׳ תָּמִיד:


**When I am in distress, I call** I would always call upon the Lord.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:8:1)


**וַתִּגְעַשׁ וַתִּרְעַשׁ הָאָרֶץ.** אֵינוֹ מְחֻבָּר לְמִקְרָא עֶלְיוֹן, אֶלָּא מְחֻבָּר רֹאשׁוֹ לְסוֹפוֹ: **כִּי חָרָה לוֹ וַתִּגְעַשׁ וַתִּרְעַשׁ הָאָרֶץ.** כִּי מְשַׁמֵּשׁ בִּלְשׁוֹן כַּאֲשֶׁר: כְּשֶׁחָרָה לוֹ וּבָא לִנְקֹם נִקְמַת עַמּוֹ וַעֲבָדָיו מִפַּרְעֹה וּמֵעַמּוֹ, גָּעֲשָׁה וְרָעֲשָׁה הָאָרֶץ:


**The earth shook and quaked** This is not connected to the preceding verse, but its beginning is connected to its end; i.e., when He was angered, the earth shook and quaked. [The word] כי is used as an expression of “when.” When He was angered and came to wreak the vengeance of His people, His servants, on Pharaoh and his people, the earth shook and quaked.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:9:1)


**עָלָה עָשָׁן בְּאַפּוֹ.** אַנְשִׁישְׁנַארִילַ״שׁ בְּלַעַ״ז, כֵּן דֶּרֶךְ כָּל חֲרוֹן אַף לְהַעֲלוֹת עָשָׁן מִנְּחִירָיו:


**Smoke went up in His nostrils** (En ses nariles in Old French, in his nostrils.) So is the custom of every anger, to cause smoke to ascend from his nostrils.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:10:1)


**וַיֵּט שָׁמַיִם וַיֵּרַד.** לַעֲבוֹר בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם. **וַיֵּרַד** כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ. לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: אִיאַנְטְבִּ״שׁ בְּלַעַ״ז:


**And He bent the heavens, and He came down** to pass through the land of Egypt. “He came down” is to be understood in its simple meaning. Another explanation is “i atonvit” in Old French, to flatten, as (in Exod. 39:3), and the radical is רדד.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:11:1)


**וַיֵּדֶא.** וַיָּעֹף, כְּמוֹ ״כַּאֲשֶׁר יִדְאֶה הַנָּשֶׁר״ (דברים כח:מט):


**He swooped** Heb. וידא, He flew, as (in Deut. 28:49), “as the eagle swoops (ידאה).”



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:12:1)


**חֶשְׁכַת מַיִם.** שֶׁבְּעָבֵי שְׁחָקִים הֵם חֹשֶׁךְ אֲשֶׁר סְבִיבוֹתָיו. וְשֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר: לִפְנִים מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ אֵין אוֹר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: **מִנֹּגַהּ אֲשֶׁר נֶגְדּוֹ** וּמִתּוֹךְ מְחִיצָתוֹ, אֶת עָבָיו אֲשֶׁר סְבִיבוֹתָיו בּוֹקְעִים וְעוֹבְרִים **בָּרָד וְגַחֲלֵי אֵשׁ**:


**the darkness of waters** that are in the thick clouds of the skies are the darkness that is about Him. Lest you say that within the darkness there is no light, Scripture tells us: From the brightness before Him, and from within His partition, His thick clouds that are about Him are split, and hail and coals of fire pass through them.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:13:1)


**עָבְרוּ.** טְרִישְׁפָּא״שְׁנְט בְּלַעַ״ז, הַבָּרָד בּוֹקֵעַ וְעוֹבֵר עַל הַמִּצְרִיִּים עַל יָם סוּף (שמות יד:כא-כח):


**passed** Heb. עברו, trepasant in Old French, passed. The hail split and passes through onto the Egyptians at the Sea of Reeds.



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:16:1)


**וַיֵּרָאוּ אֲפִיקֵי מַיִם.** כְּשֶׁנִּבְקַע הַיָּם:


**And the depths of the water appeared** when the sea split.


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:16:2

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:21:2

**כְּבֹר.** לְשׁוֹן נְקִיּוּת, כְּמוֹ ״וּבַר לֵבָב״ (תהלים כד:ד). דָּבָר אַחֵר: **יִשְׁלַח מִמָּרוֹם יִקָּחֵנִי** – כְּנֶגֶד עַצְמוֹ אָמַר, עַל שֵׁם הַמַּלְאָךְ שֶׁבָּא בְּסֶלַע הַמַּחְלְקוֹת לִפְצוֹת אֶת שָׁאוּל מֵעָלָיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וּמַלְאָךְ בָּא אֶל שָׁאוּל וְגוֹמֵר״ (שמואל א כג:כז):

[David] said this about himself, concerning the angel who came to the Rock of the Divisions (I Sam. 23:27) to turn Saul away from him, as it is stated: “And an angel came to Saul, etc.”

### Verse 30

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:30:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:30:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:30:1)

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:30:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:30:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:30:2)


**וּבֵאלֹהַי אֲדַלֶּג שׁוּר.** כְּשֶׁבָּא לְהִלָּחֵם עַל יְבוּס וְאָמַר: ״כָּל מַכֵּה יְבוּסִי יִהְיֶה לְרֹאשׁ וּלְשַׂר״ (דברי הימים א יא:ו), הֵבִיא יוֹאָב בְּרוֹשׁ רַעֲנָן וּכּפָפוֹ, וְנִתְלָה בּוֹ וְעָלָה עַל הַחוֹמָה. אָמַר דָּוִד: ״יֶהֶלְמֵנִי צַדִּיק וְגוֹמֵר״ (תהלים קמא:ה), קִצֵּר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת הַחוֹמָה וְדִלֵּג. בְּמִדְרַשׁ תְּהִלִּים:


**and by my God I scale a wall** When he came to wage war against Jebus, and he said (in I Chron. 11:6): “Whoever smites the Jebusites, etc. shall be a leader and a prince.” Joab brought a green juniper tree, bent it over, suspended himself on it, and scaled the wall. Said David (in Ps. 141:5): “May a righteous man smite me with loving-kindness,” and the Holy one, blessed be He, lowered the wall, and he scaled it (Mid. Ps. 18:24).

### Verse 35

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:35:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:35:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:35:1)


**וְנִחֲתָה קֶשֶׁת נְחוּשָׁה זְרוֹעֹתָי.** וְנִחֲתָה לְשׁוֹן דְּרִיכַת קֶשֶׁת, כְּמוֹ ״חִצֶּיךָ נִחֲתוּ בִי״ (תהלים לח:ג), וּפֹעַל שֶׁלּוֹ נָחַת וּכְשֶׁמִּתְפַּעֵל בָּא דָּגֵשׁ וּמְחַסֵּר אֶת הַנּוּ״ן **וְנִחֲתָה** מִגִּזְרַת נִנְחֲתָה כְּמוֹ ״נִחַר גְּרוֹנִי״ (תהלים סט:ד) מִגִּזְרַת נִנְחַר, כְּמוֹ ״נָחַר מַפֻּחַ״ (ירמיהו ו:כט) נִדַּף מִגִּזְרָה נִנְדַּף, ״עֵינִי נִגְּרָה״ (איכה ג:מט) כְּמוֹ נִנְגְּרָה, נִתְּנָה כְּמוֹ נִנְתְּנָה, נִגַּף מִגִּזְרַת נִנְגַּף. וְאֵין לְפוֹתְרוֹ מִגִּזְרַת חָתָה, שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ לוֹמַר נִחְתְּתָה כְּמוֹ מִן עָשָׂה נֶעֶשְׂתָה מִן עָנָה נַעֲנְתָה. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **וְנִחֲתָה קֶשֶׁת נְחוּשָׁה זְרוֹעֹתָי** חִיֵּת לְשׁוֹן דְּרִיכַת קֶשֶׁת כְּמוֹ ״חִצֶּיךָ נִחֲתוּ״ (תהלים לח:ג) הַנּוּ״ן אֵינָהּ יְסוֹד בַּתֵּבָה אֶלָּא כְּמוֹ נִחֲלוּ וְנִדְרְכָה קֶשֶׁת נְחוּשָׁה עַל יְדֵי זְרוֹעוֹתַי, קַשָּׁתוֹת שֶׁל נְחֹשֶׁת הָיוּ תְּלוּיוֹת לוֹ לְדָוִד בְּבֵיתוֹ וְרוֹאִין אוֹתָם מַלְכֵי הָאֻמּוֹת וְאוֹמְרִים זֶה לָזֶה אַתָּה סָבוּר שֶׁיֵּשׁ כֹּחַ בְּיַד דָּוִד לְדוֹרְכָן אֵין זֶה אֶלָּא לְיָרְאֵנוּ, וְהוּא הָיָה שׁוֹמֵעַ וְדוֹרְכָן בִּפְנֵיהֶם:


**so that a copper bow is bent by my arms** Heb. ונחתה, an expression of treading the bow, as (below 38:3): “Your arrows were driven (נחתו) into me.” Its radical [or its active voice] is נחת. When it is used in the passive voice, a dagesh comes and causes the “nun” to drop out. Hence נחתה is derived from ננחתה as (below 69:4): “My throat is dried (נחר),” derived from ננחר as (in Jer. 6:29): “The bellows is heated (נחר)”; נדף, rattling (in Lev. 26:36) is derived from ננדף ; “My eyes stream (נגרה)” (in Lam. 3:49), is like ננגרה ; “was given (נתנה)” (Gen. 38:14) is like ננתנה ; “they were smitten (נגף)” (II Sam. 10:15) is derived from ננגף. We cannot interpret it as being of the radical חתת, for then it would say נחתתה, as [it says] נעשתה, was done, from עשה ; נענתה, was answered, from ענה. Another explanation: and a copper bow is bent by my arms: חית is an expression of treading a bow, as (below 38:3): “Your arrows were driven (נחתו).” The “nun” is not of the radical but it is like נחלו “gave for inheritance” (in Jos. 14:1), and the copper bow was bent by my arms. Copper bows were hanging in David’s house. The kings of the nations would see them and say to each other, “Do you think that David has the strength to bend them? This is only to frighten us.” But he would hear [them] and bend the bows before them.

**קַרְסֻלָּי.** הֵם הָרַגְלַיִם מִן הָאִסְתּוֹרִין, שֶׁקּוֹרִין קָבִילָ״א בְּלַעַ״ז, וּלְמַטָּה:

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:42:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:42:2)


**וְאֵין מוֹשִׁיעַ.** שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ יְכֹלֶת, וְחוֹזְרִים וְקוֹרְאִים אֶל ה׳, וְלֹא עָנָם:


**but no one saves them** Because it [their prayer] has no power, and they return and call upon the Lord, but He does not answer them.



### Verse 43

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:43:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:43:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:43:1)


**וְאֶשְׁחָקֵם.** לְשׁוֹן כְּתִישָׁה:


**Then I ground them** Heb. ואשחקם, an expression of crushing.


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:43:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:43:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:43:2)


**אֲרִיקֵם.** כְּטִיט הַנָּרוּק, שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָב. כְּמוֹ ״הֵם מְרִיקִים שַׂקֵּיהֶם״ (בראשית מב:לה), ״לֹא הוּרַק מִכְּלִי אֶל כֶּלִי״ (ירמיהו מח:יא):


**I did pour them** like loose mud, which is not thick, as (in Gen. 42:35): “when they emptied (מריקים) their sacks”; (in Jer. 48:11), “has not been poured (הורק) from one vessel to another vessel.”



### Verse 44

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:44:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:44:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:44:1)


**תְּפַלְּטֵנִי מֵרִיבֵי עָם.** שֶׁלֹּא אֵעָנֵשׁ בְּדִין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַטּוֹת מִשְׁפָּט, וְלֹא לְשַׁעְבֵּד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹתֵר מִן הָרְשׁוּת:


**You allowed me to escape from the contenders of the people** so that I should not be punished according to Jewish law, for perverting justice or for subjugating an Israelite more than is permitted.


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:44:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:44:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:44:2)


**תְּשִׂימֵנִי לְרֹאשׁ גּוֹיִם.** שֶׁאֵין עֹנֶשׁ בָּהֶם:


**You shall make me the head over nations** for whom there is no punishment.



### Verse 45

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:45:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:45:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:45:1)


**לְשֵׁמַע אֹזֶן.** אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנַי, אֶלָּא שֶׁיִּשְׁמְעוּ שְׁלִיחוּתִי:


**As soon as they hear** Even in my absence, as long as they hear my message.


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:45:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:45:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:45:2)


**יִשָּׁמְעוּ לִי.** יָסוּרוּ אֶל מִשְׁמַעְתִּי, וְיִהְיוּ נִשְׁמָעִים לִדְבָרַי:


**they shall obey me** They shall give heed to my bidding and obey my orders.


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:45:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:45:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:45:3)


**יְכַחֲשׁוּ לִי.** מֵחֲמַת יִרְאָה:


**shall lie to me** out of fright.



### Verse 46

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:46:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:46:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:46:1)


**יִבֹּלוּ.** יִלְאוּ, כְּמוֹ ״נָבֹל תִּבֹּל״ (שמות יח:יח), דִּמְתַרְגֵּם ״מִילְאָה תִּילְאָה״. וּמְנַחֵם פֵּירֵשׁ כְּמוֹ ״אַחֲרֵי בְלֹתִי״ (בראשית יח:יב), וְכֵן פֵּירֵשׁ ״נָבֹל תִּבֹּל״:


**shall wither** Heb. יבלו. They shall become weary, as (in Exod. 18:18): “you shall surely wither (נבל תבל),” which the Targum renders: you shall surely weary. Menachem (Machbereth p. 45) explains it as (in Gen. 18:12): “after I have become old (בלתי),” and he explained נבל תבל in the same manner.


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:46:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:46:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:46:2)


**וְיַחְרְגוּ.** לְשׁוֹן אֵימָה. ״מֵחֲדָרִים אֵימָה״ (דברים לב:כה) מְתַרְגְּמִינָן: ״חַרְגַּת מוֹתָא״:


**and they shall fear** Heb. ויחרגו, an expression of fear; (in Deut. 32:25) “and terror from within,” the Targum renders: חרגת, fear of death.


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:46:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:46:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:46:3)


**מִמִּסְגְּרוֹתֵיהֶם.** מֵחֲמַת יִסּוּרֵי מַסְגְּרוֹת כֶּלֶא שֶׁאֲנִי מַסְגִּירָם שָׁם וּמְיַסְּרָן בָּהֶן. **וְיַחְרְגוּ מִמִּסְגְּרוֹתֵיהֶם** מְנַחֵם פָּתַר אוֹתוֹ לְשׁוֹן רִפְיוֹן חֲגוֹרָה, וְכֵן פֵּרוּשׁוֹ: וְיִתְרַפּוּ מִמִּסְגְּרוֹתֵיהֶם. וְדוּנָ״שׁ פָּתַר **וְיַחְרְגוּ מִמִּסְגְּרוֹתֵיהֶם** וְיִפְסְחוּ מִכַּבְלֵיהֶם הַנְּתוּנִים עַל רַגְלֵיהֶם. וּפִתְרוֹן וְיַחְרְגוּ ״וְיִפְסְחוּ״ (ויקרא כא:יח), כְּדִמְתַרְגְּמִינָן ״חֲגִירָא״:


**their imprisonments** Because of the tortures of the imprisonments in the dungeon where I imprison them and where they torture them. Menachem (p. 94) interprets it as an expression of loosening the girdle, and so he explains it: and they will be loosened of their girdles [meaning they will be frightened or weakened]. Dunash interprets ויחגרו ממסגרותיהם, and they will be lamed from their shackles, which are placed on their feet. The meaning of ויחגרו is: they will become lame, as the Aramaic for a lame person is חגר.



### Verse 47

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:47:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:47:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:47:1)


**חַי ה׳.** הָעוֹשֶׂה לִי כָּל זֹאת:


**The Lord lives** He Who does all this for me.



### Verse 48

###### Rashi on Psalms 18:48:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:48:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:48:1)


**הַנּוֹתֵן נְקָמוֹת לִי.** נוֹתֵן בִּי כֹּחַ לְהִנָּקֵם מֵאוֹיְבַי:


**Who grants me vengeance** Who gives me strength to avenge myself upon my enemies.


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:48:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:48:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:48:2)


**וַיְדַבֵּר.** וְיַהֲרֹג, לְשׁוֹן דֶּבֶר. לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: כְּמוֹ ״וַיִּנְהַג״ (שמות ג:א), דִּמְתַרְגְּמִינַן: ״וּדְבַר״. וְכֵן חִבְּרוֹ מְנַחֵם, וְגַם כֵּן חִבֵּר ״יַדְבֵּר עַמִּים תַּחְתֵּינוּ״ (תהלים מז:ד):


**and destroys** Heb. וידבר, and He slew, an expression of דבר, pestilence. Another explanation: as (in Exod. 3:1): “and he led (וינהג),” which is translated into Aramaic as וּדְבַר. Menachem (p. 61) too associated it in this manner. Likewise, he associated (below 47:4), “He leads (יַדְבֵּר) peoples under us.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 18:48:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:48:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/18:48:3)


**תַּחְתָּי.** בִּמְקוֹמִי וְחִלּוּפִי, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וָאֶתֵּן אָדָם תַּחְתֶּיךָ״ (ישעיהו מג:ד) – ״נָתַתִּי כָפְרְךָ מִצְרַיִם״ (ישעיהו מג:ג):


**instead of me** Heb. תחתי, in my place and in my stead, as the matter is stated (in Isa. 43:4): “and I give men in your stead (תחתיך), (verse 3), “I have given Egypt as your ransom. [Cush and Seba in your stead (תחתיך)].”



## Chapter 19


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 19:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:2:1)


**הַשָּׁמַיִם מְסַפְּרִים כְּבוֹד אֵל.** הַמְשׁוֹרֵר עַצְמוֹ פֵּרַשׁ אֶת הַדָּבָר: **אֵין אֹמֶר וְאֵין דְּבָרִים**. אֵינָן מְדַבְּרִים עִם הַבְּרִיּוֹת, אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁ**בְּכָל הָאָרֶץ יָצָא קַוָּם** וּמְאִירִים לַבְּרִיּוֹת, מִתּוֹךְ כָּךְ מְסַפְּרִים הַבְּרִיּוֹת כְּבוֹד אֵל וּמוֹדִים וּמְבָרְכִין עַל הַמְּאוֹרוֹת:


**The heavens recite the glory of God** The Psalmist himself explains the matter: There is neither speech nor words. They do not speak with people but since “their line goes forth throughout the earth” and they give light to the people, thereby the creatures recite the glory of God and give thanks and bless [Him] for the luminaries.


###### Rashi on Psalms 19:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:2:2)


**וּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו מַגִּיד הָרָקִיעַ.** הַכּוֹכָבִים וְהַמַּזָּלוֹת, שֶׁהֵם מַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֲשֶׁר הֵם שָׁם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיִּתֵּן אֹתָם אֱלֹהִים בִּרְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמָיִם״ (בראשית א:יז), וּמִשָּׁם מַגִּידִים כְּבוֹדוֹ:


**and the sky tells of the work of His hands** The stars and planets, which are the work of the hands of the Holy One, blessed be He, and which are there, as it is stated (in Gen. 1:17): “And God placed them in the firmament of the heavens,” whence they proclaim His glory.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 19:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:3:1)


**יוֹם לְיוֹם יַבִּיעַ אֹמֶר.** מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית מִתְחַדֵּשׁ מִיּוֹם אֶל יוֹם; לָעֶרֶב חַמָּה שׁוֹקַעַת וְזוֹרַחַת לַבֹּקֶר, וּמִתּוֹךְ כָּךְ יַבִּיעוּ הַבְּרִיּוֹת אִמְרֵי שֶׁבַח עַל יְדֵי הַיָּמִים וְהַלֵּילוֹת, שֶׁמּוֹרִים אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת לְקַלֵּס וּלְהוֹדוֹת. מְנַחֵם פֵּתַר ״יַבִּיעַ״ לְשׁוֹן ״מַעְיָן נוֹבֵעַ״:


**Day to day utters speech** The Creation is renewed from day to day. In the evening, the sun sets, and in the morning it rises. Thereby, the people utter sayings of praise throughout these days and nights, for they teach the people to praise and to give thanks. Menachem interprets [the word] יביע as an expression of a gushing fountain (מעין נובע).


###### Rashi on Psalms 19:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:3:2)


**יְחַוֶּה.** לְשׁוֹן הַגָּדָה:


**tells knowledge** Heb. יחוה, an expression of telling.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 19:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:5:1)


**בְּכָל הָאָרֶץ יָצָא קַוָּם.** קַו הַשָּׁמַיִם שֶׁהֵם נִמְתָּחִים עַל פְּנֵי כָּל הָאָרֶץ, וּמֵחֲמַת כֵּן **בִּקְצֵה תֵבֵל מִלֵּיהֶם** שֶׁהַכֹּל מְדַבְּרִים בַּנִּפְלָאוֹת שֶׁהֵם רוֹאִים:


**Their line goes forth throughout the earth** The line of the heavens, which are stretched out over the face of the entire earth, and because of which their words are at the end of the world, for all speak of the wonders they see.


###### Rashi on Psalms 19:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:5:2)


**לַשֶּׁמֶשׁ שָׂם.** הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:


**for the sun He made** [i.e.,] the Holy One, blessed be He.


###### Rashi on Psalms 19:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:5:3)


**אֹהֶל בָּהֶם.** בַּשָּׁמַיִם, מִכָּאן שֶׁהַשֶּׁמֶשׁ נָתוּן בְּתוֹךְ תִּיקוֹ (תנחומא, תצוה ח):


**a tent therein** In the heavens. From here it is derived that the sun is placed within its case. Tanchuma.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 19:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:6:1)


**וְהוּא כְּחָתָן יֹצֵא מֵחֻפָּתוֹ.** בְּכָל בֹּקֶר, וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר **הַשָּׁמַיִם מְסַפְּרִים כְּבוֹד אֵל**:


**And it is like a bridegroom emerging from his chamber** every morning. This is what is meant by “The heavens recite the glory of God.”



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 19:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:7:1)


**וּתְקוּפָתוֹ עַל קְצוֹתָם.** הַקָּפַת סִבּוּבוֹ מִקָּצֶה אֶל קָצֶה:


**and its circuit is to their ends** The circuit of its orbit is from one end to the other.


###### Rashi on Psalms 19:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:7:2)


**וְאֵין נִסְתָּר מֵחַמָּתוֹ.** אִילְמָלֵא נִיתַּן בָּרָקִיעַ הַתַּחְתּוֹן, לֹא הָיָה אָדָם נִסְתָּר מִפָּנָיו מִפְּנֵי חֲמִימוּתוֹ. שֶׁחַמָּה וּלְבָנָה בָּרָקִיעַ הַשֵּׁנִי, כְּדְאָמְרִינַן (חגיגה יב:): שִׁבְעָה רְקִיעִים הֵם: וִילוֹן, רָקִיעַ, שְׁחָקִים, זְבוּל, מָכוֹן, מָעוֹן, עֲרָבוֹת. וּמוֹנֶה לָהֶם כְּסִדְרָן: וִילוֹן אֵינוֹ מְשַׁמֵּשׁ כְּלוּם, רָקִיעַ יֵשׁ בּוֹ חַמָּה וּלְבָנָה, כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת וְכוּ׳:


**and none is hidden from its heat** Had the sun been placed in the lowest sky, no man would be able to hide from its heat (Mid. Ps. 18:13) for the sun and the moon are in the second sky, as is stated (in Hagigah 12b): There are seven skies—Vilon, Rakia, Shehakim, Zevul, Machon, Ma’on, Aravothand he counts them in order: Vilon does not serve for anything; in Rakia are the sun, the moon, the stars, and the planets, etc.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 19:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:8:1)


**תּוֹרַת ה׳ תְּמִימָה.** גַּם הִיא מְאִירָה כַּשֶּׁמֶשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּסוֹף הָעִנְיָן **מְאִירַת עֵינָיִם** וְאוֹמֵר (משלי ו:כג) ״כִּי נֵר מִצְוָה וְתוֹרָה אוֹר״. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **וְאֵין נִסְתָּר מֵחַמָּתוֹ** לְיוֹם הַדִּין וְלִהַט אוֹתָם הַיּוֹם הַבָּא (מלאכי ג:יט), אֲבָל **תּוֹרַת ה׳ תְּמִימָה הִיא מְשִׁיבַת נָפֶשׁ** לְדַרְכֵי חַיִּים וּמְגִנָּה הִיא עַל לוֹמְדֶיהָ מֵאוֹתוֹ לַהַט, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְזָרְחָה לָכֶם יִרְאֵי שְׁמִי שֶׁמֶשׁ צְדָקָה וּמַרְפֵּא וְגוֹמֵר״ (מלאכי ג:כ):


**The law of the Lord is perfect** That too illuminates like the sun, as is written at the end of the topic: “enlightening the eyes,” and Scripture states (in Prov. 6:23): “For a commandment is a candle and the Torah is light.” Another explanation: **and none is hidden from its heat** on the Day of Judgment, [as is stated in Malachi 3:19]: “And the sun that comes shall burn them up.” But the law of the Lord is perfect; it restores the soul to ways of life and it protects those who study it from that burning, as is stated (ibid. verse 20): “And the sun of mercy shall rise with healing...for you who fear My Name.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 19:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:8:2)


**עֵדוּת ה׳ נֶאֱמָנָה.** נֶאֱמֶנֶת הִיא לְהָעִיד בְּלוֹמְדֶיהָ:


**the testimony of the Lord is faithful** It is faithful to testify for those who study it.


###### Rashi on Psalms 19:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:8:3)


**מְשִׁיבַת נָפֶשׁ.** מְשִׁיבָתוֹ מִדַּרְכֵי מִיתָה לְדַרְכֵי חַיִּים. תּוֹרַת, עֵדוּת, פִּקּוּדֵי, מִצְוַת, יִרְאַת, מִשְׁפְּטֵי – שִׁשָּׁה, כְּנֶגֶד שִׁשָּׁה סִדְרֵי מִשְׁנָה (ברכות יא:), וּבֵין כָּל שֵׁם וָשֵׁם חֲמִשָּׁה תֵּבוֹת עִם הַשֵּׁם עַצְמוֹ, כְּנֶגֶד חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תּוֹרָה. וְחוֹתֵם בְּסוֹפָן: **אֱמֶת צָדְקוּ יַחְדָּו.** כֻּלָּם יַחַד מְתֻקָּנִים בְּחֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת:


**restoring the soul** It [the law] restores it [the soul] from the ways of death to the ways of life. The law, the testimony, the orders, the commandments, the fear, and the judgments total six, corresponding to the six orders of the Mishnah. Between each name [of God] are five words including the name itself, corresponding to the Five Books of the Pentateuch. And so [the Psalmist] concludes: “true, altogether just.” They are altogether devised with kindness and truth.


###### Rashi on Psalms 19:8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:8:4)


**מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי.** נוֹתֶנֶת חָכְמָה לַפְּתָאִים:


**making the simple one wise** It gives wisdom to the simple.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 19:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:9:1)


**בָּרָה.** מַצְהֶרֶת:


**clear** Shining.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 19:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:11:1)


**וְנֹפֶת צוּפִים.** וּמֶתֶק צוּפִים בְּרוֹיְ״קָאשׁ בְּלַעַ״ז. וּמְנַחֵם פָּתַר **וְנֹפֶת** לְשׁוֹן טִפָּה, וְכֵן ״נֹפֶת תִּטֹּפְנָה״ (משלי ה:ג), ״נָפַתִּי מִשְׁכָּבִי״ (משלי ז:יז) (ס״א אינו):


**and drippings of honeycombs** Heb. ונפת צופים, sweetness of honeycombs; breche, or bresches, honeycombs. Menachem interprets ונפת as an expression of a drop, and so (in Prov. 5:3): “drip sweetness (נפת)”; (ibid. 7:17), “I sprinkled (נפתי) my couch.”



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Psalms 19:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:12:1)


**בְּשָׁמְרָם עֵקֶב רָב.** נִזְהַרְתִּי בִּשְׁמִירָתָם בִּשְׁבִיל רֹב טוּבְךָ אֲשֶׁר צָפַנְתָּ (תהלים לא:כ), וְלַלָּשׁוֹן הַזֶּה עֵקֶב כְּמוֹ ״עֵקֶב אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַע אַבְרָהָם בְּקוֹלִי״ (בראשית כו:ה). דָּבָר אַחֵר: **עֵקֶב רָב.** סוֹפָן שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים לָבֹא לִידֵי גְדֻלָּה. **עֵקֶב** לְשׁוֹן סוֹף, וְיֵשׁ לוֹ חָבֵר בִּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה: עִקְּבוֹת מְשִׁיחָא (סוטה ט:טו):


**for in observing them there is great reward** I was careful in its observance because of Your great good that You have hidden away, and according to this usage, עקב is like (Gen. 26:5): “because (עקב) Abraham hearkened to My voice.” Another explanation of עקב רב: The end of the Torah scholars is that they will come to greatness. עקב is an expression of the end, and there is a similar expression in the language of the Mishnah (Sotah 9:15): “At the end (בעקבות) of the exile, prior to the coming of the Messiah.”



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Psalms 19:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:13:1)


**שְׁגִיאוֹת מִי יָבִין.** אֲנִי נִזְהַרְתִּי בָּהֶם, אֲבָל אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִזָּהֵר שֶׁלֹּא אֶשְׁגֶּה בָּהֶם, וְאַתָּה **נַקֵּנִי מִנִּסְתָּרוֹת** שֶׁנִּסְתְּרוּ מִמֶּנִּי, וְלֹא יָדַעְתִּי בְּחֶטְאִי בִּשְׁגָגָה:


**Who understands errors?** I was careful with them but it is impossible to be so careful that one does not err in them, and You cleanse me of hidden sins, which were hidden from me; of which I was unaware when I sinned inadvertently.



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Psalms 19:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:14:1)


**גַּם מִזֵּדִים.** מִן הַזְּדוֹנוֹת:


**Also...from willful sins** Heb. מזדים, from willful sins.


###### Rashi on Psalms 19:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/19:14:2)


**אָז אֵיתָם.** אֶהְיֶה תָּמִים. אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים : לְמָה דָּוִד דּוֹמֶה? לְכוּתִי הַמְחַזֵּר עַל הַפְּתָחִים, וְהֵם מַעֲרִימִים בַּדָּבָר יוֹתֵר מִכָּל אָדָם: תְּנוּ לִי מַיִם לִשְׁתּוֹת, דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ חֶסְרוֹן כִּיס. מִשֶּׁשָּׁתָה אָמַר: יֵשׁ כָּאן בָּצָל קָטָן? מִשֶּׁנָּתְנוּ לוֹ אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ בָּצָל בְּלֹא מֶלַח? מִשֶּׁנָּתְנוּ לוֹ אָמַר: תְּנוּ לִי מְעַט לֶחֶם, שֶׁלֹּא יַזִּיקֵנִי הַבָּצָל. כָּךְ אָמַר דָּוִד: בִּתְחִלָּה עַל הַשְּׁגָגוֹת, וְאַחַר כָּךְ עַל הַזְּדוֹנוֹת, וְאַחַר כָּךְ עַל הַמְּרָדִים. פְּשָׁעִים אֵלּוּ הַמְּרָדִים, שֶׁמִּתְכַּוֵּן לְהַכְעִיס, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר (מלכים ב ג:ז): ״מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב פָּשַׁע בִּי״:


**then I will be perfect** Heb. איתם will be perfect. The Sages said (Mid. Ps. 19:17, Lev. Rabbah 5:8): To what can David be compared? To a Cuthite who goes from door to door, and they are more cunning in this matter than any other people. “Give me a drink of water,” something that costs no money. After drinking, he says, “Perhaps you have a small onion?” After he gives it to him, he says, “Is there an onion without salt?” After he gives it to him, he says, “Give me a little bread, so that the onion does not harm me.” So did David say at first concerning the inadvertent sins, and then concerning the willful sins, and afterwards concerning the rebellious sins. פשעים are rebellious sins, with which one intends to provoke, and so Scripture says (II Kings 3:7): “The king of Moab rebelled (פשע) against me.”

## Chapter 20


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 20:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/20:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/20:2:1)


**יַעַנְךָ ה׳ בְּיוֹם צָרָה.** הַמִּזְמוֹר הַזֶּה עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹלֵחַ אֶת יוֹאָב וְאֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל לַמִּלְחָמָה, וְהוּא הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם וּמִתְפַּלֵּל עֲלֵיהֶן, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״טוֹב כִּי תִהְיֶה לָנוּ מֵעִיר לַעֲזוֹר״ (שמואל ב יח:ג); וְאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ (סנהדרין מט.): אִילְמָלֵא דָוִד, לֹא עָשָׂה יוֹאָב מִלְחָמָה:


**May the Lord answer you on a day of distress** This psalm was [composed] because he [David] would send Joab and all Israel to war, and he would stand in Jerusalem and pray for them, as the matter is stated (in II Sam. 18:3): “It is better that you be for us from the city as aid.” Were it not for David, Joab would not have succeeded in battle.


###### Rashi on Psalms 20:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/20:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/20:2:2)


**שֵׁם אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב.** שֶׁהִבְטִיחוֹ בְּלֶכְתּוֹ לְחָרָן (בראשית כח:יג-טו), וְשָׁמַר הַבְטָחָתוֹ. לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר: אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב:


**the name of the God of Jacob** Who promised him [Jacob] when he went to Haran and kept His promise; therefore, it is stated: “the God of Jacob.”

### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 20:4:1

**מִנְחוֹתֶיךָ וְעוֹלָתְךָ.** הֵם הַתְּפִלּוֹת שֶׁאַתֶּם מִתְפַּלְּלִים בַּמִּלְחָמָה:


**your meal offerings...burnt offerings** They are the prayers that you pray in battle.


###### Rashi on Psalms 20:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/20:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/20:4:2)


**יְדַשְּׁנֶהָ סֶלָה.** לְשׁוֹן שׁוּמָן, כְּמוֹ (דברים לא:כ) ״וְאָכַל וְשָׂבַע וְדָשֵׁן״, כְּלוֹמַר: יְקַבְּלֵם בְּרָצוֹן כְּעוֹלוֹת מְחִים:


**fat** Heb. ידשנה, an expression of fat, as (in Deut. 31:20): “and it will eat and be satisfied, and it will become obese (ודשן),” i.e., He will accept them [the prayers] willingly like fat burnt offering.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 20:6:1

**נְרַנְּנָה בִּישׁוּעָתֶךָ.** כְּשֶׁיּוֹשִׁיעַ אוֹתְךָ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, נְרַנְּנָה כֻּלָּנוּ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:


**Let us sing praises for your salvation** When the Holy One, blessed be He, saves you, we will all sing praises to the Holy One, blessed be He.

### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 20:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/20:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/20:7:1)


**עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי.** זוֹ הִיא הָרְנָנָה שֶׁנְּרַנֵּן עַתָּה בַּתְּשׁוּעָה זוֹ שֶׁבָּאָה לְיוֹאָב וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל, יָדַעְתִּי שֶׁחָפֵץ הַמָּקוֹם בִּי וְעָנָנִי **מִשְּׁמֵי קָדְשׁוֹ**, כִּי תְּשׁוּעָתָם הִיא תְּשׁוּעָתִי:


**Now I know** This is the praise that we will sing now for this salvation that came to Joab and to Israel: I know that the Omnipresent desired me and has answered me from His holy heavens, for their salvation is my salvation.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 20:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/20:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/20:8:1)


**אֵלֶּה בָרֶכֶב.** יֵשׁ מִן הָאֻמּוֹת שֶׁבּוֹטְחִים בְּרֶכֶב בַּרְזֶל שֶׁלָּהֶם וְיֵשׁ שֶׁבּוֹטְחִים בְּסוּסֵיהֶם, אֲבָל **אֲנַחְנוּ בְּשֵׁם ה׳ נַזְכִּיר** כִּי לוֹ הַיְשׁוּעָה. **נַזְכִּיר** לְשׁוֹן הַקְטָרָה וּתְפִלָּה, כְּמוֹ (ישעיהו סו:ג) ״מַזְכִּיר לְבוֹנָה״ (ויקרא ב:ב) ״אֶת אַזְכָּרָתָהּ״. וּלְפִיכָךְ הֵמָּה יִכְרְעוּ וְיִפֹּלוּ:


**These trust in chariots** Some nations trust in their iron chariots, and some trust in horses, but we pray in the name of the Lord, because the salvation is His. נזכיר is an expression of burning sacrifices and of prayer, as (in Isa. 66:3): “he who burns (מזכיר) frankincense,” (and in Lev. 2:2): “its memorial part (אזכרתה).” Therefore, they kneel and fall...



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 20:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/20:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/20:9:1)


**וַאֲנַחְנוּ קַּמְנוּ וַנִּתְעוֹדָד.** נִתְגַּבֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם, כְּמוֹ ״מְעוֹדֵד עֲנָוִים״ (תהלים קמז:ו), לְשׁוֹן עֹז:


**but we rise and gain strength** We gain strength over them, as (below 147:6): “strengthens (מעודד) the humble,” an expression of strength.



## Chapter 21


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 21:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:2:1)


**בְּעָזְּךָ יִשְׂמַח מֶלֶךְ.** רַבּוֹתֵינוּ פָּתְרוּהוּ עַל מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ, וְנָכוֹן הַדָּבָר לְפוֹתְרוֹ עוֹד עַל דָּוִד עַצְמוֹ, לִתְשׁוּבַת אֲחֵרִים שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ בוֹ שֶׁאַחַר שֶׁלָּקַח אֶת בַּת שֶׁבַע אָמַר מִזְמוֹר זֶה:


**may the king rejoice with Your strength** Our Rabbis (Mid. Ps. 21:1) interpreted it as referring to the King Messiah, but the matter may correctly be interpreted further as referring to David himself, in order to refute the sectarians, who became bold because of it.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 21:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:3:1)


**וַאֲרֶשֶׁת.** לְשׁוֹן דִּבּוּר, וְאֵין לוֹ דִּמְיוֹן. וּמְנַחֵם הֵבִיא לוֹ חָבֵר: ״כְּרִשְׁיוֹן כּוֹרֶשׁ מֶלֶךְ פָּרַס״ (עזרא ג:ז), וּשְׁנֵיהֶם לְשׁוֹן מִבְטָא שְׂפָתַיִם:


**and the speech of** Heb. וארשת, an expression of speech, which has no similar word. Menachem (p. 167), however, brought a [word] similar to it (Ezra 3:7): “by the authorization (כרשיון) of Cyrus, king of Persia.”



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 21:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:4:1)


**כִּי תְקַדְּמֶנּוּ בִּרְכוֹת טוֹב.** קֹדֶם שֶׁשָּׁאַלְתִּי מִמְּךָ, הִקְדַּמְתָּ לִי בִּרְכָתְךָ עַל יְדֵי נָתָן הַנָּבִיא ״וְהַקִימוֹתִי אֶת זַרְעֲךָ וְגוֹמֵר״ (שמואל ב ז:יב), ״וַהֲכִינֹתִי אֶת כִּסֵּא מַמְלַכְתְּךָ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעוֹלָם״ (שמואל ב ז:יג):


**For You have preceded him with the blessings of the good man** Before I asked You, You preceded me with Your blessing through Nathan the prophet (in II Sam. 7:12f.): “then I will raise up your seed...and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 21:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:4:2)


**תָּשִׁית לְרֹאשׁוֹ עֲטֶרֶת פָּז.** ״וַיִּקַּח עֲטֶרֶת מַלְכָּם וַתְּהִי עַל רֹאשׁ דָּוִד״ (שמואל ב יב:ל):


**You have placed a gold crown on his head** (As in II Sam. 12:30): “And he took the crown of Malkam...and it was [set] upon David’s head.”



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 21:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:5:1)


**חַיִּים שָׁאַל מִמְּךָ.** כְּשֶׁהָיִיתִי בּוֹרֵחַ לְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ מִפְּנֵי שָׁאוּל, הָיִיתִי מִתְפַּלֵּל: ״אֶתְהַלֵּךְ לִפְנֵי ה׳ בְּאַרְצוֹת הַחַיִּים״ (תהלים קטז:ט):


**He asked You for life** As I fled outside the Holy Land from before Saul, I would pray, “May I walk before the Lord in the lands of the living” (below 116:9).


###### Rashi on Psalms 21:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:5:2)


**נָתַתָּה לוֹ.** שֶׁהֲשִׁיבוֹתַנִי לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל:


**You gave it to him** For You restored me to the land of Israel.


###### Rashi on Psalms 21:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:5:3)


**אֹרֶךְ יָמִים.** לְמַלְכוּתִי, שֶׁאָמַרְתָּ: ״וַהֲכִינֹתִי אֶת־כִּסֵּא מַמְלַכְתְּךָ עַד־עוֹלָם״ (שמואל ב ז:יג):


**length of days** to his kingdom, for You said, “and I will establish the throne of your (sic) kingdom forever” (II Sam. 7:13).



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 21:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:6:1)


**תְּשַׁוֶּה.** מְנַחֵם פָּתַר תְּשַׁוֶּה, ״תָּשִׂים״ (בראשית ו:טז), ״תָּשִׁית״ (תהלים כא:ד), לָשׁוֹן אֶחָד לָהֶם:


**You place** Heb. תשוה Menachem (p. 171) interpreted: תשוה, תשים, and תשית have the same meaning.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 21:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:7:1)


**תְּחַדֵּהוּ.** לְשׁוֹן חֶדְוָה:


**You shall make him happy** Heb. תחדהו, an expression of חדוה, joy.


###### Rashi on Psalms 21:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:7:2)


**אֶת פָּנֶיךָ.** בְּגַן עֵדֶן. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ, שֶׁדְּרָשׁוּהוּ בְּמֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ, הֵבִיאוּ רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר: ״וְעַד עַתִּיק יוֹמַיָּא מְטָה וּקְדָמוֹהִי הַקְרְבוּהִי״ (דניאל ז:יג); וְאוֹמֵר ״וְהִקְרַבְתִּיו וְנִגַּשׁ אֵלָי״ (ירמיה ל:כא):


**before You** in Paradise. Our Rabbis, who interpreted it as referring to the King Messiah, brought proof on that matter (from Dan. 7: 13): “and came to the Ancient of days and brought him near before Him.” Scripture also states (in Jer. 30:21): “and I will bring him near, and he shall approach Me.”



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 21:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:8:1)


**בַּל יִמּוֹט.** וּבְחֶסֶד עֶלְיוֹן הוּא בּוֹטֵחַ שֶׁלֹּא יִמּוֹט:


**that he should not falter** And he trusts in the loving-kindness of the Most High that he should not falter.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 21:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:9:1)


**תִּמְצָא יָדְךָ לְכָל אוֹיְבֶיךָ.** כָּל מַכַּת יָדְךָ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְךָ לְהָבִיא, הָבֵא עַל אוֹיְבֶיךָ:


**Your hand shall suffice for all Your enemies** All the smiting of Your hand that You have to bring, bring upon Your enemies.

###### Rashi on Psalms 21:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:10:1)


**לְעֵת פָּנֶיךָ.** לְעֵת זַעְמְךָ:


**at the time of Your anger** Heb. פניך, at the time of Your fury.


###### Rashi on Psalms 21:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:10:2)


**בְּאַפּוֹ יְבַלְּעֵם.** תְּפִלָּה הִיא זוֹ:


**destroy them with His wrath** This is a prayer.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 21:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:11:1)


**פִּרְיָמוֹ מֵאֶרֶץ תְּאַבֵּד.** לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הוּא מִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁיְּאַבֵּד זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק הָרָשָׁע:


**You shall destroy their fruit from the earth** He prays to the Holy One, blessed be He, that He destroy the descendants of the wicked Esau.



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Psalms 21:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:12:1)


**כִּי נָטוּ עָלֶיךָ רָעָה.** כְּנֶגֶד טִיטוּס הָרָשָׁע, שֶׁאָמַר: הָרַג אֶת עַצְמוֹ! (גיטין נו:):


**For they have directed evil against You** [This was said] regarding the wicked Titus, who said that he had killed Him.


###### Rashi on Psalms 21:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:12:2)


**בַּל יוּכְלוּ.** לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ:


**that they cannot** execute.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Psalms 21:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:13:1)


**כִּי תְשִׁיתֵמוֹ שֶׁכֶם.** אֲשֶׁר תָּשִׁית אוֹתָם לְחֵלֶק, שֶׁיְּחַלְּקוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת מָמוֹנָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ישעיהו כג:יח) ״וְהָיָה סַחְרָהּ וְאֶתְנַנָּהּ וְגוֹמֵר״:


**For You shall place them as a portion** For You shall place them as a portion, that Israel will divide their money, as it is stated (in Isa. 23:18): “And her commerce and her hire shall be...”


###### Rashi on Psalms 21:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/21:13:2)


**בְּמֵיתָרֶיךָ תְּכוֹנֵן עַל פְּנֵיהֶם.** בְּמֵיתְרֵי קַשְּׁתוֹתֶיךָ תְּכוֹנֵן חִצֶּיךָ וְתַזְמִינֵם לִירוֹת עַל פְּנֵיהֶם:


**with Your bowstrings You shall set toward their faces** With the strings of Your bows, You shall aim Your arrows at their faces.
