**רַגְלִי עָמְדָה בְמִישׁוֹר.** בְּדֶרֶךְ יְשָׁרָה:


**My foot stood on a straight path** Heb. במישור, on a straight path.



## Chapter 27


### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 27:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:3:1)


**בְּזֹאת אֲנִי בוֹטֵחַ.** בְּמַה שֶׁאָמַר לְמַעְלָה **ה׳ מָעוֹז חַיַּי**:


**in this I trust** In what is stated above: “The Lord is the stronghold of my life.”



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 27:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:4:1)


**וּלְבַקֵּר בְּהֵיכָלוֹ.** לֵירָאוֹת שָׁם בְּכָל בֹּקֶר וָבֹקֶר. כָּךְ פֵּרְשׁוֹ דּוֹנָשׁ, וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ עִם ״לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין טוֹב לָרָע״ (ויקרא כז:לג), אֲבָל דּוֹנָשׁ פָּתַר לְשׁוֹן בֹּקֶר:


**and to visit His Temple every morning** To appear there every morning. Dunash (Teshuvoth Dunash, p. 53) explained in this manner. Menachem (Machbereth Menachem, p. 47) however associated it with (Lev. 27:33), “He shall not inquire (יבקר),” but Dunash interpreted it as an expression of “morning” (בקר).



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 27:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:5:1)


**כִּי יִצְפְּנֵנִי בְּסֻכֹּה.** בָּטוּחַ אֲנִי שֶׁיִּצְפְּנֵנִי בְּבֵית מִקְדָּשׁוֹ, וְשָׁנִינוּ בְּסֵדֶר עוֹלָם (סדר עולם רבה יח) שֶׁהַמִּקְרָא הַזֶּה נֶאֱמַר עַל יוֹאָשׁ בֶּן אֲחַזְיָה שֶׁהִסְתִּירָתוֹ יְהוֹשֶׁבַע אֲחוֹתוֹ בַּעֲלִיַּת בֵּית קָדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיְהִי אִתָּהּ בֵּית ה׳ מִתְחַבֵּא שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים״ (מלכים ב יא:ג):


**That He will hide me in His tabernacle** I am confident that He will hide me in His Temple, and we learned in Seder Olam (ch. 18) that this verse was stated concerning Joash the son of Ahaziah, who was hidden by his sister, Jehosheba, in the attic of the Holy of Holies, as the matter is stated (in II Kings 11:3): “And he was hiding with her in the house of the Lord for six years.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 27:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:5:2)


**בְּצוּר יְרוֹמְמֵנִי.** הֶעֱמִיד עַל סֶלַע רַגְלִי (תהלים מ:ג):


**He will lift me up on a rock** He stood my feet on a rock.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 27:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:6:1)


**זִבְחֵי תְרוּעָה.** זְבָחִים שֶׁאוֹמֵר עֲלֵיהֶם שִׁיר:


**sacrifices with joyous song** Sacrifices over which a song is recited.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 27:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:8:1)


**לְךָ אָמַר לִבִּי בַּקְּשׁוּ פָנָי.** בִּשְׁבִילְךָ, בִּשְׁלִיחוּתֶיךָ אוֹמֵר (לִי) לִבִּי: בַּקְּשׁוּ כֻּלְּכֶם, יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֶת פָּנַי; וַאֲנִי שׁוֹמֵעַ לוֹ, **אֶת פָּנֶיךָ ה׳ אֲבַקֵּשׁ**:


**On Your behalf, my heart says, “Seek My presence.”** On Your behalf, as Your agent, my heart says to me, “All of you Israelites, seek My presence.” And I obey it. “Your presence, O Lord, I will seek.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 27:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:8:2)


**לְךָ.** כְּמוֹ ״הֵן אֲנִי כְפִיךָ לָאֵל״ (איוב לג:ו) – בִּמְקוֹמוֹ, ״אִם לָאֵל תְּרִיבוּן״ (איוב יג:ח) – בִּמְקוֹמוֹ, אַף כָּאן **לְךָ אָמַר לִבִּי.** בִּמְקוֹמְךָ בָּא אֵלַי לִבִּי לוֹמַר כֵּן:


[The word] לך is like (Job 33:6): “Behold I am like your mouth to God (לא-ל),” [that is,] in His stead; (ibid. 13:8), “Will you contend for God (לא-ל)?” [that is,] in His stead. Here, too, “On Your behalf, my heart says,” in Your stead, my heart comes to me to say this.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 27:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:9:1)


**אַל תַּט.** אַל תַּכְרִיעַ, כְּמוֹ ״וַיֵּט שָׁמַיִם״ (תהלים יח:י):


**do not turn...away** Heb. תט, do not bend over, as (above 18:10): “And He bent (ויט) the heavens.”



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 27:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:10:1)


**כִּי אָבִי וְאִמִּי עֲזָבוּנִי.** בִּשְׁעַת תַּשְׁמִישׁ לַהֲנָאָתָן נִתְכַּוְּנוּ; כֵּיוָן שֶׁגָּמְרוּ הֲנָאָתָן, זֶה הוֹפֵךְ פָּנָיו אֵילָךְ וְזֶה הוֹפֵךְ פָּנָיו אֵילָךְ:


**For my father and my mother have forsaken me** At the time of coitus, they intended their own pleasure. As soon as their pleasure is over, this one turns his face this way and that one turns her face the other way.


###### Rashi on Psalms 27:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:10:2)


**וַה׳ יַאַסְפֵנִי.** הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹמֵר אֶת הַטִּפָּה וְצָר אֶת הָעֻבָּר (ויקרא רבה יד, ה):


**but the Lord gathers me in** The Holy One, blessed be He, guards the droplet and forms the fetus.



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Psalms 27:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:12:1)


**בְּנֶפֶשׁ צָרָי.** בְּתַאֲוַת שׂוֹנְאַי, לִהְיוֹת תַּאֲוָתָם מִתְקַיֶּמֶת עָלַי:


**to the desires of my adversaries** To the desire of my enemies, to have their desire fulfilled through me.


###### Rashi on Psalms 27:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:12:2)


**וְיָפֵחַ חָמָס.** דּוֹבְרֵי רָעָה. לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: לְשׁוֹן מוֹקֵשׁ (ס״א אינו):


**and speakers of evil** Heb. ויפח חמס, speakers of evil. Another explanation: An expression of a trap (פח).



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Psalms 27:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:13:1)


**לוּלֵא הֶאֱמַנְתִּי וְגוֹ׳.** אִם לֹא שֶׁהֶאֱמַנְתִּי בְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, כְּבָר **קָמוּ בִי** אוֹתָם **עֵדֵי שֶׁקֶר** וְכִלּוּנִי. **לוּלֵא** נָקוּד עָלָיו, לְמִדְרָשׁ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ (ברכות ד.): יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי שֶׁאַתָּה נוֹתֵן שָׂכָר לַצַּדִּיקִים לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, אֲבָל אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם יֵשׁ לִי חֵלֶק עִמָּהֶם אִם לָאו:


**Had I not believed in seeing, etc.** If I had not believed in the Holy One, blessed be He, those false witnesses would have already risen against me and destroyed me. [The word] לולא is punctuated for the homily which our Sages expounded (Ber. 4a): I know that You give reward to the righteous in the world to come, but I do not know whether I have a share with them or not.



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Psalms 27:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/27:14:1)


**וְקַוֵּה אֶל ה׳.** וְאִם לֹא תִתְקַבֵּל תְּפִלָּתְךָ, חֲזוֹר וְקַוֵּה (ברכות לב:):


**Hope for the Lord** and if your prayer is not accepted, reinforce your hope.



## Chapter 28


### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 28:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/28:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/28:3:1)


**אַל תִּמְשְׁכֵנִי.** אַל תַּרְגִּילֵנִי עִם רְשָׁעִים. אטרירא״ש מו״י בְּלַעַ״ז:


**Do not cause me to be drawn** Heb. תמשכני, do not draw me with the wicked; treras moy in Old French.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 28:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/28:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/28:7:1)


**וּמִשִּׁירִי אֲהוֹדֶנּוּ.** וּמַה הִיא הַהוֹדָיָה? **ה׳ עֹז לָמוֹ** לְאוֹתָן הַתְּלוּיִין בּוֹ בְּעֵת שֶׁ**מָּעוֹז יְשׁוּעוֹת מְשִׁיחוֹ הוּא**:


**and I will thank Him with my song** Now what is the thanks?...**The Lord is strength to them** to those who rely on Him, viz. the entire house of Israel, at the time that He is the stronghold of the salvations of His anointed.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 28:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/28:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/28:9:1)


**וּרְעֵם.** לְשׁוֹן מִרְעֶה:


**and tend them** Heb. ורעם, an expression of pasture (מרעה).



## Chapter 29


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 29:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:1:1)


**הָבוּ לַה׳.** הָכִינוּ לַה׳ וְהָכִינוּ לוֹ, אַתֶּם, בְּנֵי אֵילֵי הָאָרֶץ; מִכָּאן שֶׁאוֹמְרִים ׳אָבוֹת׳ (ראש השנה לב.). וּמְנַחֵם חִבֵּר הָבוּ לְשׁוֹן נְתִינָה:


**Prepare for the Lord** Heb. הבו. Prepare for the Lord and prepare for Him, you sons of the mighty of the land. From here we derive the ruling that [for the first blessing of the Amidah prayer] we should say the blessing אבות, the Patriarchs (Meg. 17b, R.H. 32b, Mid. Ps. 29:2). But Menachem (p. 68) associated הבו as an expression of giving.


###### Rashi on Psalms 29:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:1:2)


**אֵלִים.** שָׂרִים (ס״א אינו):


**mighty** Heb. אלים, princes.


###### Rashi on Psalms 29:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:1:3)


**הָבוּ לַה׳ כָּבוֹד וָעֹז.** מִכָּאן שֶׁאוֹמְרִים גְּבוּרוֹת (ראש השנה לב.):


**prepare for the Lord glory and might** From here we derive that [for the second blessing of the Amidah prayer] we should say the blessing of גבורות, mighty deeds.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 29:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:2:1)


**כְּבוֹד שְׁמוֹ.** זוֹ קְדֻשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם (ראש השנה לב.), וְיֵשׁ בְּמִזְמוֹר זֶה שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה אַזְכָּרוֹת, וּכְנֶגְדָּן תִּקְּנוּ שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה בְּרָכוֹת:


**the glory due His name** This is the blessing of the sanctity of the Name [the third blessing of the Amidah]. In this psalm, there are eighteen mentions of God’s name, and corresponding to them, they instituted eighteen blessings.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 29:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:3:1)


**קוֹל ה׳ עַל הַמָּיִם.** עַל יַם סוּף יַרְעֵם מִשָּׁמַיִם ה׳ וְגוֹ׳ (תהלים יח:יד):


**The voice of the Lord is upon the waters** Upon the Sea of Reeds, “The Lord thundered from heaven” (above 18:14).


###### Rashi on Psalms 29:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:3:2)


**הִרְעִים.** טוֹרְמִינְטָאוּ״שׁ בְּלַעַ״ז:


**thunders** Heb. הרעים, tormanta in Old French.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 29:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:4:1)


**קוֹל ה׳ בַּכֹּחַ.** בְּשָׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה צִמְצֵם אֶת קוֹלוֹ לְפִי כֹּחָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְהָאֱלֹהִים יַעֲנֶנּוּ בְקוֹל״ (שמות יט:יט) – בְּקוֹלוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה (ברכות מה.):


**The voice of the Lord is in strength** At the time of the giving of the Torah, He moderated His voice according to the strength of Israel, as it is said (Exod. 19:19): “and God would answer him with a voice,” with Moses’ voice.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 29:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:5:1)


**קוֹל ה׳ שׁוֹבֵר אֲרָזִים.** הָאֻמּוֹת, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמואל א ז:י) ״וַיַּרְעֵם ה׳ בְּקוֹל גָּדוֹל עַל פְּלִשְׁתִּים וְגוֹ׳״, (ישעיהו ל:לא) ״כִּי מִקּוֹל ה׳ יֵחַת אַשּׁוּר״. וּבִשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה (דברים ה:כג) ״כִּי מִי כָל בָּשָׂר וְגוֹמֵר וַיֶּחִי״ – אַתָּה שָׁמַעְתָּ וְחָיִיתָ, וְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שׁוֹמְעִים וּמֵתִים (תנחומא, שמות כה):


**The voice of the Lord breaks the cedars** The kings of the nations, as the matter that is written (in I Sam. 7:10): “and the Lord thundered with a loud noise etc. upon the Philistines”; (in Isa. 30:31): “For from the Lord’s voice Assyria shall be broken.” And at the time of the giving of the Torah (Deut. 5: 23): “For who is there of all flesh who has heard the voice of the living God speak out of the fire as we have and remained alive?” You heard and remained alive, but the nations of the world would hear it and die.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 29:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:6:1)


**וַיַּרְקִידֵם כְּמוֹ עֵגֶל.** אֶת הָאֲרָזִים וְאֶת הֶהָרִים שֶׁבָּאוּ לִשְׁמֹעַ מַתַּן תּוֹרָה (שמות יט:יז):


**He causes them to dance like a calf** The cedars and the mountains that came to hear the giving of the Torah.


###### Rashi on Psalms 29:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:6:2)


**לְבָנוֹן וְשִׂרְיוֹן.** שֵׁמוֹת הֶהָרִים:


**Lebanon and Sirion** The names of mountains.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 29:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:7:1)


**חוֹצֵב לַהֲבוֹת אֵשׁ.** טַיְלַנְ״ט בְּלַעַ״ז, וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ פֵּרְשׁוּ (מכילתא יתרו בחדש ט), שֶׁהָיָה הַדִּבּוּר שֶׁל עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת יוֹצֵא בְּלַהֲבוֹת אֵשׁ מִפִּיו וְנֶחְקָק עַל הַלּוּחוֹת כְּתַבְנִיתָם:


**cleaves with flames of fire** taylont in Old French, to cut. Our Sages (Mechilta ibid.) explained that the utterance of the Decalogue emanated from His mouth with a flame of fire and was engraved on the tablets according to their form.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 29:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:8:1)


**יָחִיל מִדְבָּר.** לְשׁוֹן ״חִיל כַּיּוֹלֵדָה״ (ירמיה ו:כד; תהלים מח:ז):


**causes the desert to quake** Heb. יחיל, an expression of (Jer. 6:24), “pain (חיל) as a woman in travail.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 29:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:8:2)


**יָחִיל ה׳ מִדְבַּר קָדֵשׁ.** הוּא מִדְבַּר סִינַי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ בְּמַסֶּכֶת שַׁבָּת (שבת פט.): חֲמִשָּׁה שֵׁמוֹת נִקְרְאוּ לוֹ: מִדְבַּר סִינַי, מִדְבַּר צִין, מִדְבַּר קָדֵשׁ, מִדְבַּר קַדְמוֹת, מִדְבַּר פָּארָן. **מִדְבַּר קָדֵשׁ** שֶׁנִּתְקַדְּשׁוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עָלָיו:


**the Lord causes the desert of Kadesh to quake** That is the desert of Sinai, as our Sages said in Tractate Shabbath (89a): It was called by five names: the desert of Sinai, the desert of Zin, the desert of Kadesh, the desert of Kedemoth, the desert of Paran. [It was called] the desert of Kadesh because Israel was sanctified on its account.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 29:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:9:1)


**קוֹל ה׳ יְחוֹלֵל אַיָּלוֹת.** יְפַחִיד וְיָחִיל לֶעָתִיד אֶת הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת, שֶׁהֵם עַכְשָׁיו עוֹמְדִים בְּחוֹזֶק כְּאַיָּלוֹת, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״מְשַׁוֶּה רַגְלַי כָּאַיָּלוֹת״ (תהלים יח:לד). אָמַר רַבִּי פִּנְחָס: כָּאֵילִים אֵין כְּתִיב כָּאן אֶלָּא כָּאַיָּלוֹת, כַּנְּקֵבוֹת שֶׁרַגְלֵי הַנְּקֵבוֹת עוֹמְדוֹת בְּיוֹשֶׁר יוֹתֵר מִן הַזְּכָרִים. לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: יְחוֹלֵל קְרִיאָ״ה בְּלַעַ״ז, כְּמוֹ ״לִפְנֵי גְבָעוֹת חוֹלָלְתִּי״ (משלי ח:כה) (ס״א אינו):


**The voice of the Lord will frighten the hinds** In the future, it will frighten the nations of the world and cause [them] to quake, those who are now standing firmly like hinds, as the matter that is stated (above 18:34): “He makes my feet like hinds.” Said Rabbi Phinehas: It does not say, “like harts,” but “like hinds,” like the females, because the feet of the females stand straighter than those of the males (Mid. Ps. 22:1). Another explanation: יחולל is kria in Old French, to create, as (in Prov. 8: 25), “before the hills, I was created (חוללתי).”


###### Rashi on Psalms 29:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:9:2)


**וַיֶּחֱשֹׂף יְעָרוֹת.** כְּמוֹ ״מַחְשֹׂף הַלָּבָן״ (בראשית ל:לז), יְקַלֵּף עֲצֵי הַיַּעַר, כְּלוֹמַר יַפְשִׁיט מִכְּבוֹדָם הַמְּשׁוּלִים כַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר ״אֲשֶׁר כְּגֹבַהּ אֲרָזִים גָּבְהוֹ״ (עמוס ב:ט):


**and strip the forests** Like (Gen. 30:37), “by uncovering (מחשף) the white.” He will strip the forest trees, i.e., he will strip the nations, compared to forest trees, of their glory, as is stated (in Amos 2:9): “whose height is as the height of the cedar trees.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 29:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:9:3)


**וּבְהֵיכָלוֹ.** שֶׁיִּבָּנֶה:


**and in His Temple** which will be built.


###### Rashi on Psalms 29:9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:9:4)


**כֻּלּוֹ אוֹמֵר כָּבוֹד.** הַכֹּל יְקַלְּסוּהוּ שָׁם וְיֹאמְרוּ:


**everyone speaks of His glory** Everyone will praise Him there and say...



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 29:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/29:10:1)


**ה׳ לַמַּבּוּל יָשָׁב.** בִּגְדֻלָּתוֹ יְחִידִי, וְגַם עַתָּה **וַיֵּשֶׁב ה׳ לְבַדּוֹ מֶלֶךְ לְעוֹלָם**, ״וְהָאֱלִילִים כָּלִיל יַחֲלֹף״ (ישעיה ב:יח), אֲבָל לְעַמּוֹ יִתֵּן עֹז וּבִרְכַּת שָׁלוֹם. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דְּרָשׁוּהוּ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה (מדרש תהלים כט:ב) שֶׁנִּתְפַּחֲדוּ וְנִתְבַּהֲלוּ הָאֻמּוֹת וּבָאוּ לָהֶם אֵצֶל בִּלְעָם וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ: מַה קּוֹל הֶהָמוֹן שֶׁשָּׁמַעְנוּ? שֶׁמָּא מַבּוּל הוּא בָּא לְהָבִיא לָעוֹלָם? אָמַר לָהֶם: כְּבָר נִשְׁבַּע שֶׁלֹּא יָבִיא מַבּוּל, אֶלָּא קוֹל הֶהָמוֹן שֶׁשְּׁמַעְתֶּם, הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נוֹתֵן תּוֹרָה לְעַמּוֹ:


**The Lord sat [enthroned] at the flood** alone in His greatness, and now also, the Lord sits alone forever, “but the idols will completely pass away,” (as in Isa. 2:18), yet to His people He will give strength and a blessing of peace. Our Sages, however, expounded upon it in Midrash Psalms (29:2) that the nations became frightened and startled, and they came to Balaam and said to him, “What is the sound of the stirring that we heard? Is He going to bring a flood upon the world?” He replied to them, “He already swore that He would not bring a flood. Rather, the sound of the stirring that you heard is that the Holy One, blessed be He, is giving a Torah to His people.”



## Chapter 30


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 30:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:1:1)


**שִׁיר חֲנֻכַּת הַבַּיִת.** שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּהוּ הַלְוִיִּם בַּחֲנֻכַּת הַבַּיִת בִּימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה:


**A song of dedication of the House** which the Levites will say at the dedication of the House in the days of Solomon.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 30:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:2:1)


**אֲרוֹמִמְךָ ה׳ כִּי דִלִּיתָנִי.** הִגְבַּהְתָּנִי:


**I will exalt You, O Lord, for You have raised me up** Heb. דליתני, You have lifted me on high.


###### Rashi on Psalms 30:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:2:2)


**וְלֹא שִׂמַּחְתָּ אוֹיְבַי לִי.** כְּמוֹ עָלַי, שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים: אֵין לְדָוִד חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, וּכְשֶׁרָאוּ שֶׁבִּשְׁבִילוֹ נִפְתְּחוּ הַדְּלָתוֹת לָאָרוֹן, אָז יָדְעוּ שֶׁמָּחַל לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל אוֹתוֹ עָוֹן, וְנֶהֶפְכוּ פְּנֵי שׂוֹנְאֵי דָוִד כְּשׁוּלֵי קְדֵרָה (שבת ל.):


**and You have not allowed my enemies to rejoice over me** Heb. לי, like עלי, over me, for they would say, “David has no share in the world to come,” but when they saw that the doors opened for the Ark because of me, then they knew that the Holy One, blessed be He, had forgiven me for that sin, and the faces of David’s enemies became as black as the bottom of a pot.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 30:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:3:1)


**וַתִּרְפָּאֵנִי.** הִיא סְלִיחַת עָוֹן, כְּמוֹ ״וְשָׁב וְרָפָא לוֹ״ (ישעיהו ו:י):


**and You have healed me** That is the forgiving of iniquity, as (in Isa. 6:10), “and he repent and be healed.”



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 30:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:4:1)


**מִיָּרְדֵי בוֹר.** כְּמוֹ מִירִידָתִי לַבּוֹר, שֶׁלֹּא אֵרֵד לַגֵּיהִנֹּם:


**from my descent into the Pit, etc.** Heb. מירדי, like מִיְרִדָתִי, from my descent into the Pit, that I should not descend into Gehinnom.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 30:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:5:1)


**זַמְּרוּ לַה׳ חֲסִידָיו.** עַל מָה שֶׁעָשָׂה לִי, כִּי יְכוֹלִים אַתֶּם לַחֲסוֹת בּוֹ שֶׁיֵּיטִיב לָכֶם; וַאֲפִלּוּ אַתֶּם שְׁרוּיִים בְּצַעַר, אַל תִּירָאוּ:


**Sing to the Lord, His pious ones** about what He did for me, because you can take refuge in Him, and He will benefit you; and even if you are experiencing pain, have no fear.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 30:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:6:1)


**כִּי רֶגַע.** קָטָן **בְּאַפּוֹ**:


**For...but a moment** [For] His wrath lasts but a short [moment];


###### Rashi on Psalms 30:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:6:2)


**חַיִּים בִּרְצוֹנוֹ.** וְחַיִּים אֲרֻכִּים יֵשׁ בְּהֵרָצוֹתוֹ וּבְהִפָּיְסוֹ (ברכות ז.):


**life results from His favor**, there is long life in appeasing and placating Him.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 30:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:7:1)


**וַאֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי בְשַׁלְוִי.** בְּשַׁלְוָתִי הָיִיתִי חוֹשֵׁב לֹא **אֶמּוֹט לְעוֹלָם**, אֲבָל אֵין הַדָּבָר בִּרְשׁוּתִי כִּי אִם בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: בִּרְצוֹנוֹ הֶעֱמִיד אֶת **הֲרָרִי**, אֶת גְּדֻלָּתִי, לִהְיוֹת **עֹז**, וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהִסְתִּיר פָּנָיו מִמֶּנִּי, מִיָּד **הָיִיתִי נִבְהָל**:


**And I said in my tranquility** In my tranquility, I thought that I would never falter. However, the matter is not in my power, but in the power of the Holy One, blessed be He. With His will, He set up my mountain, my greatness to be [my] mightbut when He hid His countenance from me, I was immediately frightened.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 30:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:9:1)


**אֵלֶיךָ ה׳ אֶקְרָא וְגוֹ׳ וְאֶתְחַנָּן.** תָּמִיד לֵאמֹר לְפָנֶיךָ: **מַה בֶּצַע בְּדָמִי וְגוֹ׳**, וְאַתָּה שָׁמַעְתָּ קוֹלִי וְ**הָפַכְתָּ מִסְפְּדִי לְמָחוֹל לִי**:


**To You, O Lord, I would call** I would call to You and supplicate constantly, saying before You: “What gain is there in my blood, etc.,” and You heard my voice and turned my lament into dancing for me.



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Psalms 30:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:12:1)


**פִּתַּחְתָּ.** אֵלַאקְ״שׁ בְּלַעַ״ז, כְּמוֹ (בראשית כד:לב) ״וַיְפַתַּח אֶת הַגְּמַלִּים״, וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָּרְשׁוּ כָּל הַמִּזְמוֹר עַל מָרְדְּכַי וְאֶסְתֵּר וְהָמָן, בִּפְסִיקְתָּא זוּטָא (פסיקתא זוטרתא):


**You loosened** Heb. פתחת, alachas in Old French, to release, like (Gen. 24:32): “and he untied (ויפתח) the camels.” Our Sages, however, explained the entire psalm as referring to Mordecai, Esther, and Haman, in Pesikta Zuta.


###### Rashi on Psalms 30:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/30:12:2)


**וַאֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי בְשַׁלְוִי**, אָמַר הָמָן. **אֵלֶיךָ ה׳ אֶקְרָא**, אָמְרָה אֶסְתֵּר וְכוּ׳ עַד הָיָה עוֹזֵר לִי. **הָפַכְתָּ מִסְפְּדִי לְמָחוֹל לִי**, אָמַר מָרְדֳּכַי וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל:


**and I said in my tranquility** Haman said this. **To You, O Lord, I would call** Esther said this etc. until “be my helper.” **You turned my lament into dancing for me** Mordecai and all Israel said this.



## Chapter 31


### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:3:1)


**מְצוּדוֹת.** פְּלֵיְישִׁי״ץ בְּלַעַ״ז:


**a stronghold** Pleysiz in Old French, a fortress.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:4:1)


**תְּנַחֲנִי.** מוֹנַארַאשְׁמוֹ״י בְּלַעַ״ז, כְּמוֹ ״לֵךְ נְחֵה אֶת הָעָם וְגוֹ׳״ (שמות לב:לד):


**You shall lead me** Heb. תנחני, mene moi in French, lead me, as (in Exod. 32:34): “go lead (נחה) the people.”



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:6:1)


**בְּיָדְךָ אַפְקִיד רוּחִי.** קוֹמַנְדְרִיָ״ה בְּלַעַ״ז, אַפְקִיד רוּחִי תָּמִיד לְפִי שֶׁאַתָּה **פָּדִיתָה אוֹתִי** מִצָּרָה:


**I entrust** Heb. אפקיד, komondere in Old French, I will entrust. I always entrust my spirit because You redeemed me from trouble.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:7:1)


**הַשּׁוֹמְרִים הַבְלֵי שָׁוְא.** הַמְצַפִּים לִתְשׁוּעַת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה:


**those who await worthless vanities** Who await the salvation of pagan deities.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:9:1)


**הִסְגַּרְתַּנִי.** לִיבְרַאשְׁ״מְווִי. וּמְנַחֵם חִבֵּר אוֹתוֹ לְשׁוֹן סְגִירָה, וְכֵן כָּל לְשׁוֹן סָגַר:


**deliver me** Heb. הסגרתני, livras moi in French, but Menachem (p. 125) associated it as an expression of closing, and likewise every expression of סגר.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:10:1)


**עָשְׁשָׁה.** כָּהֲתָה, לְשׁוֹן עֲשָׁשִׁית. שֶׁאָדָם נוֹתֵן זְכוּכִית לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו לִרְאוֹת לְעֵבֶר הַזְּכוּכִית דָּבָר, אֵין אוֹתָהּ מַרְאָה בְּרוּרָה:


**is dimmed** Heb. עששה, an expression of a lantern, עששית. If a person puts glass in front of his eyes to see something on the other side of the glass, the appearance (of that thing) is unclear.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:11:1)


**וַעֲצָמַי עָשֵׁשׁוּ.** לְשׁוֹן רָקָב, כְּאִלּוּ אֲכָלָם עָשׁ:


**and my bones have decayed** Heb. עששו, an expression of decay, as though a moth (עש) had eaten them.



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:12:1)


**מִכָּל צוֹרְרַי.** מֵאֵת כָּל צוֹרְרַי, **הָיִיתִי חֶרְפָּה** לְגִדּוּף:


**From all my tormentors** From all my tormentors [not because of my tormentors]. **I have become a reproach** Heb. חרפה, a reproach.


###### Rashi on Psalms 31:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:12:2)


**וְלִשְׁכֵנַי.** אֲנִי חֶרְפָּה **מְאֹד וּפַחַד לִמְיֻדָּעַי.** אֵמִישְׁקְטִיֵישְׁנ״ץ. מִתְפַּחֲדִים עַל קוֹרוֹתַי:


**to my neighbors** I am very much a reproach. **and fright to my acquaintances** A mes connaissances in French, to my acquaintances. They are frightened by what happens to me.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:13:1)


**כִּכְלִי אוֹבֵד.** הַהוֹלֵךְ לְאִבּוּד; כָּל לְשׁוֹן אֲבֵדָה, אֵין הַלָּשׁוֹן נוֹפֵל עַל בַּעַל אֲבֵדָה, לוֹמַר ׳הוּא אִבֵּד אוֹתָהּ׳, אֶלָּא ׳הָאֲבֵדָה אוֹבֶדֶת מִמֶּנּוּ׳, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר תֹּאבַד מִמֶּנּוּ״ (דברים כב:ג); ״הָאֹבֶדֶת לֹא בִקַּשְׁתֶּם״ (יחזקאל לד:ד):


**like a lost utensil** Which is in the process of becoming lost. Any expression of אבדה, loss, does not refer to the owner of the lost article, saying that he lost it, but that the lost article is lost from him, as is stated (in Deut. 22:3): “which will be lost from him”; (in Ezek. 34:4), “the lost one you did not seek.”



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:14:1)


**דִּבַּת רַבִּים.** עֲצַת רַבִּים. **דִּבַּת** לְשׁוֹן ״דּוֹבֵב שִׂפְתֵי יְשֵׁנִים״ (שיר השירים ז:י) וְכֵן כָּל דִּבָּה שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא פרלר״יץ בְּלַעַ״ז:


**the gossip of many** Heb. דבת, the counsel of many. דבת is an expression of (Song 7:10): “making the lips of the sleeping speak (דבב).” Likewise, every דבת in Scripture, parledic in Old French, gossip (so Gen. 37:2, Num. 14:36, Ezek. 36:3).


###### Rashi on Psalms 31:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:14:2)


**מָגוֹר מִסָּבִיב.** שֶׁמְּיָרְאִין וּמְפַחֲדִין אוֹתִי:


**terror from all sides** that they scare and frighten me.


###### Rashi on Psalms 31:14:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:14:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:14:3)


**בְּהִוָּסְדָם.** בְּהִתְיַעֲצָם:


**when they take counsel** Heb. בהוסדם, when they take counsel.


###### Rashi on Psalms 31:14:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:14:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:14:4)


**זָמָמוּ.** לְשׁוֹן מַחֲשָׁבָה:


**they plotted** Heb. זממו, an expression of thought.



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:16:1)


**בְּיָדְךָ עִתּוֹתָי.** עִתִּים הָעוֹבְרִים עָלַי, עַל פִּיךָ הֵם וּבִגְזֵרוֹתֶיךָ:


**My times are in Your hands** The times that pass over me are through Your orders and by Your decrees.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:18:1)


**אַל אֵבוֹשָׁה וְגוֹ׳.** אַחֲרֵי שֶׁקְּרָאתִיךָ, אֵין נָאֶה שֶׁאֵבוֹשׁ:


**let me not be shamed because I called out to You** Since I called You, it is not fitting that I should be shamed.


###### Rashi on Psalms 31:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:18:2)


**יִדְּמוּ לִשְׁאוֹל.** יִשְׁתַּתְּקוּ וְיֵאָלְמוּ לָמוּת:


**let them be silenced to the grave** Heb. ידמו, let them be silenced and made dumb to die.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:19:1)


**הַדּוֹבְרוֹת עַל צַדִּיק עָתָק.** שֶׁאוֹמְרוֹת לְשָׁאוּל עָלַי: דָּוִד מְבַקֵּשׁ רָעָתְךָ:


**that speak against a righteous man falsely** That say to Saul concerning me, “David seeks to harm you.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 31:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:19:2)


**עָתָק.** סָרָה, דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ; כְּמוֹ ״וַיַּעְתֵּק מִשָּׁם״ (בראשית יב:ח). וְדוּנָשׁ פָּתַר אוֹתוֹ לְשׁוֹן דָּבָר גָּדוֹל וְקָשֶׁה, כְּמוֹ ״עָתְקוּ גַם גָּבְרוּ חָיִל״ (איוב כא:ז); ״הוֹן עָתֵק״ (משלי ח:יח); ״וְלִמְכַסֶּה עָתִיק״ (ישעיה כג:יח) (ס״א אינו):


**falsely** Heb. עתק, untruth, something unfounded, as (Gen. 12:8): “And he moved (ויעתק) from there” [i.e., something removed from the truth]. Dunash (pp. 17f.) however, interpreted it as an expression of a great and strong thing, as (in Job 21:7): “grow strong (עתקו) and powerfully rich”; (Prov. 8:18), “powerful (עתק) wealth”; (Isa. 23:18), “and for stately (עתקו) clothing.”



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:20:1)


**מָה רַב טוּבְךָ.** יָדַעְתִּי לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא יֵשׁ שָׂכָר טוֹב **לִירֵאֶיךָ**, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהָרְשָׁעִים מַקִּיפִים אוֹתָם, אֲנִי מִתְפַּלֵּל עֲלֵיהֶם שֶׁתַּסְתִּירֵם בְּסֵתֶר פָּנֶיךָ:


**How great is Your goodness** I knew that those who fear You have good reward in the world to come, nevertheless, in this world, because the wicked surround them, I pray for them that You hide them in the secrecy of Your countenance.



### Verse 21

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:21:1)


**מֵרֻכְסֵי אִישׁ.** מֵחֲבוּרֵי רְשָׁעִים הַמִּתְקַשְּׁרִים יַחַד לְהָרַע לָהֶם:


**from bands of men** Heb. מרכסי, from the groups of wicked men who group together to harm them.



### Verse 22

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:22:1)


**בְּעִיר מָצוֹר.** בִּקְעִילָה, כְּשֶׁאָמַר שָׁאוּל עָלַי ״נִסְגַּר לָבוֹא בְּעִיר דְּלָתַיִם וּבְרִיחַ״ (שמואל א כג:ז):


**for He has been wondrously kind to me in a beseiged city** In Keilah, when Saul said concerning me (I Sam. 23:7): “for he has been shut in by coming into a city with doors and bars.”



### Verse 23

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:23:1)


**וַאֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי בְחָפְזִי.** כְּשֶׁיָּצָאתִי מִקְּעִילָה וּבָאתִי אֶל מִדְבַּר מָעוֹן, וְהָיִיתִי נֶחְפָּז לָלֶכֶת מִפְּנֵי שָׁאוּל כִּי הִשִּׂיגַנִי, וְשָׁאוּל וַאֲנָשָׁיו עוֹטְרִים אֵלַי וְאֶל אֲנָשַׁי לְתָפְשָׂם (שמואל א כג:כו):


**But I said in my haste** When I left Keilah and came to the desert of Maon, I was hastening to leave because Saul and his men were surrounding me and my men, to seize us.


###### Rashi on Psalms 31:23:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:23:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:23:2)


**אָמַרְתִּי.** בְּלִבִּי:


**I said** in my heart.


###### Rashi on Psalms 31:23:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:23:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:23:3)


**נִגְרַזְתִּי.** נִכְרַתְּתִי, לְשׁוֹן גַּרְזֶן הַכּוֹרֵת אֶת הָעֵץ. עַל שֵׁם גְּזִירָתוֹ נִקְרָא גַּרְזֶן. כָּךְ פֵּרֵשׁ דּוּנַשׁ. וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ כְּמוֹ ״נִגְרַשְׁתִּי״ (יונה ב:ה), וְאֵין לוֹ דִּמְיוֹן בַּתּוֹרָה (ס״א אינו):


**I have been cut off** Heb. נגרזתי, I have been cut off, an expression of an ax (גרזן) which cuts the tree. Because of its cutting (גרזתו), it is called גרזן, an ax. This is how Dunash explained it (p. 57). (Menachem, however, defined it like נגרשתי, I have driven out, but it has no parallel in the Torah. (p. 59).



### Verse 24

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:24:1)


**אֱמוּנִים נֹצֵר ה׳.** שׁוֹמֵר ה׳ אֶת הַמַּאֲמִינִים בִּישׁוּעָתוֹ וְסוֹמְכִים עָלָיו:


**The Lord guards those who believe** in His salvation and rely on Him.


###### Rashi on Psalms 31:24:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:24:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:24:2)


**עַל יֶתֶר.** מִדָּה בְּמִדָּה, מְכֻוֶּנֶת כְּחֵץ עַל יֶתֶר הַקֶּשֶׁת. אוֹ יֵשׁ לִפְתּוֹר **עַל יֶתֶר** – חֶבֶל כְּנֶגֶד חֶבֶל, קַו כְּנֶגֶד קַו. לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: יֶתֶר הוּא לְשׁוֹן גַּאֲוָה, כְּמוֹ ״יִתְרָה עָשָׂה״ (ישעיהו טו:ז), פֵּרוּשׁ וּמְשַׁלֵּם עַל יֶתֶר – בְּגַאֲוָה לְעוֹשֵׂי גַאֲוָה (ס״א אינו):


**with a bowstring** Heb. יתר (with measure for measure and with exactitude, like an arrow on a bowstring. Not in all editions.) Or, יתר can be interpreted as a rope for a rope, a line for a line. Another interpretation: יתר is an expression of haughtiness, as (in Isa. 15:7): “Because of the haughtiness (יתרה) with which they acted.”



### Verse 25

###### Rashi on Psalms 31:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/31:25:1)


**חִזְקוּ וְיַאֲמֵץ לְבַבְכֶם.** כְּמוֹ שֶׁרְאִיתֶם שֶׁעָשָׂה לִי לְהוֹשִׁיעֵנִי, שֶׁהוֹחַלְתִּי לוֹ:


**Strengthen yourselves, and He will give your heart courage** as you see that He did for me, to save me because I hoped for Him.



## Chapter 32


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 32:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:1:1)


**לְדָוִד מַשְׂכִּיל.** אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים (פסחים קיז.): כָּל מִזְמוֹר שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ מַשְׂכִּיל, עַל יְדֵי מְתוּרְגְּמָן אֲמָרוֹ:


**Of David, a maskil** The Sages said (Pes. 117a): Every Psalm in which “maskil” is mentioned was said through an interpreter.


###### Rashi on Psalms 32:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:1:2)


**אַשְׁרֵי נְשׂוּי פֶּשַׁע.** שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נוֹשֵׂא פֶּשַׁע וּמְכַסֶּה חֲטָאָיו:


**Praiseworthy is he whose transgression is forgiven** Whose transgression the Holy One, Blessed Be He, forgives, and He conceals his sins.


###### Rashi on Psalms 32:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:1:3)


**נָשׂוּי.** אַנְפוֹרְדוֹנִי״ץ בְּלַעַ״ז:


(נשוי is anpardone in Old French, pardoned. The implication is forgiveness, because the forgiveness of iniquity represents [the sin] being lifted up and withdrawn from upon a person.)



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 32:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:2:1)


**וְלֹא יַחְשֹׁב לוֹ עָוֹן.** וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא תִּהְיֶה בְּרוּחוֹ רְמִיָּה לִהְיוֹת בְּדַעְתּוֹ לָשׁוּב אֶל קִיאוֹ (משלי כו:יא):


**to whom the Lord ascribes no iniquity** provided that in his spirit there is no guile, thinking to revert to his “vomit.”



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 32:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:3:1)


**כִּי הֶחֱרַשְׁתִּי.** כַּאֲשֶׁר הֶחֱרַשְׁתִּי מִלְּהִתְוַדּוֹת עַל פְּשָׁעַי לְפָנֶיךָ:


**When I was silent** When I was silent, [when I refrained] from confessing my transgressions before You.


###### Rashi on Psalms 32:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:3:2)


**בָּלוּ עֲצָמָי.** מֵרוֹב אַנְחוֹתַי וּדְאָגוֹתַי כָּל הַיּוֹם שֶׁהָיִיתִי דּוֹאֵג מִפְּנֵי הַפֻּרְעָנוּת:


**my bones decayed** because of my many sighs and my worries all day, that I was worrying about the punishment.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 32:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:4:1)


**כִּי יוֹמָם וָלַיְלָה.** הָיָה כָבֵד עָלַי מוֹרָא יָדְךָ וּגְזֵרוֹתֶיךָ:


**For [both] day and night** the fear of Your hand and Your decrees was heavy upon me.


###### Rashi on Psalms 32:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:4:2)


**נֶהְפַּךְ לְשַׁדִּי.** לַחְלוּחַ שֶׁלִּי, וְכֵן ״לְשַׁד הַשֶּׁמֶן״ (במדבר יא:ח), לַחְלוּחַ שֶׁמֶן. כָּךְ פֵּרְשׁוֹ דוּנַשׁ, וּמְנַחֵם חִבֵּר לְשׁוֹן שְׁדִידָה כְּמוֹ ״מִשֹּׁד עֲנִיִּים״ (תהלים יב:ו), ״רְשָׁעִים זוּ שַׁדּוּנִי״ (תהלים יז:ט):


**my freshness was transformed** Heb. לשדי, my moisture, and so (in Num. 11:8): “the moisture (לשד) of oil,” the moisture of oil. This is how Dunash explained it (p. 14). Menachem (p. 171) associates [it with] an expression of plunder as (above 12:6): “from the plunder (משד) of the poor”; (above 17: 9) “Because of the wicked who have robbed me (שדוני).”


###### Rashi on Psalms 32:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:4:3)


**בְּחַרְבוֹנֵי קַיִץ.** עַד שֶׁיִּיבַשׁ בְּחֹרֶב הַקַּיִץ מִפְּנֵי דַּאֲגַת כֹּבֶד יָדְךָ, שֶׁהָיִיתִי דּוֹאֵג עַל חַטָּאתִי; וּלְפִיכָךְ:


**as in the droughts of summer** Until it dries up as the drought of summer out of my worry of the heaviness of Your hand, that I was worrying about my sins; therefore...



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 32:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:5:1)


**חַטָּאתִי אוֹדִיעֲךָ.** תָּמִיד וּלְשׁוֹן הֹוֶה הוּא, כִּי אָמַרְתִּי: טוֹב שֶׁאוֹדֶה עֲלֵי פְשָׁעַי לַה׳. וְעַתָּה כְּשֶׁהוֹדֵיתִי וְאָמַרְתִּי לְנָתָן הַנָּבִיא ״חָטָאתִי״ (שמואל ב יב:יג), **נָשָׂאתָ עֲוֹן חַטָּאתִי**, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שם): ״גַּם ה׳ הֶעֱבִיר חַטָּאתְךָ וְגוֹ׳״:


**I would inform You of my sin** always. This is a present tense. For I said, It is good that I should confess my transgressions to the Lord, and now that I confessed and said to Nathan the prophet, “I have sinned,” (as in II Samuel 12:13)...**You forgave the iniquity of my sin** as the matter that is stated there (verse 13): “Also the Lord has removed your sin, etc.”



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 32:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:6:1)


**לְעֵת מְצוֹא.** בְּהִמָּצְאֲךָ לְקַבֵּל תְּפִלָּתוֹ, וּמַה הִיא זֹאת? **רַק לְשֵׁטֶף מַיִם רַבִּים** אֲשֶׁר **לֹא יַגִּיעוּ אֵלָיו** – שֶׁלֹּא יִפֹּל בְּיַד הָאֻמּוֹת, שֶׁהֵם כְּמַיִם שׁוֹטְפִים. וְכֵן מָצִינוּ שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל דָּוִד עַל זֹאת וְאָמַר: ״נִפְּלָה נָּא בְיַד ה׳ כִּי רַבִּים רַחֲמָיו וּבְיַד אָדָם אַל אֶפֹּלָה״ (שמואל ב כד:יד):


**at the time that You are found** When You are found to accept his prayer, and what is this?...**only about a flood of vast waters** that they should not reach him, that he should not fall into the hands of enemies, who are like flooding waters. And so we find that David prayed for this and said (II Sam. 24: 14): “Let us fall now into the hand of the Lord, for His mercies are great; but into the hand of man let me not fall.”



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 32:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:7:1)


**אַתָּה סֵתֶר לִי.** לְהִסָּתֵר בְּצִלְּךָ מִפְּנֵי פַּחַד אוֹיֵב:


**You are a shelter for me** to hide in Your shadow from before the enemy.


###### Rashi on Psalms 32:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:7:2)


**תִּצְּרֵנִי.** כְּמוֹ תִּשְׁמְרֵנִי:


**You guard me** Heb. תצרני, like תשמרני.


###### Rashi on Psalms 32:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:7:3)


**רָנֵּי פַלֵּט.** רִנָּה שֶׁל הַצָּלָה:


**songs of deliverance** A song of rescue.


###### Rashi on Psalms 32:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:7:4)


**תְּסוֹבְבֵנִי.** לְשׁוֹן הֹוֶה הוּא: סִבַּבְתַּנִי תָּמִיד רָנֵּי פַלֵּט. וְכָךְ אָמַרְתָּ לִי:


**You encompass me** Heb. תסובבני. This is the present tense. You always encompassed me with songs of deliverance. And so You said to me...



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 32:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:8:1)


**אַשְׂכִּילְךָ וְאוֹרְךָ.** דֶּרֶךְ לָלֶכֶת:


**I will enlighten you and instruct you which way** to go.


###### Rashi on Psalms 32:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:8:2)


**אִיעֲצָה.** אֶרְמֹז לְךָ בְּעֵינִי רֶמֶז מַה תַּעֲשֶׂה, **אִיעֲצָה** לְשׁוֹן קְרִיצַת עַיִן כְּמוֹ ״עֹצֵם עֵינָיו לַחְשֹׁב תַּהְפֻּכוֹת״ (משלי טז:ל):


**I will wink** With My eye; I will hint to you what to do. איעצה is an expression of winking the eye, as (in Prov. 16:30): “He winks (עצה) his eyes to think perverse thoughts.”



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 32:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:9:1)


**אַל תִּהְיוּ כְּסוּס כְּפֶרֶד.** שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵבִין בֵּין הָעוֹשֶׂה לוֹ טוֹבָה לְעוֹשֶׂה לוֹ רָעָה, כְּשֶׁאַתָּה מְמַתְּגָם בּוֹ בְּמֶתֶג הוּא בּוֹלֵם פִּיו וּמְכַסְכֵּס בְּרִסְנוֹ, וּכְשֶׁאַתָּה מְקָרְדוֹ וּמְקַרְצְפוֹ אַתָּה צָרִיךְ לִבְלֹם וְלִסְגֹּר פִּיו וּלְיַסְּרוֹ **בְּמֶתֶג וָרֶסֶן** כְּשֶׁאַתָּה מְעַדֵּהוּ עֲדִי וּמְיַפֵּהוּ:


**Be not like a horse, like a mule** which does not discern between one who benefits him and one who does him harm, for when you insert a bit into his mouth, he closes his mouth and shakes his bridle, and when you curry him and brush him, you must close his mouth and chastise him with a bit and bridle while you adorn him and groom him.


###### Rashi on Psalms 32:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/32:9:2)


**בַּל קְרֹב אֵלֶיךָ.** שֶׁלֹּא יִקְרַב אֵלֶיךָ, לְהַזִּיקְךָ כְּשֶׁאַתָּה מְיַפֵּהוּ. **בְּמֶתֶג וָרֶסֶן עֶדְיוֹ לִבְלוֹם.** בִּשְׁעַת עֶדְיוֹ, שֶׁאַתָּה מְקַרְדּוֹ וּמְקַרְצְפוֹ, אַתָּה צָרִיךְ לְסוֹגְרוֹ בְּמֶתֶג וָרֶסֶן שֶׁלֹּא יִקְרַב אֵלֶיךָ. בְּלִימָה בִּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה לְשׁוֹן מַסְגֵּר: פִּיו בָּלוּם, רַגְלָיו מְבֻלָּמוֹת (בכורות מ:). וּמְנַחֵם חִבֵּר **לִבְלוֹם** וְכֵן ״עַל בְּלִימָה״ (איוב כו:ז) לְשׁוֹן תֹּכֶן (ס״א אינו):


**so that...he does not come near you** So that he should not come near you to hurt you while you groom him, with bit and bridle (when he is being groomed, to close his mouth. When he is being groomedwhile you curry him and brush himyou must close his mouth with a bit and bridle so that he does not come near you.) בלימה is an expression of closing in the language of the Mishnah: Its mouth is closed (בלום), its feet are closed (מבלמות), in Tractate Bechoroth (40b). (Menachem associated לבלום, and also בלימה [Job 26:7] as an expression of regulating [p. 45].)



## Chapter 33


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 33:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/33:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/33:2:1)


**בְּנֵבֶל עָשׂוֹר.** שֶׁל עֶשֶׂר מִינֵי נְעִימָה (ערכין יג:):


**with a lyre of ten melodies** Heb. בנבל עשור, of ten kinds of melody.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 33:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/33:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/33:7:1)


**כַּנֵּד.** לְשׁוֹן גּוֹבַהּ, וְכֵן תַּרְגּוּם אוּנְקְלוֹס ״נִצְּבוּ כְמוֹ נֵד״ (שמות טו:ח): ״קָמוּ כְשׁוּר״, וְכֵן פֵּרֵשׁ מְנַחֵם, וְאֵין ׳נֵד׳ וְ׳נֹאד׳ שָׁוִין:


**as a mound** Heb. כנד, an expression of height, and so did Onkelos render (Exod. 15:8): נצבו כמו נד, they stood up like a wall, and so did Menachem (p. 121, missing) explain it. נד and נאד do not have the same meaning.


###### Rashi on Psalms 33:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/33:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/33:7:2)


**נוֹתֵן בְּאוֹצָרוֹת תְּהוֹמוֹת.** תַּחַת הָאָרֶץ:


**He puts the deeps into treasuries** under the earth.



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Psalms 33:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/33:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/33:14:1)


**הִשְׁגִּיחַ.** הִבִּיט:


**He oversees** He looks.



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Psalms 33:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/33:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/33:15:1)


**הַיּוֹצֵר יַחַד לִבָּם.** לֵב כֻּלָּם יַחַד וְיוֹדֵעַ כָּל הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת, וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ (ראש השנה יח.) הֱסִיבוּהוּ אֶל **מִמְּכוֹן שִׁבְתּוֹ הִשְׁגִּיחַ, הַיּוֹצֵר יַחַד לִבָּם**, וְדָרְשׁוּ מִכָּאן שֶׁכֻּלָּן נִסְקָרִין בִּסְקִירָה אַחַת:


**He Who forms their hearts together** All of their hearts together and knows all the thoughts. Our Sages, however, explain that it refers back to “From His dwelling place, the Creator oversees their hearts together,” and they derived from here that all are examined with a single glance (Rosh Hashana 18a).



## Chapter 34


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 34:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:1:1)


**בְּשַׁנּוֹתוֹ אֶת טַעְמוֹ.** כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמואל א כא:יד) ״וַיְתָו עַל דַּלְתוֹת הַשַּׁעַר וְגוֹ׳ וַיְשַׁנּוּ אֶת טַעְמוֹ בְּעֵינֵיהֶם״, שֶׁשִּׁנָּה דְּבָרוֹ וְטַעְמוֹ וְעָשָׂה עַצְמוֹ שׁוֹטֶה וְהוֹרִיד רִירוֹ עַל זְקָנוֹ (ס״א אינו):


**when he disguised his sanity** as the matter that is stated (in I Sam. 21:14): “And he changed his speech before their eyes, etc. And he scribbled upon the doors of the gates.” That he disguised his speech and his sanity and feigned madness and let his saliva run down upon his beard.


###### Rashi on Psalms 34:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:1:2)


**לִפְנֵי אֲבִימֶלֶךְ.** כָּךְ כָּל מַלְכֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים נִקְרָאִים, וְכָל מַלְכֵי מִצְרַיִם פַּרְעֹה. וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ אָכִישׁ, קוֹרִין לוֹ אֲבִימֶלֶךְ. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: שֶׁהָיָה צַדִּיק כַּאֲבִימֶלֶךְ (בראשית כ) שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה לְהָרְגוֹ, וַאֲנָשָׁיו אוֹמְרִים לוֹ ״הֲלֹא זֶה דָּוִד מֶלֶךְ הָאָרֶץ״ (שמואל א כא:יב), כִּדְאִיתָא בְּמִדְרַשׁ תְּהִלִּים:


**before Abimelech** All Philistine kings were called thus, and all Egyptian kings [were called] Pharaoh. Although his name was Achish, he was called Abimelech. The Midrash Aggadah explains that he was as righteous as Abimelech (mentioned in the Torah in relation to Sarah), for he did not want to kill him although his men said to him, “Is this not David, the king of the land?” As is stated in Midrash Psalms (34:1).



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 34:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:3:1)


**בַּה׳ תִּתְהַלֵּל נַפְשִׁי.** מִתְפָּאֵר אֲנִי וּמִתְהַלֵּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי פַּטְרוֹן כָּזֶה לְהוֹשִׁיעַ וּלְהָגֵן:


**My soul boasts of the Lord** I boast, and praise myself that I have a patron like this to save me and protect me.


###### Rashi on Psalms 34:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:3:2)


**תִּתְהַלֵּל נַפְשִׁי.** שֶׁפּוֹרְוְונְטְרָ״א בְּלַעַ״ז:


**I will boast.** Se porvantera in French.


###### Rashi on Psalms 34:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:3:3)


**יִשְׁמְעוּ עֲנָוִים.** נִפְלָאוֹת שֶׁעָשָׂה לִי, מִתּוֹךְ מַהֲלָלִי יָבִינוּ אוֹתָם **וְיִשְׂמָחוּ**:


**may the humble hear** the wonders that He did for me. Through my praise, they will understand it and rejoice.

###### Rashi on Psalms 34:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:5:1)


**מְגוּרוֹתַי.** לְשׁוֹן פַּחַד, כְּמוֹ ״וַיָּגָר מוֹאָב״ (במדבר כב:ג):


**my terrors** Heb. מגורותי, an expression of fear, as (in Num. 22:3): “and Moab became terrified (ויגר) .”

**seek peace** in your place.


###### Rashi on Psalms 34:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:15:2)


**וְרָדְפֵהוּ.** בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר (תנחומא, חקת כב):


**and pursue it** elsewhere.



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Psalms 34:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:17:1)


**פְּנֵי.** פָּנִים שֶׁל זַעַם לִישַׁאיְרָא״שׁ בְּלַעַ״ז, כְּמוֹ (ויקרא כ:ה) ״וְשַׂמְתִּי פָנַי בָּאִישׁ הַהוּא״, כָּךְ חִבְּרוֹ מְנַחֵם:


**The face of the Lord** His angry face, les ires in Old French, ire, as (in Lev. 20:5): “And I will direct My face, etc.” So did Menachem (p. 143) associate it.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Psalms 34:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:18:1)


**צָעֲקוּ.** הַצַּדִּיקִים **וַה׳ שָׁמֵעַ**:


**They cry out** i.e., the righteous, and the Lord hearkens.



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Psalms 34:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:20:1)


**רַבּוֹת רָעוֹת צַדִּיק.** הַרְבֵּה רָעוֹת וּפְחָדִים בָּאוֹת עָלָיו, **וּמִכֻּלָּם** נִצּוֹל:


**Many evils befall the righteous** Many evils and terrors befall him, and he is saved from all of them.



### Verse 21

###### Rashi on Psalms 34:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:21:1)


**שׁוֹמֵר.** הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא **כָּל עַצְמוֹתָיו**:


**He guards** The Holy One, blessed be He, [guards] all his bones.



### Verse 22

###### Rashi on Psalms 34:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:22:1)


**תְּמוֹתֵת רָשָׁע רָעָה.** תְּמוֹתֵת אֶת הָרָשָׁע הָרָעָה שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה:


**Evil will kill the wicked** The evil that the wicked man does will kill him.


###### Rashi on Psalms 34:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:22:2)


**תְּמוֹתֵת.** תָּמִית:


**will kill** Heb. תמותת, [equivalent to] תמית.



### Verse 23

###### Rashi on Psalms 34:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/34:23:1)


**לֹא יֶאְשְׁמוּ.** לֹא יִתְחָרְטוּ לֵאמֹר: אָשַׁמְנוּ שֶׁחָסִינוּ בְּךָ; רִיפוֹנְטִירוֹנְ״ט בְּלַעַ״ז:


**shall not be accounted guilty** They will not regret saying, “We are guilty, because we took shelter in You.” Repontiront in Old French, se repentiront: they repent.



## Chapter 35


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:1:1)


**רִיבָה ה׳ אֶת יְרִיבַי.** עֲשֵׂה מְרִיבָה עִם אוֹתָם שֶׁעוֹשִׂים מְרִיבָה עִמִּי:


**O Lord, strive with those who strive against me** Make a quarrel with those who make quarrels with me.


###### Rashi on Psalms 35:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:1:2)


**לְחַם.** לְשׁוֹן מִלְחָמָה, וְכֵן **לוֹחֲמַי**: הִלָּחֵם עִם הַנִּלְחָמִים עִמִּי:


**battle** Heb. לחם an expression of war (מלחמה), and so לחמי, battle those who battle with me.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:3:1)


**וְהָרֵק חֲנִית.** הִזְדַּיֵּן, כְּמוֹ ״אָרִיק חַרְבִּי״ (שמות טו:ט), ״וַיָּרֶק אֶת חֲנִיכָיו״ (בראשית יד:יד):


**And arm Yourself with a spear** Heb. והרק. Arm Yourself, as (in Exod. 15:9) “I will arm myself (אריק) with my sword”; (Gen. 14:14), “And he armed (וירק) his trained men.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 35:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:3:2)


**וּסְגֹר לִקְרַאת רֹדְפָי.** הָגֵן בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיהֶם כִּמְחִיצָּה:


**and bar the way before my pursuers** Protect between me and them, as a barrier.


###### Rashi on Psalms 35:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:3:3)


**לְנַפְשִׁי.** אִימוֹיְמֵאִימָ״שׁ בְּלַעַ״ז, כְּמוֹ ״כָּרוּ שׁוּחָה לְנַפְשִׁי״ (ירמיהו יח:כ):


**to my soul** A moi meme in French, to myself, as (in Jer. 18:20): “for they have dug a pit for me (לנפשי).”



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:6:1)


**חֹשֶׁךְ וַחֲלַקְלַקּוֹת.** שְׁנֵיהֶם יַחַד, כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּחֲלִיקוּ רַגְלֵיהֶם בַּחֲלַקְלַקּוֹת, וְהַחֹשֶׁךְ אֵינוֹ מַנִּיחָם לְהִשָּׁמֵר מִן הַחֲלַקְלַקּוֹת. כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר ״לָכֵן יִהְיֶה דַרְכָּם לָהֶם כַּחֲלַקְלַקּוֹת בָּאֲפֵלָה יִדָּחוּ וְנָפְלוּ בָהּ״ (ירמיה כג:יב):


**dark and slippery** Both together, so that their feet should slip on the slippery places and the darkness should not allow them to beware of the slippery places, as it is written (in Jer. 23: 12): “Therefore, their way shall be for them like slippery places in the dark: ‘let them be thrust and fall therein.’ “



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:7:1)


**חָפְרוּ לְנַפְשִׁי.** שׁוּחָה לִיפּוֹל בָּהּ:


**they have dug it for my soul** they have dug a pit into which I should fall.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:8:1)


**שׁוֹאָה.** חֹשֶׁךְ, בְּרוּאִינָ״ה בְּלַעַ״ז:


**darkness** Heb. שואה, darkness, broine in Old French, obscurity.


###### Rashi on Psalms 35:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:8:2)


**וְרִשְׁתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר טָמַן.** כֵּן דֶּרֶךְ לִטְמוֹן הָרֶשֶׁת וּלְכַסּוֹתוֹ בְּקַשׁ אוֹ בְּעָפָר, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יַרְגִּישׁ בָּהּ הָעוֹבֵר עָלֶיהָ עַד שֶׁנִּלְכַּד בָּהּ:


**and his net that he hid** So is the custom to hide the net and to cover it with straw or with earth, in order that the one who passes over it should not notice it until he is trapped in it.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:9:1)


**וְנַפְשִׁי תָּגִיל.** כְּשֶׁאֶרְאֶה בְּמַפַּלְתָּם:


**And my soul shall exult** when I see their downfall.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:10:1)


**כָּל עַצְמוֹתַי.** יְקַלְּסוּךָ עַל כָּךְ, כִּי עַתָּה:


**All my bones** will praise You for everything, for now...



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:11:1)


**יְקוּמוּן.** עָלַי תָּמִיד **עֵדֵי חָמָס וְגוֹ׳**:


**False witnesses rise up** constantly against me, etc.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:13:1)


**וּתְפִלָּתִי עַל חֵיקִי תָשׁוּב.** כְּלוֹמַר: וְאִם יֹאמְרוּ לֹא עִנֵּיתִי נַפְשִׁי אֶלָּא לְרָעָתָם, שֶׁיִּכְבַּד עֲלֵיהֶם חָלְיָם, תְּפִלָּתִי שֶׁהִתְפַּלַּלְתִּי עֲלֵיהֶם תָּשׁוּב עָלַי:


**and may my prayer return upon my bosom** That is to say: If they say that I afflicted myself only for their detriment, that their illness should become more serious, may my prayer that I prayed for them return to me.



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:14:1)


**כְּרֵעַ כְּאָח לִי הִתְהַלָּכְתִּי.** כְּאִלּוּ הָיוּ לִי אָחִי וְרֵעִי הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי, מֵיצַר עֲלֵיהֶם עַל צָרָתָם:


**I walked about as though it were a friend or as though it were my own brother** As though it were my brother or my friend; I walked about depressed because of their distress.


###### Rashi on Psalms 35:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:14:2)


**כְּאָבֶל.** אִם כְּבֵן הַמִּתְאַבֵּל עַל אִמּוֹ, אוֹ כְּאֵם הַמִּתְאַבֶּלֶת עַל בְּנָהּ:


**as the mourning of a mother** As a son who mourns for his mother or as a mother who mourns for her son.


###### Rashi on Psalms 35:14:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:14:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:14:3)


**קוֹדֵר.** לְשׁוֹן שַׁחֲרוּת:


**with gloom** Heb. קדר, an expression of blackness.


###### Rashi on Psalms 35:14:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:14:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:14:4)


**שַׁחוֹתִי.** לְשׁוֹן שִׁפְלוּת:


**I was bowed** An expression of humility.



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:15:1)


**וּבְצַלְעִי שָׂמְחוּ וְנֶאֱסָפוּ.** וּכְשֶׁאֲנִי צוֹלֵעַ, שֶׁשֶּׁבֶר בָּא עָלַי, **שָׂמְחוּ וְנֶאֱסָפוּ**:


**And, when I limped, they rejoiced and gathered** And when I limped because I suffered a fracture, they rejoiced and gathered [around me].


###### Rashi on Psalms 35:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:15:2)


**נֶאֶסְפוּ עָלַי נֵכִים.** אֲנָשִׁים פִּסְחִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָנוּ מְתַרְגְּמִינָן ״נָכֶה״: ״חֲגִירָא״ (תרגום יונתן מלכים ב כג:כט), וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ כְּמוֹ ״נְכָאִים״ (ישעיה טז:ז), אימנויישי״ץ בְּלַעַ״ז:


**lame people gathered about me** Heb. נכים, lame people, as we translate “Pharaoh-neco,” חגירא, lame. Menachem (p. 122f.) associated it with (Isa. 16: 7), נכאים, broken-hearted, amenuyze in Old French, crushed.


###### Rashi on Psalms 35:15:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:15:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:15:3)


**קָרְעוּ וְלֹא דָמּוּ.** אִלּוּ הָיוּ קוֹרְעִין אֶת בְּשָׂרִי, לֹא הָיָה דָמִי שׁוֹתֵת לָאָרֶץ כְּשֶׁמַּלְבִּינִין פָּנַי:


**Were they to tear, they would not draw blood** Were they to tear my flesh, my blood would not flow to the ground when they embarrass me [lit. make my face white].



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:16:1)


**בְּחַנְפֵי לַעֲגֵי מָעוֹג וְגוֹ׳.** בִּשְׁבִיל חֲנִיפוּת שֶׁל לֵיצָנוּת, אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה, שֶׁמַּחֲנִיפִין לְשָׁאוּל בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיַּאֲכִילֵם וְיַשְׁקֵם, חוֹרְקִים עָלַי שִׁנֵּיהֶם:


**Because of the flattery of scorn for food, they gnash, etc.** Because of the flattery of scorn of eating and drinking, that they flatter Saul in order that he give them to eat and drink, they gnash their teeth against me.


###### Rashi on Psalms 35:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:16:2)


**מָעוֹג.** לְשׁוֹן אֲכִילָה, כְּמוֹ ״אִם יֶשׁ לִי מָעוֹג״ דְּאֵלִיָּהוּ (מלכים א יז:יב). וּמְנַחֵם פָּתַר אוֹתוֹ לְשׁוֹן ״עֻגָה קְטַנָּה״ (מלכים א יז:יג), וְכֵן ״אִם יֶשׁ לִי מָעוֹג״:


**food** Heb. מעוג, an expression of eating, as (in I Kings 17:12): “if I have food (מעוג),” written regarding Elijah, but Menachem (p. 130) interpreted it as an expression of a loaf of bread, and so “if I have a cake (מעוג).”



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:17:1)


**כַּמָּה תִּרְאֶה.** כַּמָּה אֹרֶךְ אַפַּיִם יֵשׁ לְפָנֶיךָ, לִרְאוֹת כָּל אֵלֶּה:


**how long will You look on?** How much patience do You have to look upon all these?


###### Rashi on Psalms 35:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:17:2)


**מִשּׁוֹאֵיהֶם.** מֵחֹשֶׁךְ שֶׁלָּהֶם:


**from their darkness** Heb. משאיהם, from their darkness.


###### Rashi on Psalms 35:17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:17:3)


**מִכְּפִירִים יְחִידָתִי.** מוּסָב עַל **הָשִׁיבָה נַפְשִׁי**: הָשִׁיבָה מִכְּפִירִים יְחִידָתִי, (יְחִידָתִי נִשְׁמָתִי ס״א אינו):


**my only one from young lions** This refers to “Return my soul.” Return my only one from young lions.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:19:1)


**אוֹיְבֵי שֶׁקֶר.** שֶׁשּׂוֹנְאִין אוֹתִי עַל דְּבַר שֶׁקֶר, שֶׁמְּעִידִין עָלַי מַה שֶּׁלֹּא עָלָה בְמַחֲשַׁבְתִּי מֵעוֹלָם. **אַל יִשְׂמְחוּ** בִּמְפַלְתִּי:


**those who are my enemies for an unjust cause** who hate me because of a false matter, that they testify against me what never entered my mind. Let them not rejoice at my downfall.


###### Rashi on Psalms 35:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:19:2)


**שׂוֹנְאַי.** שֶׁשּׂוֹנְאִים אוֹתִי, **אַל יִקְרְצוּ עָלַי עָיִן** וְלִלְעוֹג בְּעֵינֵיהֶם עַל מַפַּלְתִּי:


**who hate me** Let those who hate me not wink their eyes at me, to mock my downfall with their eyes.


###### Rashi on Psalms 35:19:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:19:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:19:3)


**יִקְרְצוּ.** צִינַאנְ״ט בְּלַעַ״ז:


יקרצו means seynt in Old French, signal.



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:20:1)


**עַל רִגְעֵי אֶרֶץ.** עַל דַּכָּאֵי אֶרֶץ, וְכֵן ״רֹגַע הַיָּם״ (ירמיהו לא:לה), ״עוֹרִי רָגַע״ (איוב ז:ה), וְכֵן פֵּרֵשׁ דּוּנַשׁ:


**and against the crushed people of the earth** Heb. רגעי, on the crushed people of the earth, and so (in Jer. 31:34): “Who stirs up (רגע) the sea”; (Job 7:5), “my skin wrinkled (רגע).” And so did Dunash explain it.



### Verse 21

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:21:1)


**הֶאָח הֶאָח.** לְשׁוֹן שִׂמְחָה מִתְהַלֵּל בְּתַאֲוַת לִבּוֹ מֵרוֹב שִׂמְחָתָם שֶׁרוֹאִים תַּאֲוָתָם מִתְקַיֶּמֶת:


**Aha! Aha!** Heb. האח, an expression of joy of one who boasts with the lust of his heart, out of their [sic] great joy, that they see their lust gratified.



### Verse 23

###### Rashi on Psalms 35:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/35:23:1)


**הָעִירָה וְהָקִיצָה.** פַּמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה, לִשְׁפּוֹט מִשְׁפָּטִי מֵאוֹיְבַי (סנהדרין לח:):


**Arouse Yourself and awaken** the heavenly retinue to judge my cause from my enemies.



## Chapter 36


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 36:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:2:1)


**נְאֻם פֶּשַׁע לָרָשָׁע בְּקֶרֶב לִבִּי וְגוֹ׳.** הֲרֵי זֶה מִקְרָא מְסֹרָס: יֵשׁ **בְּקֶרֶב לִבִּי**, שֶׁהַפֶּשַׁע, הוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע, אוֹמֵר **לָרָשָׁע** שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא **פַּחַד אֱלֹהִים לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו**:


**The word of the transgression to the wicked man, in the midst of my heart, etc.** This is a transposed verse. I feel within my heart that the transgressioni.e., the evil inclinationsays to the wicked man that the fear of God should not be before his eyes.


###### Rashi on Psalms 36:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:2:2)


**וּבְקֶרֶב לִבִּי.** כְּאָדָם שֶׁאוֹמֵר: כִּמְדֻמֶּה אֲנִי:


**in the midst of my heart** Like a person who says, “It seems to me.”



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 36:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:3:1)


**כִּי הֶחֱלִיק.** הַפֶּשַׁע עַל הָרָשָׁע בַּחֲלַקְלַקּוֹת בְּעֵינָיו, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּמְצָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת **עֲוֹנוֹ, לִשְׂנֹא** אוֹתוֹ:


**For it smoothed** The transgression made smooth places appear to his eyes in order that the Holy One, blessed be He, find his iniquity to hate him.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 36:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:4:1)


**חָדַל לְהַשְׂכִּיל לְהֵיטִיב.** מָנַע עַצְמוֹ מֵהַשְׂכִּיל, לְהֵיטִיב מַעֲשָׂיו:


**he refrained from learning to improve** He refrained from contemplating to improve his deeds.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 36:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:5:1)


**יִתְיַצֵּב עַל דֶּרֶךְ לֹא טוֹב.** הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נָתַן לְפָנָיו דֶּרֶךְ הַטּוֹב וְדֶרֶךְ הַמָּוֶת, וְהוּא בּוֹחֵר לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ לֹא טוֹב:


**he stands on a way that is not good** The Holy One, blessed be He, placed before him the good way and the way of death, yet he chooses for himself a way that is not good.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 36:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:6:1)


**ה׳ בַּשָּׁמַיִם חַסְדֶּךָ.** בִּשְׁבִיל רְשָׁעִים הַלָּלוּ אַתָּה מְסַלֵּק חֶסֶד מִן הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים, וּמַגְבִּיהַּ אֱמוּנָתְךָ **עַד שְׁחָקִים** לְסַלְּקָהּ מִבְּנֵי אָדָם:


**O Lord, Your kindness is in the heavens** Because of these wicked men, You remove [Your] kindness from the earth creatures and raise up Your faith until the sky to remove it from the sons of men.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 36:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:7:1)


**צִדְקָתְךָ.** יְקָרָה מִן הַבְּרִיּוֹת **כְּהַרְרֵי אֵל**, בִּשְׁבִיל מַעֲשֵׂי הָרְשָׁעִים, וּ**מִשְׁפָּטֶךָ** בָּאִים לָעוֹלָם עַד **תְּהוֹם רַבָּה** (ויקרא רבה כז:א). דָּבָר אַחֵר: **צִדְקָתְךָ כְּהַרְרֵי אֵל** מִי שֶׁאַתָּה רוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת צְדָקָה עִמּוֹ, אַתָּה מַגְבִּיהוֹ וּמְתַקְּפוֹ כְּהַרְרֵי אֵל, לְשׁוֹן תּוֹקֶף, כְּמוֹ (יחזקאל יז:יג) ״וְאֶת אֵילֵי הָאָרֶץ לָקָח״:


**Your charity** is as scarce to the creatures as the mighty mountains because of the deeds of the wicked, and Your judgments come upon the world until the vast deep. Another explanation: **Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains** The one with whom You wish to deal charitably, You raise up and strengthen like the mighty mountains. אל is an expression of strength, as (in Ezek. 17: 13): “and he has taken away the mighty of (אילי) the land.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 36:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:7:2)


**מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ תְּהוֹם רַבָּה.** מִי שֶׁאַתָּה רוֹצֶה לָדוּן אוֹתוֹ וְלִיקַּח נִקְמָתְךָ מִמֶּנּוּ, אַתָּה מוֹרִידוֹ עַד תְּהוֹם רַבָּה:


**Your judgments are the vast deep** Whomever You wish to judge, and wreak vengeance upon, You humble him to the vast deep.


###### Rashi on Psalms 36:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:7:3)


**מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ.** יוּשְׁטִיצָ״א בְּלַעַ״ז:


**Your judgments** Heb. משפטיך, joustiza in Old French, justice.


###### Rashi on Psalms 36:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:7:4)


**אָדָם וּבְהֵמָה תּוֹשִׁיעַ ה׳.** בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁהֵם עֲרוּמִים בְּדַעַת כְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן וּמְשִׂימִין עַצְמָן כַּבְּהֵמָה בַּעֲנָוָה, תּוֹשִׁיעַ ה׳:


**You save both man and beast** People who are as astute as Adam, but who make themselves as humble as beasts, You save, O Lord.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 36:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/36:8:1)


**מַה יָּקָר חַסְדְּךָ.** אֵינוֹ כְּדַאי לְהִמָּשֵׁךְ עַל הָרְשָׁעִים הַלָּלוּ, אֲבָל בְּנֵי אָדָם אֲשֶׁר **בְּצֵל כְּנָפֶיךָ יֶחֱסָיוּן** הֵם **יִרְוְיוּן מִדֶּשֶׁן בֵּיתֶךָ וְגוֹ׳**:


**How precious is Your kindness** It is not fitting that it be extended to these wicked, but the children of men who take refuge in the shadow of Your wingsthey will be sated from the fat of Your house, etc.



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Psalms 36:12:1

**אַל תְּבוֹאֵנִי רֶגֶל גַּאֲוָה.** אַל תָּבוֹא עִמִּי רֶגֶל הָרְשָׁעִים הַלָּלוּ בְּעֵת קִבּוּל שָׂכָר לִהְיוֹת חֶלְקָם עִם הַצַּדִּיקִים, (לשון חלק אהלא פרט״יאה בלע״ז ס״א אינו):


**Let the foot of haughtiness not come with me** Let the foot of these wicked men not come with me at the time of the reception of reward, [because] their lot should [not] be with the righteous.


###### Rashi on Psalms 36:12:2

**וְיַד רְשָׁעִים אַל תְּנִדֵנִי.** מִמְּקוֹמִי בְּבוֹאִי לִירַשׁ מִשְׁנֶה, חֶלְקִי וְחֶלְקוֹ (שֶׁל רָשָׁע) בַּטּוֹבָה, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ישעיהו סא:ז): ״לָכֵן בְּאַרְצָם מִשְׁנֶה יִירָשׁוּ״. וְאָז:


**neither shall the hand of the wicked cause me to wander** from my place when I return to inherit a double [portion]: my portion and the portion of the wicked man, in the goodness, as the matter that is stated (in Isa. 61:7): “Therefore, in their land they shall inherit twofold.” And then...



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Psalms 36:13:1

**שָׁם נָפְלוּ פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן.** שָׁם יָבִינוּ בְּמַפַּלְתָּם, וְשָׁם **דֹּחוּ וְלֹא יָכְלוּ קוּם**:

## Chapter 37


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 37:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/37:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/37:1:1)


**אַל תִּתְחַר בַּמְּרֵעִים.** מוֹכִיחַ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא שֶׁלֹּא יִתְחָרוּ בְּהַצְלָחַת הַמְּרֵעִים לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם, כְּמוֹ ״וְאֵיךְ תְּתַחֲרֶה אֶת הַסּוּסִים״ (ירמיה יב:ה) לָרוּץ בִּמְרוּצָתָם, הָאָטִיר בְּלַעַ״ז:


**Do not compete with the evildoers** He reproves Israel that they should not compete with the success of the evildoers to do as their deeds, as (in Jer. 12:5): “how will you compete (תתחרה) with horses,” to run as they run, a atir in Old French, to compete.

**אַל תְּקַנֵּא בְּעוֹשֵׂי עַוְלָה.** לַעֲשׂוֹת עַוְלָה כְּמוֹתָם:


**do not envy those who commit injustice** to commit injustice like them.

**יִמָּלוּ.** שְׁרוֹנְ״ט טְרַנְקִיי״ץ בְּלַעַ״ז, לְשׁוֹן כְּרִיתָה:


**they will be...cut off** Heb. ימלו, seront tronke in Old French, they will be cut off, an expression of cutting off.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 37:3:1

**בְּטַח בַּה׳.** וְאַל תֹּאמַר: אִם לֹא אֶגְזֹל וְאֶגְנֹב, אוֹ אֶתֵּן לֶעָנִי צְדָקָה, בַּמֶּה אֶתְפַּרְנֵס?


**Trust in the Lord** and do not say, “If I do not rob and steal,” or “If I give charity to a poor man, how will I sustain myself?”


###### Rashi on Psalms 37:3:2

**וַעֲשֵׂה טוֹב.** וְאָז תִּשְׁכֹּן אֶרֶץ לְאֹרֶךְ יָמִים:


**and do good** Then you will dwell in the land for a long time.


###### Rashi on Psalms 37:3:3

**וּרְעֵה אֱמוּנָה.** תֹּאכַל וְתִתְפַּרְנֵס מִשְּׂכַר הָאֱמוּנָה שֶׁהֶאֱמַנְתָּ בְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִסְמֹךְ עָלָיו וְלַעֲשׂוֹת טוֹב:


**and be nourished by faith** You will eat and be sustained from the reward of [your] faith, that you believed in the Holy One, blessed be He, to rely on Him and do good.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 37:4:1

**וְהִתְעַנַּג עַל ה׳.** הִתְעַנֵּג בְּתַפְנוּקִים עַל מִשְׁעַנְתּוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
