### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Psalms 55:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:13:1)


**כִּי לֹא אוֹיֵב יְחָרְפֵנִי.** מִיָּמַי שֶׁאֶשָּׂא חֶרְפָּתִי, אֶלָּא קַמְתִּי עָלָיו וַהֲרַגְתִּיו:


**For no enemy reviled me** all my life that I should bear my vilification, but I rose up against him and slew him.


###### Rashi on Psalms 55:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:13:2)


**לֹא מְשַׂנְאִי עָלַי הִגְדִּיל.** וַאֲנִי בָּרַחְתִּי וְנִסְתַּרְתִּי מִמֶּנּוּ, אֲבָל עַתָּה עַל כָּרְחִי אֲנִי נוֹשֵׂא אֶת חֶרְפָּתְךָ שֶׁאַתָּה תְּחָרְפֵנִי, לְפִי שֶׁאַתָּה אָדָם גָּדוֹל בַּתּוֹרָה:


**my enemy did not open his mouth** that I should flee and hide from him, but now I bear the abuse with which you reviled me because you are a man who is great in Torah.



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Psalms 55:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:14:1)


**אֱנוֹשׁ כְּעֶרְכִּי.** אִישׁ חָשׁוּב כָּמוֹנִי:


**a man of my equal** A man as important as I.


###### Rashi on Psalms 55:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:14:2)


**וּמְיֻדָּעִי.** כְּמוֹ אַלּוּפִי, לְשׁוֹן ״וָאֵדָעֲךָ בְשֵׁם״ (שמות לג:יז), דִּמְתַרְגְּמִינָן ״וְרַבִּיתָךְ״. וּמְנַחֵם פֵּירֵשׁ: כִּי לֹא אוֹיֵב יְחָרְפֵנִי וְאֶשָּׂא, יֵשׁ עָלָיו מִן הָעִנְיָן מִי יִתֵּן לִי אֵבֶר כַּיּוֹנָה אָעוּפָה וְאֶשְׁכֹּנָה, אִילּוּ יָכֹלְתִּי לְהַעֲלוֹת אֵבֶר הָיִיתִי טָס וְנוֹדֵד מִפְּנֵי עָקַת רָשָׁע, כִּי בְּצֵאתִי מִקֶּרֶב מְעָרַת פָּרִיצִים לָלוּן בַּמִּדְבָּר סֶלָה, אָז לֹא אוֹיֵב יְחָרְפֵנִי וְלֹא הָיִיתִי נוֹשֵׂא כְּלִמָּתִי וּבָשְׁתִּי, וְלֹא נִסְתַּרְתִּי מִפָּנָיו כַּאֲשֶׁר הָיִיתִי נִסְתָּר מִפְּנֵיהֶם כְּשֶׁהָיִיתִי בְתוֹכָם. וּפִתְרוֹן זֶה לֹא יִתָּכֵן מִפְּנֵי הַפְּסוּקִים הַכְּתוּבִים אַחֲרֵיהֶם, וְהֵם **וְאַתָּה אֱנוֹשׁ כְּעֶרְכִּי אַלּוּפִי וּמְיֻדָּעִי אֲשֶׁר יַחְדָּו נַמְתִּיק סוֹד בְּבֵית אֱלֹהִים נְהַלֵּךְ בְּרָגֶשׁ.** לָכֵן פּוֹתֵר אוֹתוֹ דּוּנַשׁ בְּעִנְיָן אַחֵר, וְזֶה פִּתְרוֹנוֹ: כִּי לֹא אוֹיֵב יְחָרְפֵנִי וְאֶשָּׂא חֶרְפָּתוֹ, וְלֹא מְשַׂנְאִי עָלַי הִגְדִּיל וְאֶסָּתֵר מִמֶּנּוּ, כִּי אִם **אַלּוּפִי וּמְיֻדָּעִי אֲשֶׁר יַחְדָּיו נַמְתִּיק סוֹד בְּבֵית אֱלֹהִים נְהַלֵּךְ בְּרָגֶשׁ.** וְהַדָּבָר הַזֶּה יָדוּעַ, כִּי הָאָדָם קָשֶׁה עָלָיו חֶרְפַּת הָאוֹהֵב מֵחֶרְפַּת הָאוֹיֵב, וְגַם יוּכַל לְהִסָּתֵר מֵאוֹיְבוֹ וְלֹא יוּכַל לְהִסָּתֵר מֵאוֹהֲבוֹ בְּהַגִּידוֹ לוֹ אֶת כָּל לִבּוֹ. כֵּן מוֹכִיחַ הָעִנְיָן:


**and my esteemed one** Heb. ומידעי, like אלוּפי, my prince, an expression of (Exod. 33:17): “and I recognized you (ואדעך),” which is translated וְרַבִּיתָךְ “and I made you great.” Menachem (p. 94), however, explained that “For no enemy would revile me that I should bear” is connected to (verse 7): “If only I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and be at rest.” If I could raise my wings, I would fly away and wander on account of the distress of the wicked [inflicted upon me], for when I would leave the midst of the assembly of the profligate to lodge in the desert forever, then no enemy would revile me; I would not [have to] bear my disgrace and my shame, and I would not hide from him as I hid from them when I was among them. However, this interpretation is impossible, because of the verses following it, namely: And you are a man of my equal, my prince, and my esteemed one (verse 14); that together we would devise counsel; in the house of God we would walk with a multitude (verse 15). Therefore, Dunash (p. 94) interprets it in another manner, and this is its interpretation: For it is not an enemy who reviles me that I should bear my abuse, and it is not my enemy who opens his mouth wide against me, but my prince and my esteemed one, that together we would take counsel; in the house of God we would walk with a multitude. This thing is known, that the abuse of a friend is harder for a person [to bear] than the abuse of an enemy. Moreover, one can hide from his enemy, but one cannot hide from his friend when he tells him all that is in his heart. The context corroborates this [interpretation].



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Psalms 55:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:15:1)


**אֲשֶׁר יַחְדָּו.** הָיִינוּ רְגִילִים לְהַמְתִּיק סוֹד בַּתּוֹרָה, וּבְבֵית אֱלֹהִים הָיִינוּ מְהַלְּכִים בְּרָגֶשׁ, בְּרוֹב עָם:


**That together** we used to devise counsel in the Torah and in the house of God we would walk בְרָגֶשּׁ, with a multitude.


###### Rashi on Psalms 55:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:15:2)


**בְּבֵית אֱלֹהִים.** בָּתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת:


**in the house of God** In the study-halls.



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Psalms 55:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:16:1)


**יִשַּׁי מָוֶת עָלֵימוֹ.** יַשִּׁיא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עֲלֵיהֶם אֶת מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת, **יִשַּׁי** יְסַכְסֵךְ וְיָסִית לְשׁוֹן ״הַנָּחָשׁ הִשִּׁיאַנִי וָאֹכַל״ (בראשית ג:יג), וּמְנַחֵם פָּתַר **יִשַּׁי** לְשׁוֹן יֵשׁ כְּמוֹ ״אִם יֶשְׁכֶם עוֹשִׂים״ (בראשית כד:מט) ״אֲשֶׁר יֶשְׁנוֹ פֹּה״ (דברים כט:יד):


**May He incite Death upon them** May the Holy One, blessed be He, incite the Angel of Death upon them. Heb. יַשִּׁיא, incite and entice, an expression of (Gen. 3:13): “The serpent enticed me and I ate.” Menachem (p. 101) interpreted יַשִּׁיא, as an expression of יש, there is, as (Gen. 24:49): “If you wish (ישכם) to do kindness”; (Deut. 29:14), “who is (ישנו) here.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 55:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:16:2)


**בִּמְגוּרָם.** בִּמְלוֹנָם:


**in their dwelling** במגורם, in their lodging.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Psalms 55:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:18:1)


**עֶרֶב וָבֹקֶר וְצָהֳרַיִם.** עַרְבִית וְשַׁחֲרִית וּמִנְחָה, שָׁלֹשׁ תְּפִלּוֹת (ברכות כו:):


**Evening, morning, and noontime** The evening prayer, the morning prayer, and the afternoon prayer, three prayers.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Psalms 55:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:19:1)


**מִקְּרָב לִי.** מִן הַמִּלְחָמָה הַבָּאָה עָלַי:


**from the battle that came upon me** from the war that came upon me.


###### Rashi on Psalms 55:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:19:2)


**כִּי בְרַבִּים הָיוּ עִמָּדִי וְגוֹ׳.** כִּי זֹאת עָשָׂה לִי בִּשְׁבִיל הָרַבִּים שֶׁהָיוּ בְּעֶזְרָתִי לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עָלַי, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל וִיהוּדָה אֹהֵב אֶת דָּוִד״ (שמואל א יח:טז):


**because of the many [people who] were with me** For He did this because of the many people who came to my aid to pray on my behalf, as it is stated (I Sam. 18:16): “And all Israel and Judah loved David.”



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Psalms 55:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:20:1)


**יִשְׁמַע אֵל.** תְּפִלָּתָם שֶׁל אוֹתָם רַבִּים:


**May God hear** the prayer of those many people.


###### Rashi on Psalms 55:20:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:20:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:20:2)


**וְיַעֲנֵם.** הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁהוּא **יֹשֵׁב קֶדֶם**:


**and answer them** the King, Who dwells from time immemorial.


###### Rashi on Psalms 55:20:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:20:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:20:3)


**אֲשֶׁר אֵין חֲלִיפוֹת לָמוֹ.** לְאוֹתָם הָרְשָׁעִים הָרוֹדְפִים אוֹתִי אֵין נוֹתְנִים לִבָּם אֶל יוֹם חֲלִיפָתָם, אֵין חֲרֵדִים מִיּוֹם הַמִּיתָה:


**for there is no passing for them** For those wicked men who pursue me. They do not pay heed to the day of their passing, and they do not quake from the day of death.



### Verse 21

###### Rashi on Psalms 55:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:21:1)


**שָׁלַח יָדָיו.** זֶה אֲחִיתֹפֶל הָרָשָׁע (שמואל ב טו:לא):


**He stretched forth his hands** This refers to Ahithophel the wicked.


###### Rashi on Psalms 55:21:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:21:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:21:2)


**שָׁלַח.** טָאנְדִ״יט בְּלַעַ״ז:


**He stretched forth** Heb. שלח, tandit or tondet in Old French, stretched forth, tendait in modern French.


###### Rashi on Psalms 55:21:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:21:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:21:3)


**בִּשְׁלוֹמָיו.** בְּמַה שֶּׁהָיָה שָׁקֵט וְשָׁלֵם עִמּוֹ:


**against him who was at peace with him** Heb. בשלמיו, against him who was tranquil and at peace with him.



### Verse 22

###### Rashi on Psalms 55:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:22:1)


</b>חָלְקוּ.</b> לְשׁוֹן **חֲלַקְלַקּוֹת**:


**Smooth were** Heb. חלקו, an expression of (above 35:6): “and slippery (וחלקלקות).”


###### Rashi on Psalms 55:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:22:2)


**מַחְמָאוֹת.** לְשׁוֹן חֶמְאָה, וְהַמֵּ״ם הָרִאשׁוֹנָה יְסוֹד נוֹפֵל הִיא בַּתֵּיבָה, כְּמֵ״ם שֶׁל מַעֲשֶׂה וּכְמֵ״ם שֶׁל ״מַאֲמָר״ (אסתר א:טו):


**the buttery words of his mouth** Heb. מחמאת, an expression of חמאה butter. The first “mem” is a defective radical in the word, like the “mem” of מעשה and the “mem” of מאמר.


###### Rashi on Psalms 55:22:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:22:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:22:3)


**וּקְרָב לִבּוֹ.** לִבּוֹ לְמִלְחָמָה:


**but his heart was set on war** Heb. וקרב, to war.


###### Rashi on Psalms 55:22:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:22:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:22:4)


**וְהֵמָּה פְתִחוֹת.** מְנַחֵם פָּתַר לְשׁוֹן חֲרָבוֹת, כְּמוֹ ״וְאֶת אֶרֶץ נִמְרֹד בְּפִתְחֶיהָ״ (מיכה ה:ה): כְּפִיּוֹת חֶרֶב (ס״א אינו). וְאוֹמֵר אֲנִי: לְשׁוֹן קְלָלָה הוּא בִּלְשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי, כְּדַאֲמַר: כָּתַב אֲמֵימַר פְּתִיחָא עֲלָהּ – וְהוּא שְׁטַר שַׁמְתָּא:


**but they are curses** Heb. פתחות. Menachem (p. 147) interpreted it as an expression of swords, as (Micah 5:5): “and the land of Nimrod with its swords (בפתחיה),” with the edges of the sword. I say, however, that it is an expression of curse in Aramaic, as the Talmud (R.H. 31b) states: Amemar wrote a pethicha on her, which is a warrant decreeing excommunication.



### Verse 23

###### Rashi on Psalms 55:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:23:1)


**יְהָבְךָ.** מַשָּׂאֲךָ, רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מֵשִׁיב לוֹ כֵּן:


**your burden** Heb. יהבך, your burden. The Holy Spirit answers him thus.


###### Rashi on Psalms 55:23:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:23:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:23:2)


**יְכַלְכְּלֶךָ.** יִסְבּוֹל מַשָּׂאֲךָ, כְּמוֹ (מלכים א ח:כז) ״הַשָּׁמַיִם וּשְׁמֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם לֹא יְכַלְכְּלוּךָ״. לְשׁוֹן ״כִּלְכּוּל״ מְתֻרְגָּם ״מְסוֹבַר״ כְּתַרְגּוּם יוֹנָתָן בֶּן עֻזִּיאֵל:


**and He will bear you** Heb. יכלכלך. He will bear your burden, as (I Kings 8:27): “the heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain You (יכלכלוך). The expression of כלכול is rendered מסובר, bearing, in Targum Jonathan ben Uzziel.


###### Rashi on Psalms 55:23:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:23:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/55:23:3)


**מוֹט.** מְעִידַת רֶגֶל:


**to falter** Heb. מוט, the faltering of the foot.



## Chapter 56


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 56:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:1:1)


**יוֹנַת אֵלֶם רְחוֹקִים.** עַל עַצְמוֹ אָמַר, שֶׁהָיָה רָחוֹק מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵצֶל אָכִישׁ, וְהָיוּ אֶחָיו שֶׁל גָּלְיָת מְבַקְּשִׁים רְשׁוּת מֵאָכִישׁ לְהָרְגוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״הֲלֹא זֶה דָּוִד מֶלֶךְ הָאָרֶץ״ (שמואל א כא:יב), וְהוּא הָיָה בֵּינֵיהֶם כְּיוֹנָה אִלֶּמֶת (סוטה י:):


**yonath elem rehokim** He said this concerning himself, for he was with Achish, far from the land of Israel, and Goliath’s brothers were requesting permission from Achish to kill him, as it is said (I Sam. 21:12): “Is this not David, the king of the land?” And he was among them as a mute dove.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 56:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:2:1)


**שְׁאָפַנִי.** מְצַפִּים לְבָלְעֵנִי, גולושי״ר בְּלַעַ״ז, כְּמוֹ ״שָׁאֲפָה רוּחַ״ (ירמיה ב:כד):


**yearn** Heb. שאפנו, yearn to swallow me up, goloseir or goloser, to long, to be impatient. (Cf. Rashi to Amos 2:7.) As (Jer. 2:24): “that snuffs up (שאפה) the wind.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 56:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:2:2)


**לֹחֵם.** לְשׁוֹן מִלְחָמָה:


**the warrior** Heb. לחם, an expression of war (מלחמה).



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 56:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:3:1)


**מָרוֹם.** הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, שֶׁהוּא יוֹשֵׁב מָרוֹם:


**O Most High** The Holy One blessed be He, Who dwells on High.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 56:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:5:1)


**בֵּאלֹהִים אֲהַלֵּל דְּבָרוֹ.** אַף בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהוּא בָּא עִמִּי בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין, אֲהַלֵּל דְּבָרוֹ וְאֶבְטַח בּוֹ:


**With God, I will praise His word** Even when He deals with me with the Divine standard of justice I will praise His word and trust in Him.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 56:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:6:1)


**כָּל הַיּוֹם דְּבָרַי יְעַצֵּבוּ.** מְעַצְּבִים אוֹתִי רוֹדְפַי, עַד שֶׁכָּל דִּבְרֵי פִּי עֶצֶב וּצְעָקָה:


**All day long, my words grieve [me]** My pursuers grieve me until all the words of my mouth are grief and cries.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 56:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:7:1)


**יָגוּרוּ יִצְפּוֹנוּ.** הֵמָּה אוֹרְבִים וְלָנִים בַּמָּקוֹם שֶׁהֵם מְקַוִּים שֶׁאֲנִי אֵלֵךְ שָׁם, וְשׁוֹמְרִים אֶת עֲקֵבַי, טר״צש בְּלַעַ״ז, לְרַגְּלֵנִי וּלְהוֹלִיךְ רוֹדְפַי שָׁם. כָּל זֶה הָיָה מְקֻבָּל עַל רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָאוֹרְבִים לוֹ, וּמֵאֵימָתָם בָּרַח אֵצֶל אָכִישׁ (שמואל א כא:יא):


**They lodge, they hide** They lurk and lodge in the place they hope I will go, and they watch my steps (traces in French, tracks, explained in Gen. 49:19, Song of Songs 1:8) to spy on me and to lead pursuers there. All this he would complain about the wicked of Israel: that they would lie in wait for him and out of fear of them he had fled to Achish.


###### Rashi on Psalms 56:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:7:2)


**יָגוּרוּ.** יָלִינוּ:


###### Rashi on Psalms 56:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:7:3)


**יִצְפּוֹנוּ.** יֶאֱרֹבוּ:


**they hide** They lurk.


###### Rashi on Psalms 56:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:7:4)


**כַּאֲשֶׁר קִוּוּ נַפְשִׁי.** כְּשֶׁהֵם יוֹדְעִים וּמְקַוִּים לִי: דֶּרֶךְ זוֹ יֵלֵךְ:


**when they hope for my life** When they know [that I will pass] and hope for me, “He will go this way.”



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 56:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:8:1)


**עַל אָוֶן פַּלֶּט לָמוֹ.** לִמְצוֹא הַצָּלָה וְעֹשֶׁר עַל דְּבַר עָוֹן וָרֶשַׁע, **פַּלֶּט** כְּמוֹ לְפַלֵּט; מְצַפִּים שָׂכָר מֵאֵת שָׁאוּל עַל כָּךְ:


**For iniquity, they expect rescue** To find rescue and riches for a matter of iniquity and wickedness. And פַלֶט is like לפלט, to rescue. They expect reward from Saul for that.


###### Rashi on Psalms 56:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:8:2)


**בְּאַף עַמִּים הוֹרֵד.** בְּאַפְּךָ הוֹרֵד אוּמָּה זוֹ שֶׁאֲנִי בְּתוֹכָם מֵחָכְמָתָם וּמִמַּחְשְׁבוֹתָם, שֶׁאוֹמְרִים לְהָרְגֵנִי:


**Bring down...with anger** With Your anger, bring down this nation in whose midst I am, from their wisdom and from the plots that they devise to kill me.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 56:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:9:1)


**נוֹדִי סָפַרְתָּה.** אַתָּה יָדַעְתָּ מִנְיַן הַמְּקוֹמוֹת שֶׁנָּדַדְתִּי לִבְרֹחַ:


**You counted my wanderings** You know the number of the places to which I wandered, to flee.


###### Rashi on Psalms 56:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:9:2)


**שִׂימָה דִמְעָתִי בְנֹאדֶךָ.** שִׂים דִּמְעָתִי בְּנֹאד שֶׁלְּךָ, וּתְהֵא שְׁמוּרָה לְפָנֶיךָ:


**place my tears in Your flask** Place my tears in Your flask, and let them be preserved before You.


###### Rashi on Psalms 56:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:9:3)


**הֲלֹא בְּסִפְרָתֶךָ.** בְּמִנְיָנְךָ תִּתְּנֶנָּה, לִמְנוֹתָהּ עִם שְׁאָר צָרוֹתַי. (וּמְנַחֵם חֲבֵרוֹ לְשׁוֹן סֵפֶר מַמָּשׁ):


**Is it not in Your accounting** Place them in Your accounting, to count them with the rest of my troubles. Menachem, however, associated it (p. 128) as an expression of an actual book.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 56:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:11:1)


**בֵּאלֹהִים אֲהַלֵּל, בַּה׳ אֲהַלֵּל.** עַל מִדַּת הַדִּין וְעַל מִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים אֲהַלֵּל (ירושלמי ברכות ט,ה):


**With God I will praise a word; with the Lord I will praise** For the Divine standard of justice and for the Divine standard of mercy I will praise.



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Psalms 56:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/56:14:1)


**בְּאוֹר הַחַיִּים.** לָשׁוּב לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל:


**in the light of life** To return to the Land of Israel.



## Chapter 57


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 57:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:1:1)


**לַמְנַצֵּחַ אַל תַּשְׁחֵת.** כָּךְ כִּנָּה דָּוִד הַמִּזְמוֹר הַזֶּה בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁהָיָה קָרוֹב לָמוּת, וְיִסֵּד מִזְמוֹר זֶה לֵאמֹר: אַל תַּשְׁחֵת אוֹתִי ה׳:


**For the conductor, al tashcheth** David called this psalm by this name because he was near death, and he established this psalm, saying, “Do not destroy me, O Lord.”



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 57:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:2:1)


**חָנֵּנִי, חָנֵּנִי.** חָנֵּנִי שֶׁלֹּא אֶהֱרֹג וְשֶׁלֹּא אֵהָרֵג (שמואל א כד:יא):


**Be gracious to me, etc., be gracious to me** that I should neither kill nor be killed.


###### Rashi on Psalms 57:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:2:2)


**עַד יַעֲבֹר הַוּוֹת.** עַד תַּעֲבֹר הָרָעָה:


**until the destruction passes** Heb. הוות, until the evil passes.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 57:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:4:1)


**חֵרֵף שֹׁאֲפִי.** וְיוֹשִׁיעֵנִי מֵחֶרְפַּת שֹׁאֲפִי הָאוֹמֵר לְבָלְעֵנִי. שֹׁאֲפִי גּוֹלוֹשְׁנְטְמוֹ״י בְּלַעַ״ז:


**from the disgrace of him who yearns to swallow me up** And He will save me from the disgrace of ֹשֹאַפִי, who says to swallow me up, golosa moy in Old French, longs to swallow me up. (See above 56: 2.)



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 57:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:5:1)


**נַפְשִׁי בְּתוֹךְ לְבָאִם.** אַבְנֵר וְעַמָשָׂא, שֶׁהָיוּ לְבָאִים בַּתּוֹרָה וְאֵינָם מוֹחִים בְּשָׁאוּל:


**My soul is among lions** Abner and Amassa, who were “lions” [leaders] the in Torah, and who do not protest against Saul.


###### Rashi on Psalms 57:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:5:2)


**אֶשְׁכְּבָה לוֹהֲטִים.** אֶשְׁכְּבָה בְּלוֹהֲטִים, אַנְפַנְבְּלוֹיְיאַנְ״ץ בְּלַעַ״ז, בֵּין הַזִּיפִים שֶׁלּוֹהֲטִים אַחַר לָשׁוֹן הָרָע (שמואל א כג:יט-כ):


**I lie among men who are aflame** En flanboyanz, or enflamoyonz, among those who are flaming. Among the Ziphim, who are aflame after slander.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 57:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:6:1)


**רוּמָה עַל הַשָּׁמַיִם.** הִסְתַּלֵּק מִן הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים, שֶׁאֵינָם כְּדַי שֶׁתִּשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָתְךָ בֵּינֵיהֶם, וְ**עַל הָאָרֶץ** תִּתְכַּבֵּד בָּזוֹ:


**Be exalted above the heavens** Withdraw from the earthlings, who are unworthy of having Your Shechinah rest among them, and on the earth You shall be honored by this.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 57:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:7:1)


**כָּפַף נַפְשִׁי.** הָאוֹיֵב:


**he bent down my soul** i.e., the enemy.


###### Rashi on Psalms 57:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:7:2)


**נָפְלוּ בְתוֹכָהּ.** סוֹפָן לִיפּוֹל בְּתוֹכָהּ. כָּפַף קְלִינָ״א בְּלַעַ״ז, לְשׁוֹן ״וְזוֹקֵף לְכָל הַכְּפוּפִים״ (תהלים קמה:יד):


**they will fall into it** They will ultimately fall into it. כפף is cline, or clina in Old French, bent, bent down, an expression of (below 145:14): “and straightens all who are bent down (הכפופים).”



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 57:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:8:1)


**נָכוֹן לִבִּי אֱלֹהִים נָכוֹן לִבִּי.** נֶאֱמָן עִמְּךָ בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין וְנֶאֱמָן עִמְּךָ בְּמִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים (ירושלמי ברכות ט,ה):


**My heart is steadfast with God, my heart is steadfast** Faithful to You in the Divine standard of justice and faithful to You in the Divine standard of mercy.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 57:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:9:1)


**עוּרָה כְבוֹדִי.** וְלֹא אִישַׁן עַד שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁעוֹת בִּכְבוֹדִי כִּשְׁאָר מְלָכִים (משנה ברכות א:ב):


**Awaken, my honor** and let me not sleep until three hours [of the day have passed], as other kings do.


###### Rashi on Psalms 57:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:9:2)


**עוּרָה הַנֵּבֶל וְכִנּוֹר.** הָעִירָה אוֹתִי אַתָּה, הַנֵּבֶל וְכִנּוֹר הַתָּלוּי עַל מִטָּתִי, פָּתוּחַ לְצַד הַצָּפוֹן; וְכֵיוָן שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ חֲצוֹת לַיְלָה, רוּחַ צְפוֹנִית מְנַשֶּׁבֶת בּוֹ, וְדָוִד עוֹמֵד וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה (ברכות ג:):


**awaken [me], lyre and harp** Awaken me, you lyre and harp hanging on my bed, open to the north side. And as soon as midnight arrived, the north wind would blow on it, and David would get up and engage in Torah.


###### Rashi on Psalms 57:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/57:9:3)


**אָעִירָה שָּׁחַר.** אֲנִי מְעוֹרֵר אֶת הַשַּׁחַר, וְאֵין הַשַּׁחַר מְעוֹרְרֵנִי (ברכות ג:):


**I will awaken the dawn** I awaken the dawn; the dawn does not awaken me.



## Chapter 58


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 58:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:1:1)


**מִכְתָּם.** שֵׁם נְעִימוּת שִׁיר:


**michtam** The name of the melody of a song.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 58:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:2:1)


**הַאֻמְנָם.** לְשׁוֹן אֱמוּנָה הוּא:


**Is it true** Heb. האמנם. This is an expression of truth.


###### Rashi on Psalms 58:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:2:2)


**הַאֻמְנָם אֵלֶם צֶדֶק תְּדַבֵּרוּן וְגוֹ׳.** מִזְמוֹר זֶה אָמַר עַל שֶׁבָּא אֶל הַמַּעְגָּל אֲשֶׁר שָׁאוּל שׁוֹכֵב שָׁם, וְלָקַח אֶת הַחֲנִית וְאֶת הַצַּפַּחַת וְהָלַךְ לוֹ, וְקָרָא: ״הֲלֹא תַעֲנֶה אַבְנֵר״ (שמואל א כו:יד), כְּלוֹמַר: הֲלֹא יֵשׁ לְךָ עַתָּה לְהוֹכִיחַ לְשָׁאוּל וּלְהַרְאוֹתוֹ, שֶׁעַל חִנָּם הוּא רוֹדְפֵנִי; שֶׁאִלּוּ רָצִיתִי הֲרַגְתִּיו. וְכָךְ אָמַר בְּשִׁירוֹ: הַאֻמְנָם נֶאֱלַם מִפִּיכֶם הַצֶּדֶק שֶׁהָיָה לָכֶם לְדַבֵּר, וְהַמֵּישָׁרִים שֶׁהָיָה לָכֶם לִשְׁפֹּט **הַצֶּדֶק אֲשֶׁר תְּדַבֵּרוּן**:


**Is it true that you were silent about the righteousness that you should have spoken, etc.** He recited this psalm concerning [the incident] when he entered the barricade where Saul was lying, took the spear and the jug, went away, and called, “Will you not answer, Abner?” (I Sam. 26:14). That is to say, “Shouldn’t you now prove to Saul and show him that he pursues me for no reason? For had I wished, I would have killed him.” And so did he say in his song: Is it true that the righteousness that you should have said and the equities with which you should have judged have been silenced from your mouth? The righteousness that you should have spoken.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 58:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:3:1)


**אַף בְּלֵב עוֹלוֹת תִּפְעָלוּן.** וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁבִּלְבַבְכֶם אַתֶּם חוֹרְשִׁים רָעָה לִפְעוֹל עָוֶל:


**Even in your heart, you plot injustice** And not only that, but in your heart you plot evil, to do injustice.


###### Rashi on Psalms 58:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:3:2)


**עוֹלוֹת.** כְּמוֹ עֲוָלוֹת, כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵאָמֵר מִן שׁוֹר – שְׁוָרִים, וּמֵעִיר – עֲיָרִים: ״וּשְׁלֹשִׁים עֲיָרִים לָהֶם״ (שופטים י:ד), שֶׁהֵם לְשׁוֹן עִיר וְקִרְיָה:


**injustice** lit. wrongs, like עַוָלוֹת as one says from שוֹר, שורים, and from עיר, עירים (Jud. 10: 4): “and they had thirty cities (עירים),” which is an expression of עיר, a city.


###### Rashi on Psalms 58:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:3:3)


**בָּאָרֶץ חֲמַס יְדֵיכֶם תְּפַלֵּסוּן.** בְּתוֹךְ הָאָרֶץ אַתֶּם מַכְרִיעִים חֲמַס יְדֵיכֶם, עַד שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹקֵל מִשְׁקָל רַב. תְּפַלֵּסוּן קוֹנְטֶרְפֵּיי״שׁץ בְּלַעַ״ז:


**in the earth, you weigh down the violence of your hands** Inside the earth, you weigh down the violence of your hands until it is very heavy. תְפַלֵּסוּן is contrepesez or contrepezeres in Old French, you outweigh. (See Isa. 26:7.)



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 58:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:4:1)


**זֹרוּ רְשָׁעִים מֵרָחֶם.** מִמְּעֵי אִמָּם הֵם נַעֲשִׂים זָרִים לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁעָשָׂה עֵשָׂו: ״וַיִּתְרוֹצְצוּ הַבָּנִים בְּקִרְבָּהּ״ (בראשית כה:כב):


**The wicked become estranged [even] from the womb** From their mother’s womb they become strange to the Holy One, blessed be He, in the way that Esau did (Gen. 25:22): “And the children moved violently against each other in her womb.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 58:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:4:2)


**זֹרוּ.** נָזוֹרוּ, כְּמוֹ ״שֹׁמּוּ שָׁמַיִם״ (ירמיהו ב:יב), ״וַיְמָרְרֻהוּ וָרֹבּוּ״ (בראשית מט:כג), ״רֹמּוּ מְעָט״ (איוב כד:כד), כֻּלָּן לְשׁוֹן נִפְעֲלוּ:


**become estranged** Heb. זֹרו, like נזורוּ, the same construction as (Jer. 2:12): “O heavens (שֹֹֹמו), be astonished”; (Gen. 49:23), “they heaped bitter abuse upon him and became [his] opponents (ורֹבו)”; (Job 24:24), “They are taken away (רוֹמוּ) in a second.” All these are in the passive voice.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 58:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:5:1)


**חֲמַת לָמוֹ.** אֶרֶס יֵשׁ לָהֶם לַהֲרוֹג אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת **כִּדְמוּת** הַנָּחָשׁ:


**They have venom** They have venom to kill people, like the venom of a serpent.


###### Rashi on Psalms 58:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:5:2)


**כְּמוֹ פֶתֶן חֵרֵשׁ יַאְטֵם אָזְנוֹ.** הַנָּחָשׁ, כְּשֶׁהוּא מַזְקִין, נַעֲשֶׂה חֵרֵשׁ בְּאָזְנוֹ אַחַת וְאוֹטֵם הַשֵּׁנִית בֶּעָפָר, שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁמַע אֶת הַלַּחַשׁ, כְּשֶׁחַבָּר מַשְׁבִּיעוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יַזִּיק:


**like a deaf cobra that closes its ear** When the snake ages, it becomes deaf in one ear, and closes the other ear with dust so that it should not hear the incantation of the charmer, adjuring it not to cause injury.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 58:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:6:1)


**אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִשְׁמַע וְגוֹ׳.** מְחֻבָּר לַמִּקְרָא שֶׁלְּפָנָיו, וְאוֹטֵם אָזְנוֹ בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁמַע לְקוֹל מְלַחֲשִׁים:


**Which will not hear, etc.** This is connected to the preceding verse: “and it closes its ear in order not to hear the voice of charmers.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 58:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:6:2)


**חוֹבֵר חֲבָרִים.** שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לִלְחוֹשׁ אֶת הַנְּחָשִׁים (שבת קנג:):


**caster of spells** who knows how to charm snakes.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 58:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:7:1)


**מַלְתְּעוֹת.** שִׁנַּיִם הַפְּנִימִיּוֹת, שֶׁקּוֹרִין מייש״ליש בְּלַעַ״ז:


**molars** The inner teeth, called messelers in Old French, molars, grinders.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 58:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:8:1)


**יִמָּאֲסוּ.** לְעַצְמָם שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִמְאָסִים בְּעֵינֵיהֶם מִדְּאָגָה, וּכְמוֹ בַמַּיִם יִתְהַלָּכוּ. דּוּגְמָתוֹ (יחזקאל כא:יב) ״כָּל בִּרְכַּיִם תֵּלַכְנָה מַּיִם״ מִדְּמָעוֹת (ס״א אינו):


**Let them be rejected** by themselves, that they will be rejected in their own eyes from worry, and as [if] in water let them walk. Similar to this is (Ezek. 7:17): “and all knees will go [as in] water,” from tears.


###### Rashi on Psalms 58:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:8:2)


**יִדְרֹךְ חִצָּיו.** הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְנֶגְדָּם, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְמוֹלְלוּ. יִתְמוֹלְלוּ שיאנ״ט פרוייאיי״ץ בְּלַעַ״ז:


**He will aim His arrows** i.e., the Holy One, blessed be He, so that they will be cut off. יתמֹללוּ is soyent preciz, let them be cut off.



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 58:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:9:1)


**שַׁבְּלוּל.** יֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִין לימצ״א בְּלַעַ״ז, וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִין כְּמוֹ ״שִׁבֹּלֶת מַיִם״ (תהלים סט:ג), וְכָפַל הַלָּמֶ״ד כְּמוֹ מִן ״יִמַּל קְצִירוֹ״ (איוב יח:טז), ״יְמוֹלֵל״ (תהלים צ:ו):


**a snail** Heb. שבלול. Some interpret it as limace in Old French, a snail (as in Lev. 11:30). Others interpret it as שבֹּלת, a current of water (below 69:16). The “lammed” is doubled, as from (Job 18: 16): “his branch will be cut off (ימל) ; (below 90:6), “will be cut off (ימולל) and will dry up.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 58:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:9:2)


**תֶּמֶס.** נָמֵס וְהוֹלֵךְ, **תֶּמֶס** שֵׁם דָּבָר הוּא, הַמֵּ״ם יְסוֹד וְעִקָּר הוּא, וְהַתָּי״ו בּוֹ יְסוֹד נוֹפֵל, כְּמוֹ תָּי״ו שֶׁל ״תֶּבֶל עָשׂוּ״ (ויקרא כ:יב):


**melts** it continuously melts. תֶּמֶס is a noun, the “mem” being the fundamental radical and the “tav” a defective radical, like the “tav” of (Lev. 20:12): “they committed a disgraceful act (תבל).”


###### Rashi on Psalms 58:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:9:3)


**נֵפֶל אֵשֶׁת.** טַלְפָּ״א בְּלַעַ״ז, שֶׁאֵין לָהּ עֵינַיִם, וְהִיא ״תִּנְשֶׁמֶת״ (ויקרא יא:ל) דִּמְתַרְגְּמִינָן ״אֲשׁוּתָא״, כָּךְ פֵּרְשׁוּהוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ (מועד קטן ו:). וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִין: נֵפֶל שֶׁל אִשָּׁה. כְּמוֹ ״אֵשֶׁת הַזִּמָּה״ (יחזקאל כג:מד), וְיֵשׁ תָּי״ו בְּלֹא דְבֵקוּת כְּמוֹ ״עֲטֶרֶת תִּפְאֶרֶת תְּמַגְּנֶךָּ״ (משלי ד:ט), כְּמוֹ נֵפֶל שֶׁל אִשָּׁה שֶׁלֹּא חָזוּ הַנְּפָלִים שֶׁמֶשׁ. וְלַלָּשׁוֹן רִאשׁוֹן הֲוֵי נֵפֶל וְאֵשֶׁת כְּמוֹ ״וַאֲנִי כְּכֶבֶשׂ אַלּוּף״ (ירמיה יא:יט) שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹ כֶּבֶשׂ וְאַלּוּף, וּפֵירֵשׁ מְנַחֵם כְּכֶבֶשׂ וְאַלּוּף הוּא שׁוֹר, אַף כָּאן נֵפֶל וְאֵשֶׁת (צִוָּה לְהַגִּיהַּ ס״א אינו):


**a mole** Heb. נפל אשת, talpe in Old French, which has no eyes. It is identified as תִּנְשֶׁמֶת (in Lev. 11:30), translated [by Onkelos] as אשותא. So did our Sages explain it (M.K. 6b). Others explain it as a stillbirth of a woman. אשת is like (Ezek. 23:44): “women of (אשת) lewdness.” There is a “tav” without the construct state, as (Prov. 4:9): “she will transmit to you, a crown of glory (עטרת תפארת),” like “a stillbirth of a woman (אשה),” for the stillbirths born did not see the sun. According to the former explanation, it is like נפל ואשת, a stillbirth and a mole, as (Jer. 11:19): “And I was like a lamb a bull (ככבש אלוף),” which Menachem explained: like a lamb and a bull (ככבש ואלוף). That is, a bull; here too, a stillbirth and a mole נפל ואשת. It is proper to emend.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 58:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:10:1)


**בְּטֶרֶם יָבִינוּ סִירוֹתֵיכֶם אָטָד.** אֲשֶׁר בְּטֶרֶם יֵדְעוּ קוֹצִים רַכִּים שֶׁלָּכֶם לִהְיוֹת אֲטָדִים קָשִׁים, כְּלוֹמַר: עַד שֶׁלֹּא יִגְדְּלוּ בְּנֵי הָרְשָׁעִים:


**Before your tender briars develop into hardened thorns** lit. before your tender briars know hardened thorns. That before your tender briars know to be hardened thorns, i.e., before the children of the wicked grow up.


###### Rashi on Psalms 58:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:10:2)


**כְּמוֹ חַי כְּמוֹ חָרוֹן.** כְּלוֹמַר: בִּגְבוּרָה וּבְחֹזֶק וּבְחָרוֹן יִסְעָרֵם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:


**with vigor, with wrath** i.e., with might, with strength, and with wrath will the Holy One, blessed be He, drive them away as [with] a storm wind.


###### Rashi on Psalms 58:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:10:3)


**חַי.** לְשׁוֹן גְּבוּרָה:


**with vigor** חי is an expression of might.



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Psalms 58:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/58:12:1)


**וְיֹאמַר אָדָם אַךְ פְּרִי לַצַּדִּיק.** וְאָז יֹאמְרוּ הַבְּרִיּוֹת: וַדַּאי יֵשׁ פֵּרוֹת וְתַשְׁלוּם שָׂכָר בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַצַּדִּיקִים, שֶׁנָּקַם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִקְמָתָם:


**And man will say, “Truly, the righteous man has reward”** Then people will say, “Surely there is reward and recompense in the deeds of the righteous, since the Holy One, blessed be He, avenged their wrongs.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 58:12:2

**there is a God** A Judge, Who judges the wicked on the earth.



## Chapter 59


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 59:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/59:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/59:1:1)


**אַל תַּשְׁחֵת.** כָּךְ קָרָא שֵׁם הַמִּזְמוֹר, עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהָיָה קָרוֹב לָמוּת וְלִהְיוֹת נִשְׁחָת, מְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל הַדָּבָר:


**al tashcheth** He called the psalm by this name because he was close to dying and to being destroyed, and he begged for mercy in the matter.


###### Rashi on Psalms 59:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/59:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/59:1:2)


**וַיִּשְׁמְרוּ אֶת הַבַּיִת.** כְּשֶׁאָמְרָה לָהֶם מִיכַל: ״חוֹלֶה הוּא״ (שמואל א יט:יד), וְהִבְרִיחַתּוֹ בַּלַּיְלָה:


**and they guarded the house** when Michal told them that he was ill (I Sam. 19:14) and she allowed him to flee at night.

**arise to visit upon all the nations** And judge these wicked men according to the statutes of the nations. Do not be gracious to them.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 59:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/59:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/59:7:1)


**יָשׁוּבוּ לָעֶרֶב וְגוֹ׳, הִנֵּה יַבִּיעוּן בְּפִיהֶם.** פִּתְרוֹן שְׁנֵי מִקְרָאוֹת הַלָּלוּ נוֹפֵל זֶה עַל זֶה, **יָשׁוּבוּ לָעֶרֶב** לֹא דַיָּם מַה שֶּׁעָשׂוּ בַּיּוֹם אֶלָּא אַף לָעֶרֶב יָשׁוּבוּ עַל רָעָתָם לִשְׁמֹר שֶׁלֹּא אֶבְרַח וְאֵצֵא מִן הָעִיר, וּמַה עָשׂוּ בַּיּוֹם? הִנֵּה כָּל הַיּוֹם יַבִּיעוּ בְּפִיהֶם לְרַגֵּל עָלַי אֶל שָׁאוּל:


**They return in the evening, etc...** **Behold, they spew forth with their mouth** The interpretation of these two verses connects one to the other. **They return in the evening** What they did by day does not suffice them; in the evening they repeat their evil: guarding me that I do not escape and leave the city Now what did they do by day? Behold, all day they spew forth with their mouth, to spy on me to Saul.

## Chapter 60


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 60:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:1:1)


**עַל שׁוּשַׁן עֵדוּת מִכְתָּם לְדָוִד לְלַמֵּד.** (תוספת מִכְתָּם לְשׁוֹן ״כֶּתֶם פָּז״ (שיר השירים ה:יא) דָּבָר חָמוּד, וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָּרְשׁוּ עַל דָּוִד שֶׁהָיָה מַנְהִיג עַצְמוֹ כְּמָךְ וְתָם אֲפִלּוּ בְּמַלְכוּתוֹ וְאַגָּדָה אַחֶרֶת שֶׁהָיְתָה מַכָּתוֹ תַמָּה שֶׁנּוֹלַד מָהוּל עד כאן ס״א אינו) מִכְתָּם לְדָוִד עַל עֵדוּתָן שֶׁל סַנְהֶדְרִין שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלוּ לְשׁוֹשַׁנָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״שָׁרְרֵךְ אַגַּן הַסַּהַר וְגוֹ׳״ (שיר השירים ז:ג) ״סוּגָה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים״, כְּשֶׁנִּצְרַךְ שֶׁיְּלַמְּדוּהוּ מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה כְּשֶׁנִּלְחַם עִם אֲרַם נַהֲרַיִם וְשָׁלַח אֶת יוֹאָב עֲלֵיהֶם, אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְיוֹאָב וְלֹא מִבָּנָיו שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אַתֶּם הֵיכָן הִיא הַשְּׁבוּעָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּע לְלָבָן ״עַד הַגַּל הַזֶּה״ (בראשית לא:נב), וְלֹא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ מַה לְּהָשִׁיב, בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל דָּוִד אָמַר לְדָוִד כָּךְ אָמְרוּ לִי בְּנֵי אֲרָם בָּאוּ וְשָׁאֲלוּ אֶת סַנְהֶדְרִין אָמְרוּ לָהֶם וְלֹא הֵם עָבְרוּ תְּחִלָּה אֶת הַשְּׁבוּעָה שֶׁאָמַר (במדבר כג:ז) ״מִן אֲרָם יַנְחֵנִי בָלָק מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב״, וְעוֹד כּוּשַׁן רִשְׁעָתַיִם (שופטים ג:ח) אֲרַמִּי הָיָה:


**on shushan eduth, a michtam of David, to teach** (Addendum: Michtam is an expression of (Song 5: 11), “as finest gold (כתם פז),” a coveted thing. Our Sages, however, expounded this as referring to David, who behaved as a humble (מך) and innocent man, even when he occupied the throne. Another Aggadah explains that his wound (מכתו) was perfect (תמה), i.e., he was born circumcised (Sotah 10b). Michtam of David concerning the testimony of the Sanhedrin, who were compared to a rose (שושן), as it is stated (Song 7:3): “Your navel is like a round basin, etc., fenced in with roses,” when he required that they teach him what to do. When he fought with Aram Naharaim and sent Joab against them, they said to Joab, “Aren’t you of the sons of Jacob? Where is the oath that he swore to Laban, ‘this pile is a witness’” (Gen. 31:52)? And he did not know what to answer. He came to David and said to David, “This is what the Arameans said to me.” They went and asked the Sanhedrin, [who] replied to them, “Did they not transgress the oath first, as it is stated (Num. 23:7): ‘From Aram has Balak king of Moab brought me’? Moreover, Cushan-Rishathaim was an Aramean.”



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 60:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:2:1)


**בְּהַצּוֹתוֹ.** כְּמוֹ ״בְּהַצּוֹתָם עַל ה׳״ (במדבר כו:ט), שֶׁנִּלְחַם בָּהֶם עַל שֶׁעָזְרוּ לִבְנֵי עַמּוֹן:


**and Joab returned and smote of Edom, etc.** [of] the eighteen thousand stated in Scripture (II Sam. 8:13, I Chron. 18:12), Abishai slew six thousand the first time, and Joab slew twelve thousand when he returned from battling Aram.


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:2:2)


**וַיָּשָׁב יוֹאָב וַיַּךְ אֶת אֱדוֹם וְגוֹ׳.** שְׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר אֶלֶף הַכְּתוּבִים בִּמְלָכִים (שמואל ב ח:יג) וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים (דברי הימים א יח:יב) הָרַג אֲבִישַׁי פַּעַם רִאשׁוֹנָה, שֵׁשֶׁת אֲלָפִים, וְיוֹאָב שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר אֶלֶף, כְּשֶׁשָּׁב מֵהַכּוֹת אֶת אֲרָם:


**When he fought** Heb. בהצותו, as (Num. 26:9): “when they quarreled (בהצותם) with the Lord,” that he fought with them because they aided the Ammonites.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 60:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:3:1)


**זְנַחְתָּנוּ פְרַצְתָּנוּ.** כְּשֶׁנָּפְלָה אֱדוֹם בְּיָדוֹ, צָפָה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁעֲתִידִים אֲדוֹמִיִּים לִמְשֹׁל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְלִגְזֹר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל גְּזֵרוֹת רָעוֹת. עָמַד וּבִקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל שִׁעְבּוּד הַגָּלֻיּוֹת. הַרְבֵּה צָרוֹת סָבַלְנוּ בִּימֵי הַשּׁוֹפְטִים מֵאוֹיְבֵינוּ סָבִיב:


**You have forsaken us; You have breached us** When Edom fell into his hand, he foresaw with the holy spirit that they are destined to rule over Israel and to levy evil decrees upon Israel. He stood up and begged for mercy on account of the subjugation of the exile. “We suffered many troubles in the time of the Judges from the enemies around us.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:3:2)


**אָנַפְתָּ.** קָצַפְתָּ עָלֵינוּ, מֵעַתָּה **תְּשׁוֹבֵב** רְצוֹנְךָ עָלֵינוּ:


**You were angry** You were angry with us. From now on, restore Your goodwill upon us.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 60:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:4:1)


**הִרְעַשְׁתָּה.** אַרְצֵנוּ בְּכַמָּה גְּיָסוֹת:


**You caused...to quake** our land, with many troops.


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:4:2)


**פְּצַמְתָּהּ.** שָׁבַרְתָּ אוֹתָהּ, וְרָאִיתִי בְּדִבְרֵי דוּנָשׁ שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן עֲרָבִי, אֲבָל לֹא פֵּרֵשׁ אוֹתוֹ. וּבִיסוֹדוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֹשֶׁה הַדַּרְשָׁן פֵּרְשׁוֹ לְשׁוֹן קְרִיעָה, וּרְאָיָה הֵבִיא לַדָּבָר: ״וְקָרַע לוֹ חַלּוֹנָי״ (ירמיהו כב:יד) מְתֻרְגָּם: ״וּפְצִים״. אַךְ אֲנִי אוֹמֵר: ״וּפְצִים״ שֶׁתִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן – לְשׁוֹן תִּקּוּן חַלּוֹן הוּא, כְּכָל הַפְּתָחִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם פְּצִימִין (מנחות לד.):


**You split it** Heb. פצמתה, You broke it. I saw in Dunash’s writings (p. 68) that it is Arabic, but he did not explain it. In the works of Rabbi Moshe Hadarshan, he explains it as an expression of tearing and cites evidence for that assertion (from Jer. 22:14): “And he cuts out windows,” which Jonathan translates, וּפצים. But I say that וּפצים, as Jonathan translated, is an expression of the construction of a window, as “all the entrances that have door frames (פצימין).”


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:4:3)


**רְפָה שְׁבָרֶיהָ כִּי מָטָה.** לְשׁוֹן רְפוּאָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּהֵ״א. הַרְבֵּה תֵּיבוֹת מְשַׁמְּשׁוֹת כֵּן:


**heal its breaches for it has faltered** Heb. רפה, an expression of healing. Although it is spelled with a “hey,” many words are used in this manner.


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:4:4)


**כִּי מָטָה.** לְשׁוֹן שִׁפְלוּת:


**for it has faltered** An expression of lowliness.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 60:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:5:1)


**יַיִן תַּרְעֵלָה.** הָאוֹטֵם אֶת הַלֵּב וְעוֹטְפוֹ. רַעַל לְשׁוֹן עֲטִיפָה הוּא, כְּמוֹ ״וְהַבְּרוֹשִׁים הָרְעָלוּ״ (נחום ב:ד). וּבִלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה: מָדִיּוֹת רְעוּלוֹת (שבת ו:ו):


**wine of bewilderment** Heb. תרעלה. [Wine] that stops up the heart and envelops it. רַעַל is an expression of envelopment, as (Nahum 2:4): “and the cypresses are enwrapped (הרעלו),” and the language of the Mishnah (Shab. 6:6): “Median women shawled (רעולות).”



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 60:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:6:1)


**נָתַתָּה לִּירֵאֶיךָ נֵּס.** נִסְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁל צָרוֹת הַרְבֵּה:


**You have given those who fear You trials** Trials of many troubles.


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:6:2)


**לְהִתְנוֹסֵס.** לִהְיוֹת מְנֻסִּים בָּהֶם, אִם יַעַמְדוּ בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ:


**to be tested** With which to be tested whether they would stand [steadfast] in awe of You.


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:6:3)


**מִפְּנֵי קֹשֶׁט.** לְקַשֵּׁט מִדּוֹתֶיךָ בָּעוֹלָם, שֶׁכְּשֶׁתִּתֵּן לָהֶם הַטּוֹבָה לֹא יְהַרְהֲרוּ הָאֻמּוֹת אַחֲרֶיךָ, אֶלָּא יְקַשְּׁטוּ דִּינֶיךָ וְיֹאמְרוּ: יָפֶה הֵיטִיב לָהֶם, כִּי הֵם עָמְדוּ לוֹ בְּכַמָּה נִסְיוֹנוֹת:


**in order to beautify forever** To beautify Your standards in the world, so that when You give them goodness, the gentiles will not criticize You, but they will beautify Your judgments and say that He justly did good to them because they passed many tests for Him.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 60:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:7:1)


**יֵחָלְצוּן.** יִנָּצְלוּ מֵרָע:


**should be rescued** Should be saved from harm.


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:7:2)


**הוֹשִׁיעָה יְמִינְךָ.** אֲשֶׁר הֲשִׁיבוֹתָ אָחוֹר (איכה ב:ג) בְּהִתְחַזֵּק אוֹיְבֵיהֶם עֲלֵיהֶם:


**save Your right hand** which You brought back so that their enemies should overpower them.


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:7:3)


**וַעֲנֵנִי.** כִּי אִם תַּעֲנֵנִי **יֵחָלְצוּ** הֵם, שֶׁאֲנִי נִלְחָם בִּשְׁבִילָם:


**and answer me** For, if You answer me, they will be rescued, because I fight against them [the enemies] for them [Israel].



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 60:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:8:1)


**אֱלֹהִים דִּבֶּר בְּקָדְשׁוֹ.** שֶׁיְּקַבֵּץ הַגָּלוּת וְזַרְעוֹ יִמְשְׁלוּ בָהֶם (ס״א אינו). דָּבָר אַחֵר: **אֱלֹהִים דִּבֶּר בְּקָדְשׁוֹ** שֶׁאֶהְיֶה מֶלֶךְ עֲלֵיהֶם:


**God spoke in His Sanctuary** that He would gather the exiles and his [David’s] seed would rule over them. Another explanation: God spoke in His Sanctuary [saying] that I would be king over them.


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:8:2)


**אֶעְלֹזָה.** בִּישׁוּעָתוֹ. בְּפֵרוּשׁ אַחֵר מָצָאתִי: **אֱלֹהִים דִּבֶּר בְּקָדְשׁוֹ** לְעָזְרֵנִי, כְּדִכְתִיב (שמואל ב ג:יח) ״כִּי בְיַד דָּוִד עַבְדִּי אוֹשִׁיעַ אֶת עַמִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל״:


**I will exult** in His salvation. In another explanation, I found: God spoke in His Sanctuaryto help me, as it is written (II Sam. 3:18): “For (sic) by the hand of My bondsman David shall I deliver My people Israel.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:8:3)


**אֲחַלְּקָה שְׁכֶם.** אֲחַלֵּק לָהֶם שְׁכֶם בְּנִכְסֵי אוֹיְבֵיהֶם:


**I will divide a portion** I will divide for them a portion of the property of their enemies.


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:8:4)


**וְעֵמֶק סֻכּוֹת אֲמַדֵּד.** סֻכּוֹת זֶה אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מֵאֵיזֶה אֻמָּה הִיא. לֹא יָדַעְתִּי סֻכּוֹת שֶׁבָּאוּ לוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּשֶׁנָּסְעוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵרַעְמְסֵס (שמות יב:לז) הֵיכָן הוּא. וּבְפֵרוּשִׁים אֲחֵרִים מָצָאתִי **אֲחַלְּקָה שְׁכֶם**, אַחֲזִיר לָהֶם נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אֲבִיהֶם. **וְעֵמֶק סֻכּוֹת אֲמַדֵּד**, כְּשֶׁאֲחַלְּקֵהוּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל. שְׁכֶם וְסֻכּוֹת בִּקְצֵה אֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן הָיָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ תְּחִלַּת בִּיאָתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב לָאָרֶץ דֶּרֶךְ סֻכּוֹת שְׁכֶם (בראשית לג:יז-יח). דָּבָר אַחֵר: **וְעֵמֶק סֻכּוֹת אֲמַדֵּד**, סֻכּוֹת לְשׁוֹן צוּרוֹת וְדִמְיוֹנוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְאֵת סֻכּוֹת בְּנוֹת״ (מלכים ב יז:ל):


**and I will measure the valley of Succoth** I do not know of what nation this Succoth is, and I do not know where the Succoth is that Israel came to when they traveled from Rameses. In other commentaries I found (this is not in all editions): I will divide Shechem—I will restore to them the heritage of their father Jacob. Another explanation: **And I will measure the valley of Succoth** when I divide it for Israel. Shechem and Succoth were at the edge of the land of Canaan, as we find Jacob’s entry to the land through Succoth and Shechem. Another explanation: **and I will measure the valley of Succoth** Succoth is an expression of shapes and imaginations, as is written (II Kings 17:30): “Succoth- Benoth.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:8:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:8:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:8:5)


**אֲמַדֵּד.** אֲנִי מוֹדֵד אֶת צוּרָתָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמואל ב ב:ח): ״שְׁנֵי חֲבָלִים לְהָמִית וּמְלֹא הַחֶבֶל לְהַחֲיוֹת״ (ס״א אינו):


**I will measure** I measure their form, as is written (II Sam. 8:2): “two cord-lengths to put to death and one full cord-length to keep alive.”



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 60:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:9:1)


**לִי גִלְעָד.** לִמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיהֶם:


**Gilead is mine** to reign over them.


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:9:2)


**מְחֹקְקִי.** שָׂרִים שֶׁלִּי. מְחוֹקֵק לְשׁוֹן שְׂרָרָה, שֶׁמְּחוֹקֵק וְשׁוֹלֵחַ סְפָרִים וּמְצַוֶּה, כְּמוֹ ״לֹא יָסוּר שֵׁבֶט מִיהוּדָה וּמְחֹקֵק מִבֵּין רַגְלָיו״ (בראשית מט:י) (ס״א אינו):


**my lawgiver** My ministers. מחקקי is an expression of administration, that he makes the law and sends scrolls and commands, as (Gen. 49:10): “The scepter will not turn away from Judah, nor the lawgiver from between his feet.”



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 60:10:1

**מוֹאָב סִיר רַחְצִי.** אֶשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶם כְּסִיר שֶׁל נְחוֹשֶׁת הַמּוּכָן לִרְחוֹץ בּוֹ:


**Moab is my washbasin** I will use them as a copper pot prepared for washing therein.


###### Rashi on Psalms 60:10:2

**נַעֲלִי.** מַסְגֵּר שֶׁלִּי:

###### Rashi on Psalms 60:10:3

**עָלַי פְּלֶשֶׁת הִתְרֹעָעִי.** הִתְחַבְּרִי עַל מֶמְשַׁלְתִּי לִהְיוֹת מְשֻׁעְבָּדִים לִי, כִּי גַת מֵאֶרֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּים, וְכֵן עַזָּה (שמואל א ו:יז), שֶׁכְּבָשָׁן דָּוִד:


**join me** Join my kingdom to be subordinate to me, for Gath, and also Gaza, which David vanquished, are of the land of the Philistines.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 60:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/60:11:1)


**מִי יוֹבִלֵנִי עִיר מָצוֹר.** אוֹ לְעִיר מִבְצָר לִכְבּוֹשׁ אֶת בָּצְרָה אִם לֹא אַתָּה תַּעֲזֹר אוֹתִי עַל מִבְצְרֵי אֱדוֹם **מִי יֹבִילֵנִי** וּמִי יַנְחֵנִי עֲלֵיהֶם, בְּפֵרוּשִׁים אֲחֵרִים מָצָאתִי כֵּן עַל מִבְצְרֵי אֱדוֹם אֲשֶׁר נָחִיתִי עַתָּה עֲלֵיהֶם:


**Who will bring me to a fortified city** then to a fortified city, to conquer the city of Rome; if You will not help me against the fortress of Edom, who will bring me and who will lead me upon them? (Shem Ephraim suggests this emendation: If You will not help me now to conquer Edom, upon which You have now led me.) In other commentaries, I found as follows: upon the fortresses of Edom, upon whom You have led me now.

**אֵלֶיךָ אֶקְרָא בַּעֲטֹף לִבִּי.** עֲלֵיהֶם. וְעַל מָה אֲנִי קוֹרֵא לְךָ? שֶׁתַּנְחֵנִי **בְּצוּר** – שֶׁהוּא רָם וְחָזָק מִמֶּנִּי:

## Chapter 62


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 62:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:1:1)


**עַל יְדוּתוּן.** שֵׁם כְּלִי שִׁיר, וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה : עַל הַדָּתוֹת וְעַל הַדִּינִין הַנִּגְזָרִים עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאוֹיְבֵיהֶם:


**on jeduthun** The name of a musical instrument. The Midrash Aggadah, though, [explains it to mean]: concerning the ordinances (דתות) and laws that are decreed upon Israel by their enemies.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 62:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:2:1)


**דּוּמִיָּה נַפְשִׁי.** מְצַפָּה נַפְשִׁי, כְּמוֹ ״דּוֹם לַה׳ וְהִתְחוֹלֵל לוֹ״ (תהלים לז:ז):


**does my soul hope** Heb. דומיה. My soul hopes, as (above 37:7): “Wait (דום) for the Lord and hope for Him.”



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 62:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:3:1)


**לֹא אֶמּוֹט רַבָּה.** מְטוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת, וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: רַבָּה גֵּיהִנֹּם:


**I shall not falter greatly** Great falterings. According to the Midrash Aggadah (Mid. Ps. 62: 2), “greatly” refers to Gehinnom.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 62:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:4:1)


**תְּהוֹתְתוּ.** מְנַחֵם פֵּירֵשׁ מִגִּזְרַת ״הֵתָיוּ לְאָכְלָה״ (ירמיהו יב:ט), ״וַיֵּתֵא רָאשֵׁי עָם״ (דברים לג:כא): עַד אָנָה תֵּאָסְפוּ עַל אִישׁ. וְלִי נִרְאֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְפוֹתְרוֹ לְשׁוֹן ״הַוּוֹת״ (תהלים ה:י), וִיהֵא הֵ״א וְתָי״ו שֹׁרֶשׁ: כַּאֲשֶׁר יֹאמַר מִן ׳מֵת׳ – ׳מוֹת׳, כָּךְ נֹאמַר מִן יְסוֹד ׳הֵת׳ – ׳הוֹת׳, וּלְשׁוֹן רַבִּים ׳הַוּוֹת׳; וְהוּא לְשׁוֹן מַחֲשֶׁבֶת שֶׁבֶר וְתַרְמִית. וְיֵשׁ מְפָרְשִׁין: **תְּהוֹתְתוּ** כְּמוֹ תַּאֲרִיכוּ לְשׁוֹנְכֶם עַל בְּנֵי אָדָם בְּרַע. וְדִמּוּהָּ לִלְשׁוֹן הָעֲרָב כְּשֶׁמַּרְבֶּה בִּדְבָרִים (ס״א אינו):


**will you plan destruction** Heb. תהותתו. Menachem (p. 69) explained it as derived from (Jer. 12: 9): “come (התיו) to eat”; (Deut. 33:21), “He came (ויתא) to the head of the people.” How long will you gather against a man? But it appears to me that it should be interpreted as an expression of הַוּוֹת destruction, and the “hey” and “tav” are the radical. As one says from מֵת, מוֹת, so shall we say from the root הֵת, הוֹת, and the plural is הוּוֹת. It is an expression of a destructive and deceitful plot. Others explain תְּהוֹתֲתוּ as “you extend.” i.e., you extend your tongue on the sons of men with evil, and they compared it to Arabic, when one speaks overly much.


###### Rashi on Psalms 62:4:2

**as a leaning wall** which is ready to fall upon the sons of men.

###### Rashi on Psalms 62:5:1

**בְּפִיו.** שֶׁל כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מֵהֶם **יְבָרֵכוּ**:


**with his mouth** of each of them they bless.


###### Rashi on Psalms 62:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:5:3)


**וּבְקִרְבָּם.** וּבְמַחְשְׁבוֹתָם **יְקַלְלוּ סֶלָה**:


**but inwardly** But in their thoughts they curse forever.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 62:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:10:1)


**אַךְ הֶבֶל בְּנֵי אָדָם.** וְאַל תִּירְאוּ מֵהֶם מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַחֲסֶה לָנוּ בְּעֵת צָרָה סֶלָה:


**The sons of men are but vanity** Do not fear them, since God is forever our shelter in time of trouble.


###### Rashi on Psalms 62:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:10:2)


**בְּמֹאזְנַיִם לַעֲלוֹת.** אִם בָּאוּ לַעֲלוֹת בְּמֹאזְנַיִם וְהַבְלֵיהֶם שָׁוִים, כֵּן פְּשׁוּטוֹ. וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ לְעִנְיַן הַזּוּגוֹת (ויקרא רבה כט:ח):


**were they to be put on a scale** If they came to go up on a scale, they and their vanities would be equal. This is the simple meaning, but midrashically, it is interpreted as concerning couples (Lev. Rabbah 29:8).



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 62:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:11:1)


**חַיִל כִּי יָנוּב.** אִם תִּרְאוּ רְשָׁעִים שֶׁמָּמוֹנָם מַצְלִיחַ וְגָדֵל, **אַל תָּשִׁיתוּ לֵב**:


**if wealth burgeons** If you see wicked men whose money prospers and increases, pay it no heed.


###### Rashi on Psalms 62:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:11:2)


**חַיִל.** מָמוֹן:


חיל is money.


###### Rashi on Psalms 62:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:11:3)


**יָנוּב.** יִצְמַח, לְשׁוֹן ״תְּנוּבָה״ (ישעיה כז:ו):


**burgeons** Heb. ינוב, grows, an expression of produce (תנובה).



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Psalms 62:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:12:1)


**אַחַת דִּבֶּר אֱלֹהִים.** שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי מִתּוֹכָהּ שְׁתַּיִם, וּמָה הֵן שְׁתַּיִם? **כִּי עֹז** לְךָ לְשַׁלֵּם **לְאִישׁ כְּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ**, וְהַשֵּׁנִי **כִּי לְךָ ה׳ הַחֶסֶד.** וּמֵאֵיזֶה דִּבּוּר שְׁמַעְנוּם? מִדִּבּוּר שֵׁנִי שֶׁל עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת שָׁמַעְנוּ מִמֶּנּוּ, שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא פּוֹקֵד עָוֹן וְנוֹצֵר חֶסֶד, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ (שמות כ:ה) ״פֹּקֵד עֲוֹן אָבוֹת וְגוֹ׳״. לְכָךְ בָּטוּחַ אֲנִי שֶׁיְּשַׁלֵּם שָׂכָר טוֹב לַצַּדִּיקִים וּפֻרְעָנוּת לָרְשָׁעִים. זוֹ לָמַדְתִּי מִיסוֹדוֹ שֶׁל ר׳ מֹשֶׁה הַדַּרְשָׁן. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דְּרָשׁוּהוּ (מכילתא יתרו בחדש ז) בְּזָכוֹר וְשָׁמוֹר בְּדִבּוּר אֶחָד נֶאֶמְרוּ:


**God spoke one thing** I heard two things from it, and what are the two things? First, that God has strength to repay a man according to his deed. Second, that You, O Lord, have kindness. Now, from which statement do we derive this? From the second commandment of the Decalogue. We derive from it that the Holy One, blessed be He, punishes iniquity and preserves kindness, as it is stated therein: “I visit the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, etc.” Therefore, I am confident that He will pay a good reward to the righteous and punishment to the wicked. I learned from the work of Rabbi Moshe Hadarshan, but our Sages interpreted it as referring to [the maxim that] “Remember” and “Keep” were stated in a single utterance.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Psalms 62:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/62:13:1)


**וּלְךָ אֲדֹנָי חָסֶד.** וּמַהוּ הַחֶסֶד? **כִּי אַתָּה תְשַׁלֵּם לְאִישׁ כְּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ**, וְלֹא מַעֲשֵׂהוּ מַמָּשׁ אֶלָּא מִקְצָתוֹ, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי אַתָּה אֱלֹהֵינוּ חָשַׂכְתָּ לְמַטָּה מֵעֲוֹנֵנוּ״ (עזרא ט:יג). כָּךְ נִדְרַשׁ בְּאַגָּדַת תְּהִלִּים (מדרש תהלים סב:ד). וְיֵשׁ לִפְתֹּר עוֹד: **וּלְךָ ה׳** הַחֶסֶד, כִּי יֵשׁ בְּיָדְךָ לְשַׁלֵּם **לְאִישׁ כְּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ**:


**And You, O Lord, have kindness** And what is the kindness? That You repay a man according to his deed; not really his deed but part of it, as the matter that is stated (Ezra 9:13): “for You, our God, have punished us less than our iniquities [deserve].” In this manner it is interpreted in Aggadath Tehillim (Mid. Ps. 62:4). It may also be interpreted: And You, O Lord, have kindness because You have the power to repay a man according to his deed.



## Chapter 63


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 63:1:1

**בְּמִדְבַּר יְהוּדָה.** בּוֹרֵחַ מִפְּנֵי שָׁאוּל (שמואל א כב-כד):


**in the desert of Judah** when he was fleeing from Saul.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 63:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/63:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/63:2:1)


**אֲשַׁחֲרֶךָּ.** אֲבַקֵּשׁ וְאֶדְרוֹשׁ לְךָ, כְּמוֹ ״וְשִׁחַרְתַּנִי וְאֵינֶנִּי״ (איוב ז:כא), ״אִם אַתָּה תְּשַׁחֵר אֶל אֵל״ (איוב ח:ה):


**I seek You** Heb. אשחרך, I seek and search for You, as (Job 7:21): “and You shall seek me (ושחרתני), but I am not here”; (Job 8:5), “If you seek (תשחר) God.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 63:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/63:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/63:2:2)


**צָמְאָה לְךָ נַפְשִׁי.** צָמֵא וְתָאֵב אֲנִי לָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ בְּבֵית תְּפִלָּתְךָ:


**My soul thirsts for You** I thirst and long to come to You in Your house of prayer.


###### Rashi on Psalms 63:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/63:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/63:2:3)


**כָּמַהּ לְךָ בְשָׂרִי.** לְשׁוֹן תַּאֲוָה, וְאֵין לוֹ דִּמְיוֹן:


**my flesh longs for You** Heb. כמה, an expression of desire. There is no similar [Scriptural expression].


###### Rashi on Psalms 63:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/63:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/63:2:4)


**בְּאֶרֶץ צִיָּה.** בַּמִּדְבָּר:


**in an arid land** in the desert.

###### Rashi on Psalms 63:3:1

**כֵּן בַּקֹּדֶשׁ חֲזִיתִיךָ וְגוֹ׳.** כְּמוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר: צָמֵאתִי לִרְאוֹת עֻזְּךָ וּכְבוֹדְךָ כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁחֲזִיתִיךָ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, מִשְׁכַּן שִׁילֹה; תִּשְׂבַּע נַפְשִׁי בְּמַרְאוֹת עֻזְּךָ וּכְבוֹדֶךָ:


**As I saw You in the Sanctuary, etc.** Heb. כן, like כאשר, as. I thirst to see Your strength and Your glory as I saw You in the Sanctuary, the Tabernacle of Shiloh. My soul will be sated with the visions of Your strength and Your glory.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 63:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/63:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/63:5:1)


**כֵּן אֲבָרֶכְךָ בְחַיָּי.** כְּמוֹ אָז, כִּי ״אָז״ (דברים כט:יט) מְתַרְגְּמִינָן: ״וּבְכֵן״. כְּלוֹמַר: אָז, כְּשֶׁאָבוֹא לְפָנֶיךָ, אֲבָרֶכְךָ כָּל יְמֵי חַיַּי:


**Then I shall bless You in my lifetime** Heb. כן, like אָז, then, because אָז is translated ובכן. That is to say: Then, when I come before You, I shall bless You all the days of my life.


###### Rashi on Psalms 63:5:2

**בְּשִׁמְךָ אֶשָּׂא כַפָּי.** לְהִתְפַּלֵּל וּלְהַלֵּל:


**in Your name I shall lift my hands** to pray and laud.

###### Rashi on Psalms 63:6:1

**וְשִׂפְתֵי רְנָנוֹת.** לְשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁל רְנָנוֹת, כְּמוֹ ״וַיְהִי כָל הָאָרֶץ שָׂפָה אֶחָת״ (בראשית יא:א) דִּמְתַרְגְּמִינַן: ״לִישָׁנָא חַד״:


**when my mouth praises with expressions of song** Heb. ושפתי, languages of songs, as (Gen. 11: 1): “And all the earth was of one language (שפה),” which is translated: לישן חד.

### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 63:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/63:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/63:11:1)


**יְגִירוּהוּ עַל יְדֵי חָרֶב.** יָבוֹאוּ עַל רוֹדְפֵי אוֹיְבִים, וִיגִירוּהוּ כָּל אֶחָד מֵהֶם עַל יְדֵי חֶרֶב שֶׁיָּמִיתוּ אוֹתוֹ. וּמִקְרָא קָצָר הוּא זֶה שֶׁלֹּא פֵּירֵשׁ מִי יְגִירוּהוּ. **יְגִירוּהוּ** לְשׁוֹן גְּרִירָה, כְּמוֹ ״מוֹגָרִים בַּמּוֹרָד״ (מיכה א:ד), ״פָּרַץ נַחַל מֵעִם גָּר״ (איוב כח:ד):


**May he be dragged by the sword** May enemies come upon my pursuers and drag each one of them with a sword, killing him. This is an elliptical verse, since it does not explain who will drag him. יגירהוּ is an expression of dragging, as (Micah 1:4): “as water poured down (המוגרים) a steep place”; (Job. 28:4), “A stream bursts forth from the place of its flow (גר).”

(מָצָאתִי **מְנָת שׁוּעָלִים.** יִשּׁוּבָם חָרֵב, שׁוּעָלִים יֵלְכוּ בוֹ (איכה ה:יח)):


**the portion of foxes** (I found: the portion of foxes May their dwellings be destroyed, that foxes should walk there.)

###### Rashi on Psalms 63:12:1

###### Rashi on Psalms 63:12:2

###### Rashi on Psalms 63:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/63:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/63:12:3)


**כִּי יִסָּכֵר.** יִסָּתֵם, כְּמוֹ ״וַיִּסָּכְרוּ כָּל מַעְיְנוֹת תְּהוֹם רַבָּה״ (בראשית ח:ב):


**for...will be closed** Heb. יסכר, will be closed up, as (Gen. 8:2). “The fountains of the great deep...were closed (ויסכרו).”



## Chapter 64


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 64:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:2:1)


**שְׁמַע אֱלֹהִים קוֹלִי בְשִׂיחִי.** מִזְמוֹר זֶה דָּרְשׁוּהוּ בַּעֲלֵי אַגָּדַת תְּהִלִּים עַל דָּנִיֵּאל שֶׁהוּשְׁלַךְ לְגוֹב אֲרָיוֹת, וְיָפֶה נוֹפֵל כָּל לְשׁוֹן הַמִּזְמוֹר עַל הָאַגָּדָה. צָפָה דָוִד בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ כָּל הַמְּאוֹרָע לוֹ, וְהִתְפַּלֵּל עָלָיו; שֶׁדָּנִיֵּאל מִזַּרְעוֹ הָיָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לְחִזְקִיָּה: ״וּמִבָּנֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר תּוֹלִיד יִקָּחוּ וְהָיוּ סָרִיסִים בְּהֵיכַל מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל״ (ישעיהו לט:ז) – אֵלּוּ דָּנִיֵּאל חֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה:


**Hear, O God, my voice in my prayer** The authors of Aggadoth Tehllim (Mid. Ps.) interpreted this psalm as referring to Daniel, who was cast into the lions’ den. The language of the psalm fits the Aggadah very well. David foresaw with the holy spirit all that would happen to him [Daniel], and prayed for him, because Daniel was his descendant. As was said to Hezekiah (Isa. 39:7): “And they shall take [some] of your sons, etc., whom you shall beget, and they shall be officers in the palace of the king of Babylon.” These are Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.


###### Rashi on Psalms 64:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:2:2)


**מִפַּחַד אוֹיֵב.** אֵלּוּ הָאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנִים שֶׁנִּתְיַעֲצוּ עָלָיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דניאל ו:ה) ״אֱדַיִן סָרְכַיָּא וַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּא הֲווֹ בָעַיִן עִלָּה לְהַשְׁכָּחָה לְדָנִיֵּאל״:


**from fear of the enemy** These are the satraps, who plotted against him, as it is stated (Dan. 6:5): “Then the viziers and the satraps sought to find a pretext against Daniel.”



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 64:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:3:1)


**מֵרִגְשַׁת פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן.** שֶׁהֵם מִתְרַגְּשִׁים לְבַקֵּשׁ לִי עֲלִילוֹת מָוֶת, כְּדִכְתִיב ״אַרְגִּישׁוּ עַל מַלְכָּא וְגוֹ׳״ (דניאל ו:ז):


**from the gathering of workers of iniquity** For they gather seeking against him a pretext of death, as it is written (Dan. 6:7): “...assembled about the king, etc.”



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 64:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:4:1)


**דָּרְכוּ חִצָּם.** הוּא לְשׁוֹנָם הָרָע:


**who aimed...their arrow** That is their slander.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 64:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:5:1)


**לִירוֹת בַּמִּסְתָּרִים תָּם.** יוֹרוּהוּ בְּחִצֵּיהֶם:


**To shoot at the innocent in secret places** They will shoot him with their arrows.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 64:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:6:1)


**יְסַפְּרוּ לִטְמוֹן מוֹקְשִׁים.** יְדַבְּרוּ אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּעָרְמָה דְּבָרִים טְמוּנִים, שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ הַמֶּלֶךְ לֹא הֵבִין לָמָּה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין כָּךְ. וְהֵם הָיוּ מִתְכַּוְּנִים לִטְמוֹן לְדָנִיֵּאל מוֹקְשִׁים לְהִלָּכֵד בָּהֶם, שֶׁאָמְרוּ לְדָרְיָוֶשׁ: ״אִתְיְעַטוּ כָּל סָרְכֵי מַלְכוּתָא וְגוֹ׳ לְקַיָּמָא קְיָם מַלְכָּא וְגוֹ׳״ (דניאל ו:ח), שֶׁלֹּא יִתְפַּלֵּל שׁוּם אָדָם תְּפִלָּתוֹ לִפְנֵי שׁוּם אֱלוֹהַּ חוּץ מִמְּךָ עַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם:


**they tell to hide snares** They speak cunningly to the king secret words, for even the king did not know why they were doing this. But they intended to hide snares to entrap Daniel, for they said to Darius, “All the viziers of the kingdom, etc., have conferred to establish the king’s law, etc.” [stating] that no one should offer up prayer to any god except you until thirty days [have passed].



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 64:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:7:1)


**יְחַפְּשׂוּ עוֹלוֹת.** מְבַקְּשִׁים עֲלִילוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״הֲווֹ בָּעַיִן עִלָּה הַשְׁכָּחָה לְדָנִיֵּאל״ (דניאל ו:ה):


**They seek pretexts** Heb. עולות. They seek pretexts (עלילות), as it is stated (Dan. 6:5): “sought to find a pretext against Daniel.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 64:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:7:2)


**טָמְנוּ.** בְּלִבָּם וְלֹא גִלּוּ דַּעְתָּם אֶת חֵפֶשׂ הָעֲלִילָה הַמְחֻפָּשׂ עַל יָדָם, **וְקֶרֶב** מַחְשְׁבוֹתָם עֹמֶק לִבָּם:


**they hid** Heb. טמנו. They hid their thoughts in their heart and did not reveal the search for a pretext, which was searched out through them, and the midst of their thoughts and the depth of their heart.


###### Rashi on Psalms 64:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/64:7:3)


**וְקֶרֶב אִישׁ.** אִישׁ מֵהֶם: כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד טָמַן מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ:


**hidden within man** Each man of them. Each one concealed his thought.

**וַיּוֹרֵם אֱלֹהִים.** יָרָה אוֹתָם לְגוֹב הָאֲרָיוֹת, כְּדִכְתִיב (דניאל ו:כה): ״וַאֲמַר מַלְכָּא וְהַיְתִיו לְגֻבְרַיָּא אִלֵּךְ דִּי אֲכַלוּ קַרְצוֹהִי דִּי דָנִיֵּאל וּלְגֹב אַרְיָוָתָא רְמוֹ וְגוֹ׳״:


**And God cast them down** He cast them into the lions’ den, as it is written (Dan. 6:25): “And the king commanded, and they brought these men who had slandered Daniel, and they cast them into the lions’ den, etc.”

**וַיַּכְשִׁילוּהוּ עָלֵימוֹ לְשׁוֹנָם.** הַכִּשָּׁלוֹן שֶׁדִּמּוּ לְהַכְשִׁילוֹ, עָלֵימוֹ נֶהְפַּךְ לְשׁוֹנָם:


**That which they hoped would make him stumble, their tongue brought upon them** The stumbling they planned to inflict on him, their tongue turned over upon them.

**וְיִתְהַלְלוּ כָּל יִשְׁרֵי לֵב.** יִתְפָּאֲרוּ עַל יֹשֶׁר לִבָּם וְיִשְׁתַּבְּחוּ בְּעַצְמָם, כִּי בְּטוּחִים הֵם שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעֶזְרָתָם:


**and all upright of heart will boast** They will boast about the uprightness of their heart, and they will praise themselves because they are confident that the Holy One, blessed be He, will help them.



## Chapter 65


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 65:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:2:1)


**לְךָ דֻמִיָּה תְהִלָּה.** הַשְּׁתִיקָה תְּהִלָּה לְךָ, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין קֵץ לְשִׁבְחֲךָ; וְהַמַּרְבֶּה בְּשֶׁבַח אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא גּוֹרֵעַ:


**Silence is praise to You** Silence is praise to You; because there is no end to Your praise, the more one praises, the more one detracts.


###### Rashi on Psalms 65:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:2:2)


**אֱלֹהִים בְּצִיּוֹן.** אֱלֹהִים הַשּׁוֹכֵן בְּצִיּוֹן, (מצאתי ״שִׂימוּ כָבוֹד תְּהִלָּתוֹ״ (תהלים סו:ב), לֹא יוֹתֵר מִדַּאי, אַךְ **דֻּמִיָּה תְהִלָּה**, וְכִמְדוּמֶּה הַלְלוּהוּ בְּאֵימָה בִּלְשׁוֹן הַלְלוּיָהּ שֵׁם בֶּן שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת, מְתֻרְגָּם ״דְּחִילָא״ ״עָזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ״ (שמות טו:ב) ״וְיָד עַל כֵּס יָהּ״ (שמות יז:טז) וְלָשׁוֹן ״וְגִילוּ בִּרְעָדָה״ (תהלים ב:יא) דּוֹמֶה לָזֶה) דָּבָר אַחֵר **לְךָ דֻמִיָּה תְהִלָּה אֱלֹהִים בְּצִיּוֹן** אֶת אֲשֶׁר דּוֹמַמְתָּ וְהֶחֱרַשְׁתָּ עַל מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה אוֹיְבֶיךָ בְּצִיּוֹן תְּהִלָּה הָיָה לְךָ שֶׁהַיְּכֹלֶת בְּיָדְךָ לְהִנָּקֵם וְאַתָּה מַאֲרִיךְ אַף:


**O God in Zion** God, Who dwells in Zion. [I found the following: **make glorious His praise** Not effusion, but silence is praise. It appears that דמיה means “praise God with awe,” with the expression “praise Ya-h.” The name consisting of two letters is translated (Exod. 15:2) as, the fear of God, for “My strength and my praise is God (י-ה).” Also (Exod. 17:16), “For a hand is on the throne of God (י-ה).” And the expression (above 2:11): “and rejoice with quaking” resembles this. Shem Ephraim comments: It appears to me that Rashi should read as follows: **Make glorious, etc.** But silence to God is praise, and its interpretation is: Praise Him with awe, etc.” The intention is that the word דמיה is divided into two words. For it was difficult for him to understand why it should appear that one is to recite any praise of the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore he says, “Make glorious His praise,” but not excessively, for that is equivalent to detracting. Therefore he says, “To You is silence (דום),” meaning that silence is fitting, but י-ה is praise, i.e., with the name consisting of two letters. His statement that the expression, “rejoice with quaking” resembles this, should read: “Worship the Lord with awe and rejoice with quaking.” His intention is that both verses mean that one may worship the Lord with awe; that is, one may worship the Holy One, blessed be He, with the name י-ה. Otherwise, worship with love is superior. It is also possible that the reading, “and it appears that, etc.” is a copyist’s error. It should read instead: “But be silent and praise Him with the name י-ה, in the expression Hallelujah. But this needs study. Later I found (below 68:5) that Rashi writes something similar. There, for him to write that the expression “and rejoice with quaking” resembles this is more appropriate, because there it says: “and rejoice before Him.” Compare. Therefore, it appears to me that this entire statement was erroneously copied here.) The gloss belongs below 66:2.] Another explanation: **To You is silence praise, O God, in Zion** That You were silent and still concerning Your enemies’ deeds in Zion is praise to You, for You are able to take revenge, yet You are slow to anger.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 65:4:1

**דִּבְרֵי עֲוֹנוֹת גָּבְרוּ מֶנִּי.** וְאֵין אָנוּ יְכוֹלִים לְהַסְפִּיק לְסַדֵּר כֻּלָּם לְפָנֶיךָ, לְפִי שֶׁהֵם רַב, אֶלָּא בִּכְלָל אֶחָד אָנוּ מִתְפַּלְּלִים לְפָנֶיךָ, שֶׁ**פְּשָׁעֵינוּ אַתָּה תְכַפְּרֵם**:


**Words of iniquities have overcome me** and we cannot manage to arrange them all before You because they are many. However, we offer a general prayer before You that You atone for our transgressions.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 65:5:1

**אַשְׁרֵי.** מִי אֲשֶׁר תִּבְחַר וּתְקָרֵב, אֲשֶׁר **יִשְׁכֹּן בַּחֲצֵרֶיךָ**:

###### Rashi on Psalms 65:5:2

**נִשְׂבְּעָה בְּטוּב.** שֶׁבְּבֵיתֶךָ וּמִקְּדֻשַּׁת הֵיכָלֶךָ, שֶׁשְּׁכִינָתְךָ שׁוֹרָה שָׁם:
