### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 65:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:6:1)


**נוֹרָאוֹת בְּצֶדֶק תַּעֲנֵנוּ.** בְּצִדְקָתְךָ תַּעֲנֵנוּ, לַעֲשׂוֹת נוֹרָאוֹת בַּגּוֹיִם:


**With awesome deeds, through [Your] charity You shall answer us** Through Your charity, You shall answer us by performing awesome deeds upon the heathens.


###### Rashi on Psalms 65:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:6:2)


**מִבְטָח.** אַתָּה וּמָנוֹס לְכָל יוֹשְׁבֵי קַצְווֹת אֶרֶץ, מִקְּצֵה הָאָרֶץ וְעַד קָצֵהוּ:


**the trust** You are [the trust] and the refuge of all the dwellers of the ends of the earth, from one end of the earth to the other.


###### Rashi on Psalms 65:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:6:3)


**וְיָם רְחוֹקִים.** אֲפִלּוּ לָרְחוֹקִים שֶׁבַּיָּם אַתָּה **מִבְטָח**, שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם מֶמְשַׁלְתְּךָ:


**distant...and the sea** Even to the distant ones in the sea You are the trust, for Your rule is everywhere.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 65:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:7:1)


**מֵכִין הָרִים בְּכֹחוֹ.** שֶׁמַּצְמִיחַ הֶהָרִים, שֶׁהֵם קָשִׁים, בְּכֹחוֹ, וּמְזַמֵּן וּמֵכִין בָּהֶן מְזוֹנוֹת וּמֵכִין מָטָר, כְּדִכְתִיב (תהלים קמז:ח) ״הַמֵּכִין לָאָרֶץ מָטָר הַמַּצְמִיחַ הָרִים״:


**Who sets mountains with His strength** With His strength, He makes the mountainswhich are hardsprout, and He prepares and readies food through them and prepares rain, as it is written (below 147:8): “Who prepares rain for the earth, Who makes the mountains grow grass.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 65:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:7:2)


**נֶאֱזָר בִּגְבוּרָה.** לְפִי שֶׁבָּא לְהַזְכִּיר גְּבוּרַת גְּשָׁמִים, אָמַר: נֶאֱזָר בִּגְבוּרָה:


**Who is girded with might** Because he wishes to mention the mighty deeds of the rains, he says, “Who is girded with might.”



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 65:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:8:1)


**מַשְׁבִּיחַ.** מַשְׁפִּיל, וְכֵן ״וְחָכָם בְּאָחוֹר יְשַׁבְּחֶנָּה״ (משלי כט:יא), ״בְּשׂוֹא גַלָּיו אַתָּה תְשַׁבְּחֵם״ (תהלים פט:י):


**Who humbles** Heb. משביח, He humbles. Similarly (Prov. 29:11): “but afterwards, a wise man will quiet it (ישבחנה) ; (below 89:10), “When it raises its waves, You humble them (תשבחם).”



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 65:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:9:1)


**מוֹצָאֵי בֹקֶר וָעֶרֶב תַּרְנִין.** לְךָ אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת יוֹשְׁבֵי הַקְּצָווֹת, בַּבֹּקֶר אוֹמְרִים בָּרוּךְ יוֹצֵר הַמְּאוֹרוֹת, וּבָעֶרֶב בָּרוּךְ הַמַּעֲרִיב עֲרָבִים:


**with the emergence of the morning and evening, You cause [them] to sing praises** [You cause] the creatures who dwell at the extremes to sing praises. In the morning, they say, “Blessed is He Who formed the luminaries,” and in the evening “Blessed is He Who brings about evening.”



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 65:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:10:1)


**פָּקַדְתָּ הָאָרֶץ.** כְּשֶׁאַתָּה חָפֵץ לְהֵיטִיב, אַתָּה פּוֹקֵד אֶת הָאָרֶץ וּמַשְׁקֶה אוֹתָם:


**You remember the earth** When You wish to do good, You remember the earth and water it.


###### Rashi on Psalms 65:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/65:10:2)


**רַבַּת תַּעְשְׁרֶנָּה.** הַרְבֵּה אַתָּה מְעַשְּׁרָהּ מִפֶּלֶג שֶׁלְּךָ, שֶׁהוּא **מָלֵא מָיִם** (תענית ח:), וְתָכִין בּוֹ **דְּגָנָם** שֶׁל יוֹשְׁבֵי קְצָווֹת, כִּי בְּכֵן אַתָּה מֵכִין אוֹתָהּ:


**You enrich it greatly** You enrich it greatly from Your stream, which is full of water, and You prepare therewith the corn of the dwellers of “the ends,” for therewith You prepare it.

**its furrows** Heb. תלמיה. They are the rows of the plowshare.

**רַוֵּה.** כְּמוֹ לְרַוָּה:

**נַחֵת גְּדוּדֶיהָ.** כְּמוֹ לְנַחֵת גְּדוּדֶיהָ, לְהָנִיחַ לִגְדוּדֶיהָ לַעֲשׂוֹת נַחַת לַבְּרִיּוֹת. אַתָּה **תְּמֹגְגֶנָּה** בִּרְבִיבִים שֶׁל מָטָר:


**to afford pleasure to its troops** Heb. נחתגדודה, like לְנַחֵתגְדוּדֶהָ, to give rest to its troops. To afford pleasure to its creatures, You dissolve it with drops of rain.

**and Your paths** They are the heavens, which are the dust of Your feet.

### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Psalms 65:14:1

**לָבְשׁוּ כָרִים הַצֹּאן.** יִתְלַבְּשׁוּן הַשָּׁרוֹן וְהָעֲרָבָה מִן הַצֹּאן, הַבָּאִים לִרְעוֹת הַדֶּשֶׁא אֲשֶׁר הִצְמִיחַ הַמָּטָר:

**וַעֲמָקִים יַעַטְפוּ בָר.** עַל יְדֵי הַמָּטָר יִהְיוּ מְעֻטָּפִים הָעֲמָקִים בִּתְבוּאָה, וְאָז יִתְרוֹעֲעוּ הַבְּרִיּוֹת תְּרוּעַת שִׂמְחָה וְיָשִׁירוּ מֵרֹב הַבְּרָכָה:


**and valleys are enwrapped with corn** Through the rain, the valleys will be enwrapped with grain. Then the creatures will shout with shouts of joy and sing because of the abundant blessing.



## Chapter 66


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 66:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:2:1)


**זַמְּרוּ כְבוֹד שְׁמוֹ.** זַמְּרוּ בִּכְבוֹד שְׁמוֹ. אִי נַמִּי: סַפְּרוּ כְּבוֹד שְׁמוֹ בְּזֶמֶר וְשִׁיר:


**Sing the glory of His name** Sing in honor of His name. Or: Recite the glory of His name with music and song.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 66:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:3:1)


**מַה נּוֹרָא.** כָּל אֶחָד מִמַּעֲשֶׂיךָ:


**How awesome** is each one of Your deeds!


###### Rashi on Psalms 66:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:3:2)


**בְּרֹב עֻזְּךָ.** כְּשֶׁאַתָּה מַרְאֶה לָעוֹלָם עֻזְּךָ עַל יְדֵי דֶּבֶר אוֹ חֶרֶב אוֹ רָעָב אוֹ בְּרָקִים:


**Through the greatness of Your might** When You show the world Your mightthrough pestilence, sword, famine, or lightning—


###### Rashi on Psalms 66:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:3:3)


**אוֹיְבֶיךָ.** הָרְשָׁעִים, מֵרוֹב פַּחַד מוֹדִים עַל כַּחַשׁ וַעֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבְּיָדָם:


**Your enemies**, the wicked, confess their lies and sins because of their great fear.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 66:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:5:1)


**נוֹרָא עֲלִילָה.** יָראוּי עַל בְּנֵי אָדָם פֶּן יִמְצָא לָהֶם פֶּשַׁע, כִּי כָל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם גְּלוּיִים לְךָ:


**awesome in His deeds** Feared by mankind, lest He find a transgression in them, for all their deeds are revealed to You.



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 66:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:6:1)


**הָפַךְ יָם לְיַבָּשָׁה.** יַם סוּף:


**He turned the sea into dry land** The Sea of Reeds.


###### Rashi on Psalms 66:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:6:2)


**שָׁם נִשְׂמְחָה בּוֹ.** מָצָאתִי: שָׁם הָיָה דָּבָר שֶׁהַיָּם נִשְׂמַח בּוֹ, כְּלוֹמַר שֶׁרָאָה הַיָּם אֶת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:


**there it rejoiced with it** I found: There was a thing with which the sea rejoiced, i.e., that the sea saw the Holy One, blessed be He.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 66:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:7:1)


**אַל יָרוּמוּ.** אַל תְּהִי יָדָם רָמָה:


**will not exalt themselves** Their hand will not be high.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 66:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:8:1)


**בָּרְכוּ עַמִּים אֱלֹהֵינוּ.** עַל נִפְלְאוֹתָיו, שֶׁהוּא שָׂם נַפְשֵׁנוּ בַּחַיִּים בַּגָּלוּת, וְאֵינְכֶם יְכוֹלִים לְהַשְׁמִיד אוֹתָנוּ:


**O peoples, bless our God** for His wonders, that He kept our soul alive in exile, and you cannot annihilate us.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 66:10:1

**כִּי בְחַנְתָּנוּ.** בְּצָרָה בַּגּוֹלָה:


**You tested us** with distress in the exile.


###### Rashi on Psalms 66:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:10:2)

**You refined us** to remove the dross from us when we repent before You, as they refine silver to remove its dross.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 66:11:1

**הֲבֵאתָנוּ בַמְּצוּדָה.** בְּמָקוֹם צַר כְּמוֹ בְּמַאֲסָר:


**You brought us into a trap** A narrow place, like in a prison.

###### Rashi on Psalms 66:12:1

### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Psalms 66:13:1

**all you who fear God** They are the proselytes who became converted.



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Psalms 66:17:1

**אֵלָיו פִּי קָרָאתִי.** כְּשֶׁהָיִינוּ בַּגּוֹלָה קְרָאנוּהוּ וְסִפַּרְנוּ רוֹמְמוֹתָיו בִּלְשׁוֹנֵנוּ:


**My mouth called out to Him** When we were in exile, we called out to Him, and we recited His exaltation with our tongue.


###### Rashi on Psalms 66:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/66:17:2)


**וְרוֹמָם.** כְּמוֹ וְנִתְרוֹמֵם. מָצָאתִי בְּפִי קָרָאתִי אֵלָיו **וְרוֹמַם** שֵׁם מִלָּה: רוֹמְמוּת שֶׁלּוֹ מוּכָן **תַּחַת לְשׁוֹנִי**, לְהוֹצִיאוֹ בַּפֶּה, כְּמוֹ ״יַכְחִידֶנָּה תַּחַת לְשׁוֹנוֹ״ (איוב כ:יב):


**and He was exalted** Heb. ורומם, like ונתרומם, and He was exalted. I found: With my mouth, I called out to Him. ורומם is a noun. His exaltation is ready under my tongue to be let out of my mouth, as (Job 20:12): “though he hide it under his tongue.”

**If I saw iniquity, etc.** He did not deal with us according to our sins, but He made Himself as though He neither saw nor heard the iniquity that was in our hearts.

**תַּנְחֵם.** תְּנַהֲגֵם בְּדֶרֶךְ הַמִּישׁוֹר, וְעַל זֹאת יוֹדוּךָ עַמִּים כֻּלָּם:

## Chapter 68


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:2:1

**יָקוּם אֱלֹהִים יָפוּצוּ אוֹיְבָיו.** עֲמָלֵק וְכַיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ (בראשית רבה סה,יח):


**May God rise; His enemies scatter** Amalek and his ilk.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:3:1)


**כְּהִנְדֹּף.** כְּהִתְנַדֵּף; כַּאֲשֶׁר יִתְנַדֵּף הֶעָשָׁן, כֵּן תִּנְדְּפֵם:


**As smoke is driven away** as it is driven away. As the smoke is driven away so will You drive [them] away.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:3:2)


**מִפְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים.** מִפְּנֵי הָאָרוֹן בִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה, ״וּבְנֻחֹה יֹאמַר שׁוּבָה ה׳ וְגוֹ׳״ (במדבר י:לו):


**from before God** From before the Ark in the days of Moses. (And it came to pass when the Ark traveled, that Moses said, “Arise, O Lord, and Your enemies will scatter.”Shem Ephraim) And when it rested, he would say, “Return, O Lord, etc.”



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:4:1

**וְיָשִׂישׂוּ בְשִׂמְחָה.** וְזֶהוּ הַמָּשׂוֹשׂ, וְכֵן יֹאמְרוּ: **שִׁירוּ לֵאלֹהִים וְגוֹ׳**:


**and they will delight with joy** And this is the joy, and so will they say, “Sing to God, etc.”



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:5:1)


**סֹלּוּ.** לְשׁוֹן שֶׁבַח, וְכֵן ״לֹא תְסֻלֶּה בְּכֶתֶם״ (איוב כח:טז), ״הַמְסֻלָּאִים בַּפָּז״ (איכה ד:ב):


**praise** Heb. סולו, an expression of praise. Similarly (Job 28:16): “It cannot be praised (תסלה) with the jewelry of Ophir”; (Lam. 4:2), “worth their weight (המסלאים) in fine gold.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:5:2)


**בְּיָהּ שְׁמוֹ.** בְּשֵׁם יָ״הּ, שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן יִרְאָה, כְּדִמְתַרְגְּמִינָן: ״דְּחִילָא״ ״עָזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ״ (תהלים קיח:יד), וְכֵן ״כִּי יָד עַל כֵּס יָהּ״ (שמות יז:טז) בְּתַרְגּוּם, וְכֵן ״כִּי בְיָהּ ה׳״ (ישעיה כו:ד) ״אֲרֵי בְּכֵן תִּתְפָּרְקוּן בְּמֵימְרָא דְּחִילָא ה׳ וְתַקִּיף עָלְמָא״. אוֹמֵר הַמְשׁוֹרֵר: שַׁבְּחוּ לְפָנָיו וְגוּרוּ מִפָּנָיו וְעִלְזוּ, וְזֶהוּ דֻּגְמַת הָאָמוּר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר ״וְגִילוּ בִּרְעָדָה״ (תהלים ב:יא):


**by His name Yah** By the name י-ה, which is an expression of fear, as we translate it דחילא, fear (below 118:14): “My might and my praise is the fear of the Lord (י-ה).” Likewise (Exod. 17:16): “For a hand is on the throne of the Lord (י-ה),” in the Targum: [And he said, “This is stated with an oath from below the fear of the Shechinah on the throne of His glory, etc.] Similarly (Isa. 26:4): “for in Yah the Lord,” is paraphrased by the Targum: for then You will be redeemed by the word of the fear of the Lord, the Strongest of the world.” The Psalmist says, “Praise Him, fear Him, and rejoice.” This resembles what is said elsewhere (above 2:11): “and rejoice with quaking.”



### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:6:1)


**אֲבִי יְתוֹמִים.** זֶהוּ הַשֶּׁבַח שֶׁתְּשַׁבְּחוּ לְפָנָיו, כָּל הָעִנְיָן עַד סוֹף כָּל הַמִּזְמוֹר:


**O Father of orphans** And this is the praise that You shall praise before Him: the entire matter until the end of the psalm.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:6:2)


**אֲבִי יְתוֹמִים.** שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה אָב לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם יְתוֹמִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״יְתוֹמִים הָיִינוּ וְאֵין אָב״ (איכה ה:ג):


**Father of orphans** Who became a father to Israel, who are orphans, as it is said (Lam. 5:3): “We were orphans without a father.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:6:3)


**וְדַיַּן אַלְמָנוֹת.** שֶׁעָשָׂה מִשְׁפָּטָהּ שֶׁל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהּ ״הָיְתָה כְּאַלְמָנָה״ (איכה א:א):


**and Judge of widows** Who performed the judgment of Jerusalem, concerning which it says (Lam. 1:1): “was like a widow.”



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:7:1)


**מוֹשִׁיב יְחִידִים בַּיְתָה.** יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהָיוּ מְפֻזָּרִין, כִּנְּסָם יַחַד אִישׁ אִישׁ מִנִּדְחוֹ וְהוֹשִׁיבָם בַּיִת שָׁלֵם וּכְנֵסִיָּה שְׁלֵימָה (איכה רבה פתיחתא כט):


**settles the solitary in a house** Israel, who were spread out. He gathered together each one from the place where he was lost and settled them in a complete household and a complete nation.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:7:2)


**מוֹצִיא אֲסִירִים בַּכּוֹשָׁרוֹת.** הוֹצִיא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרַיִם בְּחֹדֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא כָּשֵׁר לְהוֹלְכֵי דְרָכִים, לֹא חַמָּה וְלֹא צִנָּה (ספרי דברים קכד):


**He takes the prisoners out at the most opportune time** He took Israel out of Egypt in the month that is best suited for travelers, neither hot nor cold.

**אַךְ סוֹרְרִים.** מִצְרַיִם:


**but the rebellious** The Egyptians.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:7:4

**שָׁכְנוּ צְחִיחָה.** וְנִשְׁאֲרָה אַרְצָם צִיָּה וּצְמֵאָה (מצאתי):


**dwell in an arid land** Their land remained arid and thirsty. I found [this].



### Verse 8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:8:1)

### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:10:1)

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:10:2)


**נַחֲלָתְךָ וְנִלְאָה אַתָּה כוֹנַנְתָּהּ.** כְּשֶׁהָיְתָה נַחֲלַת אַרְצְךָ נִלְאָה וּצְמֵאָה לְמָטָר, אַתָּה כוֹנַנְתָּ אוֹתָהּ. (מצאתי) **נַחֲלָתְךָ וְנִלְאָה** הַקְּרוּיָה נַחֲלָתְךָ וְהִיא נִלְאָה, כְּלוֹמַר: פְּעָמִים שֶׁהִיא כָּךְ:


**Your heritage, which was weary, You established** When the heritage of Your land was weary and thirsty for rain, You established it [Your heritage]. I found: **Your heritage which was weary** Which is called your heritage, and which is weary; i.e., sometimes it is so.



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:11:1)


**חַיָּתְךָ יָשְׁבוּ בָהּ.** עֲדָתְךָ יָשְׁבוּ בָהּ, כְּמוֹ ״וַיֵּאָסְפוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים אֶת מַחֲנֵיהֶם לַחַיָּה״ (שמואל ב כג:יא). דָּבָר אַחֵר: **חַיָּתְךָ**, כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל קְרוּיָה בְּהֶמְתּוֹ וְחַיָּתוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:


**Your congregation dwelt therein** Heb. (חיתך). Your congregation has dwelt therein, as (II Sam. 23:11): “and the Philistines gathered together their camp (sic) into a troop (לחיה).” Another explanation: The congregation of Israel is known as the animal and the beast of the Holy One, blessed be He.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:11:2)


**תָּכִין בְּטוֹבָתְךָ.** כְּשֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם הֲסִבּוֹתָם בַּמִּדְבָּר אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה, לְפִי שֶׁעָמְדוּ כְּנַעֲנִיִּים וְגָדְעוּ אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת; וּבְתוֹךְ כָּךְ שֶׁעִכְּבוּ בַמִּדְבָּר, עָמְדוּ וְתִקְּנוּ הַכֹּל (מכילתא בשלח ויהי פתיחתא):


**You prepare with your goodness** When they left Egypt, You led them around in the desert for forty years because the Canaanites rose and cut down the trees. During the interim, when they tarried in the desert, they rose and rectified it all.



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:12:1)


**אֲדֹנָי יִתֵּן אֹמֶר הַמְבַשְּׂרוֹת וְגוֹ׳. אֹמֶר** מַאֲמָר; עוֹד הוּא יִשְׁאַג בְּקוֹל לְהַשְׁמִיעַ צִבְאוֹת הַגּוֹיִם הָרַבִּים, וּמַהוּ הָאֹמֶר?


**The Lord will give out a word; they will announce it to a great multitude** Heb. אמר, [like] מאמר, statement. He will yet roar with [His] voice to allow the hosts of the great nations to hear it. Now what is the word?



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:13:1)


**מַלְכֵי צְבָאוֹת הַגּוֹיִם יִדֹּדוּן יִדֹּדוּן.** יִתְנַדּוּ וְיֻשְׁלְכוּ מִתּוֹךְ אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִיא **נְוַת בַּיִת תְּחַלֵּק** אֶת שְׁלָלָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְהָיָה סַחְרָהּ וְאֶתְנַנָּהּ קֹדֶשׁ וְגוֹמֵר״ (ישעיהו כג:יח):


**The kings of the hosts of nations will wander, yea they will wander.** They will wander and be cast out of the land of Israel, and the congregation of Israel, who is the dweller of the house, will divide their spoils, as it is said (Isa. 23:18): “And her commerce and her hire shall be holy, etc.”



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:14:1)


**אִם תִּשְׁכְּבוּן בֵּין שְׁפַתָּיִם וְגוֹ׳.** כָּל זֶה הָאֹמֶר יֹאמַר לָהֶם: אִם אַתֶּם שְׁכַבְתֶּם בֵּין תְּחוּמֵיכֶם וְהִתְעַנַּגְתֶּם בְּתַעֲנוּגִים, זֹאת יוֹנָתִי, כְּנֵסִיָּתִי, כְּנָפֶיהָ **נֶחְפָּה בַכֶּסֶף.** וּמַהוּ הַכֶּסֶף וְהֶחָרוּץ? **בְּפָרֵשׂ שַׁדַּי וְגוֹ׳** כְּשֶׁפֵּרַשׂ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִפְנֵיהֶם תּוֹרָתוֹ, אֲשֶׁר הַמְּלָכִים נִשְׁלָגִים וּמִתְלַבְּנִים בָּהּ בְּאֶרֶץ צַלְמָוֶת וְחֹשֶׁךְ, אָז נֶחְפּוּ כְנָפֶיהָ (כַּנְפֵי יוֹנָָָָה) בְּכַסְפָּהּ וְחֶמְדָּתָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת. **כַּנְפֵי יוֹנָה.** פְּלוּמָ״א בְּלַעַ״ז:


**If you lie between the borders, etc.** All this is the word. He says to them, “If you had lain between your borders and had enjoyed pleasures, this My dove, My congregation, whose feathers are covered with silver.” Now what is the silver, and what is the gold? **(15) When the Almighty spreads out, etc.** When the Holy One, blessed be He, explained His Torah, with which the kings are “snowed and whitened” in a land of the Shadow of Death and darkness then its feathers (dove’s feathers) were covered with the desire and yearning for the Torah and [its] Commandments. **the feathers of a dove** Plumes in French.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:14:2)


**וְאֶבְרוֹתֶיהָ.** כְּנָפֶיהָ שֶׁעוֹפֶפֶת בָּהֶן:


**and its pinions** Its wings, with which it flies.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:14:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:14:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:14:3)


**בִּירַקְרַק חָרוּץ.** פָּתַר דּוּנָשׁ בֶּן לַבְרַט: הֶחָרוּץ הוּא זָהָב, וְלָכָךְ נְתָנוֹ הַמְשׁוֹרֵר אֵצֶל הַכֶּסֶף, וִירַקְרַק הֶחָרוּץ הוּא הַזָּהָב אֲשֶׁר יוּבָא מֵאֶרֶץ הַחֲוִילָה וּמֵאֶרֶץ כּוּשׁ, זָהָב טוֹב מְאֹד מְאֹד (בראשית ב:יא-יג; איוב כח:יט). לֹא הוּא יָרוֹק וְלֹא הוּא אָדוֹם, וְלָכָךְ קְרָאוֹ יְרַקְרַק; כְּמוֹ ״לָבָן אֲדַמְדָּם״ (ויקרא יג:מב) – שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא לָבָן וְלֹא אָדוֹם. לְכָךְ נִכְפַּל: יְרַקְרַק, אֲדַמְדָּם:


**with brilliant gold** Heb. בירקרק חרוץ. Dunash the son of Labrat interpreted חרוּץ as gold. Therefore, the Psalmist juxtaposed it to silver, and ירקרק חרוץ is the gold brought from the land of Havilah and from the land of Cush; very good gold, neither yellow nor red. Therefore, it is called ירקרק, as (Lev. 13:42): “reddish white (לבן אדמדם),” which is neither white nor red. Therefore, it is doubled: אדמדם, ירקרק.



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:15:1)


**בְּפָרֵשׂ.** לְשׁוֹן ״וּפָרְשׂוּ אֶת הַשִּׂמְלָה״ (דברים כב:יז), בּוֹרְרִין אֶת הַדָּבָר כְּשִׂמְלָה חֲדָשָׁה (כתובות מו.):


**When... spreads out** Heb. בפרש, an expression of (Deut. 22:17): “and they will spread out (ופרשו) the garment”; they clarify the matter as a new garment.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:15:2)


**מְלָכִים.** אֵלּוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: (משלי ח:טו) ״בִּי מְלָכִים יִמְלֹכוּ״:


**kings** These are the Torah scholars, as it is said (Prov. 8:15): “Kings reign with me.”



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:16:1)


**הַר אֱלֹהִים הַר בָּשָׁן.** וְהֵיכָן פֵּרְשָׁהּ? בְּהַר סִינַי, שֶׁהוּא הַר אֱלֹהִים סָמוּךְ לַבָּשָׁן בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן:


**The mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan** And where did He spread it out? On Mt. Sinai, which is the mountain of God and is near Bashan on the eastern side of the Jordan.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:16:2)


**הַר גַּבְנֻנִּים.** הַר הַמְיֻחָד שֶׁבֶּהָרִים:


**the mountain of peaks** The special mountain among the mountains.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:16:3)


**גִּבְנֻנִּים.** לְשׁוֹן הָרִים, עַל שֵׁם גָּבְהָם, כְּמוֹ ״וַתִּבְנִי לָךְ גָּב״ (יחזקאל טז:כד). כָּל דָּבָר גָּבוֹהַּ קָרוּי גַּב:


**peaks** Heb. גבננים, an expression of mountains, because of their height, as (Ezek. 16:24): “and you built for yourself a platform (גב).” Any high thing is called גַב.



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:17:1)


**לָמָּה תְּרַצְּדוּן הָרִים גַּבְנֻנִּים.** כָּל זֶה מוּסָב עַל **ה׳ יִתֵּן אֹמֶר.** עוֹד יֹאמַר לָהֶם **לָמָּה תְּרַצְּדוּן הָרִים גַּבְנֻנִּים**, לָמָּה תְּאָרְבוּן אַתֶּם הַהָרִים גַּבְנֻנִּים הַגְּבוֹהִים לְהַשְׁחִית אֶת הָהָר אֲשֶׁר **חָמַד אֱלֹהִים לְשִׁבְתּוֹ** לִשְׁרוֹת עָלָיו שְׁכִינָה, הוּא הַר הַבַּיִת? **אַף הוּא לָנֶצַח יִשְׁכֹּן שָׁם**, קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ קְדֻשַּׁת עוֹלָם. מִשֶּׁנִּבְחַר לְשִׁבְתּוֹ, לֹא שָׁרְתָה שְׁכִינָה בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר. רָאִיתִי בִּיסוֹדוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֹשֶׁה הַדַּרְשָׁן: רָצַד הוּא מַאֲרָב בִּלְשׁוֹן עֲרָבִי, אֲבָל מְנַחֵם פֵּרֵשׁ **תְּרַצְּדוּן** כְּמוֹ תְּרַקְּדוּן, אַף אוֹתוֹ לָשׁוֹן נוֹפֵל עַל הַשִּׁיטָה הַזֹּאת:


**Why do you lurk, you lofty mountains** All this refers back to “The Lord will give out a word.” He says further to them, “Why do you lurk (תרצדון), you lofty mountains?” Why do you lurk, you lofty mountains, to destroy the mountain that God desired for His dwelling, to cause His Shechinah to rest upon it? That is the Temple Mount. Even He will dwell there forever. Its sanctity is a perpetual sanctity. After it was chosen for His dwelling, the Shechinah did not rest elsewhere. I saw in the works of Rabbi Moshe Hadarshan that רצד is “ambush” in Arabic. But Menachem (p. 166) explained תרצדוּן like תרקדוּן, you prance. That expression, too, fits the context.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:18:1)


**רֶכֶב אֱלֹהִים וְגוֹ׳.** עוֹד זֶה מוּסָב עַל **ה׳ יִתֵּן אֹמֶר** לְהַזְכִּיר חִבַּת עַמּוֹ: אַף כְּשֶׁנִּגְלָה **רֶכֶב אֱלֹהִים רִבֹּתַיִם שֶׁל אַלְפַּיִם שִׁנְאָנִים.** שְׁנוּנִים, מַלְאָכִים חַדִּים, **וַה׳ הָיָה** בֵּינֵיהֶם **בְּסִינַי בַּקֹּדֶשׁ**, אַף שָׁם:


**God’s chariot, etc.** This too refers back to the “The Lord will give forth a word,” to mention the love of His people. Even when God’s chariot of “twice ten thousand times thousands of” brilliant “sharpened” angels appeared, and the Lord was among them at Sinai with His holiness, there too,



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:19:1)


**עָלִיתָ.** אַתָּה נָגִיד עַמּוֹ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן עַמְרָם לַמָּרוֹם, **שָׁבִיתָ שֶׁבִי** אֶת הַתּוֹרָה, **וְלָקַחְתָּ מַתָּנוֹת** מִן הָעֶלְיוֹנִים וּלְתִתָּם לִבְנֵי אָדָם:


you, the leader of His people, Moses the son of Amram **ascended** on high and took captives.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:19:2)


**וְאַף סוֹרְרִים לִשְׁכֹּן יָהּ אֱלֹהִים.** אַף עוֹד גָּרַמְתָּ שֶׁשָּׁכַן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בַּמִּשְׁכָּן בְּתוֹךְ עַם שֶׁהָיוּ סוֹרְרִים וּמַמְרִים וּמַקְצִיפִים אוֹתוֹ:


**and also rebellious ones for Yah God to dwell** Also you brought about that the Holy One, blessed be He, rested in the Tabernacle of the Torah, and you took gifts from the celestial beings to give them to the sons of men, also among a people who were rebellious and were rebelling against Him and provoking Him.



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:20:1)


**בָּרוּךְ אֲדֹנָי וְגוֹ׳.** זֶה מִן הַשִּׁיר הָאָמוּר לְמַעְלָה, **שִׁירוּ לֵאלֹהִים**:


**Blessed is the Lord, etc.** This is part of the song mentioned above: “Sing to God.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:20:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:20:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:20:2)


**יַעֲמָס לָנוּ.** יִתֵּן לָנוּ יְשׁוּעָה רַבָּה מִכָּל עֹמֶס כְּכָל אֲשֶׁר נוּכַל שְׂאֵת, (מצאתי **יוֹם יוֹם יַעֲמָס לָנוּ** כָּל הַיָּמִים כֵּן נוֹהֵג בָּנוּ לְכָל צָרָה יְשׁוּעָה):


**lavishes upon us** He will give us a great salvation, [greater] than any burden, as much as we can carry. (I found: **every day...lavishes upon us** He always behaves in this manner to us, that for every distress there is a salvation.)



### Verse 21

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:21:1)


**הָאֵל לָנוּ אֵל לְמוֹשָׁעוֹת.** אֵל מוֹשִׁיעַ הוּא לָנוּ, וּלְפָנָיו יֵשׁ הַרְבֵּה תּוֹצָאוֹת מִינֵי מָוֶת. **תּוֹצָאוֹת** דְּרָכִים אֶל הַמָּוֶת, אַךְ לֹא עָלֵינוּ הוּא נוֹתְנָם, אֲבָל יִמְחַץ בָּהֶם רֹאשׁ אוֹיְבָיו:


**God is to us the God of salvations** God is our Savior, but He has many paths, i.e., kinds of death. תוצאות means, ways to death. However, He does not lay them upon us, but with them He wounds the head of His enemies.



### Verse 22

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:22:1)


**קָדְקֹד שֵׂעָר.** קָדְקֳדוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו שֶׁהוּא אִישׁ שָׂעִיר (בראשית כז:יא), הַמִּתְהַלֵּךְ תָּמִיד בַּאֲשָׁמָיו (וְאֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר מֵרָעָתוֹ):


**the hairy pate** The pate of Esau, who is a “hairy man,” and who always goes with his guilt.



### Verse 23

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:23:1)


**אָמַר ה׳ מִבָּשָׁן אָשִׁיב.** כִּי כֵן הִבְטִיחַ, לְהָשִׁיב אוֹתָנוּ מִתּוֹךְ אַבִּירֵי בָשָׁן וּמֵאִיֵּי הַיָּם (ישעיה יא:יא):


**The Lord said, “I shall restore from Bashan”** For so He promised to restore us from the mighty ones of Bashan and from the islands of the sea.



### Verse 24

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:24:1)


**לְמַעַן תִּמְחַץ.** רַגְלֵינוּ **בְּדָם.** כְּשֶׁיִּמְחַץ אֶת רֹאשׁ הָאוֹיֵב, תְּהֵא רַגְלֵינוּ בּוֹקַעַת בְּדָמָם. תִּמְחַץ לְשׁוֹן בּוֹקֵעַ בְּתוֹךְ הַדָּם, כְּמוֹ ״מָחֲצָה וְחָלְפָה רַקָּתוֹ״ (שופטים ה:כו) כְּמוֹ בָּקְעָה. וּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה הוּא: וְהָיוּ עוֹלֵי רְגָלִים בּוֹקְעִים עַד אַרְכֻּבּוֹתֵיהֶם בְּדָם. דָּבָר אַחֵר: תִּמְחַץ שֵׁם כְּלִי שֶׁשּׁוֹאֲבִין בּוֹ יַיִן מִן הַבּוֹר מַחַץ שְׁמוֹ בְּמַסֶּכֶת עֲבוֹדַת גִּלּוּלִים (עבודה זרה עד:):


**In order that your foot may wade through blood** When He crushes the head of the enemy, our feet will wade through their blood. תִּמְחַץ is an expression of splitting into the blood, as (Jud. 5: 26): “she split (ומחצה) and penetrated his temple,” like בָּקְעָה, she split. This is Mishnaic Hebrew: “and the pilgrims were wading (בוקעים) up to their knees in blood.” Another explanation: תִּמְחַץ The name of a vessel with which they draw wine from the pit is called מַחַץ, in Tractate Avodah Zarah (72b).


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:24:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:24:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:24:2)


**מֵאוֹיְבִים.** מִדַּם הָאוֹיְבִים:


**from the enemies** From the blood of the enemies.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:24:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:24:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:24:3)


**מִנֵּהוּ.** תִּהְיֶה פַּרְנָסָתוֹ, כְּדְאָמְרִינַן: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּ״מָן״ לִישְׁנָא דִּמְזוֹנֵי הוּא? דִּכְתִיב (דניאל א:י) ״אֲשֶׁר מִנָּה אֶת מַאֲכַלְכֶם וְגוֹמֵר״ (סוכה לט:):


**will have its portion** Heb. מנהו, its sustenance will be, as we say (Suc. 39b): “How do we know that מן is an expression of food?” For it is written (Dan. 1: 10): “who appointed (מנה) your food, etc.”



### Verse 25

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:25:1)


**רָאוּ הֲלִיכוֹתֶיךָ אֱלֹהִים.** כְּלוֹמַר: לְאֵלּוּ נָאֶה לְךָ לְהוֹשִׁיעַ, שֶׁכְּשֶׁרָאוּ הֲלִיכוֹתֶיךָ בִּקְדֻשָּׁתְךָ בַּיָּם, קִדְּמוּ שָׁרִים לְשׁוֹרֵר לְפָנֶיךָ שִׁירַת הַיָּם (שמות טו:א), וְאַחֲרֵיהֶם בָּאוּ הַנּוֹגְנִים, אֵלּוּ הַמַּלְאָכִים:


**They saw Your ways, O God** That is to say, it is fitting that You save these people, for when they saw Your ways in Your sanctity in the sea, singers came first to sing before You the Song of the Sea, and after them came the minstrels—these are the angels.



### Verse 26

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:26:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:26:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:26:1)


**בְּתוֹךְ עֲלָמוֹת תּוֹפֵפוֹת.** בְּתוֹךְ מִרְיָם וְנַעֲרוֹתֶיהָ אֲשֶׁר לָקְחָה הַתֹּף בְּיָדָהּ (שמות טו:כ) וְאָמְרוּ בְּשִׁבְחָם:


**in the midst of maidens playing timbrels** With Miriam and her maidens, who took the timbrel in her hand, and they said with their praise...



### Verse 27

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:27:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:27:1)


**בְּמַקְהֵלוֹת בָּרְכוּ אֱלֹהִים אֲדֹנָי מִמְּקוֹר יִשְׂרָאֵל.** אַף עוּבָּרִים מִמְּעֵי אִמָּן אָמְרוּ שִׁירָה:


**In congregations bless God, the Lord, from the womb of Israel** Even the fetuses in their mothers’ wombs recited the Song.



### Verse 28

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:28:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:28:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:28:1)


**שָׁם בִּנְיָמִין.** הַצָּעִיר נַעֲשָׂה רוֹדֶה עֲלֵיהֶם:


**There Benjamin** the youngest became the ruler over them.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:28:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:28:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:28:2)


**רֹדֵם.** כְּמוֹ רוֹדָם בְּקָמָ״ץ, מִשָּׁם זָכָה לִהְיוֹת מֶלֶךְ, לְפִי שֶׁיָּרַד תְּחִלָּה לַיָּם. וְכֵן אָמַר לוֹ שְׁמוּאֵל לְשָׁאוּל: ״הֲלוֹא אִם קָטֹן אַתָּה בְּעֵינֶיךָ רֹאשׁ שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אָתָּה״ (שמואל א טו:יז), וְתִרְגְּמוֹ יוֹנָתָן: ״שִׁבְטָא דְבִנְיָמִין עֲבַר בְּיַמָּא בְּרֵישׁ כָּל שְׁאָר שִׁבְטַיָּא״:


**rules over them** Heb. רֹדֵם, like רֹדָם, with a “kamatz.” From there, he merited to become king because he descended first into the sea, and so did Samuel say to Saul (I Sam. 15:17): “Even if you are small in your own eyes, are you not the head of the tribes of Israel?” which Jonathan paraphrases: The tribe of Benjamin crossed the sea at the head of all the other tribes.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:28:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:28:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:28:3)


**שָׂרֵי יְהוּדָה רִגְמָתָם.** מִתְקַנְּאִים בָּהֶם וְזוֹרְקִין בָּהֶם אֲבָנִים, וְכֵן שָׂרֵי זְבוּלוּן וְנַפְתָּלִי. וְכֵן אָמַר לוֹ: **צִוָּה אֱלֹהֶיךָ עֻזֶּךָ** (ס״א אינו). דָּבָר אַחֵר: (**רִגְמָתָם** – רִקְמָתָם, לְבוּשָׁן בִּגְדֵי וְכוּ׳) רִקְמָתָם לְשׁוֹן אַרְגָּמָן, כָּךְ חִבְּרוֹ מְנַחֵם:


**the princes of Judah pelt them with stones** They envy them and throw stones at them, and so do the princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naftali. So, he says to him, “Your God has commanded your strength.” Another explanation: רִגְמָתָם is the equivalent of רִקְמָתָם, their embroidery, their embroidered garments, an expression of purple (ארגמן). In this way Menachem associated it (p. 161).



### Verse 29

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:29:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:29:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:29:1)


**עוּזָּה אֱלֹהִים וְגוֹ׳.** עַכְשָׁיו חוֹזֵר הַמְשׁוֹרֵר לִתְפִלָּתוֹ שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל **יָקוּם אֱלֹהִים וְיָפוּצוּ אוֹיְבָיו** :**עוּזָּה אֱלֹהִים** וְהִתְגַּבֵּר, אֲשֶׁר כָּל אֵלֶּה **פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ**:


**show this strength, O God, etc.** Now the Psalmist returns to his prayer that he prayed, “Let God rise, and let His enemies scatter.” Show Your strength, O God, and strengthen Yourself, for You have wrought all these for us.



### Verse 30

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:30:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:30:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:30:1)


**מֵהֵיכָלֶךָ עַל יְרוּשָׁלִָם.** וּמִמַּה שֶּׁיִּרְאוּ הַמְּלָכִים כְּבוֹד הֵיכָלְךָ אֲשֶׁר עַל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, **יוֹבִילוּ לְךָ** דּוֹרוֹן **וְשָׁי**:


**From Your Temple, which is over Jerusalem, etc.** And since the kings will see the glory of Your temple, which is over Jerusalem, they will bring You a gift and a tribute.



### Verse 31

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:31:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:31:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:31:1)


**גְּעַר חַיַּת קָנֶה.** זֶה עֲמָלֵק שֶׁנִּמְשַׁל כְּחַיַּת יַעַר הַדָּר בֵּין הַקָּנִים (תהלים פ:יד):


**Rebuke the people of the forest** This is Ishmael [Esau], who is compared to the “boar from the forest,” which dwells among the reeds (below 80:14).


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:31:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:31:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:31:2)


**עֲדַת אַבִּירִים בְּעֶגְלֵי עַמִּים.** עַם שֶׁשָּׁמְנוּ וְעָשְׁתוּ כְּפָרִים אַבִּירִים בְּתוֹךְ שְׁאָר הָאֻמּוֹת, שֶׁאֵינָם אֶלָּא כַּעֲגָלִים לְנֶגְדָּם:


**the congregation of mighty bulls, among peoples like calves** A people that has become fat and thick like mighty bulls among the other nations, which are merely like calves as compared to them.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:31:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:31:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:31:3)


**מִתְרַפֵּס בְּרַצֵּי כָסֶף.** אֵינָם מִתְרַצִּים לְכָל אָדָם, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מְרַצֶּה לָהֶם מָעוֹת (פסחים קיח:):


**submitting himself for pieces of silver** They do not submit themselves to any person unless he persuades them with money.


###### Rashi on Psalms 68:31:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:31:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:31:4)


**בִּזַּר עַמִּים.** פִּזְּרוּ אֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר: ״אַף חֹבֵב עַמִּים״ (דברים לג:ג). וְתָמִיד קְרָבוֹת יֶחְפָּצוּן, חֲפֵצִים לְהִלָּחֵם בָּנוּ:


**he scatters peoples** They scattered the tribes, as it is said: (Deut. 33:3): “Also He loves the peoples,” and they always desire battles. They want to fight with us.



### Verse 32

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:32:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:32:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:32:1)


**יֶאֱתָיוּ חַשְׁמַנִּים.** וְאָז, כְּשֶׁתַּחֲרִיב אֶת עֲמָלֵק וְיָקוּם מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ, יָבִיאוּ לְךָ דּוֹרוֹנוֹת מִמִּצְרַיִם וּמִכּוּשׁ. וּמְנַחֵם פָּתַר חַשְׁמַנִּים שֵׁם מְדִינָה יוֹשְׁבֵי חַשְׁמוֹנָה (במדבר לג:כט), וְהַפּוֹתְרִים פּוֹתְרִין אוֹתוֹ לְשׁוֹן דּוֹרוֹן:


**Gifts will be brought** (Then, when You destroy Esau and the King Messiah arises, they will bring you gifts from Egypt and from Cush.Parshandatha) Then, when You scatter the enemy, and the King Messiah arises in the future, they will bring you gifts from Egypt and from Cush. Menachem interpreted חשמנים as the name of a province, the dwellers of Hashmonah (p. 96), but the commentators interpret it as an expression of a gift.



### Verse 33

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:33:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:33:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:33:1)


**שִׁירוּ לֵאלֹהִים.** שֶׁהֶרְאָם גָּדְלוֹ וְגָאַל אֶת עַמּוֹ:


**sing to God** Who showed His greatness and redeemed His people.



### Verse 34

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:34:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:34:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:34:1)


**הֵן יִתֵּן.** הֵן נוֹתֵן:


**behold He gives forth** Heb. יתן, behold He gives.



### Verse 36

###### Rashi on Psalms 68:36:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:36:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/68:36:1)


**נוֹרָא אֱלֹהִים מִמִּקְדָּשֶׁיךָ.** מִמַּה שֶׁהֶחֱרַבְתּוֹ אַתָּה יָראוּי, אִם לְמִקְדָּשׁוֹ לֹא נָשָׂא פָנִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר לָרְשָׁעִים. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: אַל תִּקְרֵי מִמִּקְדָּשֶׁיךָ אֶלָּא מִמְּקֻדָּשֶׁיךָ, שֶׁכְּשֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה דִּין בַּצַּדִּיקִים מִתְיָרֵא וּמִתְעַלֶּה וּמִתְקַלֵּס, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר ״בִּקְרֹבַי אֶקָּדֵשׁ״ (ויקרא י:ג) ״וְנִקְדַּשׁ בִּכְבֹדִי״ (שמות כט:מג) בְּמִיתַת שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן (זבחים קטו:). וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָּרְשׁוּ כָּל הַמִּזְמוֹר עַד **בָּרוּךְ ה׳ יוֹם יוֹם** עַל מַתַּן תּוֹרָה וְגֶשֶׁם נְדָבוֹת בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה וְחַיָּתְךָ יָשְׁבוּ בָהּ. וַאֲנִי אֵין לִבִּי מִתְיַשֵּׁב לְאֻמָּן לְשׁוֹן יָשְׁבוּ בָהּ בִּלְשׁוֹן נִתְיַשְּׁבוּ בַּתּוֹרָה, וְהָהָר חָמַד אֱלֹהִים לְשִׁבְתּוֹ אֵין מִתְיַשֵּׁב לְדָרְשׁוֹ עַל הַר סִינַי שֶׁהֲרֵי לֹא לְשִׁבְתּוֹ חֲמָדוֹ וְלֹא לִשְׁכֹּן בּוֹ לָנֶצַח, וְכָאן כְּתִיב יִשְׁכֹּן לָנֶצַח וְכֵן מַלְכֵי צְבָאוֹת פֵּרְשׁוּ כְּמוֹ מַלְאֲכֵי צְבָאוֹת וְאֵין זֶה לְשׁוֹן הַמִּקְרָא:


**You are feared, O God, from Your Sanctuary** Because You destroyed it, You are feared. If He did not show favoritism to His [own] Sanctuary, surely [He will] not [show favoritism] to the wicked of the heathens. The Midrash Aggadah explains: Do not read: מִמִּקְדָּשֶׁיךָ, “from Your Sanctuaries,” but מִמְּקֻדְּשֶׁיךָ, “from Your hallowed ones.” When the Holy One, blessed be He, executes justice upon the righteous, He is feared, elevated, and praised. Similarly, it is said (Lev. 10:3): “Through those near to me I will be sanctified.” [Also] (Exod. 29:43), “and it will be sanctified with My honor” [i.e., with My honored ones]. With the death of Aaron’s two sons (Zev. 115b). Our Rabbis, however, expounded on the entire psalm until (verse 20): “Blessed is the Lord; every day” as referring to the giving of the Torah; (verse 10) “generous rain” refers to the giving of the Torah, and (verse 11) “Your congregation dwelt therein,” means that they became engrossed in Torah (Mid. Ps. 68 with variations). But as for me I feel uncertain in explaining the expression ישבוּ as meaning that they became engrossed in Torah. Also, my heart is uneasy at explaining (verse 17) “the mountain that God desired for His dwelling” as referring to Mt. Sinai, because He did not desire it for His dwelling and [did] not [want] to dwell there forever, whereas here it is written: “Even the Lord will dwell there forever.” Likewise (verse 13): “Kings (מלכי) of hosts,” he explained as “angels (מלאכי) of hosts,” which is not the language of Scripture.



## Chapter 69


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 69:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:1:1)


**עַל שׁוֹשַׁנִּים.** עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם ״כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין הַחוֹחִים״ (שיר השירים ב:ב), שֶׁהַחוֹחִים מְנַקְּבִין אוֹתָם, וְהִתְפַּלֵּל עֲלֵיהֶם:


**on shoshannim** Concerning Israel, who are like a rose (שושנה) among the thorns, pricked by the thorns, and he prayed for them.

###### Rashi on Psalms 69:2:1

**in muddy depths** In the mire, the mud of the deep.


###### Rashi on Psalms 69:3:2

**וְשִׁבֹּלֶת.** הוּא שֶׁטֶף חֹזֶק הַנָּהָר, פִּי״ל בְּלַעַ״ז:


**and the current** That is the flood of the strength of the river, fil in Old French, current.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 69:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:4:1)


**נָחַר.** יָבֵשׁ, כְּמוֹ ״חָרָה מִנִּי חֹרֶב״ (איוב ל:ל):


**has become parched** Heb. נחר, dry, as (Job 30:30): “are burned (חרה) with heat.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 69:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:4:2)


**כָּלוּ עֵינַי.** כָּל תּוֹחֶלֶת מְמֻשָּׁכָה קְרוּיָה כִּלְיוֹן עֵינַיִם, כְּמוֹ ״וְכָלוֹת אֲלֵיהֶם כָּל הַיּוֹם״ (דברים כח:לב), ״מְכַלּוֹת עֵינַיִם״ (ויקרא כו:טז), ״וְעֵינֵי רְשָׁעִים תִּכְלֶינָה״ (איוב יא:כ):


**my eyes fail** Any drawn-out hope is called “failure of the eyes,” as (Deut. 28:32): “and pine after them all day”. [Similarly] (Lev. 26:16): “that cause the eyes to pine away”; (Job 11:20), “and the eyes of the wicked will pine away.”

**אוֹיְבֵי שֶׁקֶר.** שׂוֹנְאִים אוֹתִי עַל שֶׁקֶר, שֶׁאֵין אֲנִי רוֹדֵף אַחַר שֶׁקֶר שֶׁלָּהֶם לִתְפֹּשׂ טָעוּתָם:


**who are my enemies because of lies** They hate me because of a lie, because I do not pursue their lies to adopt their error.

**Do not let those who hope for You be shamed** Do not leave me in their hands lest those who hope for You be shamed by what happens to me and say, “Didn’t that happen to one who hopes to the Holy One, blessed be He?”

### Verse 21

###### Rashi on Psalms 69:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:21:1)


**וָאָנוּשָׁה.** וָאֵאָנַשׁ וָאֶחֱלֶה, כְּמוֹ ״כִּי אֲנוּשָׁה מַכּוֹתֶיהָ״ (מיכה א:ט), וּכְמוֹ ״וַיֵּאָנַשׁ הַיֶּלֶד״ דְּבַת שֶׁבַע (שמואל ב יב:טו). וְאִם תֹּאמַר: הֵיאַךְ הָאָלֶ״ף זוֹ מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת שֹׁרֶשׁ וּמְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת שִׁמּוּשׁ הַמֵּסֵב הַדִּבּוּר אֶל הַמְדַבֵּר? כֵּן דֶּרֶךְ תֵּבָה שֶׁתְּחִלָּתָהּ אָלֶ״ף, כְּגוֹן: ״וָאֹהַב אֶת יַעֲקֹב״ (מלאכי א:ב), ״אֲנִי אֹהֲבַי אֵהָב״ (משלי ח:יז) – הֲרֵי הוּא כְּמוֹ ׳וָאֶאֱהַב׳, וְכֵן ״אָסֹף אָסֵף״ (צפניה א:ב) – כְּמוֹ ׳אֶאֱסֹף׳:


**and I have become ill** Heb. ואנושה, I am ailing and sick, as (Micah 1:9): “For she is mortally ill (אנושה) [from] her wounds,” and as (II Sam. 12:15): “and the child (sic) became mortally ill (ויאנש),” of Bathsheba. Now if you ask how this “aleph” serves as a radical and also as a prefix denoting the first person, this is the way of a word beginning with “aleph.” For example, (Mal. 1:2): “and I loved (וָאֹהַב) Jacob”; (Prov. 8:17), “I will love (אֵהָב) those who love me.” It is equivalent to וָאֶאֶהַב Similarly, (Zeph. 1:2): “I will totally destroy (אָסֹף אָסֵף),” like אֶאֶסֹף.

###### Rashi on Psalms 69:27:2

**רָדָפוּ.** אַתָּה קָצַפְתָּ מְעַט וְהֵם עָזְרוּ לְרָעָה (זכריה א:טו):


**they pursued** For You were a little angry, and they helped cause harm.


###### Rashi on Psalms 69:27:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:27:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:27:3)


**וְאֶל מַכְאוֹב חֲלָלֶיךָ יְסַפֵּרוּ.** דִּבְרֵיהֶם לָבוֹא בְּעֵצָה: נַשְׁחִיתֵם ״בִּהְיוֹתָם כֹּאֲבִים״ (בראשית לד:כה):


**and about the pain of those whom You wounded they tell** their words, to plot: “Let us destroy them while they are in pain.”



### Verse 32

###### Rashi on Psalms 69:32:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:32:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:32:1)


**וְתִיטַב.** הִלּוּלִי לַה׳:


**And it will appeal to the Lord** My praise to the Lord.


###### Rashi on Psalms 69:32:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:32:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:32:2)


**מִשּׁוֹר פָּר.** הוּא שׁוֹר שֶׁהִקְרִיב אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן, שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּקוֹמָתוֹ; וּבַיּוֹם שֶׁנִּקְרָא שׁוֹר, בּוֹ בַיּוֹם הֱבִיאוֹ. שֶׁהַשּׁוֹר בֶּן יוֹמוֹ קָרוּי שׁוֹר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שׁוֹר אוֹ כֶשֶׂב אוֹ עֵז כִּי יִוָּלֵד״ (ויקרא כ״ב:כ״ז). בּוֹ בַיּוֹם נִדְמָה לְפַר, שֶׁהוּא בֶּן שָׁלֹשׁ (ראש השנה י.):


**more than a young bull that is mature** That is the bull sacrificed by Adam, which was created at its height. On the day it was called שּׁוֹר, on that very day, he brought it, for a bull on day of its birth is called שּׁוֹר, as it is said (Lev. 22:27): “A bull (שור), a lamb, or a goat, that is born.” On that very day, it resembled a פַּר, which is a three-year old.


###### Rashi on Psalms 69:32:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:32:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/69:32:3)


**מַקְרִן מַפְרִיס.** קַרְנוֹתָיו קָדְמוּ לְפַרְסוֹתָיו, שֶׁהֲרֵי בְּקוֹמָתוֹ וּבְקַרְנָיו נִבְרָא, וְרֹאשׁוֹ יָצָא מִן הָאָרֶץ תְּחִלָּה; כְּדֶרֶךְ כָּל הַנּוֹלָדִים הוֹצִיאַתָן הָאָרֶץ, נִמְצְאוּ קַרְנָיו קָדְמוּ לְרַגְלָיו (חולין ס.):


**with horns and hooves** Its horns preceded its hooves, because it was created at its height with its horns, and its head emerged from the ground first; the earth thrust them forth in the manner in which all creatures are born, so that its horns preceded its feet.



## Chapter 70


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 70:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/70:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/70:1:1)


**לְדָוִד לְהַזְכִּיר.** לְשׁוֹן תְּפִלָּה הוּא, כְּמוֹ ״וַאֲנַחְנוּ בְּשֵׁם ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ נַזְכִּיר״ (תהלים כ:ח), וְכֵן בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ״לְהַזְכִּיר וּלְהוֹדוֹת לַה׳״ (דברי הימים א טז:ד). וּבְמִדְרַשׁ תְּהִלִּים רָאִיתִי: מָשָׁל לְמֶלֶךְ שֶׁכָּעַס עַל צֹאנוֹ וְסָתַר אֶת הַדִּיר וְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַצֹּאן וְאֶת הָרוֹעֶה. אַחַר זְמַן הֶחֱזִיר אֶת הַצֹּאן וּבָנָה אֶת הַדִּיר, וְלֹא הִזְכִּיר אֶת הָרוֹעֶה. אָמַר הָרוֹעֶה: הֲרֵי הַצֹּאן מֻחְזָר וְהַדִּיר בָּנוּי, וַאֲנִי אֵינִי נִזְכָּר? כָּךְ, לְמַעְלָה מִן הָעִנְיָן נֶאֱמַר ״כִּי אֱלֹהִים יוֹשִׁיעַ צִיּוֹן וְגוֹ׳״ (תהלים סט:לו), ״וְאוֹהֲבֵי שְׁמוֹ יִשְׁכְּנוּ בָהּ״ (תהלים סט:לז): הֲרֵי הַדִּיר בָּנוּי וְהַצֹּאן כָּנוּס, וְהָרוֹעֶה (זֶה דָוִד) לֹא נִזְכָּר. לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר: **לְדָוִד לְהַזְכִּיר אֱלֹהִים לְהַצִּילֵנִי**:


**of David, to make mention** This is an expression of prayer, as (above 20:8): “but we pray (נזכיר) in the name of the Lord our God.” Similarly, in (I) Chronicles (16:4): “to invoke (להזכיר) and to give thanks to the Lord.” In Midrash Psalms (70:1) I saw: This is comparable to a king who became wroth with his flock, and demolished the sheepcote and took out the flock and the shepherd. Sometime later, he restored the flock and rebuilt the sheepcote, but he did not mention the shepherd. Said the shepherd, “Behold, the flock is restored and the sheepcote is rebuilt, but I am not mentioned.” Similarly, in the preceding chapter it says: “When God saves Zion, etc., and those who love His name dwell therein.” Behold the sheepcote is built and the flock is brought into it, but I am not mentioned. Therefore it says: “Of David, to make mention. O God, to save me.”

**יָשׁוּבוּ עַל עֵקֶב בָּשְׁתָּם.** מִדָּה בְּמִדָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁעָשׂוּ לִי:

### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 72:1:1

###### Rashi on Psalms 72:1:2
