### Verse 6

###### Rashi on Psalms 111:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/111:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/111:6:1)


**כֹּחַ מַעֲשָׂיו הִגִּיד לְעַמּוֹ.** כְּשֶׁנָּתַן **לָהֶם נַחֲלַת גּוֹיִם** הוֹדִיעָם כֹּחוֹ וּגְבוּרָתוֹ. וּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא (תנחומא, בראשית יא) כָּתַב לְיִשְׂרָאֵל מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית, לְהוֹדִיעָם שֶׁהָאָרֶץ שֶׁלּוֹ וּבְיָדוֹ לְהוֹשִׁיב בָּהּ כָּל מִי שֶׁיִּרְצֶה וְלַעֲקֹר אֵלּוּ וּלְהוֹשִׁיב אֲחֵרִים, שֶׁלֹּא יוּכְלוּ הָאֻמּוֹת לוֹמַר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל גַּזְלָנִים אַתֶּם שֶׁכְּבַשְׁתֶּם אֶרֶץ שִׁבְעָה גּוֹיִם:


**The strength of His works He related to His people** When He gave them the inheritance of the nations, He let them know His strength and His might. And Midrash Tanchuma (Buber, Bereishith 11): He wrote for Israel [about] the Creation to let them know that the earth is His and that it is in His power to settle in it anyone He wishes, and to move these out and settle others, so that the nations will not be able to say to Israel, “You are thieves, for you conquered the land of the seven nations.”



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 111:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/111:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/111:8:1)


**סְמוּכִים.** הֵם פְּקוּדָיו עַל סֶמֶךְ עֹז, מְחֻזָּקִין בָּעֳנָשִׁין וְאַזְהָרוֹת, וְהַפָּרָשִׁיּוֹת קְבוּעוֹת זוֹ עַל זוֹ כְּסֵדֶר וְלִדְרֹשׁ. וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר שְׁלֹמֹה: ״שׁוֹקָיו עַמּוּדֵי שֵׁשׁ וְגוֹ׳״ (שיר השירים ה:טו):


**Steadfast** are His commandments, supported by might, strengthened with punishments and warnings, and the chapters are set one next to the other in sequence and to expound on them. This is what Solomon said (Song 5:15): “His thighs are pillars of marble, etc.”



## Chapter 112


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 112:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/112:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/112:2:1)


**דּוֹר יְשָׁרִים.** אֲשֶׁר **יְבֹרָךְ יִהְיֶה זַרְעוֹ**:


**a generation of upright ones** which will be blessed, will be his seed.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 112:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/112:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/112:4:1)


**זָרַח בַּחֹשֶׁךְ אוֹר.** כְּמוֹ הִזְרִיחַ, וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ: הוּא עַצְמוֹ כִּבְיָכוֹל נַעֲשָׂה לָהֶם אוֹר, כְּמוֹ ״ה׳ אוֹרִי וְיִשְׁעִי״ (תהלים כז:א):


**He shone a light in the darkness** Heb. זרח [the “kal” conjugation], like הזריח, [the “hiph’il” or causative conjugation]. Its midrashic interpretation is that He Himself, so to speak, becomes a light for them, as (above 27:1): “The Lord is my light and my salvation.”



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 112:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/112:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/112:5:1)


**טוֹב אִישׁ חוֹנֵן וּמַלְוֶה וְגוֹ׳.** שֶׁחוֹנֵן דַּלִּים וּמַלְוֶה לָהֶם, וְאֵינוֹ מְדַקְדֵּק לוֹמַר: אֵין יְכֹלֶת בְּיָדִי, וְאֶת דְּבָרָיו הַצְּרִיכִין לוֹ בְּמַאֲכָל וּבְמִשְׁתֶּה וּבִכְסוּת מְכַלְכֵּל **בְּמִשְׁפָּט** וּבְמִדָּה, וְחָס עַל נְכָסָיו:


**Good is the man who is gracious, etc.** who is gracious to the poor and lends [to] them, and is not strict, saying, “I cannot afford it,” but [instead] his things, which he needs for himself, in food, drink, and clothing,


###### Rashi on Psalms 112:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/112:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/112:5:2)


**יְכַלְכֵּל דְּבָרָיו בְּמִשְׁפָּט.** מַנְהִיג חֲפָצָיו (חולין פד:):


**he conducts with moderation and with a measure**, and he spares his property.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 112:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/112:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/112:7:1)


**נָכוֹן לִבּוֹ.** נֶאֱמָן לִבּוֹ לְיוֹצְרוֹ:


**his heart is steadfast** His heart is faithful to His Maker.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 112:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/112:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/112:8:1)


**סָמוּךְ לִבּוֹ.** נִשְׁעָן וּבָטוּחַ עַל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:


**His heart is steadfast** He leans on and trusts in the Holy One, blessed be He.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 112:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/112:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/112:10:1)


**רָשָׁע יִרְאֶה וְכָעָס.** לְשׁוֹן פֹּעַל כְּמוֹ וַיִּכְעַס, לְפִיכָךְ נָקוּד חֶצְיוֹ קָמַץ וְחֶצְיוֹ פַּתַּח וְטַעֲמוֹ לְמַטָּה:


**A wicked man will see and become angry** Heb. וכעס, an expression of a verb in the past tense, equivalent to ויכעס [i.e., the “vav” converts the past tense to the future]. Therefore, it is vowelized half with a “kamatz” and half with a “pattah,” and the accent is at the end of the word.



## Chapter 113


### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 113:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/113:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/113:5:1)


**מִי כַּה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ.** בַּשָּׁמַיִם וּבָאָרֶץ, שֶׁהוּא **מַגְבִּיהִי לָשָׁבֶת** וּמַשְׁפִּיל לִרְאוֹת. מַגְבִּיהִי, מַשְׁפִּילִי, מְקִימִי, לְהוֹשִׁיבִי, מוֹשִׁיבִי – כֻּלָּם יוֹ״ד יְתֵרָה בָּהֶם:


**Who is like the Lord, our God** in heaven and earth, who dwells on high and lowers His eyes to see? מושיבי, להושיבי, מקימי, משפילי, מגביהי, all have a superfluous “yud.”



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 113:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/113:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/113:9:1)


**עֲקֶרֶת הַבַּיִת.** צִיּוֹן, שֶׁהִיא כַּעֲקָרָה, יוֹשִׁיבֶנָּה:


**the barren woman of the house** Zion, which is like a barren woman—He will seat her.


###### Rashi on Psalms 113:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/113:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/113:9:2)


**אֵם הַבָּנִים שְׂמֵחָה.** ״כִּי חָלָה גַּם יָלְדָה צִיּוֹן אֶת בָּנֶיהָ״ (ישעיהו סו:ח):


**as a happy mother of children** (Isa. 66:8): “that Zion both experienced birth pangs and bore her children.”



## Chapter 114


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 114:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/114:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/114:1:1)


**מֵעַם לוֹעֵז.** עַם שְׂפַת לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר שֶׁאֵינוֹ לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ, וְחֲבֵרוֹ: ״אֶת עַם נוֹעָז לֹא תִרְאֶה עַם עִמְקֵי שָׂפָה וְגוֹ׳״ (ישעיה לג:יט), וְנוּ״ן וְלָמֶ״ד נֶחְלָפוֹת זוֹ בָּזוֹ, כְּמוֹ ״נִשְׁכָּה״ שֶׁהוּא לִשְׁכָּה בְּסֵפֶר עֶזְרָא (נחמיה יג:ז-ח):


**a people of a strange tongue** With another language, which is not the Holy Tongue. A similar expression is (Isa. 33:19): “A people of a strange tongue you shall not see, a people of speech too obscure, etc.” The “nun” and the “lammed” are interchangeable, like נִשְׁכָּה, chamber, which is [equivalent to] לִשְׁכָּה, in the Book of Ezra (Neh. 13:7).



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 114:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/114:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/114:2:1)


**הָיְתָה יְהוּדָה לְקָדְשׁוֹ.** לָקַח יְהוּדָה לְגוֹרַל חֶבְלוֹ וּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ, וְאַף הֵם קִדְּשׁוּ שְׁמוֹ בִּירִידַת הַיָּם, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (תהלים סח:כח) ״שָׂרֵי יְהוּדָה רִגְמָתָם״. וּכְמוֹ כֵן נִדְרַשׁ בָּאַגָּדָה מִקְרָא זֶה **הָיְתָה יְהוּדָה לְקָדְשׁוֹ**, שֶׁקָּפַץ נַחְשׁוֹן לְתוֹךְ הַיָּם וְאָמַר: אֲנִי אֵרֵד תְּחִלָּה. וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר **הָיְתָה יְהוּדָה לְקָדְשׁוֹ**:


**Judah became His holy nation** He took Judah as the lot of His portion and His sanctity, and even they sanctified His name when they descended into the sea, as the matter that is stated (above 68: 28): “the princes of Judah pelt them with stones.” Similarly, this verse is explained in the Aggadah (Mid. Ps. 114:8): Judah became His holy people, for Nahshon sprang into the sea and said, “I shall descend first,” and that is what [the Psalmist] says: Judah became His holy people.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 114:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/114:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/114:3:1)


**הַיַּרְדֵּן יִסֹּב לְאָחוֹר.** שֶׁכָּל מֵימֵי בְרֵאשִׁית נִבְקְעוּ:


**the Jordan turned backward** because all the water of Creation split.



### Verse 7

###### Rashi on Psalms 114:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/114:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/114:7:1)


**חוּלִי אָרֶץ.** הַמְּחוֹלֵל אֶרֶץ, יוֹ״ד יְתֵרָה בּוֹ, כְּמוֹ ״מַגְבִּיהִי״ (תהלים קיג:ה) ״מַשְׁפִּילִי״ (תהלים קיג:ו) וְ״הַהֹפְכִי״ (תהלים קיד:ח):


**Who created the earth** Heb. חולי, Who created the earth. The “yud” is superfluous as מגביהי, משפילי and ההוֹפכי.



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 114:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/114:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/114:8:1)


**לְמַעְיְנוֹ מָיִם.** וָי״ו יְתֵירָה, כְּמוֹ וָי״ו שֶׁל ״וְחַיְתוֹ יַעַר״ (תהלים נ:י):


**into a fountain of water** Heb. למעינו. The “vav” is superfluous, as the “vav” in (above 104:11, 20) “the beasts (חיתו) of the forest.”

**לֹא לָנוּ.** לֹא בִּשְׁבִילֵנוּ וּבְכֹשֶׁר מַעֲשֵׂינוּ תַּעֲשֶׂה עִמָּנוּ:

###### Rashi on Psalms 115:7:1

**וְלֹא יְמִישׁוּן.** לְשׁוֹן ״יְמֻשֵּׁנִי אָבִי״ (בראשית כז:יב):


**but they do not feel** Heb. ימישון, an expression of (Gen. 27:12): “Perhaps my father will feel me (ימשני).”

**יִרְאֵי ה׳.** אֵלּוּ הַגֵּרִים:

## Chapter 116


### Verse 1

###### Rashi on Psalms 116:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:1:1)


**אָהַבְתִּי כִּי יִשְׁמַע ה׳ אֶת קוֹלִי.** כָּךְ אָמַר דָּוִד לְאַחַר שֶׁנִּפְטַר שָׁאוּל וְהוּא מָלַךְ, **שׁוּבִי נַפְשִׁי לִמְנוּחָיְכִי כִּי ה׳ גָּמַל עָלָיְכִי, חֶסֶד**, וְלָךְ קוֹנִי אֲנִי מִתְאַוֶּה, **כִּי חִלַּצְתָּ נַפְשִׁי מִמָּוֶת**:


**I wished that the Lord would hear my voice** So did David say after Saul’s demise, when he became king, “Return, my soul, to your resting place, for the Lord has bestowed kindness upon you.” And to You, my Master, I pine, for You extricated my soul from death.


###### Rashi on Psalms 116:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:1:2)


**אָהַבְתִּי כִּי יִשְׁמַע ה׳.** תָּאַבְתִּי שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע ה׳ אֶת קוֹלִי (ס״א אינו):


**I wished that the Lord would hear** Heb. אהבתי, I wished (תאבתי) that God would hear my voice.



### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 116:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:2:1)


**וּבְיָמַי אֶקְרָא.** בִּימֵי צָרָתִי אֶקְרָאֶנּוּ, וּבִימֵי גְּאֻלָּתִי אֲשַׁבְּחֶנּוּ (תנחומא, יתרו טז):


**and I shall call out in my days** In the days of my distress I shall call Him, and in the days of my redemption I shall praise Him.



### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 116:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:3:1)


**חֶבְלֵי מָוֶת.** חֲבוּרוֹת אוֹיְבֵינוּ הַמְּבַקְשִׁים לַהֲמִיתֵנִי:


**bands of death** Heb. חבלי, bands of enemies who sought to kill me.


###### Rashi on Psalms 116:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:3:2)


**חֶבְלֵי מָוֶת.** ״חֶבְלֵי שְׁאוֹל״ (תהלים יח:ו) – כֻּלָּם לְשׁוֹן חֲבוּרוֹת הֵם, כְּמוֹ ״חֶבֶל נְבִיאִים״ (שמואל א י:ה):


[The expressions] חבלי מות, חבלי שאוֹל, are all an expression of bands, like (I Sam. 10:5): “a band of (חבל) prophets.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 116:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:3:3)


**וּמְצָרֵי שְׁאוֹל.** גְּבוּלֵי שְׁאוֹל:



### Verse 9

###### Rashi on Psalms 116:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:9:1)


**בְּאַרְצוֹת הַחַיִּים.** אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁגֵּרְשׁוּנִי אוֹיְבַי וְרוֹדְפַי מִמֶּנָּה בִּימֵי שָׁאוּל, וְעַל כָּרְחָם חָזַרְתִּי:


**in the lands of the living** The land of Israel, for my enemies and my pursuers chased me out of it in the days of Saul, and against their will, I returned.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 116:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:10:1)


**הֶאֱמַנְתִּי כִּי אֲדַבֵּר.** הֶאֱמַנְתִּי אֶת דִּבְרֵי צִיבָא שֶׁאָמַר עַל מְפִיבֹשֶׁת, כְּשֶׁאֲדַבֵּר ״הִנֵּה לְךָ כֹּל אֲשֶׁר לִמְפִיבֹשֶׁת״ (שמואל ב טז:ד). אָז **אֲנִי עָנִיתִי מְאֹד.** דִּבַּרְתִּי קָשֶׁה וְנַעֲנֵיתִי לְךָ:


**I believed so that I spoke** I believed the words of Ziba which he spoke about Mephibosheth, so that I should say (II Sam. 16:4), “Behold, all that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours.” Then I humbled myself exceedingly. I had spoken harshly, and I submitted myself to you [Mephibosheth].



### Verse 11

###### Rashi on Psalms 116:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:11:1)


**אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי בְחָפְזִי.** לָנוּס מִפְּנֵי אַבְשָׁלוֹם (שמואל ב טו:יד):


**I said in my haste** to flee from before Absalom.


###### Rashi on Psalms 116:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:11:2)


**כָּל הָאָדָם כֹּזֵב.** וּבוֹגֵד בְּאוֹהֵב בּוֹ, כִּי רָאִיתִי אֶת בְּנִי בּוֹגֵד בִּי וּמְבַקֵּשׁ אֶת נַפְשִׁי, וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹמְלִים לִי רָעָה תַּחַת טוֹבָה. לְפִיכָךְ הֶאֱמַנְתִּי לְצִיבָא וְאָמַרְתִּי: אַף מְפִיבֹשֶׁת כּוֹזֵב וּבוֹגֵד בִּי (שמואל ב טז:ד). כָּל לְשׁוֹן כָּזָב אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן חֶסְרוֹן מִבְטָח שֶׁבָּטְחוּ עָלָיו, פילנ״צא בְּלַעַ״ז, כְּמוֹ (ישעיה נח:יא) ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא יְכַזְּבוּ מֵימָיו״. וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִין אוֹתוֹ **אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי בְחָפְזִי** בְּסֶלַע הַמַּחְלְקוֹת, שֶׁהָיוּ שָׁאוּל וַאֲנָשָׁיו עוֹטְרִין עָלַי וְאֶל אֲנָשַׁי לְתָפְשֵׂנִי, וְשָׁם נֶאֱמַר ״וַיְהִי דָוִד נֶחְפָּז לָלֶכֶת״ (שמואל א כג:כו). **כָּל אָדָם כֹּזֵב**, אַף שְׁמוּאֵל הַנָּבִיא שֶׁהוּא נֶאֱמָן לְנָבִיא אַף הוּא כּוֹזֵב, שֶׁמְּשָׁחַנִי לְמֶלֶךְ (מצאתי):


**“All men are liars”** Heb. כזב, [meaning that one] betrays his friend, for I saw my son betray me and seek my life, and [I saw] all Israel repay me with evil for good; therefore, I believed Ziba and said that Mephibosheth also lies and betrays me. Every expression of כָּזָב is purely an expression of lack of trust that they trusted in him; falenze in Old French, betrayal, deceit, like (Isa. 58:11): “whose water does not fail (יכזבו).” Others interpret it: **I said in my haste** at the Rock of the Divisions, when Saul and his men were encircling me and my men, to seize me, and there it says (I Sam. 23:26): “and David was hastening to get away.” **“All men are liars”** Even the prophet Samuel, who is faithful as a prophet, even he is a deceiver, for he anointed me king.



### Verse 13

###### Rashi on Psalms 116:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/116:13:1)


**כּוֹס יְשׁוּעוֹת אֶשָּׂא.** אָבִיא הַנְּסָכִים עַל הַתּוֹדוֹת שֶׁנָּדַרְתִּי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר **לְךָ אֶזְבַּח זֶבַח תּוֹדָה**, וְעַל אוֹתוֹ הַכּוֹס בְּשִׁמְךָ **אֶקְרָא** עַל הַיְשׁוּעָה זוֹ. שֶׁכֵּן אֵין הַלֵּוִי אוֹמֵר שִׁירָה אֶלָּא עַל הַיַּיִן:


**I shall lift up a cup of salvations** I shall bring the libations for the thanksgiving offerings that I vowed, as he says, “To You I shall slaughter a thanksgiving offering,” and on that cup I shall call out about this salvation, for the Levite does not recite a song unless over the wine [libations].

**יָקָר בְּעֵינֵי ה׳.** הֶרְאַנִי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, שֶׁדָּבָר קָשֶׁה וְכָבֵד הוּא בְּעֵינָיו לְהָמִית אֶת **חֲסִידָיו**:


**Difficult in the eyes of the Lord** The Holy One, blessed be He, showed me that it is a difficult thing and heavy in His eyes to kill His pious ones.

**You loosed my thongs** You untied from my neck the bars and the thongs.

**כִּי גָבַר עָלֵינוּ חַסְדּוֹ.** כְּלוֹמַר: וְאַף כִּי אֲנַחְנוּ, אֲשֶׁר **גָּבַר עָלֵינוּ חַסְדּוֹ**:


**For His kindness has overwhelmed us** That is to say: and surely we [must praise Him], for His kindness has overwhelmed us.


###### Rashi on Psalms 117:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/117:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/117:2:2)


**וֶאֱמֶת ה׳ לְעוֹלָם.** שֶׁשָּׁמַר הַבְטָחָתוֹ שֶׁהִבְטִיחַ אֶת הָאָבוֹת (בראשית טו:יח-כא):


**and the truth of the Lord is eternal** For He kept His promise that He promised the Patriarchs.



## Chapter 118


### Verse 2

###### Rashi on Psalms 118:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:2:1)


**הוֹדוּ לַה׳ וְגוֹ׳ יֹאמַר נָא יִשְׂרָאֵל.** לְפִי **שֶׁלְּעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ** :


**Give thanks to the Lord, etc.** **Israel shall now say** because His kindness is eternal.



### Verse 4

###### Rashi on Psalms 118:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:4:1)


**יִרְאֵי ה׳.** אֵלּוּ בְּנֵי לֵוִי, שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּהֶם (שמות לב:כו) ״מִי לַה׳ אֵלַי וַיֵּאָסְפוּ אֵלָיו כָּל בְּנֵי לֵוִי״ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הָעֵגֶל, וְנִלְחֲמוּ עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּשֶׁאָמְרוּ (במדבר יד:ד) ״נִתְּנָה רֹאשׁ וְנָשׁוּבָה מִצְרָיְמָה״:


**Those who fear the Lord** These are the Levites, about whom it is written (Exod. 32:26): “Whoever is the Lord’s, let him come to me! And all the sons of Levi gathered around him,” in the episode of the [Golden] Calf, and they fought with Israel when they said (Num. 14:4), “Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt.”



### Verse 8

###### Rashi on Psalms 118:8:1

**טוֹב לַחֲסוֹת בַּה׳ וְגוֹ׳.** חֶסְיוֹן זֶה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן חֶסְיוֹן צֵל, וְדָבָר מוּעָט הוּא:


**It is better to take shelter in the Lord** Heb. לחסות. This shelter (חסיון) is only an expression of the shelter of a shadow, a small thing.


###### Rashi on Psalms 118:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:8:2)


**מִבְטָח.** דָּבָר בָּרִיא וְסֶמֶךְ חָזָק, וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן **לַחֲסוֹת בַּה׳ טוֹב** מֵהַבְטָחַת בְּנֵי אָדָם:


Trust (מבטח) is a stout and strong support. Nevertheless, to take shelter in the Lord is better than the promises of human beings.



### Verse 10

###### Rashi on Psalms 118:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:10:1)


**כָּל גּוֹיִם סְבָבוּנִי.** מְדַבֵּר בְּמִלְחֲמוֹת גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג (יחזקאל לח-לט) שֶׁכָּל הַגּוֹיִם יִהְיוּ שָׁם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְאָסַפְתִּי אֶת כָּל הַגּוֹיִם אֶל יְרוּשָׁלִַם לַמִּלְחָמָה״ (זכריה יד:ב):


**All nations surrounded me** This speaks about the war of Gog and Magog, when all the nations will be there, as it is said (Zech. 14:2): “And I shall gather all the nations to Jerusalem to wage war.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 118:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:10:2)


**אֲמִילַם.** אַכְרִיתֵם, לְשׁוֹן ״יְמוֹלֵל וְיָבֵשׁ״ (תהלים צ:ו):


**I shall cut them off** Heb. אמלים, I shall cut them off, an expression of (above 90:6): “it is cut off (ימולל) and withers.”



### Verse 12

###### Rashi on Psalms 118:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:12:1)


**דָּעֲכוּ כְּאֵשׁ קוֹצִים.** כָּל לְשׁוֹן דְּעִיכָה נוֹפֵל עַל לְשׁוֹן קְפִיצָה וְנִתּוּר: מְמַהֵר לִהְיוֹת נִתָּר וְנִתָּק מִמְּקוֹמוֹ. עַל כֵּן הוּא נוֹפֵל עַל לְשׁוֹן אֵשׁ וְעַל לְשׁוֹן מַיִם, כְּמוֹ ״נִדְעֲכוּ מִמְּקוֹמָם״ (איוב ו:יז), וְכֵן ״יָמַי נִדְעָכוּ״ (איוב יז:א), וְכֵן ״נֵרוֹ עָלָיו יִדְעָךְ״ (איוב יח:ו), כְּדֶרֶךְ שַׁלְהֶבֶת הַנִּתֶּקֶת מִן הַפְּתִילָה וְעוֹלָה לְמַעְלָה כְּשֶׁהִיא כָּבָה:


**they were extinguished like a thorn fire** Every expression of דעיכה coincides with an expression of springing and skipping. It hastens to spring and skip from its place. Therefore, it fits with an expression of fire or with an expression of water, like (Job 6:17): “they jump (נדעכו) from their place.” Similarly (Job 17:1), “my days flicker (נדעכו)”; similarly (Job 18:6), “and his candle that is over him shall go out (ידעך),” in the way that the flame springs from the wick and ascends upward when it is extinguished.

###### Rashi on Psalms 118:13:1

**דָּחֹה דְחִיתַנִי לִנְפֹּל.** אַתָּה, אוֹיְבִי:


**You pushed me to fall** You, my enemy.



### Verse 14

###### Rashi on Psalms 118:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:14:1)


**עָזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ וַיְהִי לִי לִישׁוּעָה.** עָזִּי וְזִמְרַת גְּבוּרַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הָיָה לִי לִישׁוּעָה. עָזִּי יוֹ״ד יְתֵירָהף כִּי לֹא מָצִינוּ בַמִּקְרָא עָזִּי נָקוּד חֲטַף קָמַץ אֶלָּא שׁוּרֵק, חוּץ מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת שֶׁהוּא סָמוּךְ אֵצֶל וְזִמְרַת, וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ וְזִמְרַת דָּבוּק לְתֵיבַת הַשֵּׁם, וְאֵינְךָ יָכוֹל לְפָרְשׁוֹ וְזִמְרָתִי, וְאַל תִּתְמַהּ עַל **וַיְהִי לִי**, שֶׁלֹּא אָמַר הָיָה לִי לִישׁוּעָה, שֶׁהַרְבֵּה כָּאֵלֶּה בַמִּקְרָא, ״וַאֲשֶׁר לֹא שָׂם לִבּוֹ וְגוֹ׳ וַיַּעֲזֹב אֶת עֲבָדָיו וְגוֹ׳״ (שמות ט:כא) הָיָה לוֹ לִכְתֹּב עָזַב:


**The might and the cutting power of God was my salvation** Heb. עזי וזמרת, the might of the Holy One, blessed be He, was my salvation. עזי has a superfluous “yud” because we do not [usually] find עזי vowelized with a short “kamatz” instead of a “shuruk,” except in three places, where it is next to וזמרת, and perforce is attached to the word denoting the name of God. You cannot explain it as “my praise.” Do not wonder about ויהי לי, that he did not say היה לי לישועה, for there are many like these in Scripture, [e.g.] (Exod. 9:21): “And whoever did not pay attention...left (ויעזב) his slaves, etc.” He should have written עַזָב.



### Verse 15

###### Rashi on Psalms 118:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:15:1)


**קוֹל רִנָּה וִישׁוּעָה.** תִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד **בְּאָהֳלֵי צַדִּיקִים**, וּמַהוּ קוֹל הָרִנָּה? **יְמִין ה׳ עֹשָׂה חָיִל**, יְרַנְּנוּ, **יְמִין ה׳ רוֹמֵמָה וְגוֹ׳**:


**A voice of singing praises and salvation** will in the future be in the tents of the righteous, and what is that voice of singing praises? “The right hand of the Lord deals valiantly.” They will sing, “The right hand of the Lord is exalted, etc.”



### Verse 16

###### Rashi on Psalms 118:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:16:1)


**יְמִין ה׳ רוֹמֵמָה.** מִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: עֶלְיוֹנִים בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּיָמִין, לְפִיכָךְ לֹא שָׁלְטָה בָּהֶם מִיתָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״אַף יָדִי יָסְדָה אֶרֶץ״ (ישעיה מח:יג) זֶה שְׂמֹאל ״וִימִינִי טִפְּחָה שָׁמַיִם״ (ישעיה מח:יג) זֶה יָמִין. וְכֵן אָמַר הַמְשׁוֹרֵר **יְמִין ה׳ רוֹמֵמָה** שֶׁבָּרָאתָ אוֹתָם שֶׁבְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, הִיא **יְמִין ה׳** שֶׁתַּעֲשֶׂה חֲיָלוֹת שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא, וְגַם בָּהּ יְחַיֶּה אוֹתָם וְיִחְיוּ לְעוֹלָם, וְאָז **לֹא אָמוּת כִּי אֶחְיֶה** לְעוֹלָם:


**The right hand of the Lord is exalted** The Midrash Aggadah states: The Holy One, blessed be He, created the celestial beings with His right hand; therefore, death has no power over them; as it says (Isa. 48:13): “Even my hand laid the foundation of the earth.” This is the left hand. “And My right hand measured the heavens with handbreadths.” This is the right hand. Similarly, the Psalmist says: “The right hand of the Lord is exalted,” that created those [that are] in the heights of the world. That is the right hand of the Lord that will make armies of righteous men in the future, and also with it [the right hand] He will resurrect them and they will live forever. And then, I shall not die, but I shall live forever.

### Verse 27

###### Rashi on Psalms 118:27:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:27:1)


**אִסְרוּ חַג בַּעֲבוֹתִים.** הַזְּבָחִים וְהַחֲגִיגוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ נְקִיִּים וּבְדוּקִין מִמּוּם קוֹשְׁרִין בְּכַרְעֵי מִטּוֹתֵיהֶם, עַד שֶׁיְּבִיאוּם לָעֲזָרָה בְּ**קַרְנוֹת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ**. וְיֵשׁ לִפְתּוֹר כָּל סוֹף הַמִּזְמוֹר הַזֶּה מִ**לֹּא אָמוּת כִּי אֶחְיֶה** בְּדָוִד עַצְמוֹ:


**Bind the sacrifice with ropes** The sacrifices and the festival offerings, which were clean and examined for a blemish, they would bind to the feet of their beds until they brought them to the Temple court at the corners of the altar. It is also possible to interpret the entire end of this psalm from (verse 17), “I shall not die but I shall live,” as referring to David himself:


###### Rashi on Psalms 118:27:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:27:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:27:2)


(יח) **יִסּוֹר יִסְּרַנִּי יָּהּ.** עַל מַעֲשֵׂה בַת שֶׁבַע בְּיִסּוּרִין, כְּגוֹן ״תַּחַת הַכִּבְשָׂה יְשַׁלֵּם אַרְבַּעְתַּיִם״ (שמואל ב יב:ו). שִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים נִצְטָרַע דָּוִד (יומא כב:):


[18] **God has chastised me** For the episode of Bath sheba with torments, e.g. (II Sam. 12:6): “And the ewe-lamb he shall repay fourfold.” David was stricken with zaraath for six months.


###### Rashi on Psalms 118:27:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:27:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:27:3)


**וְלָמוּת לֹא נְתָנָנִי.** שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״גַּם ה׳ הֶעֱבִיר חַטָּאתְךָ לֹא תָמוּת״ (שמואל ב יב:יג):


**but He has not delivered me to death** (II Sam. 13) “Also the Lord has removed your sin; you shall not die.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 118:27:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:27:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:27:4)


(יט) **פִּתְחוּ לִי שַׁעֲרֵי צֶדֶק.** וְאֵלּוּ הֵן שַׁעֲרֵי צֶדֶק? אוֹתָם הַשְּׁעָרִים שֶׁל בָּתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת וּמִדְרָשׁוֹת, אֲשֶׁר הֵם **לַה׳**, וְהַצַּדִּיקִים בָּאִים בָּהֶם:


[19] **Open for me the gates of righteousness** And these are the gates of righteousnessthose gates of synagogues and study halls, which are the Lord’sand the righteous enter through them.


###### Rashi on Psalms 118:27:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:27:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/118:27:5)


(כא) **אוֹדְךָ כִּי עֲנִיתָנִי.** מִכָּאן וָאֵילָךְ אָמַר דָּוִד וּשְׁמוּאֵל וְיִשַׁי וַאֲחֵי דָוִד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּפֹרָשׁ בְּעַרְבֵי פְסָחִים (פסחים קיט.): מִי שֶׁאָמַר זֶה לֹא אָמַר זֶה:


[21] **I shall thank You because You have answered me** From here on, David, Samuel, Jesse, and David’s brothers recited this, as is delineated in [the chapter entitled] “The eves of Passovers,” (Pes. 119a). He who said this did not say the other.



## Chapter 119


### Verse 3

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:3:1)


**אַף לֹא פָעֲלוּ עַוְלָה.** אַשְׁרֵיהֶם אִם כָּל זֶה בָּהֶם:


**Not only have they committed no injustice** They are praiseworthy if all this is in them.


###### Rashi on Psalms 119:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:3:2)


**בִּדְרָכָיו הָלָכוּ.** אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא פָּעֲלוּ עַוְלָה, אֵין שְׂכָרָם שָׁלֵם אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן בִּדְרָכָיו הָלָכוּ. וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר ״סוּר מֵרָע וַעֲשֵׂה טוֹב״ (תהלים לד:טו) – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאַתָּה סָר מֵרָע, אֵין הַכֹּל שָׁלֵם אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן תַּעֲשֶׂה טוֹב (מדרש אגדה):


**they walked in His ways** Although they committed no injustice, their reward is incomplete unless they walked in His ways. And so he says (above 43:15): “Shun evil and do good.” Even though you shun evil, everything is not complete unless you do good. Midrash Aggadah.



### Verse 5

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:5:1)


**אַחֲלַי יִכֹּנוּ דְרָכָי.** אָלֶ״ף יְסוֹד בַּתֵּיבָה, הַנּוֹפֵל מִמֶּנּוּ לִפְרָקִים, כְּמוֹ אָלֶ״ף שֶׁבְּ״אַחֲוָתִי בְאָזְנֵיכֶם״ (איוב יג:יז) וְאָלֶ״ף שֶׁל ״אָסוּךְ שָׁמֶן״ (מלכים ב ד:ב). **אַחֲלַי** תְּפִלּוֹתַי אֵלּוּ הֵן: שֶׁיִּכּוֹנוּ דְרָכָי. וְכֵן ״אַחֲלֵי אֲדֹנִי לִפְנֵי הַנָּבִיא אֲשֶׁר בְּשֹׁמְרוֹן וְגוֹ׳״ (מלכים ב ה:ג) – צָרְכֵי אֲדוֹנִי, לְהִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁיֵּלֵךְ לִפְנֵי הַנָּבִיא אֲשֶׁר בְּשׁוֹמְרוֹן. וְלָשׁוֹן אַחֲלִיּוּת שוהיי״ט בְּלַעַ״ז, כְּאָדָם הָאוֹמֵר: הַלְוַאי וְהָיִיתִי נָבִיא וְחָכָם:


**My prayers are that my ways should be established** Heb. אחלי. The “aleph” is a radical that is sometimes dropped, like the “aleph” in (Job 13:17): “and my speech (ואחותי) in your ears,” and the “aleph” of (II Kings 4:2): “a jug (אסוך) of oil.” **My prayers** These prayers of mine are that my ways should be established Likewise (II Kings 5:3): “The supplications (אחלי) for my master should be that he go before the prophet who is in Samaria, etc.” The supplications of those who pray should be that he go before the prophet who is in Samaria, and it is an expression of wishes, souhait in French, as a person says, “If only I were a prophet and a sage.”

**I shall occupy myself** Heb. אשתעשע, I shall engage, like (Isa. 17:7): “man shall turn to his Maker”; (Exod. 5:9) “and let them not engage (ישעו) in useless things.”



### Verse 17

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:17:1)


**גְּמֹל עַל עַבְדְּךָ.** דָּבָר שֶׁאֶחְיֶה בּוֹ בִּגְמוּל חַסְדְּךָ:


**Bestow kindness upon Your servant** A thing with which I shall be able to live, through the bestowal of your kindness.



### Verse 18

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:18:1)


**נִפְלָאוֹת מִתּוֹרָתֶךָ.** דְּבָרִים הַמְכֻסִּים בָּהּ, שֶׁאֵינָם מְפֹרָשִׁים בָּהּ:


**hidden things from Your Torah** Hidden things in it, which are not explained therein.


###### Rashi on Psalms 119:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:18:2)


**מִתּוֹרָתֶךָ.** נִפְלָאִים מִפֵּירוּשֵׁי תּוֹרָתֶךָ שֶׁאֵינָם מְפוֹרָשִׁים בָּהּ (מצאתי):


**(from Your Torah)** Wonders from the explanations of your Torah which are not explained therein.



### Verse 19

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:19:1)


**גֵּר אָנֹכִי בָאָרֶץ.** יָמִים מוּעָטִים:


**I am a stranger in the land** for a short time.


###### Rashi on Psalms 119:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:19:2)


**אַל תַּסְתֵּר מִמֶּנִּי.** מִצְוֹתֶיךָ הַנֶּעֱלָמוֹת שֶׁאוּכַל לְקַיְּמָם, שֶׁאִם לֹא עַכְשָׁיו אֵימָתַי:


**do not hide Your commandments from me** The hidden ones, so that I should be able to fulfill them, for if not now, when?



### Verse 20

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:20:1)


**גָּרְסָה.** מִשְׁתַּבֶּרֶת נַפְשִׁי מֵחֲמַת תַּאֲוָה, כְּמוֹ ״גֶּרֶשׂ כַּרְמֶל״ (ויקרא ב:יד). וּמְנַחֵם חִבֵּר לְתַאֲבָה עִם ״מְתָאֵב אָנֹכִי אֶת גְּאוֹן יַעֲקֹב״ (עמוס ו:ח), וּשְׁנֵיהֶם לְשׁוֹן שֶׁבֶר:


**is crushed** Heb. גרסה. My soul breaks because of longing, as (Lev. 2:14): “crushed kernels (גרשׂ) of the fresh ears.” Menachem (p. 183), however, associated “from longing” (לתאבה) with (Amos 6:8) “I destroy (מתאב) the pride of Jacob,” and both are an expression of breaking.



### Verse 22

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:22:1

**גַּל מֵעָלַי.** לְשׁוֹן גִּלְגּוּל, כְּמוֹ ״וַיָּגֶל אֶת הָאָבֶן״ (בראשית כט:י):


**Remove from me** Heb. גל, an expression of rolling, like (Gen. 29:10): “and he rolled (ויגל) the stone.”



### Verse 23

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:23:1)


**בִּי נִדְבָּרוּ.** אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמַּלְכֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מִתְלוֹצְצִים עָלַי שֶׁאֲנִי עוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה:


**talked about me** Although the kings of the heathens scorn me because I engage in the Torah.

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:24:1

**שַׁעֲשׁוּעָי.** עִסְקִי:



### Verse 25

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:25:1)


**חַיֵּנִי כִּדְבָרֶךָ.** כְּמוֹ שֶׁהִבְטַחְתַּנִי עַל יְדֵי נָתָן הַנָּבִיא טוֹבָה (שמואל ב ז:יב-טז):


**revive me according to Your word** Just as You promised me good, through Nathan the prophet.



### Verse 26

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:26:1

**סִפַּרְתִּי.** לְךָ אֶת צְרָכַי וְאֶת חֲטָאתִי, וְאַתָּה עֲנִיתָנִי:


**I told of my ways** to You, [of] my needs and my sin, and You answered me.

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:28:1

**My soul drips** Heb. דלפה, drips; i.e., it is becoming less and less.



### Verse 30

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:30:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:30:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:30:1)


**מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ שִׁוִּיתִי.** שַׂמְתִּי עַצְמִי לְמִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ וְדָבַקְתִּי בְּעֵדוֹתֶיךָ, לִבְחוֹר בְּ**דֶרֶךְ אֱמוּנָה**. לְךָ אֲנִי שׁוֹאֵל: **דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁקֶר הָסֵר מִמֶּנִּי**:


**Your judgments I have set** I applied myself to your judgments and I clung to your testimony, to choose the way of faith. Therefore, I ask, “Remove from me the way of falsehood.”



### Verse 33

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:33:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:33:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:33:1)


**וְאֶצְּרֶנָּה עֵקֶב.** אֶשְׁמְרֶנָּה בְּכָל מַעְגְּלוֹתֶיהָ וְעִקְּבֵי נְתִיבוֹתֶיהָ, לְשׁוֹן עֲקֵבִים, טְרָאצֵ״שׁ בְּלַעַ״ז:


**and I shall keep it at every step** Heb. עקב. I shall keep it in all its paths and the steps of its paths, an expression of “heels” (עקבים), traces in French, footsteps.



### Verse 38

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:38:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:38:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:38:1)


**הָקֵם לְעַבְדְּךָ אִמְרָתֶךָ.** אֲשֶׁר הִבְטַחְתַּנִי:


**Fulfill for Your servant Your word** that You promised me.


###### Rashi on Psalms 119:38:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:38:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:38:2)


**אֲשֶׁר לְיִרְאָתֶךָ.** שֶׁאֶהְיֶה אֲנִי וְזַרְעִי יִרְאֵי שְׁמֶךָ, שֶׁעַל מְנָת כֵּן הִבְטַחְתַּנִי: ״אִם יִשְׁמְרוּ בָנֶיךָ אֶת דַּרְכָּם וְגוֹ׳״ (מלכים א ב:ד):


**that is for Your fear** That I and my children shall fear Your name, for on that condition You promised me (I Kings 2:4): “if your children take heed in their way, etc.”



### Verse 39

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:39:1

**הַעֲבֵר חֶרְפָּתִי.** מְחוֹל לִי עַל אוֹתוֹ עָוֹן, וְשׁוּב לֹא יוּכְלוּ אוֹיְבַי לְחָרְפֵנִי בּוֹ:


**Remove my disgrace** Forgive me for that sin [with Bath-sheba], and my enemies will no longer be able to disgrace me with it.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:39:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:39:2)

**for Your judgments are good** and I already accept upon myself “to repay the ewe-lamb fourfold.”



### Verse 41

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:41:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:41:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:41:1)


**וְיִבֹאֻנִי.** תְּשׁוּעָתְךָ תָּבֹא אֵלַי **כְּאִמְרָתֶךָ** שֶׁהִבְטַחְתַּנִי:


**And may...befall me** May Your salvation befall me according to Your word which You promised me.

**And do not take...from my mouth a word of truth** Heb. תצל. Do not separate from my mouth a word of truth, as (Gen. 31:9): “And God separated (ויצל) your father’s property and gave it to me.” I found this.

**דְּבַר אֱמֶת עַד מְאֹד.** בְּכָל הוֹרָאוֹתַי וּבְכָל דִּינַי, שֶׁלֹּא אֶכָּשֵׁל בָּהֶם:


**utterly...a word of truth** in all my instructions [regarding ritual law] and in all my legal decisions, that I should not stumble over them.

### Verse 49

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:49:1

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:52:1

**Your judgments of old** that You bring sufferings and You repent of your anger and forgive. Therefore, I was consoled.



### Verse 55

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:55:1

**At night I remembered** At a time of distress and darkness.



### Verse 56

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:56:1

**זֹאת הָיְתָה לִּי.** עֲטֶרֶת הַהוֹלֶמֶת אוֹתִי לִי לְעֵדוּת, וּלְזַרְעִי הָרָאוּי לִמְלוֹךְ, בִּשְׂכַר שֶׁ**פִּקֻּדֶיךָ נָצָרְתִּי.** כָּךְ דְּרָשׁוּהוּ חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (עבודה זרה מד.) (מצאתי):


**This came to me** A crown that fits me [was given] to me as a testimony and to my children who are fit to reign, as a reward for my having kept Your precepts. So did the Sages of Israel explain it. I found this:



### Verse 57

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:57:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:57:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:57:1)


**לִשְׁמֹר דְּבָרֶיךָ.** קַיֵּם דְּבָרֶיךָ שֶׁיִּחַלְתַּנִי בְּכָךְ, אַתָּה חֶלְקִי:


**to keep Your words** the fulfillment of your words, with which You gave me hope, in that You are my portion.



### Verse 58

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:58:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:58:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:58:1)


**חִלִּיתִי פָנֶיךָ.** בִּלְשׁוֹן ״חֶלְקִי ה׳ אָמְרָה נַפְשִׁי עַל כֵּן אוֹחִיל לוֹ״ (איכה ג:כד):


**I entreated You** Heb. חליתי, from the expression of (Lam. 3:24): “‘The Lord is my portion,’ says my soul; ‘therefore, I will hope (אוחיל) to Him.’”



### Verse 59

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:59:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:59:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:59:1)


**חִשַּׁבְתִּי דְרָכָי.** הֶפְסֵד מִצְוָה כְּנֶגֶד שְׂכָרָהּ, וּשְׂכַר עֲבֵרָה כְּנֶגֶד הֶפְסֵדָהּ, לְפִיכָךְ **וָאָשִׁיבָה רַגְלַי אֶל עֵדוֹתֶיךָ**, כִּי רָאִיתִי שֶׁהִיא הַטּוֹבָה שֶׁבְּכֻלָּן (ויקרא רבה לה.):


**I considered my ways** The loss of a commandment as compared to its gain, and the gain of a transgression as compared to its loss. Therefore, “I returned my feet to Your testimonies,” because I saw that it [Your way] is the best of all of them.



### Verse 61

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:61:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:61:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:61:1)


**חֶבְלֵי רְשָׁעִים עִוְּדוּנִי.** סִיעוֹת שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים שְׁלָלוּנִי, כְּמוֹ ״יֹאכַל עַד״ (בראשית מט:כז), כָּךְ חִבְּרוֹ מְנַחֵם. וְיֵשׁ לְפוֹתְרוֹ לְשׁוֹן עוֹד, כְּלוֹמַר: נוֹסְפוּ וְרָבוּ עָלַי:


**Bands of wicked men robbed me** Heb. עודני. Bands of wicked men plundered me, like (Gen. 49: 27): “in the morning he will eat plunder (עד).” In this manner, Menachem (p. 131) associated it. It may also be interpreted as an expression of עוֹד, more, i.e., increased and outnumbered me.



### Verse 67

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:67:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:67:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:67:1)


**טֶרֶם אֶעֱנֶה.** אוֹתְךָ בְּמִצְוֹתֶיךָ, טֶרֶם הָגִיתִי בָּהֶם בְּבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת **אֲנִי שֹׁגֵג** בָּהֶם וְחוֹטֵא. **וְעַתָּה** מִשֶּׁנַּעֲנֵיתִי בָּהֶם **תּוֹרָתְךָ שָׁמָרְתִּי**, שֶׁהַמִּדְרָשׁ מְלַמְּדֵנִי לָסוּר מִן הָעֲבֵירָה. לָכֵן אֲנִי מְבַקֵּשׁ מִמְּךָ **טוּב טַעַם וָדַעַת לַמְּדֵנִי**:


**Before I recited** to You about Your commandments, before I uttered them in the study halls, I erred in them and sinned. But now that I have recited them, I kept your Torah, for study teaches me to turn away from sin: therefore, I beg of You, “Teach me the best of reason and knowledge.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 119:67:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:67:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:67:2)


**אֶעֱנֶה.** לְשׁוֹן שׁוֹנֶה וְהוֹגֶה בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ הוּא, כְּמוֹ **תַּעַן לְשׁוֹנִי אִמְרָתֶךָ**. וְכֵן ״יַכְרֵת ה׳ לָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂנָּה עֵר וְעֹנֶה מֵאָהֳלֵי יַעֲקֹב״ (מלאכי ב:יב), עֵר בַּחֲכָמִים וְעוֹנֶה בַּתַּלְמִידִים:


**I recited** Heb. אענה, an expression of studying and reciting in the study hall, like (verse 172): “My tongue will utter (תען) Your word.” Similarly (Mal. 2:12): “From the man who commits it, the Lord shall cut off one of acuity or erudition (ועונה) from the tents of Jacob.” An ingenious one among the sages, and one who can answer among the students.



### Verse 69

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:69:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:69:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:69:1)


**טָפְלוּ עָלַי שֶׁקֶר.** חִבְּרוּ עָלַי שֶׁקֶר, וְכֵן ״וְתִטְפֹּל עַל עֲוֹנִי״ (איוב יד:יז):


**Willful sinners have heaped false accusations upon me** Heb. טפלו, they joined upon me, and similarly (Job 14:17): “and You have attached Yourself (ותטפל) to my iniquity.”



### Verse 71

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:71:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:71:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:71:1)


**טוֹב לִי כִּי עֻנֵּיתִי.** שֶׁנִּתְיַסַּרְתִּי וְעֻנֵּיתִי **לְמַעַן** אָשׁוּב מִדֶּרֶךְ רָעָה וְאֶשְׁמֹר חֻקֶּיךָ. בְּפֵרוּשִׁים אֲחֵרִים מָצָאתִי כֵּן: **טוֹב לִי כִּי עֻנֵּיתִי וְגוֹ׳,** טוֹב הָיָה בְּעֵינַי כְּשֶׁהָיִיתִי סוֹבֵל יִסּוּרִים כְּדֵי לִלְמֹד תּוֹרָה בְּצַעַר:


**It is good for me that I was afflicted** That I was chastised and afflicted in order that I repent of the evil way and keep Your statutes. In other commentaries I found the following: **It is good for me that I was afflicted, etc.** It appeared good to me when I suffered privations in order to learn Your statutes, when I learned the Torah in pain.



### Verse 74

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:74:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:74:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:74:1)


**יְרֵאֶיךָ יִרְאוּנִי.** בְּטוֹבָה וְיִשְׂמָחוּ, כִּי כִּגְמוּלִי גְּמוּלָם, שֶׁהֲרֵי מִיְּרֵאֶיךָ אֲנִי וְ**לִדְבָרְךָ יִחָלְתִּי**:


**Those who fear You will see me** in prosperity and rejoice, because what was bestowed upon me will be bestowed upon them, for I am among those who fear You, and I hoped for Your word.



### Verse 75

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:75:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:75:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:75:1)


**וֶאֱמוּנָה עִנִּיתָנִי.** בְּדִין עִנִּיתָנִי:


**in faith You afflicted me** With justice, You afflicted me.



### Verse 78

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:78:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:78:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:78:1)


**כִּי שֶׁקֶר עִוְּתוּנִי.** כִּי עַל חִנָּם הִרְשִׁיעוּנִי (מצאתי). אוֹמֵר אֲנִי: עַל לִבּוּן פָּנִים, שֶׁאוֹמֵר לוֹ: הַבָּא עַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ – מִיתָתוֹ בַּמֶּה? וְהוּא לֹא חָטָא (סנהדרין קז.):


**for they condemned me falsely** For no reason they condemned me. (I found:) I say that this deals with the embarrassment [of David] when they would say to him, “If one is intimate with a married woman, with what [method] is his death penalty?” when he [David] had not sinned.



### Verse 79

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:79:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:79:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:79:1)


**יָשׁוּבוּ לִי יְרֵאֶיךָ.** שֶׁפֵּרְשׁוּ הֵימֶנּוּ סַנְהֶדְרִין כְּשֶׁנִּצְטָרַע מֵאוֹתוֹ עָוֹן (סנהדרין קז.). אַף אִם גְּרוּשָׁה הִיא נָתַן עֵינָיו בָּהּ, כָּל הַנּוֹגֵעַ לֹא יִנָּקֶה (משלי ו:כט):


**May those who fear You...return to me** For the Sanhedrin separated from him when he became a mezora because of that iniquity [with Bath-sheba]. Even if she was divorced, whoever puts his eyes on her, anyone who touches her, will not be guiltless.



### Verse 81

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:81:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:81:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:81:1)


**כָּלְתָה וְגוֹ׳ נַפְשִׁי.** אִוְּתָה:


**pines** Heb. כלתה, desires.



### Verse 82

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:82:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:82:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:82:1)


**כָּלוּ עֵינַי.** צוֹפִים תָּמִיד עַד כִּי כָּלוּ:


**My eyes pine** Heb. כלו, lit. fail. My eyes look constantly until they fail.



### Verse 83

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:83:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:83:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:83:1)


**כְּנֹאד בְּקִיטוֹר.** כְּנֹאד שֶׁל עוֹר הַמִּתְיַבֵּשׁ בֶּעָשָׁן:


**like a wineskin in smoke** Like a flask of skin that dries in smoke.



### Verse 84

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:84:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:84:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:84:1)


**מָתַי תַּעֲשֶׂה.** שֶׁאֶרְאֶה בְּיָמַי:


**When will You execute** that I might see it in my days.



### Verse 85

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:85:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:85:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:85:1)


**כָּרוּ לִי זֵדִים שִׁיחוֹת.** שֶׁלֹּא כַתּוֹרָה הַבָּאִים לְפָסְלֵנִי:


**Willful sinners have dug pits for me** Those who come to disqualify me do not do so according to the Torah.



### Verse 86

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:86:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:86:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:86:1)


**כָּל מִצְוֹתֶיךָ אֱמוּנָה.** מוֹאָבִי וְלֹא מוֹאָבִית (יבמות עז.), וְהֵם עַל שֶׁקֶר רָדְפוּ לְאָסְרֵנִי:


**All Your commandments are faithful** A Moabite and not a Moabitess; but they pursue [me] to prohibit me [from entering the congregation of the Lord].


###### Rashi on Psalms 119:86:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:86:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:86:2)


**שֶׁקֶר רְדָפוּנִי.** לַשָּׁוְא רְדָפוּנִי אוֹיְבַי:


**they pursued me in vain** My enemies pursued me in vain.



### Verse 87

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:87:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:87:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:87:1)


**כִּמְעַט כִּלּוּנִי.** כְּלֹא הָיִיתִי אֶהְיֶה בָּאָרֶץ (איוב י:יט), וַאֲנִי עָמַדְתִּי עַל בֻּרְיִי, וְכֵן **לִי קִוּוּ רְשָׁעִים לְאַבְּדֵנִי** מִבֹּא בַּקָּהָל:


**They almost destroyed me** I was on the earth as nothing, but I stood with my strength. Likewise (verse 95): “Concerning me, the wicked hoped to destroy me” from entering the congregation, and so (above 116:16): “You loosed my thongs.”



### Verse 96

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:96:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:96:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:96:1)


**לְכָל תִּכְלָה וְגוֹ׳.** לְסַלְסֵל וּלְפַלְפֵּל בָּהּ, וְכֵן ״פִּתַּחְתָּ לְמוֹסֵרָי״ (תהלים קטז:טז):


**or every finite thing, etc.** to search them and to debate about them.


###### Rashi on Psalms 119:96:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:96:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:96:2)


**לְכָל תִּכְלָה.** לְכָל סִיּוּם דָּבָר יֵשׁ **קֵץ** גְבוּל, אֲבָל **מִצְוָתְךָ** אֵין קֵץ וּגְבוּל לְתַכְלִיתָם (מצאתי):


**Of every finite thing** To every conclusion of a thing there is an end and a boundary, but Your commandments have no end or boundary to their conclusion.



### Verse 98

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:98:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:98:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:98:1)


**מֵאוֹיְבַי תְּחַכְּמֵנִי מִצְוֹתֶיךָ.** עַל דּוֹאֵג וַאֲחִיתֹפֶל אָמְרוּ, דְּלָא אָתְיָא לְהוּ שְׁמַעְתָּא אֲלִיבָּא דְהִלְכְתָא (סוטה כא.). לְעוֹלָם סוֹד הַתּוֹרָה בְּיָדִי, שֶׁכֵּן **מִכָּל מְלַמְּדַי הִשְׂכַּלְתִּי.** מִזֶּה לָמַדְתִּי קְצָת וּמִזֶּה לָמַדְתִּי קְצָת (לְאַחַר שֶׁלָּמַדְתִּי מֵרַבִּי מֻבְהָק):


**Each of Your commandments makes me wiser than my enemies** Concerning Doeg and Ahithophel they [the Rabbis] said that their final conclusions did not agree with adopted practice. The secret of the Torah is in my hands forever, for I gained understanding from all my teachers; I learned a little from this one and I learned a little from that one (after I learned from my distinguished teacher).



### Verse 99

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:99:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:99:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:99:1)


**שִׂיחָה לִי.** כָּל שִׂיחָתִי הָיְתָה בָּם:


**are my conversation** All my conversation was about them.



### Verse 101

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:101:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:101:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:101:1)


**כָּלִאתִי רַגְלָי.** מָנַעְתִּי, כְּמוֹ ״אֲשֶׁר כְּלִיתִנִי הַיּוֹם מִבּוֹא בְדָמִים״ (שמואל א כה:לג):


**I restrained my feet** Heb. כלאתי, I restrained, as (I Sam. 25:33): “who have restrained me (כלתני) this day from coming into bloodshed.”



### Verse 103

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:103:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:103:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:103:1)


**נִמְלְצוּ.** נִמְתְּקוּ:



### Verse 105

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:105:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:105:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:105:1)


**נֵר לְרַגְלִי דְבָרֶךָ.** כְּשֶׁאֲנִי בָּא לְהוֹרוֹת הוֹרָאָה, אֲנִי רוֹאֶה בַּתּוֹרָה, וְהִיא מַפְרֶשֶׁת אוֹתִי מִן הָאִסּוּר כְּנֵר הַמַּצִּיל אֶת הָאָדָם מִן הַפְּחָתִים:


**Your words are a lamp for my foot** When I come to promulgate a decision of law, I look in the Torah and it separates me from [transgressing] the prohibition, like a lamp which saves a man from [falling into] the pits.



### Verse 107

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:107:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:107:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:107:1)


**נַעֲנֵיתִי.** נַעֲשֵׂיתִי עָנִי וְשָׁפָל, כְּמוֹ ״לֵעָנוֹת מִפָּנַי״ (שמות י:ג), וְ״עָנָה גְאוֹן יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּפָנָיו״ (הושע ה:ה) תַּרְגּוּם יוֹנָתָן: ״וְיִמָּאךְ״. וְעָנִי חָשׁוּב כְּמֵת, לְפִיכָךְ **חַיֵּנִי כִדְבָרֶךָ**:


**I have been... humbled** Heb. נעניתי, I have been made poor and humble, like (Exod. 10): “to humble Yourself from before Me”; (Hos. 5:5), “And the pride of Israel shall be humbled before them,” which Jonathan renders: וימאךְ. And a poor man is accounted as dead. Therefore, revive me according to Your words.


###### Rashi on Psalms 119:107:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:107:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:107:2)


**נַעֲנֵיתִי.** חֳלִי הוּא שֶׁמְּטָרֵף אֶת הַדַּעַת, וּשְׁמוֹ עֲנִיָּה בִּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה (חולין ס:):


**I have been...humbled** Heb. נעניתי. This is a sickness that deranges the mind, and it is called עֲוִית convulsion, in the language of the Mishnah (Chul. 60b).



### Verse 108

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:108:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:108:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:108:1)


**נִדְבוֹת פִּי.** דָּבָר רָצוּי שֶׁפִּי מִתְנַדֵּב לְךָ, כָּל נְדָבָה לְשׁוֹן רָצוֹן הוּא:


**The freewill offering of my mouth** Words of appeasement that my mouth offers You. Every נדבה, is an expression of appeasement.



### Verse 109

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:109:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:109:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:109:1)


**נַפְשִׁי בְכַפִּי תָמִיד.** הַרְבֵּה נִסְתַּכַּנְתִּי, בִּסְכָנוֹת רַבּוֹת קְרוֹבוֹת לְמִיתָה, וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן אֲנִי **תוֹרָתְךָ לֹא שָׁכָחְתִּי** (על דרך חש בראשו יעסוק בתורה):


**My soul is constantly in my hand** I have very often been in serious danger, close to death, but nonetheless, I have not forgotten Your Torah (following the pattern of “Whoever has a headache should engage in the Torah”).



### Verse 112

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:112:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:112:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:112:1)


**לְעוֹלָם עֵקֶב.** עַל מַעְגְּלוֹתָם וְעַל נְתִיבוֹתָם:


**forever on their paths** On their paths and their roads.



### Verse 113

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:113:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:113:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:113:1)


**סֵעֲפִים שָׂנֵאתִי.** חוֹשְׁבֵי מַחְשְׁבוֹת אָוֶן, כְּמוֹ (איוב כ:ב) ״לָכֵן שְׂעִיפַי יְשִׁיבוּנִי״, (מלכים א יח:כא) ״עַל שְׁתֵּי הַסְּעִפִּים״. כְּשֶׁאַתָּה קוֹרֵא סְעִיפִים הוּא שֵׁם הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה, וּכְשֶׁאַתָּה קוֹרֵא סֵעֲפִים נוֹפֵל הַלָּשׁוֹן עַל הַחוֹשְׁבִים אוֹתָם:


**I hate those who harbor iniquitous thoughts** Those who think thoughts of iniquity, like (Job 20: 2): “Therefore, my thoughts (סעפי) answer me”; (I Kings 18:21), “between two ideas (הסעפים).” When you read סְעִפִים, it concerns the thought, but when you read סֵעֲפִים, the language refers to those who think it.



### Verse 117

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:117:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:117:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:117:1)


**וְאֶשְׁעָה בְחֻקֶּיךָ.** וְאֶתְעַסֵּק, כְּמוֹ ״וְאַל יִשְׁעוּ בְּדִבְרֵי שָׁקֶר״ (שמות ה:ט). דָּבָר אַחֵר: **וְאֶשְׁעָה** לְשׁוֹן סִפּוּר וְשִׁנּוּן, כְּדִמְתַרְגְּמִינָן ״וְלִשְׁנִינָה״ (דברים כח:לז): ״וּלְשׁוֹעִין״ (תרגום אונקלוס):


**and I shall constantly engage in Your statutes** Heb. ואשעה, and I shall engage, like (Exod. 5: 9): “and let them not engage (ישעו) in useless things.” Another explanation: [It is] an expression of telling and reciting, as we translate (Deut. 28:37): “and a recitation (ולשועין).”



### Verse 118

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:118:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:118:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:118:1)


**סָלִיתָ.** רָמַסְתָּ, נְתַתָּם לְמִרְמָס, כְּמוֹ ״סִלָּה כָּל אַבִּירַי ה׳״ (איכה א:טו):


**You trampled** Heb. סלית, You trampled; You made them a thing trampled on, like (Lam. 1: 15): “The Lord trampled (סלה) all my mighty men.”



### Verse 120

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:120:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:120:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:120:1)


**סָמַר.** כְּמוֹ (איוב ד:טו) ״תְּסַמֵּר שַׂעֲרַת בְּשָׂרִי״, כְּאָדָם שֶׁעָמְדוּ שַׂעֲרוֹתָיו. הִירִיצִיי״ר בְּלַעַ״ז:


**bristles** Heb. סמר, like (Job 4:15): “it made the hair of my flesh stand on end (מסמר),” as a person whose hair stands on end, harizer in Old French, se herisser in modern French, to bristle.


###### Rashi on Psalms 119:120:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:120:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:120:2)


**וּמִמִּשְׁפָּטֶיךָ יָרֵאתִי.** מִפֻּרְעָנוּת גְּזֵרוֹתֶיךָ:


**and I dread Your judgments** The retribution for Your decrees.



### Verse 122

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:122:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:122:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:122:1)


**עֲרֹב עַבְדְּךָ.** לְשׁוֹן הַצָּלָה, גרנטיי״ה בְּלַעַ״ז. הֱיֵה עָרֵב בִּשְׁבִילִי לְנֶגֶד הָרָעָה (כְּלוֹמַר הָיָה עָרֵב שֶׁאֶשְׁמֹר פְּקוּדֶיךָ):


**Be surety** Heb. ערב, garantis in French, to vouch for. Be a guarantor for me against the evil (i.e., be a guarantor that I keep Your precepts).



### Verse 123

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:123:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:123:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:123:1)


**וּלְאִמְרַת צִדְקֶךָ.** הַבְטָחָה שֶׁהִבְטַחְתַּנִי:


**and for the word of Your righteousness** The promise that You promised me.



### Verse 126

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:126:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:126:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:126:1)


**עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה׳ וְגוֹ׳.** מוּסָב עַל מִקְרָא שֶׁלְּפָנָיו **הֲבִינֵנִי וְאֵדְעָה עֵדוֹתֶיךָ**, לְהָבִין **עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת** לְשִׁמְךָ, אֵיךְ יַעֲשׂוּ אוֹתָם שֶׁ**הֵפֵרוּ תוֹרָתֶךָ** לִמְצֹא רָצוֹן וּסְלִיחָה וְתִמָּצֵא לָהֶם, וְאֶעֱשֶׂה כֵּן עַל כָּל עֲבֵירָה שֶׁבְּיָדִי. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָּרְשׁוּ מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁעוֹבְרִין עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת סְיָג וְגָדֵר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּגוֹן גִּדְעוֹן וְאֵלִיָּה בְּהַר הַכַּרְמֶל שֶׁהִקְרִיבוּ בַּבָּמָה (ברכות סג.). עוֹד רָאִיתִי נִדְרָשׁ בָּאַגָּדָה (ירושלמי ברכות ט:ד, מדרש שמואל א:א) פֵּרוּשׁ: אִישׁ פָּנוּי וְטַיְלָן הָעוֹשֶׂה תוֹרָתוֹ עִתִּים מֵפֵר בְּרִית, שֶׁאָדָם (פָּנוּי) צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת יָגֵעַ בַּתּוֹרָה כָּל שָׁעוֹת הַיּוֹם:


**A time to do for the Lord, etc.** This goes back to the verse preceding it: Enable me to understand, and I shall know Your testimonies, to know a time to do for Your name. What should they do, those who made Your Torah void, to find good will and forgiveness, and that You should be found by them, and I will do so for every transgression that I have committed. Our Rabbis, however, derived from it [from this verse] that we may transgress the words of the Torah in order to make a fence and a wall [a safeguard] for Israel, e.g. Gideon and Elijah on Mount Carmel, who sacrificed on high places (Ber. 63a). I saw [it] further expounded upon in the Aggadah (Yerushalmi Ber. 9:4, Mid. Sam 1:1) as meaning: A person who is idle and leisurely, who devotes [only occasional] times to his Torah, makes void the covenant, for an idle person must toil in the Torah all hours of the day.



### Verse 127

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:127:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:127:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:127:1)


**עַל כֵּן אָהַבְתִּי.** עַל אֲשֶׁר אָהַבְתִּי מִצְוֹתֶיךָ רָאוּי לְךָ לְלַמְּדֵנִי עֵת רָצוֹן וּמָה אֶעֱשֶׂה לְךָ וְתִרְצֵנִי. יֵשׁ עַל כֵּן הַרְבֵּה שֶׁפִּתְרוֹנוֹ עַל אֲשֶׁר, כְּמוֹ ״כִּי עַל כֵּן רָאִיתִי פָנֶיךָ״ (בראשית לג:י), ״כִּי עַל כֵּן יָדַעְתָּ חֲנֹתֵנוּ״ (במדבר י:לא), ״עַל כֵּן יִתְרָה עָשָׂה״ (ישעיהו טו:ז):


**Because I loved** Heb. על-כן. Because I loved Your commandments, it is fitting that You teach me a time of good will, and what I should do for You that You should accept me. There are many [instances of] על-כן that are to be interpreted as “because”; e.g., (Gen. 33:10): “because (כי על-כן) I have seen your face”; (Num. 10:33). “because (כי על-כן) you know our encampment”; (Isa. 15: 7), “Because of (כי על-כן) the many things they did.”



### Verse 128

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:128:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:128:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:128:1)


**כָּל פִּקּוּדֵי כֹל יִשָּׁרְתִּי.** כָּל פִּקּוּדֵי – כָּל דָּבָר אֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתָ בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ:


**Because I considered all precepts of all things upright** All precepts, everything that You commanded in your Torah.


###### Rashi on Psalms 119:128:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:128:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:128:2)


**יִשַּׁרְתִּי.** יָשְׁרוּ בְּעֵינַי, וְאָמַרְתִּי עֲלֵיהֶם: יָשְׁרוּ. כָּל זֶה כְּדַאי אֲנִי שֶׁתִּמְחוֹל וְתִרְצֶה לִי:


**I considered upright** Heb. ישרתי. They were upright in my eyes, and I said about them that they are upright. Because of this, I deserve that You forgive me and favor me.



### Verse 129

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:129:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:129:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:129:1)


**פְּלָאוֹת עֵדְוֺתֶיךָ.** מְכֻסִּים הֵם וְנִפְלָאִים עֵדְוֺתֶיךָ מִבְּנֵי אָדָם. יֵשׁ מִצְווֹת קַלּוֹת שֶׁהִרְבֵּיתָ בְּמַתַּן שְׂכָרָן, כְּגוֹן שִׁלּוּחַ הַקֵּן (דברים כב:ו-ז):


**Your testimonies are hidden** They are covered, and your testimonies are hidden from the sons of men. There are easy commandments for which He gave a large reward, such as sending away the nest.


###### Rashi on Psalms 119:129:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:129:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:129:2)


**עַל כֵּן נְצָרָתַם נַפְשִׁי.** כֻּלָּם, כִּי לֹא נוֹדַע אֵיזֶה יִכְשַׁר (קהלת יא:ו):


**therefore, my soul kept them** All of them, because it is not known which is better.



### Verse 130

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:130:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:130:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:130:1)


**פֵּתַח דְּבָרֶיךָ יָאִיר.** תְּחִלַּת דְּבָרֶיךָ הֵאִירוּ אֶת לֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁאַתָּה הַ**מֵּבִין פְּתָיִים** בְּאָמְרְךָ (שמות כ:ב) ״אָנֹכִי אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִיךָ״, הוֹדַעְתָּם בַּטּוֹבָה שֶׁעָשִׂיתָ לָהֶם, שֶׁקְּנִיתָם מִבֵּית עֲבָדִים לָדַעַת כִּי אָדוֹן אַתָּה לָהֶם וִיקַבְּלוּ אֱלֹהוּתְךָ עֲלֵיהֶם, ״לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וְגוֹ׳״, וְאַחַר כָּךְ גָּזַרְתָּ גְּזֵרוֹתֶיךָ. דָּבָר אַחֵר: **פֵּתַח דְּבָרֶיךָ יָאִיר** תְּחִלַּת דְּבָרֶיךָ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית (בראשית א:ג) ״יְהִי אוֹר״:


**The commencement of Your words enlightens** The beginning of your words enlightened the heart of Israel, that You understated the simple, by Your statement (Exod. 20:2): “I am...Who took you out.” You let them know the favor that You did for them—that You acquired them from the house of bondageto know that You are their Master, and they should accept Your kingdom upon themselves. (Exod. 20:3): “You shall not have another god, etc.” and afterwards You made Your decrees (Cf. Mechilta ad loc.). Another explanation: **The commencement of Your words enlightens** The beginning of Your words in the Creation was (Gen. 1:3): “Let there be light.”


###### Rashi on Psalms 119:130:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:130:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:130:2)


**מֵבִין פְּתָיִים.** מִשָּׁם יָבִינוּ הַכֹּל וְיִפְתְּחוּ (לְהַתְחִיל וְלִפְתֹּחַ) בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, תַּנְחוּמָא (תנחומא, ויקהל ו):


**You make the simple understand** From there, everyone will understand and will commence with words of Torah. Tanchuma (Vayakhel 6).



### Verse 131

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:131:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:131:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:131:1)


**וָאֶשְׁאָפָה.** לְשׁוֹן בְּלִיעָה, כְּמוֹ ״שָׁאֲפָה רוּחַ״ (ירמיהו ב:כד):


**and panted** Heb. ואשאפה, an expression of swallowing, as (Jer. 2:24): “snuffs up (שאפה) the wind.”



### Verse 134

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:134:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:134:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:134:1)


**פְּדֵנִי מֵעֹשֶׁק אָדָם.** מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע הָעוֹשֵׁק אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת. בְּפֵרוּשִׁים אֲחֵרִים מָצָאתִי **פְּדֵנִי מֵעֹשֶׁק אָדָם**, פְּדֵנִי מֵעוֹשְׁקוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם:


**Redeem me from the oppression of man** From the evil inclination, which oppresses the people (from the good path—Parshandatha). In other commentaries I found: **Redeem me from the oppression of man** Redeem me so that no man oppress me.



### Verse 139

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:139:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:139:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:139:1)


**צִמְּתַתְנִי קִנְאָתִי.** הַקִּנְאָה שֶׁאֲנִי מְקַנֵּא לְשִׁמְךָ עַל הַשּׁוֹכְחֵי **דְבָרֶיךָ**, הִיא צוֹמְתָה אוֹתִי וּמַקְנֶטֶת אוֹתִי בָּהֶם (מצאתי):


**My zeal incenses me** Heb. קנאתי. The zeal with which I am zealous for Your name against those who forget Your words, cuts me and incenses me against them.



### Verse 141

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:141:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:141:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:141:1)


**צָעִיר אָנֹכִי וְנִבְזֶה.** כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר ״וְדָוִד הוּא הַקָּטָן״ (שמואל א יז:יד), נִבְזֶה אֲנִי לְהַקְטִין עַצְמִי אֵצֶל עוֹסְקֵי תוֹרָה לְהִתְלַמֵּד, כִּי **פִּקֻּדֶיךָ לֹא שָׁכַחְתִּי** מִלְּסַלְסֵל וּמִלְּפַלְפֵּל בָּהֶם בְּצִדְקָתְךָ שֶׁבְּתוֹכָן צֶדֶק וֶאֱמֶת עוֹלָמִית, וְאַף כִּי מְצָאוּנִי צָרוֹת הָיוּ הֵם עִסְקִי, וּלְעוֹלָם הֲבִינֵנִי צִדְקָם וְאֶחְיֶה בָהֶם ״כִּי הִיא חַיֶּיךָ וְגוֹמֵר״ (דברים ל:כ):


**I am young and despised** As it is stated (I Sam. 17:14): “And David was the youngest.” I am despised to the extent that I humble myself beside those who engage in the Torah, to learn, for I have not forgotten Your precepts; [nor have I refrained] from searching and debating with them about Your righteousness that is within them [the precepts], which is righteousness and truth to eternity; and even though troubles have befallen me, they were my occupation. And forever enable me to understand their righteousness and I shall live by them (Deut. 30:20): “for it [the Torah] is your life and the length of your days.”



### Verse 146

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:146:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:146:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:146:1)


(הַסִּימָן שֶׁל **עֵדְֹתֶיךָ** דָּמָה בֶּן פֶּרֶ״ץ, הַוָּי״ו חוֹלָם, אֲבָל מִשְּׁאָר עֵדֹתֶיךָ הַדָּלֶ״ת חוֹלָם):


**and I shall keep** (The acronym of, עֵדְוֹתֶיךָ is דמה בן פֶרֶץ ; the “vav” is vowelized with a “holam,” but in the other instances, it is עֵדֹתֶיךָ ; the “daleth” is vowelized with a “holam.”)



### Verse 148

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:148:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:148:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:148:1)


**אַשְׁמֻרוֹת.** חֲצִי הַלַּיְלָה, שְׁתֵּי אַשְׁמוּרוֹת (איכה רבה ב:כב); וּלְדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר (איכה רבה ב:כב) ׳שָׁלֹשׁ מִשְׁמָרוֹת הֲוֵי לַיְלָה׳, הָיָה דָּוִד עוֹמֵד מִמִּטָּתוֹ בִּשְׁלִישׁ הַלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה עַד חֲצוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: **לָשִׂיחַ בְּאִמְרָתֶךָ**, וּמֵחֲצוֹת וּלְהַלָּן עוֹסֵק בְּשִׁירוֹת וְתוּשְׁבָּחוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר **חֲצוֹת לַיְלָה אָקוּם לְהוֹדוֹת לָךְ**:


**watches** Half the night, two watches, and according to one who says that the night consists of three watches, David would rise from bed at the first third of the night and engage in Torah until midnight, as it is said: “to speak of Your word.” From midnight on, he would engage in songs and praises, as it is said (verse 62): “At midnight, I rise to give thanks to You.”



### Verse 150

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:150:1

**קָרְבוּ רוֹדְפֵי זִמָּה.** עֲצַת חַטָּאִים הוֹלְכִים בַּעֲצַת חַטָּאֵיהֶם, וּמִתְרַחֲקִים **מִתּוֹרָתְךָ** לִקָּרֵב אֶל עֲצַת רָעָתָם:


**Pursuers of lewdness have drawn near** a counsel of sins. They follow the counsel of their sins and distance themselves from your Torah to draw near to the counsel of their evil.



### Verse 151

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:151:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:151:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:151:1)


**קָרוֹב אַתָּה.** לָרְחוֹקִים הַלָּלוּ הַמִּתְרַחֲקִים מִתּוֹרָתֶךָ, אִם יָשׁוּבוּ מִדַּרְכָּם:


**You are near** to these faraway people, who distance themselves from Your Torah, if they repent of their way.



### Verse 152

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:152:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:152:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:152:1)


**קֶדֶם יָדַעְתִּי מֵעֵדֹתֶיךָ.** קוֹדֶם הֱיוֹת הַדָּבָר יְדַעְתִּיו מִתּוֹךְ עֵדֹתֶיךָ: קֹדֶם יָרְשׁוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ צִוִּיתָ לָהֶם עַל הַבִּכּוּרִים וּתְרוּמוֹת וּמַעַשְׂרוֹת, וְקֹדֶם הֲנִיחוֹת לָהֶם מֵאוֹיְבֵיהֶם צִוִּיתָ לָהֶם ״וְהָיָה בְּהָנִיחַ ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְךָ וְגוֹ׳״ (דברים כה:יט) לְהַעֲמִיד מֶלֶךְ וּלְהַכְרִית עֲמָלֵק וְלִבְנוֹת בֵּית הַבְּחִירָה (סנהדרין כ:):


**From before, I knew from Your testimonies** Before the thing came about, I knew it from Your testimonies. Before they inherited the land, You commanded them about the first fruits, heave offerings, and tithes, and before You gave them rest from their enemies, You commanded them (Deut. 25:19): “And it will be, when the Lord Your God gives you rest, etc.” to appoint a king, to annihilate Amalek, and to build the Temple.


###### Rashi on Psalms 119:152:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:152:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:152:2)


**כִּי לְעוֹלָם יְסַדְתָּם.** כִּי עַל כָּל הַדְּבָרִים הָעֲתִידִים לִהְיוֹת לְסוֹף הָעוֹלָם יִסַּדְתָּ עֵדוֹתֶיךָ:


**to the world** For You established Your testimonies concerning all things destined to be until the end of the world.



### Verse 160

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:160:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:160:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:160:1)


**רֹאשׁ דְּבָרְךָ אֱמֶת.** סוֹף דְּבָרְךָ הוֹכִיחַ עַל הָרֹאשׁ שֶׁהוּא אֱמֶת, שֶׁכְּשֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ הָאֻמּוֹת ״אָנֹכִי״ וְ״לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ״ וְ״לֹא תִשָּׂא״ (שמות כ:ב-ז) אָמְרוּ: הַכֹּל לַהֲנָאָתוֹ וְלִכְבוֹדוֹ. כֵּיוָן שֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ ״כַּבֵּד״, ״לֹא תִרְצַח״, ״לֹא תִנְאָף״ (שמות כ:יב-יג), הוֹדוּ עַל רֹאשׁ דְּבָרְךָ שֶׁהוּא אֱמֶת (קידושין לא.):


**The beginning of Your word is true** And the end of Your word is not true? Rather, the end of Your word proves that the beginning of Your word is true. For, when the nations heard, “I am the Lord your God,” and “You shall not have [another god],” and “You shall not take, etc.,” they said, “Everything is for His benefit and for His glory.” As soon as they heard, “Honor, etc.; You shall not murder; You shall not commit adultery,” they admitted [that they had erred] about the beginning of Your word, that it is true.



### Verse 162

###### Rashi on Psalms 119:162:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:162:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rashi%20on%20Psalms/r/119:162:1)


**שָׂשׂ אָנֹכִי עַל אִמְרָתֶךָ.** עַל הַבְטָחָתְךָ שֶׁהִבְטַחְתַּנִי. דָּבָר אַחֵר: עַל אַחַת מֵאִמְרוֹתֶיךָ הַסְּתוּמוֹת, כְּשֶׁאֲנִי מֵבִין בָּהּ. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָּרְשׁוּ עַל הַמִּילָה (מנחות מג:): שֶׁהָיָה דָוִד בְּבֵית הַמֶּרְחָץ וְרָאָה עַצְמוֹ בְּלֹא צִיצִית וּבְלֹא תְּפִילִּין וּבְלֹא תּוֹרָה, אָמַר: אוֹי לִי שֶׁאֲנִי עָרוֹם מִכָּל מִצְווֹת. כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּסְתַּכֵּל בַּמִּילָה שָׂמַח, וְאָמַר בְּצֵאתוֹ (מִבֵּית הַמֶּרְחָץ): **שָׂשׂ אָנֹכִי עַל אִמְרָתֶךָ**, הַמִּילָה שֶׁמִּתְּחִלָּה נִתְּנָה בְּמַאֲמָר וְלֹא בְדִבּוּר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בראשית יז:ט): ״וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים אֶל אַבְרָהָם וְאַתָּה אֶת בְּרִיתִי תִשְׁמֹר״:


**I rejoice over Your word** Over Your promise that You promised me. Another explanation: Over one of Your enigmatic statements, when I understand it. Our Rabbis, however, interpreted it as referring to circumcision, for [when] David was in the bathhouse and saw himself without zizith, without tefillin, and without Torah, he said, “Woe is to me, for I am naked of all commandments.” As soon as he thought of the circumcision, he rejoiced and said when he emerged (from the bathhouse), “I rejoice over Your word.” [This refers to] circumcision, which was first given with a saying (אמירה), and not with speaking (דיבור), as it is said (Gen. 17:9): “And God said (ויאמר) to Abraham, ‘And you shall keep My covenant.’”

**שֶׁבַע בַּיּוֹם.** שַׁחֲרִית שְׁתַּיִם לִפְנֵי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וְאַחַת לְאַחֲרֶיהָ, וּבָעֶרֶב שְׁתַּיִם לְפָנֶיהָ וּשְׁתַּיִם לְאַחֲרֶיהָ (ברכות יא:):


**Seven times a day** In the morning, twice before the reading of “Shema” and once after it, and in the evening, twice before it and twice after it.

**for Your righteous judgments** For the reading of the Shema, which consists of words of Torah.

**according to Your word, enable me to understand** the words of Your Torah; according to their law and in the order in which they stand.
